title: Trump: Hormuz opens 'very soon' or Iran gets hit 'very hard'
description: Trump told reporters in California that Strait of Hormuz negotiations were going well, saying negotiators 'had a very good day' and a deal could come 'tomorrow or the next day,' but warned 'the strait's going to be open very soon, or they're going to get hit very hard.' The US, Iran and Oman were reportedly nearing a 60-day interim arrangement for safe passage, Axios reported, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said there was 'a chance we may have a deal' by Aug. 5 or 6. Iran's foreign ministry continued to deny any direct talks with Washington were underway.

title: Pentagon: US has burned through 80% of THAAD interceptor stockpile
description: CNN reported the US military has depleted nearly 80% of its roughly 452-unit pre-war THAAD interceptor stockpile and about half of its ~2,200 Patriot interceptors since the Iran war began, with commanders warning munitions are 'dangerously low.' The Army has fired 'virtually all' of its long-range PrSM and ATACMS precision missiles and burned through nearly half the global Tomahawk supply, while the Pentagon replenishes only about 15 Tomahawks and 20 Patriots a month; officials said THAAD stocks could take three or more years to rebuild. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the military 'has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the President's choosing.'

title: Bulk carrier Minoan Pioneer hit by projectile in Hormuz; crew member missing
description: The Greek-owned, Liberia-flagged bulker Minoan Pioneer was struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room while transiting northbound through Omani waters in the Strait of Hormuz, about 37km northeast of Al Khasab near the Musandam Peninsula. A fire broke out in the crew accommodation area; the rest of the crew evacuated safely but the vessel's third engineer was reported missing. No group claimed responsibility for the strike.

title: Indian ship MSV Faize Noore Oliya sinks off Yemen after suspected Houthi strike
description: The Indian-flagged cargo vessel MSV Faize Noore Oliya sank about 13 nautical miles south of Houthi-controlled Hodeidah after being struck; Yemen's Saudi-backed transport ministry blamed Iran-aligned Houthi forces for using an explosive-laden boat against the vessel, though the Houthis did not claim the attack. The Yemeni Coast Guard rescued all 14 crew members — 13 Indians and one Yemeni — and brought them to the port of Mokha.

title: Netanyahu rejects Board of Peace's Hamas disarmament draft
description: Netanyahu said in a video statement that Israel 'did not agree' to the Board of Peace's Hamas disarmament plan that Hamas accepted the prior week, calling it 'not our draft,' and vowed Israel will not withdraw 'from our current lines' in Gaza until Hamas is 'completely disarmed.' The statement contradicted earlier US-brokered characterizations of Israeli buy-in and left the disarmament roadmap's 14-day drafting deadline in doubt.

title: IDF requires chief-of-staff approval for Gaza strikes after civilian deaths
description: Israel's military tightened its rules of engagement in Gaza, requiring IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir's personal approval for all targeted-elimination strikes — a power previously delegated to division commanders — reducing the pace of strikes in the territory. The change followed criticism from the Board of Peace's lead envoy, who said 'two days of strikes across Gaza have killed civilians and destroyed medical supplies that people depend on.'

title: Trump warns Iran of 'last chance' to sign deal; Tehran denies talks underway
description: Trump said from the Oval Office Iran is facing its "last chance" to reach a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war, claiming talks were underway "at the request of Iran, backed by Saudi Arabia... UAE and... Qatar." Iran's government continued to deny any direct negotiations with Washington were taking place. Aboard Air Force One, Trump added: "nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a deal, or total surrender, is accomplished."

title: CENTCOM: Iran blockade has redirected 44 vessels, disabled 2, boarded 2
description: U.S. Central Command said that as of Aug. 3 it had redirected 44 commercial vessels attempting to enter or leave Iranian ports since resuming the naval blockade, disabling two vessels and boarding two others. The tally is up from 30 vessels redirected on Aug. 1, reflecting intensified enforcement of the blockade reinstated in mid-July.

title: Pentagon signs $3B+ deals with Northrop, Lockheed to surge interceptor output
description: The Pentagon reached framework agreements with Northrop Grumman worth over $3 billion — $2B for rocket motors and safety devices, $1B for THAAD components — aiming to quadruple THAAD interceptor production and triple PAC-3 Patriot missile output. Northrop is doubling solid rocket motor capacity at its Utah facilities and expanding its Elkton, Maryland plant by 25%, citing stockpile strain from the war.

title: IDF kills Islamic Jihad commander who held hostage Rom Braslavski
description: The IDF said it killed Mahmoud Fatair, a commander in Palestinian Islamic Jihad's Nukhba force, in a strike in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. Fatair infiltrated Israel on Oct. 7, 2023 and helped hold Israeli hostage Rom Braslavski in captivity, and was later filmed in Islamic Jihad uniform during the November 2023 hostage-release handovers. The IDF said Fatair had recently been planning attacks on Israeli civilians and troops.

title: Iran cancels planned strikes on Ukraine after Kyiv apology for Caspian ship attack
description: Khamenei adviser Mohsen Rezaee said Iran had been "set to strike three sites in Ukraine" in retaliation for Ukraine's July 25 drone strike on an Iranian cargo vessel in the Caspian Sea that killed one sailor, but canceled the attack after Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrey Sibiga told Iran's Araghchi the strike was unintentional. Rezaee warned "even if it was a mistake... there will still be consequences."

title: Iran hangs 2 men convicted of passing military coordinates to Mossad
description: Iran executed Omid Behzad and Pouria Safvat at dawn Monday after judiciary outlet Mizan and state media Fars said they were convicted of transmitting coordinates of military, police and security sites to Mossad-linked channels during the war. Fars reported Behzad used mapping apps to locate sites and forward coordinates while Safvat sent geolocation data via an overseas satellite network; the judiciary said the 'death sentences were carried out at dawn after legal proceedings, Supreme Court approval and the rejection of clemency requests.' Israel did not comment, and confessions published by Iranian state media in such cases cannot be independently verified.

title: Iran: Hormuz talks with Oman in 'final stages,' but strait won't return to pre-war status
description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that negotiations with Oman over managing transit through the Strait of Hormuz are in their 'final stages,' even as foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei insisted the waterway 'will in no way return to the status it was before February 28th.' The dual messaging signaled Tehran is willing to restore some navigational access through the Oman channel while resisting Washington's demand for full, unconditional reopening as a precondition for ending US strike threats.

title: Trump says US-Iran talks to begin Monday, sets no deadline for Hormuz deal
description: Trump said aboard Air Force One that talks with Iran on a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz would begin Monday afternoon, a day after he called off a planned bombing campaign on Iran's energy infrastructure. 'We're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon, and we'll see if it's good,' he said, declining to set any deadline for an agreement, and added, 'I'm not looking to kill people because people die, a lot of people die.' Gulf allies Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE had lobbied him to hold off on the new strikes.

title: Gaza death toll from Israeli strikes rises to 18; minister threatens 'full control'
description: The Palestinian death toll from Israeli strikes across Gaza on Sunday rose to at least 18, medics said, with deaths reported in Deir al-Balah, Mawasi near Khan Younis — where a couple and their nine-year-old son were killed in a house strike — Gaza City's Zeitoun neighborhood and near Saraya Square, and Jabalia. Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen told Army Radio there was 'no deal to halt attacks on Gaza,' saying Hamas 'must be dismantled' and that Israel, which he said already controls 70% of the territory, would need to 'take full control of it' if Hamas does not disarm.

title: Trump cancels planned Iran attack, says 'perimeters of a deal' agreed
description: Trump posted on Truth Social at 10:21pm EDT Saturday (02:21 GMT Sunday) that he had agreed 'to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL,' calling off the energy-infrastructure bombing campaign the Pentagon had readied for the weekend. He said the framework covers the 'Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat,' and that 'Israel has agreed to join the U.S. in the commitment to try to complete the agreement with Iran.' Trump said Iran and other Middle Eastern governments had asked him to hold off; no Iranian confirmation of any agreed terms followed.

title: Saudi crown prince phones Trump to argue against striking Iran's infrastructure
description: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump at about 9:25pm EDT Saturday (01:25 GMT Sunday), roughly an hour before the cancellation post, to press him not to bomb Iranian infrastructure and to seek clarity on what Washington intended, CBS News reported. The call capped a week of Saudi lobbying in which MBS sent his brother, Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, to Washington for talks with Trump and Vice President JD Vance. Qatar, the UAE, Turkey and Pakistan also pushed both capitals to de-escalate.

title: Israeli strikes kill 8 in Gaza a day after Hamas disarmament roadmap
description: Israeli forces killed at least eight Palestinians on Sunday in strikes on homes in Deir el-Balah, Khan Younis and Gaza City's Old City, Gaza's civil defence said; a helicopter strike on an apartment south of Deir el-Balah killed a man and a woman. It was the second straight day of attacks after Saturday's strikes, which killed seven and destroyed a medical supply warehouse, leaving a crater 20 by 10 metres. Israel has given no commitment to halt operations under the Board of Peace's 15-point roadmap; Hamas says it will surrender weapons only after Israel stops fighting and withdraws, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called the deal 'unacceptable.'

title: Kuwait downs Iranian drones over Bubiyan Island; debris damages government site
description: Kuwait's armed forces detected and destroyed an incursion of Iranian drones at dawn Saturday, defence ministry spokesman Colonel Saud Al-Atwan said, after they targeted a government facility in the north of the country and civilian company equipment on Bubiyan Island. 'Debris from the intercepted drones caused property damage, but there were no casualties,' Al-Atwan said. Kuwait's foreign ministry called the attacks a 'blatant violation' of its sovereignty and of UN Security Council Resolution 2817, the third consecutive night Iranian drones have reached Kuwaiti airspace.

title: Iran warns Gulf hosts of US bases they 'will burn in the fire of war'
description: Major General Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's wartime military command, said 'the United States is moving at an accelerating pace to fan the flames of a full-scale regional war' and warned that 'any country that makes itself a defensive shield for criminal, aggressor America will burn in the fire of war.' Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told regional counterparts by phone that any 'hostile action by the US or Israel — or participation or cooperation by regional countries in such actions — would be met with a decisive and proportionate response.' Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr added that 'the global economy, and US energy market and voters will pay the price' for continued strikes and the naval blockade.

title: Israel raises alert to highest level, expects Iranian missiles even if it stays out
description: Israel went to its highest state of alert ahead of the expected US offensive, with officials telling Channel 12 that Iran would fire ballistic missiles at Israel even if the IDF did not join the opening wave. 'We are very close to a decision point,' an Israeli official said. The IDF issued no public statement and Home Front Command left civilian restrictions unchanged; a separate Israeli official told CBS News that 'Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran,' contradicting US sources who said Israel was being kept informed and coordinating.

title: State Department tells Americans across Middle East to prepare to depart
description: US embassies from Jerusalem to Riyadh, Abu Dhabi and Dubai issued simultaneous security alerts telling Americans in the region to consider departing now or be ready to leave if fighting escalates, and to expect flight cancellations and periodic airspace closures. The advisory told Americans outside the region to seriously reconsider travel to or through it, citing an 'unpredictable' Iranian regime that has expanded attacks to countries not previously targeted, including Egypt. Several regional airlines postponed the resumption of normal schedules or cancelled routes outright.

title: Guterres says region 'cannot afford more war', demands Hormuz reopening
description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, wrapping up visits to Syria, Jordan and Cyprus, said 'the region — and the world — cannot afford more war' and called for fighting to stop on all fronts. He said a regional conflict had become a driver of global instability, disrupting trade through the Strait of Hormuz, raising food and energy prices and increasing the risk of hunger worldwide. Guterres demanded that navigational rights be fully restored in both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, where Houthi forces have blockaded Saudi-linked shipping.

title: US plans fresh strikes on Iran 'this weekend'; Trump vows to hit 'very hard'
description: Two US officials told CNN the US is planning fresh strikes on Iran as soon as this weekend as Trump seeks to force a resolution, though the scope and targets were unclear and both cautioned the strikes could be called off. At a Cabinet meeting Trump previewed a renewal of heavy bombardment while venting frustration at stalled diplomacy, saying 'We will be hitting them very hard.' CENTCOM has readied options including a two-week bombardment of Iran's missile sites, strikes on energy infrastructure, and plans targeting nuclear sites including the Pickaxe Mountain complex south of Tehran. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the president would not 'stand by and allow this terrorist behavior to occur' and that 'Iran will continue to pay until they come to the table' in a meaningful way. CBS News reported that planners weighed cutting electricity across Tehran and wanted the campaign concluded before financial markets opened Monday.

title: Iran extends drone barrage to US's Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain
description: Iran's army said it struck US military facilities at Sheikh Isa Air Base in southern Bahrain with drones, targeting power generators, navigation systems and support buildings, in coordinated retaliation for the previous night's US 'heavy wave' on Iran. The Bahrain strike accompanied simultaneous IRGC drone attacks on US bases in Kuwait and at Al-Azraq in Jordan; Kuwait's armed forces said an Iranian missile had killed one worker at a Chinese-owned building in the north of the country. Neither the US nor Bahrain confirmed damage, and the Iranian claims were not independently verified.

title: Tanker struck by 'unknown projectile' off Oman at mouth of Hormuz
description: A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile about 11 nautical miles northeast of Lima on Oman's Musandam Peninsula, at the southern entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, damaging its engine room and leaving it 'not under command,' the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said; no casualties or pollution were reported. A second incident followed the same day roughly 21 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, where an explosion was reported near a tanker without damage. UKMTO did not attribute the strikes, which came amid escalating US-Iran hostilities around the world's most important oil chokepoint.

title: Hamas agrees to Gaza disarmament deal; Israel balks at sequencing
description: Hamas said it reached an agreement with Trump's Board of Peace to hand its weapons to a new Palestinian National Committee and end the war, with a disarmament roadmap to be finalized within 14 days under an international verification body alongside a phased Israeli withdrawal. Trump called it 'a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace.' Israel pushed back on the sequencing, with one official saying there would be no withdrawal until Hamas undergoes 'genuine disarmament' and another minister branding the deal 'unacceptable'; the FDD noted the IDF had logged 32 Gaza ceasefire violations between July 10 and 31.

title: Iran claims drone strike on US facilities at Kuwait's Al Jaber Air Base
description: Iran's army said it launched explosive drones at 'strategic' US facilities at Kuwait's Ahmed Al Jaber Air Base, claiming it hit fighter-aircraft hangars, satellite communication systems and equipment warehouses at what it called a 'key hub' for US aerial, surveillance and logistics operations. Tehran said the strike answered 'recent attacks by the terrorist US army' and 'the brutal attack on a residential building on Qeshm Island,' where the previous day's US 'heavy wave' killed a couple and their two-year-old child. There was no immediate comment from Kuwait or the US, and the Iranian claim was not independently verified.

title: IDF destroys Hezbollah tunnel network under Beaufort Ridge with 700 tons of explosives
description: Israeli troops demolished a multi-level Hezbollah tunnel network beneath the Beaufort Ridge in southern Lebanon, detonating about 700 tons of explosives in a limited ground operation inside the security zone. The IDF said the two-decade-old, Iran-funded complex served as a Hezbollah command center for directing attacks on Israeli forces and civilians, and that Hezbollah had planned to use it to infiltrate communities in the Galilee. Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz cast the demolition as a response to Hezbollah's 'blatant' ceasefire violation a day earlier, when an explosive drone struck an Israeli engineering vehicle.

title: Saudi Arabia launches 14-nation maritime defense alliance for Red Sea
description: Saudi Arabia announced a new multinational maritime defense alliance to protect shipping in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, after hosting a Riyadh meeting attended by military representatives from 43 of 51 invited countries plus the EU. Fourteen states signed on — Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan, Yemen, Bangladesh, Sudan, Djibouti, Somalia and Comoros — with Riyadh serving as founding leader and permanent headquarters; the UAE and Oman notably did not join. Officials called the pact 'purely defensive' and not aimed at any state, framing it as a response to the Houthi maritime blockade declared on Saudi Arabia on July 20.

title: Trump announces agreement for 'complete disarmament' of Hamas in Gaza
description: President Trump announced that his Board of Peace, with mediators Egypt, Qatar and Turkey, had reached an agreement for the 'COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza,' to be carried out in phases alongside a staged Israeli withdrawal. A detailed disarmament roadmap is to be prepared within 14 days, subject to an international verification body, after which an International Stabilization Force would work with a new Palestinian police force. Hamas had not formally responded and Israeli officials voiced skepticism that Hamas would surrender its weapons, marking a rare de-escalation signal on the Gaza front as the wider Iran war intensified.

title: Saudi forces reposition for ground offensive against Houthis in al-Bayda
description: Saudi forces began repositioning from eastern Yemen to prepare a ground offensive into the Houthi-held al-Bayda governorate, expanding the kingdom's campaign against the Iran-backed group beyond air strikes. The move followed days of Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities and the group's declared maritime blockade, and came as Riyadh rallied international partners around its new Red Sea defense alliance. The escalation opened the prospect of a direct Saudi land war in Yemen tied to the broader US-Iran conflict.

title: Oil retreats about 2% as Saudi naval coalition and steadier Hormuz traffic calm markets
description: Brent crude fell nearly 2% to settle at $89.03 a barrel and US WTI slid about 1% to $83.59 on July 30, partly reversing the prior session's 8% spike, after Saudi Arabia proposed a multinational naval coalition to protect Red Sea shipping and tankers continued transiting the Gulf. Fourteen commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz in both directions on Wednesday, up from single-digit daily crossings the prior week, easing supply fears even as traffic stayed below a tenth of pre-war levels. Despite the pullback, oil was still headed for its biggest monthly gain since March, up roughly 21%.

title: US strikes dozens of IRGC targets in 'heavy wave' after Iran's Jordan attack
description: CENTCOM said it completed a 'heavy wave of strikes' against Iran at about 10 p.m. ET, hitting dozens of IRGC targets including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities, in retaliation for Iran's intercepted ballistic-missile attack on US forces in Jordan a day earlier. Explosions were reported across southern Iran, including Bandar Abbas and the islands of Kish and Qeshm, where Iranian state broadcaster IRIB said a US missile struck a residential home and search-and-rescue teams were working. Iran's IRNA later said the Qeshm strike killed three people — a couple and their two-year-old child — while three IRGC members were killed in strikes on northern Zanjan province. Trump had signaled the strikes hours earlier, telling reporters 'it's our turn to hit them' and telling Fox News that Iran 'is going to get a beating.'

title: Iranian drone strikes US-owned LNG tanker at Egypt's Damietta port
description: A drone struck the US-owned floating storage and regasification unit Energos Winter at Egypt's Damietta port on the Mediterranean coast, igniting a fire that spread to a second vessel, the Gaslog Salem; no injuries were reported. British maritime security firm Ambrey assessed a drone strike as the likely cause, and two Iranian sources told The New York Times the attack was designed to show that global shipping and energy supplies could be more deeply disrupted if Tehran chose to escalate. It was the first strike on Egyptian territory in the war, opening a new front on the Mediterranean far from the Gulf and Red Sea theaters. Egypt's petroleum ministry confirmed a fire but made no mention of a drone.

title: Netanyahu tells Trump he wants to wean Israel off US military aid
description: In a 90-minute White House meeting focused on Iran, Prime Minister Netanyahu told Trump he wants to phase out Israel's US military aid within a decade, saying 'I want to move from aid to partnership,' according to a senior Israeli official. Netanyahu proposed ending the $3.3 billion in annual Foreign Military Financing grants while keeping $500 million for missile defense, floated a $16 billion joint US-Israel weapons R&D fund, and said he had ordered Israeli officials to develop an independent fighter jet. On Iran he laid out three scenarios — a diplomatic deal, sanctions without war, or a major offensive — without endorsing one, as US retaliatory strikes on Iran got underway.

title: Public executions of Isfahan protesters spark anti-regime demonstrations
description: The dawn hanging of two protesters in Isfahan's Alikhani Square triggered anti-regime demonstrations, with crowds that gathered near the execution site chanting slogans against police rather than dispersing. An online petition against the death sentences of 12 young men convicted over the January 2026 uprising drew about 500,000 signatures on Instagram within a day. UN human rights experts and Amnesty International demanded Tehran halt what Amnesty called an 'escalating campaign of arbitrary executions,' as the regime fast-tracks capital cases against protesters amid the war.

title: Israel accuses Hezbollah of ceasefire breach in south Lebanon
description: The Israeli military accused Hezbollah of a 'blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement' over an attack on an Israeli engineering vehicle in southern Lebanon, while Lebanese state media reported Israeli forces setting fire to homes in Qantara. The exchange strained the June 1 truce, under which Israel pledged not to strike Beirut's southern suburbs and Hezbollah vowed to halt attacks, though both sides have continued operations. The cumulative Lebanese toll since fighting resumed on March 2 stood at at least 4,219 killed with more than 1.2 million displaced.

title: Oil surges back above $90 after Trump vows to hit Iran 'hard'
description: Brent crude jumped 7.9% to settle at $90.74 a barrel and US WTI rose 6.6% to $84.46 on July 29 after President Trump told Fox News that Iran 'is going to get a beating,' vowing to retaliate for Tehran's ballistic-missile attack on US forces in Jordan. The rally, which erased a three-session slide of roughly 16%, gained force through the day as Trump escalated his threats, cementing a reversal of the earlier optimism when signs of a US-Iran pause had driven Brent down 8.7% in a single session. The move followed CENTCOM's overnight interception of the Iranian missiles.

title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan; CENTCOM intercepts all
description: The IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles at US military targets in Jordan at about 5:45 p.m. ET, in what CENTCOM called an 'attempted surprise attack.' US forces intercepted every missile with no casualties, and Jordan's army said it shot down five missiles at dawn. It was Iran's first ballistic-missile attack on a US base since Trump paused strikes five days earlier to give diplomacy space, ending a brief lull. CENTCOM warned that 'the IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further U.S. military response.'

title: US and Saudi jets strike Iran-backed militias in eastern Iraq; 10 PMF killed
description: US and Saudi fighter aircraft struck terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a joint operation CENTCOM called a 'strong response' to more than 30 IRGC-directed drone attacks on US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure over 72 hours. Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces said at least 10 of its members were killed and four wounded. It was the first US military action during the five-day pause in direct strikes on Iran, and marked Saudi Arabia's deepest combat involvement after long resisting being pulled fully into the war; Riyadh's defense ministry said it 'conducted precise and targeted strikes.'

title: Reuters: Iran to receive up to 400 Chinese shoulder-fired air-defense missiles
description: Iran is expected within weeks to receive the first shipment of up to 400 Chinese-made man-portable air-defense systems, including QW-12 and FN-16 infrared-guided missiles, in a $60-70 million deal Reuters sources called one of Tehran's largest efforts to bolster short-range air defenses since the war began. The contract was signed with Zhongqing Baoshang International Investment, a Hong Kong intermediary. The mobile launchers are designed to down low-flying aircraft, helicopters and drones around military and energy sites. China's Foreign Ministry called the reports 'completely groundless.'

title: Yemeni FM: Houthis aim to replicate Iran's Hormuz control in the Red Sea
description: Yemen's Foreign Minister-designate Afrah Al-Zouba warned that the Houthis want to copy Iran's Strait of Hormuz strategy by choking shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb and have declared a blockade on Saudi vessels, emboldened by an insufficient international response. 'The Houthis want to copy the Iranian model and this will shut down two main straits, the gateways into the Gulf and Red Sea,' she said. The warning followed days of Houthi missile and drone strikes on Saudi oil facilities and Saudi reprisal airstrikes on Hodeidah, opening a second maritime front in the US-Iran war.

title: Iran publicly executes 2 January protesters in Isfahan
description: Iran hanged Amirhossein Safari and Abolfazl Sepahi at dawn in Isfahan's Alikhani Square, according to judiciary news agency Mizan, which accused the pair of killing four security personnel and committing arson during the January 2026 protests. Heavy security ringed the square overnight and witnesses reported clashes between guards and gathered crowds; the two were the third and fourth hanged in the same case after two others on July 19, with eight co-defendants still under death sentence. UN experts said the mass hearing that condemned 12 people at once 'violates established fair trial standards,' as Tehran fast-tracks capital cases amid the war.

title: Netanyahu meets Trump as Oman-brokered Hormuz deal nears decision
description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who landed in Washington on July 27, met President Trump to weigh a tentative arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz brokered by Oman. Under the proposal, Iran would run vessel transit through the strait with fewer restrictions in exchange for voluntary transit fees paid to Tehran, a mechanism Gulf sources told Reuters has regional backing. Mediators said they were close to reviving the June memorandum of understanding but awaited a final decision from Trump after the Netanyahu meeting; officials cautioned the strait deal was not intended to end the wider US-Iran war.

title: Iran FM says no negotiations with US, rejects US 'timing of war and peace'
description: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told a weekly briefing that Tehran is 'not engaged in any negotiations with the United States,' despite the pause in fighting, and that Iran 'will never allow the United States to determine the timing of war and peace.' Baqaei said Iran's only active track is talks with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz. His statement tempered Trump's claim of 'very friendly negotiations,' underscoring that the halt in strikes since early Saturday rested on indirect mediation rather than any direct US-Iran channel.

title: Trump says he paused strikes at Iran's request, warns they will resume
description: Trump said the US halted its 13-day bombing campaign over the weekend at the request of Iran's regime to give diplomacy 'space,' but warned that attacks would resume if the two sides failed to reach a new ceasefire deal. US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said the pause was meant to let talks develop. The comments came as mediators from Pakistan, Egypt and Qatar circulated proposals on Hormuz control, with a Trump administration official calling the Iran track 'a serious stage.'

title: Oil plunges 8.7% on US-Iran pause, biggest drop since April
description: Brent crude fell 8.7% to close around $88 a barrel, its biggest one-day drop since April 17, while WTI for September delivery sank 7.5% to settle at $82.61, after the US suspended air strikes and Iran said it had halted retaliation and was talking to Oman about the Strait of Hormuz. Traders read the pause as raising the odds shipping could resume through the strait. Supply relief was compounded by crude loadings restarting at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal on Russia's Black Sea coast, which Ukrainian drones had recently disrupted.

title: Houthis strike Saudi Aramco's Jizan refinery and Yanbu oil hub; Greek Patriot intercepts 2 missiles
description: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis fired missiles and drones at two of Saudi Arabia's most important Red Sea oil installations, Aramco's Jizan refinery and the Yanbu export terminal, in a sharp escalation of the war's second front. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the strikes; a large smoke column rose over Jizan, while a Greek-operated Patriot battery stationed in Saudi Arabia intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Yanbu, the kingdom's principal western export hub. The assault on land-based Saudi oil infrastructure, following the Houthis' declared blockade and earlier tanker attacks, raised fears that a combined shutdown of Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz would inflict major global economic damage.

title: Pentagon revises US war toll to 18 killed, 624 wounded amid transparency questions
description: The Pentagon updated its Defense Casualty Analysis System on Saturday, adding more than 140 wounded and restoring four soldiers killed by Iranian strikes the prior week, bringing the US toll for Operation Epic Fury to 18 killed and 624 wounded since Feb. 28 — a steep rise from the previous peak of 482 wounded observed by CNN a week earlier. The database also added a new 'Overseas Operations' category counting casualties 'starting July 7,' the date Trump told Congress a new conflict with Iran began. The Pentagon did not explain what the category covers, and critics said the shifting accounting obscured the war's real cost.

title: US gas prices hit $4.11 a gallon, up 38% since the war began
description: The US national average gasoline price reached about $4.11 a gallon over the weekend, up roughly 11 cents from a week earlier and some 38% higher than before the war began in late February, as the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping squeezed global crude supplies. Brent had topped $100 a barrel earlier in the week for the first time since May, feeding inflation fears and stagflation warnings across import-dependent economies.

title: US strike pause extends to second night as US-Iran talks gain momentum
description: US forces did not strike Iran overnight for a second consecutive night, extending the first sustained pause since the campaign resumed after 13 straight nights of bombing. The Associated Press reported both sides want to return to the interim ceasefire, with negotiators discussing a compromise letting Iran oversee vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz under fewer restrictions. Iran's Foreign Ministry said weekend technical talks with an Omani delegation in Tehran on safe Hormuz passage had made progress. Trump denied election pressure was driving him: 'I'm not in a hurry. We have to do it right,' while keeping military options open.

title: Ukraine strikes Iranian cargo vessel in Caspian Sea, killing a sailor
description: Ukraine's SBU security service said it struck an Iranian vessel transporting military cargo between Iran and Russia in the Caspian Sea early Saturday, and Iran's Foreign Ministry said the explosion killed one crew member and wounded another. President Zelensky said Ukraine had achieved 'very strong results with long-range strikes in the Caspian Sea — including vessels used in military cargo shipments involving Iran, as well as a warship.' Tehran condemned the attack as 'an act of aggression' and a breach of the UN Charter, summoned Ukraine's charge d'affaires, and warned it would 'not hesitate to defend its national interests.'

title: Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi-held Hodeidah port and telecom in Red Sea reprisal
description: Saudi Arabia said its coalition forces struck Houthi targets in Yemen in retaliation for the Iran-backed group's drone-and-missile attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea days earlier. Strikes hit the Red Sea city of Hodeidah, targeting its port and the state-run telecommunications corporation, injuring two people according to the Houthi-run health ministry. The direct Saudi assault on Yemen marked a widening of the war's second front over Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb shipping.

title: Houthis fire missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia after Hodeidah strikes
description: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said Saturday they had fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia in response to Saudi airstrikes on the Red Sea city of Hodeidah. The exchange followed the Houthis' declared maritime blockade of Saudi ports and their attacks on the tankers Encelia and Layla, and marked the first open Saudi-Houthi missile exchange since the group opened its Red Sea front in the Iran war.

title: US pauses strikes for first time in two weeks; Trump says 'not time yet' for deal
description: US Central Command announced no new attack on Iran early Friday, the first time in nearly two weeks it did not launch a wave of strikes, halting a run of 13 consecutive nights of bombing. Trump said the US and Iran remained in talks and that Tehran was 'getting more serious,' but added he doesn't 'think it's time yet' for a deal: 'I think they'd love to make a deal, but I don't think they're ready to... I'm willing to listen.' He met earlier with advisers and Cabinet officials to weigh a potential escalation if negotiations fail.

title: WSJ: Bahrain and Kuwait launch airstrikes on Iran; UAE gives air cover
description: Bahrain and Kuwait sent warplanes to strike drone and missile-storage depots inside Iran in retaliation for repeated Iranian attacks on their territory, the Wall Street Journal reported, with the UAE providing intelligence and 'defensive air cover' for the operations. The direct entry of two more Gulf states into the fighting marked a significant broadening of the war; the UAE and Saudi Arabia had struck Iran in the war's early days, with Abu Dhabi mounting dozens of attacks. The reported strikes came hours after Iran drone-attacked US facilities in Bahrain and Jordan.

title: Trump says China and Russia staying out of war, citing Xi and Putin pledges
description: President Trump said he did not believe China or Russia were arming Iran, contradicting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's July 22 Senate testimony that both were 'enabling' Tehran. Trump said Xi Jinping told him in Beijing he 'would not, under any circumstances, give or sell Weapons to the Islamic Republic of Iran,' and that Putin had made a similar pledge, adding 'I take him at his word.' 'Two major Countries that people speak of often in terms of Iran are, in my opinion, not participating. If they did, it would be very bad for them,' Trump said.

title: US completes 13th straight night of strikes; blasts across southern Iran
description: CENTCOM wrapped up a thirteenth consecutive night of strikes early Friday, saying it hit 'Iranian military command centers, drone storage facilities, communication networks, coastal surveillance sites, and maritime capabilities' to protect Hormuz shipping. Iranian media reported explosions in Khorramabad, Ahvaz, Bandar Abbas, Jask, Konarak and the Gulf islands of Qeshm, Larak and Hengam, and claimed air defenses downed a US Tomahawk over Kahnuj. A Hormozgan provincial official reported at least two people wounded, while Iranian outlets said four were killed in Khuzestan. CENTCOM insisted the Strait of Hormuz 'remains open for transit despite recent attacks.'

title: Iran drone-strikes Bahrain's Isa Air Base and Jordan's Al-Azraq; Bahrain sounds sirens
description: Iran's army said it launched drone strikes on US facilities in Bahrain and Jordan in retaliation for the 13th night of American attacks, targeting fuel tanks, equipment warehouses, silos and barracks at Isa Air Base in Bahrain and aircraft and maintenance hangars at Jordan's Al-Azraq base. Bahrain activated air-raid sirens early Friday, warning residents to shelter from detected fire hours after CENTCOM ended its strikes. Jordan had not confirmed any strikes at the time of Iran's claim.

title: Iran rejects Iraqi-brokered US ceasefire; Trump weighs 'massive attack'
description: Iran rejected a US ceasefire proposal delivered to Tehran by Iraq's prime minister, with officials saying they had no interest in a temporary deal that left control of the Strait of Hormuz unresolved. Trump said Iran 'need more of the same' and that Tehran had not 'received enough pain yet,' telling Axios he was weighing a 'massive attack' on Iran. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the US campaign 'mindless aggression' and said Tehran would not facilitate any deal under bombardment.

title: IRGC says tanker caught fire on mined route south of Hormuz
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said an oil tanker caught fire after an explosion when it attempted to pass what the IRGC called a mined route south of the Strait of Hormuz, signaling that Tehran is now using sea mines to enforce its chokehold on the waterway. Maritime trackers reported Hormuz throughput had collapsed to roughly 2% of pre-war tanker volume, leaving the strait functionally closed to commercial shipping.

title: Brent crude tops $100 for first time in two months as war widens
description: Brent crude jumped about 7% to settle at $100.69 a barrel and US WTI rose 6.17% to $92.19, both hitting their highest levels in two months as the near-shutdown of Hormuz and the Houthi Red Sea blockade choked two major oil arteries at once. US gasoline averaged $4.09 a gallon and diesel $5.34 as prices climbed for a fifth straight day. It was the first time Brent had traded above $100 since late May.

title: House rebukes Trump on Iran war for second time; Senate blocks companion measure 49-47
description: The US House passed a war-powers resolution directing President Trump to halt the Iran campaign absent congressional authorization — its second such rebuke since the ceasefire collapsed — but the Senate voted 49-47 to block the companion measure. Republican Susan Collins crossed the aisle to support it, while Rand Paul and Lisa Murkowski, who had backed earlier restraint votes, missed the tally. Neither non-binding measure would reach the White House, leaving Trump's authority to prosecute the war unchecked.

title: US completes 12th straight night of strikes; 2 killed at Shalamcheh crossing
description: CENTCOM began a twelfth consecutive night of strikes at 1:30am Gulf Standard Time, killing at least two people and wounding 11 in an attack on the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iraq. Iranian state media reported further strikes near Andimeshk, Ahvaz and Ramshir, with explosions heard in Sirik and Bushehr on Thursday morning. CENTCOM said the strikes would 'continue to further degrade Iran's ability to threaten civilian mariners and commercial vessels transiting regional waters.'

title: Houthis strike two Saudi oil tankers in Red Sea; Encelia set ablaze
description: Yemen's Houthis said they carried out missile and drone strikes on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, deepening the naval blockade of Saudi Arabia they declared on July 20. The Saudi-owned tanker Encelia was hit by a projectile that started a fire at its bow; all crew were reported safe. The attack widened a second maritime front alongside the Strait of Hormuz and pushed traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint toward a standstill.

title: Brent crude tops $95.99 after tanker struck off Saudi Arabia
description: Brent crude for September delivery rose about 2% to $95.99 a barrel and US WTI climbed 1.7% to $88.27 after a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile off Saudi Arabia and Trump threatened to bomb Iranian infrastructure over any attack on Hormuz shipping. Prices have risen roughly $20 a barrel since fighting resumed on July 7, as the near-shutdown of Hormuz and the new Red Sea blockade choke two of the world's key oil chokepoints. The IEA has called the disruption the largest supply shock in the history of the global oil market.

title: Trump threatens to bomb a Tehran bridge or power plant per ship attacked
description: Trump posted that 'Any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by Missile, Rocket, Drone, or any other device or weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT, including those located next to, or in, the Capital City of Tehran.' A senior Iranian official responded that Tehran would strike 'infrastructure and bridges across the region,' as both sides openly threatened civilian infrastructure.

title: Iran denies nuclear activity at Pickaxe Mountain, calls US focus a pretext
description: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said no nuclear activity was taking place at Pickaxe Mountain (Kolang Kouh), calling Washington's 'obsessive focus' on the site 'nothing more than a fabricated pretext for aggression, destruction, and sabotage.' Iran's joint military command, the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, warned that any US strike on Iran's nuclear or sensitive sites would widen the regional war and bring a 'powerful assault' on US interests and allied nations.

title: Trump attends dignified transfer of 4 US troops killed in Iran war
description: President Trump attended the dignified transfer of four American service members killed in recent days in the war with Iran. US officials put the American military death toll at 18 with 482 wounded in action since fighting resumed, while Iran reported 53 killed and 592 injured over the past month. The transfer came as Trump signaled preparations to significantly escalate the US campaign.

title: US completes 11th straight night of strikes; explosions rock Bushehr
description: CENTCOM said US forces completed an eleventh consecutive night of strikes at 8:15pm ET, hitting Iranian military operations centres, maritime capabilities, aircraft hangars, drone storage facilities and military logistics infrastructure, with explosions again reported around Bushehr. The command said the campaign is meant to keep degrading Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, noting Iran has attacked more than 30 commercial vessels transiting the waterway over the past three months. Iran's armed forces said they had again fired missiles and drones at US bases and assets in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan.

title: Trump vows to hit Pickaxe Mountain 'very heavily'; Iran warns of wider war
description: President Trump escalated his threats against the fortified Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site south of Natanz, saying 'We'll be hitting that area very probably pretty soon. And there's not a thing they can do about it.' Israel assesses that Iran has buried thousands of centrifuges and part of its enriched-uranium stockpile roughly 100 metres under the mountain, which regime officials call the 'most fortified nuclear facility in the world.' Iranian state media warned early Wednesday that any US attack on its nuclear facilities would be treated as an expansion of the war across the region.

title: Hegseth tells Senate war has cost $37.5bn; says Russia and China aiding Iran
description: Testifying to the Senate Appropriations Committee, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the war has cost $37.5 billion and requested an $87.6 billion supplemental, roughly $67 billion of it for the military. Hegseth said both Russia and China were 'enabling some of the things Iran is doing,' with US officials separately alleging Moscow has passed Iran real-time data on American warships and aircraft, though Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine declined to detail the assistance. Hegseth described the US naval blockade as 'effectively impenetrable' but acknowledged Iran retains fast boats, coastal missiles and the ability to mine waters and attack commercial vessels.

title: Iran executes Mehdi Khaneki for 'operational actions' aiding US and Israel
description: Iran's judiciary announced the execution of Mehdi Khaneki, convicted of carrying out 'operational actions' that benefited Israel, the United States and hostile groups, and of producing and possessing weapons, according to the Mizan news agency. Officials linked the charges to the January 2026 anti-government uprising. The hanging extends a wartime execution wave that rights groups say has killed at least 36 people on politically motivated charges since the war began on February 28.

title: Two Saudi crude tankers reverse course in Red Sea amid Houthi blockade
description: Two oil tankers carrying Saudi crude to Asia turned back in the Red Sea after threats from Yemen's Houthis, who declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia a day earlier and vowed to close the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Saudi vessels. The reversal opened a second energy chokepoint alongside the shuttered Strait of Hormuz and threatened the roughly 2.5 million barrels a day of Saudi crude that reach the Red Sea via the East-West Pipeline. Shippers had already all but abandoned Hormuz, leaving two of the world's most critical oil arteries partially blocked at once.

title: Trump approves US-Saudi nuclear deal that may let Riyadh enrich uranium
description: President Trump approved a nuclear-cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia that could allow the kingdom to enrich uranium on its own soil, two AP sources said, with a public announcement expected as early as Wednesday. The 30-year deal would involve US firms and could permit a Saudi enrichment facility following a joint study, and is to be submitted to Congress for review. Nonproliferation experts and lawmakers including Senator Ed Markey warned the terms lack weapons safeguards and could trigger a new round of Middle East proliferation, even as the US bombs Iran to halt its own enrichment.

title: US completes tenth straight night of strikes; Trump vows Iran will 'pay many times over'
description: CENTCOM completed a tenth consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with Iranian state media reporting explosions across multiple provinces. President Trump said Tehran will 'pay ... many times over' for killing US service members and said he had instructed the Pentagon to strike Iran, as Washington weighed expanding the war. The US kept surging fighter jets and refueling tankers to the region while reissuing a Worldwide Caution alert for Americans abroad.

title: Iran hits Kuwait's Camp Arifjan and Bahrain; sets two tankers ablaze in Hormuz
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired surface-to-surface missiles at US forces at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait, claiming to target HIMARS launchers, while Kuwait's army confirmed intercepting incoming missiles and drones. The IRGC said it struck a radar and Patriot air-defence system in Bahrain's Muharraq and Riffa, and reported that two oil tankers caught fire after explosions on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz. A Greek-operated oil tanker was struck and detained in the strait, which the Guards said would stay closed while US operations continue.

title: WSJ: Israel says Iran moved thousands of centrifuges to Pickaxe Mountain
description: Israeli intelligence has assessed that Iran moved thousands of nuclear centrifuges into the Pickaxe Mountain tunnel complex (Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La), about 1.5km south of Natanz, burying them deep underground to shield them from air strikes, the Wall Street Journal reported citing US and Israeli officials. Israel told Washington the move was made last fall, after the June 2025 12-day war. Trump has threatened the site directly, saying 'We're going to take out Pickaxe Mountain. Tell the Iranians to be ready.'

title: Mediators offer US and Iran 10-day ceasefire; both withhold acceptance
description: Qatar, Egypt, Pakistan and other regional mediators presented the US and Iran with a proposal for a 10-day ceasefire, according to regional sources with direct knowledge of the effort. Neither Trump nor Iran accepted, with both sides seeking to improve leverage through further strikes first; the effort had gained momentum before Iran's July 18 missile strike in Jordan killed US troops and prompted Washington to pull back. A senior US official said talks were continuing but that Trump 'has yet to finish retaliating.'

title: Houthis declare naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, closing Bab el-Mandeb to Saudi ships
description: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, calling it an 'eye for an eye,' and deputy media chief Nasruddin Amer said the Bab el-Mandeb strait would be closed to Saudi vessels. The Iran-backed group said it was retaliating for Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa International Airport that targeted a plane carrying Houthi leaders returning from Iran. Rystad Energy estimated about 2.5 million barrels a day of Saudi crude shipped via the East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea now faces disruption, opening a potential second chokepoint alongside the closed Strait of Hormuz.

title: Lebanese army takes over three southern 'pilot zones' in first withdrawal test
description: The Lebanese army began assuming security control of the southern villages of Froun, Srifa and Zawtar al-Gharbiya, the first on-the-ground test of the June 26 Trilateral Framework signed by Lebanon, Israel and the US to secure an Israeli withdrawal and Hezbollah's disarmament. The US State Department said operations had started 'under the auspices of the Military Coordination Group for Lebanon.' The deal sets no withdrawal timetable, and Israel has vowed to hold a 10km-deep security zone as long as Hezbollah remains armed; Hezbollah rejects the framework.

title: US completes ninth straight night of strikes; hits Bushehr, Tabriz area
description: CENTCOM said the US military completed its ninth consecutive night of strikes against Iran, hitting command centres, air defence sites, maritime assets, missile facilities and communications networks. Strikes struck the Bushehr nuclear power plant complex and targets in northwestern Iran near Tabriz, killing at least one person and wounding several, Iranian outlets reported. The campaign has now run without pause since US attacks resumed following Iran's July 18 killing of American troops in Jordan.

title: IRGC hits Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, Syria; claims destroying Kuwait radar and MQ-9 hangar
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired drones and missiles at US targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan and Syria, triggering air-raid sirens and explosions in Manama and engaging Kuwaiti air defences. The IRGC claimed it destroyed a US radar system in Kuwait and struck an MQ-9 Reaper hangar at Ali Al Salem Air Base, setting drones ablaze, and said it 'halted' two ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Israeli air defences also downed a drone over the Syrian border near Mount Hermon.

title: Rubio says Iran using Hormuz as 'leverage against the world'
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran was trying to use the Strait of Hormuz as 'leverage against the world' to restrict international commerce, framing Tehran's control of the chokepoint as the core obstacle to any renewed ceasefire. Commercial transit through the strait, which normally carries about 20% of global oil supply, remained a fraction of pre-crisis volume as shippers avoided the contested waterway.

title: US strikes Darkhovin nuclear plant construction site; IAEA investigates
description: On the eighth consecutive night of strikes, US forces hit the partly built Darkhovin nuclear power plant near the Iraqi border, along with targets in Hormozgan and Khuzestan provinces and on Qeshm Island. The IAEA said it was looking into Iranian reports that an overnight strike hit the unfinished plant. Iran's deputy foreign minister called the attack a 'dangerous assault' on civilian infrastructure; Iranian authorities said a desalination plant on Qeshm Island was also damaged a day after the Bonji plant's destruction left 10,000 people without drinking water.

title: Third US service member killed in Iraq detonating downed Iranian drone; toll hits 17
description: CENTCOM said a US service member was killed and another mildly injured during a 'controlled detonation' of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian one-way attack drone in northern Iraq. The death brought the number of US troops killed since the war began on February 28 to 17, coming days after two soldiers were killed and one went missing in Iran's July 18 strike on a base in Jordan. Troops also recovered unidentified remains at the Jordan strike site pending examination.

title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Jordan's Aqaba; fragments fall near Eilat
description: Iran launched ballistic missiles toward the Jordanian port city of Aqaba, adjacent to Israel's Red Sea resort of Eilat. US air defences intercepted three of the missiles while one struck an open area, and interceptor fragments fell near Eilat, causing no damage or injuries. Jordan summoned Iran's ambassador after downing incoming missiles for a second straight day.

title: GCC chief calls Iranian strikes on Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan 'war crimes'
description: The Gulf Cooperation Council's secretary-general condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, declaring that the deliberate targeting of civilian infrastructure 'constitutes war crimes requiring international accountability and prosecution' and a grave violation of the UN Charter. Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry separately denounced 'the continued brutal Iranian aggression,' and the GCC expressed solidarity with the three states and wished a speedy recovery to those injured in Kuwait.

title: Lebanese President Aoun meets Rubio in Washington; first such visit since 2009
description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington, the first visit by a Lebanese head of state since 2009. Rubio praised Beirut's efforts to disarm Hezbollah, Iran's main regional proxy, as part of the framework tied to Israel's withdrawal from Lebanon. Aoun was scheduled to meet President Trump the following Tuesday.

title: Iran executes two January uprising protesters in Isfahan
description: Iran hanged Erfan Esfandiari, 18, and Gol-Mohammad Mohammadi, a 24-year-old Afghan national, in Isfahan for their role in the January 2026 anti-government uprising. The two were convicted of 'moharebeh' (waging war against God) and 'corruption on Earth' over the killing of four security officers during the unrest. Rights groups said 10 more protesters, aged 18 to 24, remain sentenced to death, warning of imminent further executions amid the wartime crackdown.

title: Two US troops killed, one missing in IRGC missile strike on Jordan's Azraq base
description: CENTCOM said two US service members were killed and one is missing in action after Iran's Revolutionary Guard struck the American air base at Azraq in eastern Jordan with ballistic missiles and drones, the first US military deaths of the war since March. Four more troops were medevaced to Jordanian hospitals and later discharged. The IRGC's Aerospace Force said its 20th 'Nasr-2' wave hit aircraft shelters and a parking ramp, claiming at least five US aircraft destroyed, a figure US officials did not confirm; Jordan said it intercepted 10 incoming missiles. Trump called the soldiers' deaths 'a sad thing' and ordered fresh strikes to 'hold Iranian forces accountable.'

title: US strikes Bonji desalination plant; water cut to 10,000 Iranians in 20 villages
description: US strikes in a new overnight wave hit power facilities and desalination pumps at the Bonji plant in Jask, Hormozgan province, cutting drinking water to 20 villages and roughly 10,000 people, a local official told Reuters. CENTCOM said the campaign struck surveillance sites, military logistics infrastructure, underground weapons storage and maritime capabilities. At least 12 people were killed in Iran over the prior day, taking the death toll to 50 since the latest phase of strikes began on June 27, with more than 500 injured.

title: Iran sets second Kuwaiti desalination plant ablaze in two days
description: Iranian missile and drone fire set a second Kuwaiti power and water desalination plant ablaze in as many days, Kuwait's military said, after intercepting further ballistic missile and drone attacks originating from Iran. Kuwait relies on desalination for about 90% of its drinking water. Qatar condemned Iran's attacks on Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan 'in the strongest terms,' saying the targeting of electricity and water desalination plants 'crosses all red lines,' while the UAE called the strikes a clear violation of the three states' sovereignty.

title: Khamenei calls Trump's signature 'worthless'; Iran suspends interim deal
description: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei derided President Trump's signature on the June memorandum of understanding as 'utterly worthless and devoid of credibility' and warned the 'axis of resistance' had 'unforgettable lessons to offer' the United States. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran had suspended implementation of its commitments under the interim agreement after Washington 'violated its own obligations,' and Tehran said it would no longer seek to implement the deal reached last month.

title: IRGC downs US MQ-9 Reaper over Asaluyeh, halts four ships in Hormuz
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said its naval air defenses shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the southern coastal region of Asaluyeh and stopped four commercial vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz under US military protection using a combined missile-and-drone operation. Traffic through the waterway remained near a standstill, with only about 10 ships transiting versus roughly 88 per day normally and 444 vessels reported anchored or stopped in the region.

title: US surges F-35s, F-16s to hunt Iranian air defenses; issues Worldwide Caution
description: The US deployed additional F-35 stealth fighters and F-16 jets to the region to strike Iranian radars and surface-to-air missile sites, alongside dozens of aerial refueling aircraft, as Trump weighed expanded strikes on Iran's power plants and nuclear sites. The State Department issued a Worldwide Caution alert warning of heightened Middle East tensions and the potential for Iranian targeting of Americans globally.

title: Israel kills Hezbollah drone operators near Kfar Tebnit in south Lebanon
description: The Israeli military said its air force struck and killed several Hezbollah operatives piloting a surveillance drone near Kfar Tebnit in southern Lebanon, after identifying fighters operating drones while taking cover near Israeli troops, calling it a violation of ceasefire understandings. A Lebanese soldier was killed by an explosive device the IDF said Hezbollah had planted.

title: Iran executes woman Parvin Chardoli; 2026 female execution toll hits 17
description: Iran hanged Parvin Chardoli at Ghezel Hesar Prison, raising the number of women executed in 2026 to 17; an informed source said the court knew she had not committed the murder for which she was condemned but sentenced her to death after she refused to name the perpetrator. Authorities also executed Aref Khoshkar over the killing of a security force member during the 2022 protests, part of a wartime execution surge rights groups say has reached levels unseen since the 1980s.

title: US strikes Iran for seventh straight night; bridges, power grid, Chabahar tower hit
description: US Central Command struck Iran for a seventh consecutive night, a wave that ran from 3pm to 9:30pm ET hitting surveillance sites, military logistics infrastructure, underground weapons storage and maritime capabilities with fighter jets, drones and warships. Overnight strikes destroyed six highway and railway bridges in Hormozgan province to cut Bandar Abbas off from central Iran and collapsed a maritime control tower at Chabahar port; CENTCOM said destroying the tower 'directly degrades IRGC's ability to coordinate attacks on innocent civilian crew members.' Iran acknowledged 'attacks on power infrastructure' for the first time, with its Energy Ministry urging residents of southern provinces to cut electricity use amid extreme heat.

title: Iran strikes Kuwait desalination plant, Qatar's Al Udeid in five-nation Gulf barrage
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired missiles and drones at US-allied Gulf states in retaliation for the seventh night of American strikes, sparking a fire at a Kuwaiti power and water desalination plant and damaging electricity generation units; Kuwait, which relies on desalination for about 90% of its water, urged citizens to ration power. The IRGC said it hit Qatar's Al Udeid Air Base, where a child was injured by falling shrapnel, along with Bahrain's Sakhir airbase and US radar sites in Oman. Jordan shot down three Iranian missiles and Kurdish forces downed eight drones over Erbil; CENTCOM denied an IRGC claim of a strike on the al-Tanf base in Syria.

title: US to send dozens more refueling tankers to Israel ahead of possible escalation
description: The Trump administration notified Israel it is sending dozens more aerial refueling tankers ahead of a potential expansion of operations against Iran, with 5-8 aircraft expected to arrive daily on top of the roughly 33 already at Ben Gurion Airport and a similar number at Ramon Air Base. The buildup would return tanker numbers to levels seen at the start of the war and give the US greater flexibility to sustain strikes deep inside Iran. Trump is weighing options including hitting Iranian infrastructure, further strikes on nuclear facilities, and an attack on the underground Pickaxe Mountain site.

title: Iran adviser Rezaei warns of 'full-scale offensive' if US strikes continue
description: Mohsen Rezaei, an adviser to Iran's supreme leader, warned against continued US escalation or any attempt to seize Iranian territory, saying: 'If US strikes continue for several more days, we will move into a phase of full-scale offensive operations.' An IRGC commander separately vowed that 'effective and targeted strikes from across Iran against the enemy will continue' until Washington halts its campaign. Iran also told Axis of Resistance allies, including Hezbollah, to prepare for a possibly broader and more severe conflict.

title: EU signs Djibouti pact to reinforce Red Sea mission amid Bab el-Mandeb threat
description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas visited Djibouti and signed a Status of Forces Agreement for Operation Aspides to strengthen Europe's naval presence in the Red Sea, saying it 'ensures maintaining access to and support for our ships and air assets for as long as they are needed.' The move came amid reports Tehran had asked the Houthis to prepare to close the Bab el-Mandeb strait if the US strikes Iranian power infrastructure. Aspides, launched in February 2024, has escorted more than 670 merchant vessels and rescued 128 seafarers.

title: Brent crude jumps 4.6% to $88.10 after Kuwait plant strike
description: Brent crude futures rose about 4.6% to close at $88.10 a barrel on July 17 after Kuwait said Iran attacked a power and water desalination plant, pushing prices up more than 10% for the week. The rally reversed an earlier return toward pre-war levels as the seventh consecutive night of US strikes and the shuttered Strait of Hormuz clouded the outlook for roughly a quarter of the world's seaborne oil trade. Traders also weighed Iran's threat to have the Houthis close the Bab el-Mandeb strait, which would disrupt the region's second main export route.

title: US strikes hit Ahvaz children's cancer hospital area; 30+ civilians killed
description: US strikes on southern Iran during the sixth straight night of the campaign killed more than 30 civilians, government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said, with the Health Ministry reporting over 260 injured including women and children. A projectile struck near Ahvaz's Shahid Baghaei Hospital, a children's cancer center, forcing evacuation of 211 patients undergoing chemotherapy; Iran condemned the 'barbaric' attack. State media said strikes on bridges in Bandar Khamir killed seven people, while power facilities and a train station were hit in Bandar Abbas.

title: IRGC claims strike on Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base in Nasr-2 wave
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck US military facilities at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base during the tenth wave of Operation Nasr-2, hitting helicopter maintenance facilities, a hangar housing a P-8 surveillance aircraft, and a US drone command-and-control center. The IRGC said it 'completely destroyed an air surveillance and control radar, as well as the fuel pumping station serving enemy aircraft.' The strike was Iran's answer to the sixth consecutive night of US bombing.

title: Kuwait intercepts 32 Iranian drones; Jordan downs 3 missiles
description: Kuwait's Defense Ministry said its air defenses intercepted 32 attack drones since dawn on July 16, blaming 'nefarious Iranian aggression,' with falling debris damaging some residential areas but causing no casualties. Bahrain's army said it intercepted and destroyed 'a number of the treacherous Iranian aerial attacks,' and Jordan's Armed Forces reported downing three Iranian missiles over its territory with no damage. Iran's army said it had targeted US military sites in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Syria.

title: Iran tells Houthis to ready Red Sea closure if US hits power grid
description: Iran asked Yemen's Houthis to prepare to close the Bab el-Mandeb strait to shipping if the United States strikes Iran's power infrastructure, sources told Reuters, after Trump threatened to 'knock out all their power plants' and bridges unless Tehran negotiates. A source close to the Houthis said the group had finished preparations, deploying missiles and drones near Bab el-Mandeb, with IRGC representatives in Yemen controlling the decision to close the strait. A closure would disrupt both of the Middle East's main oil export routes simultaneously, alongside the shut Strait of Hormuz.

title: US expands strikes to Tehran and Semnan missile-production province
description: US Central Command widened its air campaign on July 16, striking targets around Tehran and in Semnan province, home to Iran's ballistic-missile production and space program, after five nights of strikes had concentrated on coastal defenses near the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian air defenses activated over the capital and across northern and western Iran. The expansion followed Trump's threat to knock out Iran's power plants and bridges and marked the first strikes near the capital since the campaign resumed.

title: Iran frees US citizen Dena Karari as 'gesture of goodwill'
description: Trump announced that Iran had released Dena Karari, an American citizen wrongfully detained since December 2024, calling it a 'gesture of Goodwill by Iran.' Human rights attorney Jared Genser confirmed 'Dena is now safe and traveling back to the United States.' The release came amid otherwise escalating strikes, with Trump claiming, without corroboration, that Iran had called seeking to meet and 'want to settle so badly.' Iran's foreign ministry the same week said it had no plans to negotiate while US attacks continued.

title: US disables Curaçao-flagged tanker Belma bound for Kharg Island
description: US Central Command struck and disabled the Curaçao-flagged commercial tanker Belma as it transited international waters toward Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal, the first vessel the US has disabled since Trump reinstated the naval blockade of Iranian ports. CENTCOM said the unladen tanker 'ignored multiple warnings as it attempted to violate the US blockade.' The action came as the US concluded a second round of strikes in a single day against Iranian air defenses, missile and drone sites and command centers near Bandar Abbas.

title: Trump weighs ground troops to seize Iranian islands, nuclear-site strikes
description: Trump signaled he was leaning toward widening the offensive beyond the Strait of Hormuz, with reported options including intensified airstrikes on previously untouched strategic targets, deploying ground troops to seize Iranian islands near the strait, and bombing the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear enrichment site. 'I don't like giving deadlines, but they pretty much know the story. They better behave,' Trump said, warning Iran to return to talks.

title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at US bases in Jordan; Jordan intercepts 8
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at US air bases in Jordan while the Iranian army launched kamikaze drones at US fuel-storage and communications sites, retaliation the IRGC said answered a US strike near a children's cancer hospital in Iran. Jordan's armed forces said they intercepted 8 incoming missiles; footage circulating online appeared to show a direct impact on a base in northeastern Jordan. Iran also targeted the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait and the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, and drones violated Iraqi airspace near Erbil.

title: Iran executes January protester Amini Dehaghani amid wartime surge
description: Iran hanged Mohammad Amini Dehaghani in Isfahan province after the Supreme Court upheld his death sentence for setting fire to a government building during the January 2026 protests, on charges of 'moharebeh' (waging war against God) and 'corruption on earth.' The UN said Iran executed at least 40 people in the first half of 2026, 18 in national-security cases. Amnesty International said authorities were 'using wartime conditions as a pretext to intensify their crackdown through mass arrests, accelerated trials, [and] politically motivated executions.'

title: US strikes Iran for fifth straight night; hits Bushehr, Bandar Abbas
description: US Central Command struck Iranian coastal defenses, missile and drone sites and naval assets for a fifth consecutive night, a seven-hour wave concentrated near the Strait of Hormuz. The previous night's five-hour mission had hit military targets at Bushehr, Chah Bahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa and Bandar Abbas with precision munitions. CENTCOM said more than 20 US Navy warships and hundreds of aircraft are now operating across the region; Trump claimed the US had taken out 'almost all' of Iran's military capability.

title: Iran drones hit Kuwait, Bahrain again; UAE condemns attacks
description: Kuwait's Army General Headquarters said its air defenses engaged incoming drones approaching from Iran, warning residents that explosion sounds were interceptions of hostile attacks. Bahrain's Defence Force sounded air-raid sirens as its air defenses intercepted Iranian missiles and drones targeting civilians. The UAE condemned the 'renewed hostile attacks by Iran targeting Bahrain and Jordan' as a 'flagrant violation of sovereignty.' Since the ceasefire collapse Tehran has shifted from striking the UAE to concentrating on the smaller Gulf states of Bahrain and Kuwait.

title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran's power plants and bridges 'next week'
description: In an interview with Fox News, Trump threatened to widen strikes unless Iran returns to negotiations: 'Next week it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants. Next week comes the bridges. We're gonna knock out all their power plants. We're going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate.' He said the US would 'hit them very hard tonight' and warned Iran 'you're not going to have anybody left.' On Iran's nuclear sites he added, 'It only takes a matter of minutes for us to do it and do major damage.'

title: Trump drops planned 20% Hormuz transit fee after Gulf objections
description: Trump abandoned a previously announced plan to impose a 20% fee on cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz, citing objections from Persian Gulf allies, hours before the US reinstated its blockade of Iranian ports. He said the fee would be replaced by Gulf state investment and trade deals with the United States. The reversal came as Washington maintained that no negotiations could proceed while Iran continued to disrupt shipping through the strait.

title: Norwegian chemical tanker Stolt Magnesium hit by projectile off Oman
description: The Norwegian-operated chemical tanker Stolt Magnesium was struck by an external projectile on its starboard side at about 12:40am local time, 40 nautical miles northeast of Qalhat, Oman, setting fire to its engine room. All 23 crew were evacuated safely, the ship's manager said. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency confirmed the strike. The attack was the third on commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz in two days, after the Emirati tankers Mombasa and Al Bahiyah were hit by Iranian cruise missiles.

title: Iran hangs 9 in three days as wartime execution surge accelerates
description: Iran executed at least nine prisoners between July 12 and 14, including Kurdish inmates Mohyeddin Abdollahi and Hossein Palani, hanged Tuesday on charges of 'Baghi' (armed rebellion) and ISIS membership tied to a cell in the Bamo border heights. Iran Human Rights reported at least 101 executions in June 2026 alone, a pace unmatched in decades, as the judiciary presses an accelerated crackdown amid the war. Rights groups say at least 78 protesters and dissidents remain on death row, including 41 arrested over the January 2026 protests.

title: US to reinstate naval blockade of all Iranian ports
description: US Central Command announced it will resume its naval blockade of all vessels entering or exiting Iranian ports and coastal areas at 4pm ET (20:00 GMT) Tuesday, at Trump's direction, saying any vessel suspected of running the blockade is 'subject to interception, diversion, and capture' and that non-compliant ships 'may be legally compelled with force.' The move revives the April 13–June 18 operation, during which US forces redirected more than 140 compliant vessels, disabled nine non-compliant ships and let over 50 humanitarian vessels pass. Trump said Iran had failed the 'test' of the June 17 memorandum: 'Deals are made to be broken.'

title: Iran cruise missiles strike 2 UAE tankers in Hormuz; Indian sailor killed
description: Two Iranian cruise missiles struck the Emirati tankers Mombasa and Al Bahiyah in the southern lane of the Strait of Hormuz, inside Omani territorial waters, killing an Indian crew member aboard the Mombasa and wounding eight others — six Indian nationals and two Ukrainians, four of them seriously. Both vessels caught fire before crews contained the blazes. The UAE Defence Ministry condemned the 'blatant attack' and said it retained 'its full right to respond to this escalation'; Iran's IRGC said it had 'struck and disabled' two 'rogue supertankers.'

title: US strikes southern Iran for third straight night
description: US Central Command launched a third consecutive night of strikes on Iran beginning around 4:45pm ET, hitting coastal-defense systems, missile and drone sites and naval targets across Bandar Abbas, Bushehr, Chabahar, Jask and Konarak and the islands of Abu Musa, Larak and Qeshm in a roughly five-hour operation. Residents reported multiple heavy explosions in Konarak and Chabahar; Hormozgan's governor's office said the Bandar Abbas and Qeshm strikes caused no civilian casualties or damage to residential areas.
