CENTCOM framed the strikes as continuing to degrade Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Houthis fire missiles, drones at Saudi Abha airport; declare truce over
description: Yemen's Houthis launched missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport after accusing the kingdom of bombing Sanaa International Airport earlier Monday, shattering a four-year truce. The Sanaa runway was struck to stop an Iranian aircraft carrying a Houthi delegation from returning from Khamenei's funeral; Yemen's internationally recognized government claimed responsibility while the Houthis blamed Riyadh. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said 'the targeting of Sanaa Airport ends the de-escalation phase,' warned commercial carriers to avoid Saudi airspace and vowed the strike 'will not pass without retribution.' No casualties were reported; the UN Security Council held an emergency session.

title: Oil jumps 9.4% as Trump notifies Congress war has resumed
description: WTI crude settled up 9.4% at $78.14 a barrel — its highest close since June 15 and biggest single-day jump since early April — as US and Iranian forces traded strikes around the Strait of Hormuz. Trump sent Congress formal notification that hostilities against Iran had resumed on July 7, saying he acted 'consistent with my responsibility to protect Americans and United States' national security and foreign policy interests,' and warned the US would strike Iran hard 'Monday and Tuesday' because Tehran had failed the 'test' of the June 17 memorandum.

title: IRGC claims destroying US command post, drone hangars in Jordan
description: Iran's IRGC said it destroyed the command-and-control center and MQ-9 Reaper drone hangars at the US-linked Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan with ballistic missiles, calling it retaliation for continued American strikes on southern Iran. Iran's Army separately said it launched waves of kamikaze drones at a Patriot air-defense battery, an ammunition depot and a radar site in Kuwait, and at a communications system and radar site in Bahrain. Sirens sounded across Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Oman as Gulf states scrambled air defenses; none of Iran's claimed destruction was independently confirmed.

title: US strikes Iran for second straight night; Khuzestan water station hit
description: US Central Command launched a second consecutive night of strikes against Iran beginning at 5pm ET Sunday, saying the goal was to continue degrading Iran's 'ability to attack civilian mariners and commercial ships freely transiting the Strait of Hormuz.' Iran's Fars and IRNA news agencies reported a strike hit an agricultural water pumping station in Mahshahr, Khuzestan province, killing a security guard and wounding four others; state media also reported a power outage in Ahvaz, the provincial capital.

title: CENTCOM declares Hormuz open, rejects Iran's closure claim
description: US Central Command declared the Strait of Hormuz 'open to all vessels seeking to lawfully transit the international waterway,' posting on X that 'Iran does not control the strait. Traffic is flowing,' and that US forces remain 'positioned and prepared' to preserve freedom of navigation. The statement directly contradicted Iran's declaration that the strait was closed 'until further notice'; Windward Maritime Intelligence recorded just 21 commercial vessel transits on July 11, down from roughly 140 a day before the war.

title: Iran hits Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman in coordinated Gulf barrage
description: Iran launched coordinated missile and drone attacks across the Gulf around 05:36 local time Sunday, hours after the US struck roughly 140 targets in Iran. The IRGC claimed strikes on Al-Udeid airbase in Qatar, Prince Hassan airbase in Jordan, and US-linked port facilities at Duqm, Oman. Qatar's Armed Forces intercepted multiple ballistic missiles over Doha in two waves; Qatar's Interior Ministry reported 3 people injured, including a child, from falling debris. Kuwait, Bahrain and the UAE activated air defenses and engaged incoming fire, with Kuwait's military stating explosion sounds heard were 'the result of air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks.'

title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz closed 'until further notice'
description: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to all traffic 'until further notice' and until the end of US operations in the region, warning any US attempt to challenge the closure would trigger a 'severe' military response. Iran's UN Ambassador Amir Saeid Iravani said any reopening of the shipping lane or demining operations 'rests exclusively with Iran.' The declaration followed the IRGC's attack on a container ship for using an unauthorized route and the US's third round of retaliatory strikes this week.

title: US hits ~140 targets in third round of Iran strikes this week
description: US Central Command launched a third round of strikes against Iran at 7:15pm ET Saturday, hitting roughly 140 military targets with precision munitions from land- and sea-based fighter aircraft, drones and naval vessels — including missile and drone sites, naval capabilities, ammunition storage, communications networks and coastal surveillance locations. The strikes brought the week's total to over 300 targets hit across three rounds. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said: 'Iran made a poor choice. Now they pay.'

title: IRGC attacks Cyprus-flagged container ship GFS Galaxy in Hormuz
description: The IRGC Navy fired on and disabled M/V GFS Galaxy, a Cyprus-flagged container ship, in the Strait of Hormuz, saying the vessel had deactivated its tracking system and strayed onto an 'unauthorized route' rather than Iran's approved shipping lane. The ship caught fire and suffered significant engine-room damage; the crew abandoned the vessel and one crew member was reported missing. CENTCOM called it a 'blatant' attack and launched retaliatory strikes hours later.

title: US gives Iran Saturday deadline to declare Hormuz open, halt attacks
description: US officials demanded Iran publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz fully open and pledge to stop firing on commercial ships by Saturday, warning of 'harsh consequences' otherwise; one official said 'it is not gonna be a great day for them' if Tehran refuses. Iran's chief negotiator Ghalibaf wrote on X that 'America still hasn't learned that bullying and breaking promises are no longer cost-free... if you strike, you'll get hit.' Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi was set to meet Omani counterpart Badr al-Busaidi in Muscat Saturday to discuss Hormuz arrangements.

title: UN shipping agency tells states to reject Iran's claimed control of Hormuz
description: The International Maritime Organization's governing council agreed member states should not recognize Iran's claim of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz or the jurisdiction of Iran's newly created Persian Gulf Strait Authority, which has demanded vessels obtain a 'valid passage permit' before transiting. Iran, which does not hold a Council seat, told IMO delegates it rejected the 'selective, politically motivated and legally unfounded allegations.'

title: CNN: satellite images show Iran rebuilding Parchin nuclear site despite MOU
description: Satellite imagery obtained by CNN and analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security shows Iran repairing the underground Taleghan 2 facility inside the Parchin military complex, with images from June 22 and July 7 showing excavation around three bomb-penetration holes, new concrete reinforcement and rebar installation for a permanent cap. Separate June 21 imagery showed vehicles entering tunnels at 'Pickaxe Mountain,' a suspected underground nuclear site near Isfahan. The activity shows Iran was rebuilding while the June 17 US-Iran memorandum of understanding was still formally in force.

title: Trump says he left orders to bomb Iran 'at levels never seen' if assassinated
description: Trump told the New York Post he has left standing instructions to strike Iran if Tehran succeeds in assassinating him: 'I've left instructions — if anything happens, to just literally bomb them at levels that they've never seen before.' The comments came a day after the Wall Street Journal reported Israel shared intelligence with Washington on a new Iranian plot against Trump; he said he had been 'No. 1 [on Iran's kill list] for a long time' since ordering the 2020 killing of Qassem Soleimani.

title: IDF Golani troops destroy Hezbollah weapons depots, tunnels in south Lebanon
description: Golani Brigade soldiers operating under the 36th Division in the southern Lebanon security zone located and destroyed Hezbollah weapons depots containing launchers, machine guns, explosives and missiles, the IDF said. In the Majdal Zoun area, troops also found and destroyed two underground tunnel routes totaling roughly 200 meters, which the military said were built to stage attacks on Israeli forces and civilians.

title: Strait of Hormuz shipping grinds to near-halt as fighting resumes
description: Only 5 vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz from Wednesday into Thursday morning, down from 45 transits on Monday and roughly 130 a day before the war began in February. No large vessel above 10,000 dwt has crossed via the US-coordinated 'Southern Highway' route while broadcasting its location since July 7. Brent crude stood at $76.58 a barrel as of 05:00 GMT Friday, still up about $4 on the week despite easing slightly from Wednesday's spike, as analysts warned of $10-15 further upside if refined-product inventories keep falling.

title: US says 'technical talks' with Iran continue despite Trump's 'over' remark
description: A US official said Washington remains committed to a negotiated solution and that technical talks with Iran are continuing, even after Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' at the NATO summit and after two days of strikes. The official called Iran's Hormuz tanker attacks 'failed performance at an unacceptable level' under the performance-based Islamabad memorandum, but said talks with Tehran would go on regardless.

title: US strikes ~90 targets across southern Iran; Iran reports 3 IRGC killed
description: US Central Command carried out a second wave of strikes on July 9, hitting roughly 90 targets across southern Iran including air defenses, coastal surveillance sites, missile and drone storage, naval assets and two railway bridges used to move military supplies, in an operation lasting about seven hours. Iran's Mizan news agency reported three IRGC members killed. A US official denied Iranian claims the strikes hit near the Bushehr nuclear plant, saying 'the nuclear power plant was not a target.'

title: Iran drones hit Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar; Kuwait reports one injured
description: Iran's army said it launched a large number of kamikaze drones at a Patriot missile interceptor system in Kuwait, an early-warning radar system in Qatar, and fuel tanks in Bahrain, in retaliation for the US strikes hours earlier. Kuwait's Defense Ministry said it intercepted three ballistic missiles, one cruise missile and 10 drones, but the interceptions caused damage at several locations and left one person injured in stable condition. Bahrain's air defenses intercepted and destroyed the drones aimed at it; Qatari authorities did not comment on the reported attack on their territory.

title: Iran fires 10 ballistic missiles at Jordan's Azraq base hosting Western troops
description: The IRGC fired 10 ballistic missiles at Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti air base near Azraq, which hosts US, German, Belgian and French forces, calling it the 'second phase' of its response to the US strikes. Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles with no casualties or damage; Iran claimed four structures, including hangars and command centers, were destroyed. The IRGC warned that 'if US attacks were repeated, other US bases in the region would also be targeted.'

title: Israel's Katz says IDF ready to strike Iran again 'even for a third time'
description: Speaking at an Israeli Air Force pilots' course graduation ceremony, Defense Minister Israel Katz said the IDF is 'on high alert and prepared to resume the campaign and carry out an Israeli strike against Iran, even for a third time,' adding, 'If we need to return, we will return with even greater force.' The remarks came as the US-Iran ceasefire collapsed and Iran traded strikes with US bases across the Gulf.

title: Trump briefs Netanyahu on Gulf strikes; Netanyahu warns against F-35 sale to Turkey
description: Trump and Netanyahu held a phone call in which Trump updated the Israeli prime minister on 'American moves in the Gulf' following the renewed US strikes on Iran. Netanyahu also used the call to warn Trump against approving a proposed F-35 fighter jet sale to Turkey, and raised concerns about President Erdogan's rhetoric against Israel.

title: Iran reports 14 killed, 78 wounded from two days of US airstrikes
description: Iran's Health Ministry released the first official casualty figures from the US airstrikes on July 7-8, reporting at least 14 people killed and 78 wounded. Ministry spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour released the figures as the funeral of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei concluded. Additional casualties on July 9 included at least three people killed in strikes on Khuzestan province and a firefighter killed at an airport in Iranshahr.

title: Trump declares Iran ceasefire 'over' at NATO summit in Ankara
description: At the NATO summit in Ankara, President Trump declared that the ceasefire memorandum with Iran is 'over' following the exchange of attacks. Trump said Iran violated the deal by attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. However, he said negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner would continue talks with Iran. Trump also criticized European NATO allies for not supporting the Iran campaign, saying 'I'm not happy with NATO, because of the fact that they didn't want to help us with the number one state sponsor of terror, that's Iran.'

title: Iran strikes US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain; IRGC claims 85 sites hit
description: Early on July 8, Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched drones and missiles at US military facilities across the Gulf, saying it had struck '85 US military installations' in Bahrain and Kuwait in retaliation for the previous day's US strikes on Iran. Named targets included the Sheikh Isa Air Base and the US Fifth Fleet headquarters at Salman Port in Bahrain, and the Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait; Bahrain's Interior Ministry sounded air-raid sirens and told residents to shelter, and Iran claimed it downed a US drone 'that intended to interfere with the operation.' Iran's parliament speaker and lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf declared, 'The era of bullying and extortion is over. It leads nowhere,' as Tehran threatened to abandon the Doha talks. No casualties were immediately confirmed.

title: US hits 80+ targets across southern Iran in 'offensive strikes'
description: US Central Command said it struck 'more than 80 targets' inside Iran on July 7 in retaliation for the Strait of Hormuz ship attacks, hitting air defenses, command-and-control nodes, coastal radar and anti-ship missile sites, and more than 60 IRGC small boats. Iranian accounts placed strikes on Sirik, Qeshm Island and Bandar Abbas across Hormozgan province, with Tehran saying civilian sites including fishing piers and a telecommunications tower were hit and several people hospitalized. CENTCOM labelled the operation 'offensive strikes,' a shift from June's 'self-defense' framing; the IRGC claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone. President Trump ordered the strikes from the NATO summit in Turkey, calling the campaign 'not even a war... it's a military operation, it's a denuclearization, that's really what it is, of Iran.'

title: US revokes Iran oil waiver; Brent jumps 5.6% to $76
description: The US Treasury revoked the June 21 sanctions waiver that had let companies transact in Iranian crude and petrochemicals under the ceasefire memorandum, giving firms until July 17 to wind down. A US official said the deal was always contingent on Iran's behavior and that the Hormuz ship attacks violated the understanding. Brent crude settled 3% higher at $74.16 a barrel and WTI rose 2.8% to $70.44; after the waiver was pulled, Brent jumped 5.6% to $76.04 and WTI 5.4% to $72.25 in after-hours trading.

title: IRGC missiles hit three tankers in Strait of Hormuz
description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired at least two missiles at commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz overnight, striking three tankers. The Qatari-flagged LNG carrier Al Rekayyat was hit on its port side, sparking an engine-room fire though its crew was reported safe; a Saudi-flagged crude oil tanker sustained significant damage; and a third tanker was struck by an 'unknown projectile' about 8 nautical miles off Limah, Oman, per the UKMTO. Iran did not directly claim responsibility, with state TV suggesting a tanker was hit after ignoring warnings. The attacks — on a waterway carrying roughly a fifth of the world's oil — triggered the US retaliatory strikes and the reimposition of oil sanctions.

title: Trump vows US will win Iran war 'one way or the other' as talks stay paused
description: Speaking on July 6 as Iran held the mass funeral for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, President Donald Trump said of the war, 'We're gonna win one way or the other. We'll win the nice way or not the nice way,' insisting Iran 'cannot have a nuclear weapon.' He said his administration was 'doing very well' in Pakistani- and Qatari-mediated talks focused on ending the war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and blocking an Iranian bomb, and told Axios negotiations would stay paused until at least July 9 with 'neither side' shooting. Sticking points included Iran's push to impose tolls on Hormuz transits and its demand that Israel halt strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon; Tehran disputed US claims it had agreed to UN inspections and to buy American farm goods with unfrozen assets.

title: Israeli drone strike kills 4 civilians near Nabatieh, including school principal
description: On July 6, an Israeli drone struck a car near Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon, killing four people the Lebanese Health Ministry identified as school principal Esperanza Ghandour, her mother, a female domestic worker and a male foreign laborer. Ghandour had been checking on repairs at her war-damaged home and was returning when the vehicle was hit. The IDF said it struck a vehicle carrying four people who were approaching what it calls a 'security zone' and posed a threat to its forces. The killings marked another deadly Israeli strike in the south despite the April 16 ceasefire, which has since been extended twice.

title: Khamenei's main funeral procession crosses Tehran; mourners chant to 'kill Trump'
description: On July 6, Iran held the peak day of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's state funeral, as a 12-hour procession carried his flag-draped coffin — and those of family members killed in the February 28 US-Israeli strike, including a 14-month-old granddaughter — along a 10-kilometer route from Imam Hossein Square to Azadi Square before the caskets were driven to Mehrabad International Airport. Hundreds of thousands of black-clad mourners reached out to touch the truck; one told reporters, 'They killed our imam, we should kill their leader, Trump,' while Gen. Amir Hatami vowed, 'We will avenge the blood of our martyred Imam and all of our martyrs.' Authorities projected 15-20 million participants across the multi-day rites; after Tehran the body was to travel to Qom on July 7, Najaf and Karbala on July 8, and burial in Mashhad on July 9.

title: Cargo ship attacked off Hodeidah as Houthis kill 16 Yemeni government troops
description: A skiff opened fire on a bulk carrier about 30 nautical miles southwest of Hodeidah in the Red Sea on July 5, with onboard security guards returning fire before the attackers retreated to a larger vessel; the ship and crew were reported safe and no group claimed responsibility. The attack came as the Houthis pressed their declared ban on Israeli-linked shipping in the Red Sea. Over the same weekend, Houthi fighters killed 16 government-aligned Yemeni troops and wounded 22 in clashes south of Hodeidah — described by a military officer as the deadliest Houthi assault in years — with snipers, drones and mortars inflicting most casualties from late Friday into Saturday.

title: Iran holds day-two funeral prayers over Khamenei casket; Tehran airspace shut for July 6 procession
description: On the second day of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's state funeral, prayers were offered around 8 a.m. over his casket at the Grand Mosalla complex in Tehran, where his body has lain in state since July 4, along with prayers for four family members killed in the same February 28 US-Israeli strike. Thousands massed before dawn in 100°F (38°C) heat as authorities sprayed mist to cool the crowd, and a poet drew cheers from the assembled mourners by asking of President Trump, 'Why is the most bastard man in the world still alive?' Iran ordered Tehran's airspace fully closed for the main July 6 procession, a 10-kilometer route from Imam Hossein Square to Azadi Square. New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, believed wounded in the February strike that killed his father, had still not appeared publicly since taking office.

title: Trump says US 'gave Iran a week off' for funeral in July 4 Mount Rushmore speech
description: Speaking at a July 4 Independence Day celebration at Mount Rushmore, President Donald Trump said of Iran: 'We knocked the hell out of Iran. They're dying to settle. They want to settle so badly. We gave them a week off for a funeral because we're nice.' The remark referred to the pause in US-Iran hostilities and Doha talks during Khamenei's funeral week and came on the 250th anniversary of US independence, as Iran mourned the supreme leader killed by a US strike on February 28. Trump touted the American military campaign while negotiations over Hormuz management and frozen assets stayed frozen until after the funeral processions.

title: Medvedev calls Iran's power to shut Hormuz equal to a nuclear weapon after Tehran funeral visit
description: Returning from Khamenei's funeral in Tehran, Russian Security Council deputy chairman Dmitry Medvedev said in a video posted to social media that Iran's ability to disrupt traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is 'equivalent to possession of a nuclear weapon.' Medvedev, sent by President Vladimir Putin as his special envoy, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the visit and floated creating a treaty or forum uniting states under 'illegitimate' Western sanctions, naming Russia, Iran and China. The comments underscored deepening Moscow-Tehran alignment as US-Iran talks over Hormuz management and frozen assets remained paused for the funeral.

title: Iran rights monitor documents 141 executions in June amid wartime crackdown
description: The Norway-linked monitor Iran Human Rights Movement (Iran HRM) reported on July 4 that Iranian authorities carried out 141 executions in June 2026, part of a surge in state killings during the wartime crackdown. The group said its 'No to Executions Tuesdays' campaign had entered its 127th consecutive week on June 30, with prisoners in 57 prisons joining coordinated hunger strikes. Since the February 28 outbreak of war, rights groups say Iran has arbitrarily executed dozens on politically motivated charges — including people accused of spying for the US or Israel — as authorities tightened repression under cover of the conflict.

title: Khamenei's Tehran funeral opens with vast crowd chanting 'Death to America' on US 250th anniversary
description: Iran began the multi-day state funeral for Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on July 4, unveiling his casket in a glass case at the Grand Mosalla in Tehran as a vast crowd wept and chanted 'Death to America, Death to Israel!' Authorities chose the date — the 250th anniversary of US independence — without acknowledging the symbolism, projecting 15-20 million mourners in what would be the largest state funeral in Iran's history. July 5 is set aside for funeral prayers and July 6 for the main procession, a 10-kilometer route from Imam Hossein Square to Azadi Square beginning at 6 a.m. New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father, had not made a public appearance since taking office.

title: UK's Starmer, France's Macron agree to work with Oman on Hormuz demining; France withdraws carrier
description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and French President Emmanuel Macron agreed to work with Oman to 'ensure that Oman's sovereign territorial waters are safe for navigation' through the Strait of Hormuz, widening the mine-clearance effort beyond the France-Oman arrangement reached June 29. France deployed minehunters to the strait and announced the withdrawal of its aircraft carrier from the region as flows through the waterway continued to recover. The Anglo-French initiative aimed at restoring safe maritime transit came as US-Iran talks paused for Khamenei's funeral.

title: Iran opens oil-sale talks with Japanese firms under temporary US sanctions waiver
description: Iran began negotiations with Japanese companies over resuming crude oil sales under a temporary US sanctions waiver, a senior Iranian official said, as Tehran worked to restart exports choked off during the war. The official cautioned that any deal would require Washington to extend the waiver, given the multi-week shipping time between Iran and Japan. The talks followed the partial reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the establishment of a US-Iran communications mechanism at the Doha talks.

title: Israel strikes ~10 Hezbollah sites after reservist seriously wounded in Bint Jbeil clash
description: The Israeli Air Force struck around 10 Hezbollah sites in the south Lebanon towns of Bint Jbeil, Beit Yahoun, Kounine and Baraashit, and also hit a weapons-transport truck, in retaliation for a July 2 attack on troops. The IDF said that around 6 p.m. Thursday, soldiers of the 679th 'Yiftah' Armored Brigade operating in Bint Jbeil encountered a Hezbollah gunman who opened fire, seriously wounding one reservist and lightly wounding two others; troops shelled the building he fired from before the wider airstrikes. Iran's parliament speaker and lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that Tehran would 'resume its proportionate measures' if the US and Israel failed to honor their commitments, as the strikes strained the week-old Israel-Lebanon framework and the paused US-Iran talks.

title: Iran opens Khamenei state funeral; casket displayed after 4 months in cold storage, 15-20M expected
description: Iran began farewell ceremonies for Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, releasing the first images of his casket more than four months after he was killed on February 28 by a US bunker-penetrating strike on his Tehran compound — his body held in refrigerated storage under an exception in Islamic law. The multi-day funeral runs July 4-9 across Tehran, Qom, Mashhad and the Iraqi shrine cities of Najaf and Karbala, with authorities projecting 15-20 million mourners at the July 6 Tehran procession, five public holidays declared, 50 million loaves of bread prepared and 14,000 journalists credentialed. Reports of coercion were widespread: Tehran municipality canceled all leave, the Basij warned shopkeepers that open businesses would be 'sealed,' and unions, automakers and charities were ordered to supply attendees and free meals. An Iranian army general warned the US and Israel against launching any attack during the processions, and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf urged Iranians to 'rise up' and 'demand revenge.'

title: Medvedev, China's He Wei lead foreign delegations to Khamenei funeral; no major power sends top leader
description: Officials from more than 30 countries and religious leaders from over 90 nations gathered for Khamenei's funeral, but no major world power sent its head of state. Russia's Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of the Security Council, led Moscow's delegation as Vladimir Putin's special envoy; China sent He Wei, vice chairman of the National People's Congress Standing Committee — its first senior official to visit Iran since the war began. Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif attended with a high-level delegation, while India declined to send Prime Minister Narendra Modi, dispatching a deputy foreign minister instead, and Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon and Georgia's president also attended. Analysts read the muted turnout as Tehran's post-war isolation showing through the pageantry.

title: IDF kills Hezbollah operative emerging from tunnel at Ali Taher ridge; ~30 fighters holed up below
description: The IDF said Egoz Commando Unit troops spotted a Hezbollah operative emerging from a tunnel shaft on the Ali Taher ridge inside Israel's south Lebanon security zone, and an airstrike 'eliminated the terrorist to remove the threat,' calling him 'an immediate threat to our forces.' The military said it was continuing to operate at the ridge, beneath which Hezbollah maintains a massive underground complex where roughly 30 operatives were holed up. The strike added to a steady run of clashes fraying the week-old US-brokered Israel-Lebanon framework, following an Israeli officer's killing and a reservist's severe wounding days earlier.

title: Brent falls to $70.78, lowest since war began, as Hormuz tanker traffic returns to pre-war range
description: Brent crude fell $0.79 to $70.78 a barrel and US WTI dropped to $67.74, the lowest levels since the US-Israel war on Iran began on February 28, as oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz kept recovering. Morgan Stanley said 35 oil and gas tankers exited the strait on Thursday — the first time volume had returned to within the pre-war range — and cut its oil price forecast for the second time in two weeks, warning of a looming glut. Over 20 million barrels of Iranian crude were staged for export, up 18% on the week, while China diversified purchases toward Russia, Kazakhstan and Brazil; economist Mohammad Reza Farzanegan cautioned that the market was pricing a Hormuz recovery and Iranian export opening that 'remain fragile.'

title: US expands naval buildup as Boxer group, 11th MEU arrive; ~24 warships, 50,000 troops in region
description: US Central Command said the Boxer Amphibious Ready Group — the amphibious assault ship USS Boxer and transport dock USS Portland, with the embarked 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit of more than 2,000 Marines — arrived in the Middle East on June 30, joining the Comstock already on station and a second Marine unit, the 31st MEU aboard the Tripoli group in the Arabian Sea. CENTCOM said the arrival put at least 24 Navy warships in the region, including the carriers USS Abraham Lincoln and USS George H.W. Bush and 15 destroyers, with roughly 50,000 US service members operating there. The reinforcement landed as US-Iran talks paused ahead of Khamenei's funeral, underscoring Washington's leverage even amid diplomacy.

title: Iran suspends IAEA cooperation; Israel's Sa'ar calls move 'scandalous'
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered Iran to suspend cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency, formalizing legislation that mandates removing IAEA surveillance cameras, halting inspector access, and ending data and reporting exchanges until unspecified 'conditions are met' — including guaranteed security for Iran's nuclear facilities and scientists. The move, coming after US and Israeli strikes hit Iran's nuclear sites earlier in the war, threatened to sever the last verification links to Tehran's program. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar called it 'scandalous,' saying Iran was making 'a complete renunciation of all its international nuclear obligations and commitments'; the US, France and Germany also condemned the decision.

title: US-Iran indirect Doha talks end with 'positive progress,' violations hotline, partial asset unfreeze
description: Two days of indirect US-Iran technical talks in Doha — delegations in separate rooms relaying messages through Qatari and Pakistani mediators — concluded with what Qatar's Foreign Ministry called 'positive progress,' establishing a communications mechanism to address violations of the June 17 memorandum and agreeing that a portion of Iran's $6 billion in frozen assets would be freed for domestic procurement. The sessions focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and unlocking assets, not Iran's nuclear program, which both sides deferred; Vice President JD Vance said the talks were 'going well' and that nuclear discussions 'would start soon.' Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf publicly insisted Iran was 'currently not negotiating with the United States at all,' and the next round was set for after Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral on July 9.

title: Iran exports 50M barrels in two weeks as Hormuz traffic climbs to ~35 ships in 24 hours
description: Iran exported roughly 50 million barrels of crude in the two weeks since the US lifted its naval blockade of Iranian ports — about 1.66 million barrels a day in June — signaling a partial recovery for its export-dependent economy. At least 35 commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz in the previous 24 hours, a sharp rebound from the near-total halt of recent weeks but still well below the roughly 110 ships a day that crossed before the war, with routing split unevenly between Iranian and Omani lanes. Iran signaled it would begin charging 'service fees' for passage once the toll-free window expires in mid-August.

title: US Navy MH-60S ditches in Arabian Sea; one crew member missing
description: A US Navy MH-60S Seahawk helicopter assigned to the carrier USS George H.W. Bush made an emergency water landing in the Arabian Sea around 3:30 a.m. EDT on July 1, the Navy said, with three of the four crew recovered in stable condition and a search under way for the fourth. The Navy said there was 'no indication the emergency was caused by hostile action.' It was the second US military helicopter mishap in the region in weeks, after an Army AH-64 Apache crew was rescued from the Gulf of Oman on June 9 — an incident President Trump had blamed on Iranian forces.

title: Hormuz traffic collapses to ~5 ships on Day 122 as blockade grinds on
description: On the 122nd day of the Strait of Hormuz blockade, traffic through the world's most important oil chokepoint had all but halted, with only about 5 vessels transiting versus roughly 93 per day under normal conditions, moving in convoys under naval escort. Brent crude traded around $73 a barrel as the waterway — which carries some 20% of global oil and LNG — remained effectively closed despite the June 17 US-Iran memorandum meant to reopen it. Tehran continued to insist passage occur only under Iranian authorization, even as US and Iranian delegations gathered in Doha to negotiate the strait's future management.

title: US, Iran hold indirect Doha talks; Oman floats Hormuz management plan, no face-to-face meeting
description: US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and other mediators in Doha, while separate US and Iranian technical delegations negotiated indirectly through Qatari and Pakistani channels with no face-to-face meeting. Qatar spokesman Majed Al Ansari said 'there are no direct meetings scheduled' and 'no high-level meeting between the two sides,' and that the American team's visit was 'unrelated to the Iranian delegation's trip.' Oman circulated a post-conflict framework proposing long-term management of the Strait of Hormuz — covering navigational safety, environmental protection and maritime security, with possible service fees — as the sides sought to translate the June 17 memorandum into workable terms.

title: Iran conditions talks on US forcing Israel to end Lebanon strikes; 'prepared for war'
description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baqaei said Tehran would not resume negotiations to end the war until Washington implemented the clauses of the June 17 memorandum, naming as the 'main criterion' that the US 'force' Israel to halt its attacks on Lebanon. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf set out further preconditions — no final agreement until the deal's provisions on ceasing hostilities, lifting the naval blockade and releasing frozen assets were met. Iran's negotiator warned, 'We are pursuing dialogue, but if the dialogue is not implemented, we are also prepared for war,' underscoring how far apart the two sides remained even as delegations convened in Doha.

title: Katz orders IDF to prepare independent strike on Iran; warns war possible 'tomorrow'
description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz ordered the military to draw up plans for a 'blue-and-white operation in Iran' — an attack carried out independently, without US coordination — and warned Israel could go to war with Tehran 'tomorrow' if Iran fired missiles at Israeli territory. 'If Iran fires missiles at Israel, Israel will strike Iran with force,' Katz said, adding, 'There is no equation we will accept in which Iran fires at Israel.' He said the IDF was on high alert with targets identified, and that while he did not want to disrupt President Trump's diplomacy, 'when it comes to defending ourselves, there are no compromises, not in Lebanon and not in Iran.'

title: Iran's annual inflation hits 88.6%, highest since WWII; rial firms after US deal
description: The Statistical Center of Iran reported a year-on-year inflation rate of 88.6% for the month of Khordad (ending June 21) — described as the highest recorded since the Second World War — with rural inflation reaching 108.1% and some food prices up as much as 278% over the year. The crisis, deepened by the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, eased only on the currency front: after Tehran and Washington signed their preliminary understanding in late June, the exchange rate firmed by roughly 30,000 tomans against the dollar, ending months of blockade-driven volatility. The figures underscored that even a halt to the fighting leaves Iran's economy in freefall.

title: Trump says Iran requested Doha talks Tuesday; Tehran denies any meeting is scheduled
description: President Trump posted on Truth Social that 'IRAN HAS REQUESTED A MEETING. IT WILL TAKE PLACE TOMORROW IN DOHA!' and White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were flying to Qatar for the talks. Iran's deputy foreign minister and senior negotiator Kazem Gharibabadi publicly contradicted the announcement, saying 'the holding of technical meetings of the working groups has not been scheduled for this week' and that media reports of talks in Doha were 'not confirmed.' A senior Iranian source nonetheless told Reuters that representatives would meet Tuesday to discuss managing the Strait of Hormuz and de-escalation, exposing the muddled state of diplomacy a day after both sides paused their attacks.

title: France and Oman agree to demine Hormuz; Iran warns Paris against 'provocations'
description: After hosting Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq at the Elysee Palace, French President Emmanuel Macron said France and Oman had 'decided to collaborate jointly... on demining the strait to secure maritime routes and ensure free and unconditional passage through the Strait of Hormuz.' Iran rejected any foreign role: deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said that under the Islamabad memorandum 'demining is carried out solely by Iran and by no other country,' called the situation 'sensitive and complex,' and warned, 'we strongly advise France not to complicate it further with its provocations.' The clash reflected rival interpretations of the June 17 US-Iran understanding, with Tehran asserting sole control of the waterway it had mined.

title: Israeli cyber chief says Iranian cyberattacks tripled to ~4,800 in June
description: Yossi Karadi, director-general of Israel's National Cyber Directorate, told the German daily Die Welt that hostile cyber incidents attributed to Iran jumped from about 1,600 in June 2025 to roughly 4,800 so far in June 2026 — roughly a tripling. The attacks targeted Israel's critical infrastructure, major organizations, small and medium-sized firms and the public, including law practices and accounting firms, and were accompanied by IRGC digital propaganda such as Lego-style AI animation videos. 'We can handle them, but we have to take them seriously,' Karadi said. 'Unlike in the kinetic realm, there's no ceasefire in cyberspace.'

title: Israeli reservist severely wounded in south Lebanon explosion; Hezbollah vows retaliation
description: The IDF said an Israeli reservist was severely wounded by an explosion in southern Lebanon and hospitalized for treatment, the latest casualty as the days-old Israel-Lebanon framework continued to fray. The blast came a day after a Golani Brigade officer was killed by a Hezbollah gunman in Deir Siryan, and as Hezbollah declared it 'reserves the right to retaliate' for Israel's weekend strikes, which it said repeatedly violated the ceasefire. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said Israel sought 'peace and normalization with Lebanon' by 'ending the Iranian occupation of Lebanon by Hezbollah.'

title: US and Iran agree to stand down after weekend strikes; talks to resume Tuesday
description: After two nights of US strikes on Iran and Iran's retaliatory missile and drone barrage on Kuwait and Bahrain, both sides agreed to stop attacking each other, a US official said, with vessels again permitted free movement through the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan, the war's lead mediator, said the US and Iran would resume talks on Tuesday. The de-escalation came hours after President Trump had threatened that 'the Islamic Republic of Iran will no longer exist' if strikes continued and after Iran's IRGC warned that ceasefire violations would 'lead to a complete halt of ongoing processes.' Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi insisted the strait would remain 'under the total oversight of Iran throughout the 30 coming days,' warning that any 'new or separate arrangements' would 'delay the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and increase the level of tension.'

title: IDF officer killed by Hezbollah gunman in Deir Siryan; first Israeli death since Lebanon deal
description: Capt. David Hazutt, 21, a platoon commander in the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion from Ashkelon, was killed around 2 a.m. when Israeli troops entering a structure in the southern Lebanese village of Deir Siryan encountered a Hezbollah operative who opened fire, also lightly wounding another soldier before fleeing. He was the first Israeli fatality since Israel, Lebanon and the US signed the trilateral framework on Friday. After extensive searches, the IDF said it located the gunman hiding in a nearby building later that day and killed him. The killing underscored how quickly the days-old deal was fraying.

title: Qatar says citizen killed by shrapnel amid Gulf military operations
description: Qatar's interior ministry said a Qatari national was killed by shrapnel from 'military operations in the area' after a small vessel carrying him and an Arab resident failed to return Saturday evening and was located by a maritime search-and-rescue team early Sunday. The second man was wounded and reported in stable condition. The ministry did not specify the location or explicitly link the shrapnel to the Iranian missiles and drones launched the same day at US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, but it was the first reported civilian death of the weekend's escalation across the Gulf.

title: Bahrain says Iranian munition damages residential building near airport; Kuwait intercepts 2 missiles
description: Bahrain's government said an Iranian strike damaged a residential building near Bahrain International Airport — not near the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters — with no one killed, calling it 'a dangerous escalation' that revealed 'a deliberate approach and a systematic pattern of repeated aggression.' Kuwait said its air defenses intercepted Iranian drones and two ballistic missiles with no reports of injuries or damage, condemning 'repeated heinous Iranian aggressions' against its sovereignty. The strikes were Iran's retaliation for two nights of US attacks; both Gulf states bore the brunt of Iranian fire despite having no role in the US operations.

title: IDF destroys 200-meter Hezbollah tunnel in Majdal Zoun
description: The Israeli military said it destroyed a 200-meter (660-foot) Hezbollah tunnel beneath the southern Lebanese village of Majdal Zoun, publishing footage of the demolition and saying the tunnel contained weapons and rocket-launcher shafts. The operation, days after the trilateral framework that envisages a phased Israeli handover of southern Lebanon to the Lebanese army, signaled the IDF would keep dismantling Hezbollah infrastructure even as it nominally began withdrawing from pilot zones.

title: IRGC strikes US sites in Kuwait, Bahrain; claims 8 facilities hit; Iran halts diplomacy
description: Early Sunday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired missiles and drones at US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for two nights of US strikes on Iran. The IRGC claimed it 'destroyed eight important US military facilities' at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait and at the Fifth Fleet naval base in Port Salman, Bahrain — claims that could not be verified. Kuwait's army said its air defenses were intercepting incoming attacks, while Bahrain's interior ministry activated sirens and told residents to seek shelter; a US official said nearly all projectiles were intercepted and there were no reports of US casualties or damage. The IRGC declared the US strikes a ceasefire violation that 'will result in the complete halt of all diplomatic processes.'

title: US launches second night of strikes on Iran near Sirik; Trump threatens to 'complete the job'
description: US military aircraft struck Iranian military surveillance infrastructure, communication systems, air defense sites, drone storage facilities and minelayer capabilities, with explosions reported around the village of Tahrui near the southern port of Sirik — the focal point of Friday's US attacks as well. It was the second straight night of American strikes, launched in response to the drone attack on the tanker Kiku. President Trump warned: 'There may come a point when we are no longer able to be reasonable, and will be forced to militarily complete the job that we very successfully started.' Iran's Foreign Ministry called the strikes a 'blatant violation' of the UN Charter and a 'clear breach of Paragraph 1' of the June 17 memorandum, with MP Ebrahim Azizi protesting that Washington 'once again attacked Iran in the middle of negotiations'; Vice President JD Vance said 'violence will be met with violence.'

title: Iran drone hits Panama-flagged tanker Kiku in Strait of Hormuz
description: At about 4:30 a.m. Eastern time, the Panama-flagged oil tanker Kiku — carrying more than two million barrels of crude — was struck by a one-way attack drone as it transited the Strait of Hormuz, US Central Command said, attributing the strike to Iran. The attack came two days after an Iranian drone hit the Singapore-flagged Ever Lovely, and as the IRGC continued to insist that the only authorized passage through the strait was 'the one declared by the Islamic Republic of Iran.' Iranian state media said three foreign tankers that tried to cross Hormuz without Iranian authorization had turned back after warnings. The strike triggered two consecutive nights of US retaliatory strikes on Iran.

title: IDF strikes south Lebanon kill at least 27, first attacks since framework deal
description: Israel carried out a wave of strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon overnight and into Saturday — the first since Washington announced the trilateral Israel-Lebanon framework a day earlier — saying it targeted Hezbollah after the group attacked Israeli troops in violation of the day-old ceasefire. Lebanese media and first responders reported at least 27 people killed and 26 wounded. An IDF spokesperson said one strike in the Nabatieh area hit 'suspected terrorists who posed a threat to IDF soldiers,' and several more strikes followed in the same area; an evening strike killed at least one more person and wounded two, Lebanon's health ministry said. The bloodshed underscored how fragile the newly signed framework remained as Netanyahu insisted the IDF would not withdraw.

title: US bombs Iran: 6 aircraft hit 4 missile, drone and radar sites near Hormuz and Qeshm Island
description: Six land-based US aircraft struck four Iranian targets along the Strait of Hormuz coast and on Qeshm Island, hitting missile and drone storage facilities and radar sites, US Central Command said, calling it a 'powerful response' to Iran's 'dangerous behavior' and stating the 'unwarranted aggression against commercial shipping by Iranian forces clearly violated the ceasefire.' It was the first US strike on Iran since the two sides extended their truce in the June 17 memorandum. The action retaliated for the June 25 IRGC drone attack on the Singapore-flagged cargo ship Ever Lovely; President Trump said Iran 'shot at least four One Way Attack Drones at Ships,' one of which 'solidly hit the upper deck,' calling it 'a foolish violation of our Ceasefire Agreement.' No casualties were reported and Iran did not immediately retaliate, instead reportedly opening a communications line with Washington while rejecting new shipping lanes and turning back three foreign tankers.

title: Israel, Lebanon sign US-brokered framework for partial IDF withdrawal from two pilot zones
description: Israel, Lebanon and the US signed a framework agreement at the State Department in Washington after four days of talks, under which the IDF will begin partially withdrawing from southern Lebanon by handing two 'pilot zones' — one north of the Litani river and one farther south, both already cleared of Hezbollah infrastructure by Israel — to the Lebanese Armed Forces. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called it 'the beginning of the beginning,' announcing a new trilateral Military Coordination Group for Lebanon and an 'immediate' $100 million US humanitarian donation. Netanyahu cast it as a win that lets Israel hold most of the territory it occupies 'as long as Hezbollah has not disarmed,' while Hezbollah rejected the deal — leader Naim Qassem demanding 'Israel must leave unconditionally' and MP Hassan Fadlallah denouncing 'unilateral, gratuitous concessions.'

title: Netanyahu vows IDF will stay in south Lebanon 'as long as necessary'; strikes kill civilians returning home
description: Israel pressed on with strikes in southern Lebanon as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared the military was 'not going to withdraw' from occupied areas and would remain 'as long as necessary,' brushing aside the US-Iran framework that envisages an Israeli pullback. Hezbollah accused Israel of deliberately targeting displaced residents trying to return to their homes, saying Israeli fire killed two people and wounded a third; an Israeli strike a day earlier killed three in the Tyre district, where a 76-year-old returnee found his house in Maaroub destroyed. The statements hardened a standoff that has repeatedly flared despite the June 19 Qatar-brokered ceasefire, with Economy Minister Bezalel Smotrich having already vowed the IDF would hold the south 'for years.'

title: Cargo ship struck off Oman in Gulf of Oman; IMO pauses Hormuz evacuation; US blames Iran
description: A container ship — later identified as the Singapore-flagged Ever Lovely — was hit by a projectile in the Gulf of Oman as it transited near the Strait of Hormuz off the Omani coast, sustaining damage but no injuries or pollution, the British navy's UKMTO reported. A US official told MS Now that Iran was behind the strike near Dahit, Oman; Washington publicly attributed it the next day to an IRGC one-way attack drone, while the IRGC reiterated that the only authorized passage was 'the one declared by the Islamic Republic of Iran.' IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez paused the agency's week-old Hormuz evacuation program — under which roughly 57 ships carrying about 1,100 seafarers had transited since June 23 — saying the safety of seafarers 'remains paramount' until guarantees could be reconfirmed. Brent crude reversed its slide to a four-month low, climbing about 2% to around $75.26, as the attack revived fears the waterway's reopening could unravel.

title: Oil falls below pre-war level; Brent settles $73.74, WTI under $70 for first time since March
description: Global oil prices fell to their lowest level since before the war as traders bet the US-Iran framework would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures dropped 4.3% to settle at $73.74 a barrel — below the level it traded at before the February 28 US-Israeli strikes on Iran. West Texas Intermediate closed at $70.34 after touching a session low of $69.63, the first time the US benchmark fell below $70 since March 2. Prices had spiked toward $120 during the war when the Hormuz closure choked roughly a fifth of global oil flows; the retreat reflected growing optimism that the waterway would fully reopen under the June 17 memorandum.

title: Gulf allies fear Iran deal a 'disastrous turning point'; Rubio holds 'frank' talks in Kuwait, Abu Dhabi
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio toured three Gulf states to sell the US-Iran framework to skeptical allies who fear it rewards Tehran. Officials told CNN the agreement — which includes a reported $300 billion reconstruction fund for Iran that Trump expects the Gulf to help finance — risked being a 'disastrous turning point,' with Saudi Arabia saying it had 'no details' and Qatar interested but not formally signed on. Rubio, photographed in Kuwait and Abu Dhabi, called his conversations 'very frank, honest, important' and pledged the US would not 'undermine' its Gulf partners, adding that technical talks with Iran would proceed next week. The UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait bore the brunt of Iranian missile and drone retaliation during the war.

title: US reopens embassy in Kuwait after wartime closure; Rubio raises flag
description: The US Embassy in Kuwait City resumed operations effective midnight June 24, months after the State Department suspended it in March when Iranian drones fired at the mission following US-Israeli strikes on Iran. Secretary of State Marco Rubio attended a flag-raising ceremony during his visit. Emergency services for American citizens resume immediately, with other consular services phased in, a State Department spokesperson said. The US had shut both its Kuwait and Saudi Arabia missions in March amid the Iranian retaliation campaign.

title: Qatar says LNG output will return to normal 'within a few weeks' as Hormuz reopens
description: Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani said the Gulf state would restore normal liquefied natural gas production 'within a few weeks, except the damaged facility,' as the Strait of Hormuz reopens under the US-Iran deal. QatarEnergy halted output after a February 28 drone strike on its Ras Laffan plant, and Iranian missiles in mid-March damaged Trains 4 and 6, removing about 17% of capacity. Qatar plans to restore roughly 50% of capacity within a month and 80% within two; the damaged trains may not fully return before 2028. Qatar supplies about a fifth of global LNG, and the shutdown has kept European and Asian spot prices elevated since early March.

title: Trump claims '100% inspections'; Iran denies any IAEA plan; Grossi says visits 'will happen'
description: A public contradiction over nuclear inspections deepened on June 24, the central sticking point of the war-ending framework. President Trump said Iran had 'fully and completely' agreed, posting 'They told us inside and we have it down, 100% inspections,' while adding 'There's no rush' on timing. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei flatly denied it: 'We have not had a meeting with the director general of the IAEA, nor do we have any plans for the agency to inspect Iran's nuclear facilities damaged by the U.S. and Zionist military aggression.' IAEA Director-General Rafael Grossi gave his firmest signal yet that inspectors would return, saying the memorandum 'explicitly states that nuclear activities will be supervised by the IAEA' and 'This is going to happen,' though he too left the timing undefined.

title: US Senate passes war powers resolution 50-48 to halt Iran war, rebuking Trump
description: The US Senate voted 50-48 on June 23 to pass a war powers resolution directing President Trump to remove US forces from hostilities against Iran unless explicitly authorized by Congress. Four Republicans — Bill Cassidy, Lisa Murkowski, Susan Collins and Rand Paul — crossed party lines, while Democrat John Fetterman voted against; Mitch McConnell and Dave McCormick did not vote. The House had passed the same measure 215-208 on June 3, marking the first time both chambers of Congress invoked the 1973 War Powers Act against a sitting president. The resolution is largely symbolic and expected to face a presidential veto. Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump 'promised to put maximum pressure on Iran, but he ended up delivering maximum confusion, maximum chaos.'

title: Iran says US agreed to release $12bn in frozen funds; Tehran disputes US-purchase claim
description: Iran's lead negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on June 23 that the Switzerland talks produced an agreement to release $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets, in two tranches of $6 billion, with initial arrangements made earlier in Qatar and final signing at Bürgenstock. He said sanctions on crude oil, petrochemicals and derivatives had been lifted until a final deal, extending to banking, insurance and transportation. Washington had not confirmed the figure. Trump claimed any released assets would be used to buy US agricultural products, but Iran's central bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati pushed back, saying there is 'no requirement in the memoranda to buy from the United States.'

title: Rubio arrives in UAE to reassure wary Gulf, warns Iran cannot charge Hormuz tolls
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Abu Dhabi on June 23 to begin a three-nation tour of the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain (June 23-25) aimed at easing Gulf monarchies' unease over the US-Iran framework and its implications for the regional balance. Rubio drew a hard line on the Strait of Hormuz: 'It's an international waterway. No country is allowed to charge tolls or fees on an international waterway,' as Iranian officials held talks with Oman on managing the passage. On his approach he said, 'We're really here to hear from them more than we are to talk.' Qatar's prime minister warned that escalation 'anywhere in the region, whether in Lebanon or elsewhere, will affect the negotiations.'

title: Oman and IMO open temporary Hormuz corridor, begin evacuating 11,000+ stranded seafarers
description: Oman announced on June 23 that it had coordinated with the International Maritime Organization to open a temporary maritime corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, with vessels required to coordinate transit days using coordinates issued by the IMO and Omani authorities. The IMO secretary-general said implementation of a phased evacuation plan had begun for more than 11,000 seafarers still stranded in the region, after securing safety guarantees. Oman cautioned that the confined lanes carried an elevated collision risk requiring close monitoring. Iran and Oman separately announced joint management plans for the waterway, noting in a joint statement that the services would carry 'costs associated with them' — a hint at future fees that cut against US and Omani insistence on toll-free passage.

title: Pezeshkian in Pakistan: ballistic missiles 'will never' enter deal; 'without them we'd be like Gaza'
description: Visiting Pakistan, a key mediator in the Tehran-Washington talks, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on June 23 that Iran's ballistic missiles are not part of the memorandum of understanding and 'will never be included,' calling the program non-negotiable and arguing that without its missiles Iran 'would have ended up just like Gaza.' Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif corroborated the reading of the text: 'This MoU does not mention ballistic missiles. It was never on the table, it was never on the agenda, and the Iranian side never even wanted to discuss it.' The remarks reinforced the ceiling Tehran set on the 60-day talks, days after Trump conceded it would be 'unfair' to deny Iran missiles.

title: Lebanon ceasefire 'largely holding'; Israeli fire kills 2 civilians in Nabatieh
description: The renewed Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire was 'largely holding' on June 23, the UN said, a sharp de-escalation from the preceding days that had killed dozens across southern Lebanon. Israeli troops nonetheless opened fire in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, killing two people, and Israel continued limited operations inside its declared security zone. The relative calm coincided with the opening in Washington of the fifth round of direct Israel-Lebanon talks and removed, for the moment, the Lebanon flashpoint that had twice nearly collapsed the US-Iran implementation track.

title: Israel and Lebanon open direct talks in Washington over ceasefire enforcement and Hezbollah disarmament
description: Israeli and Lebanese delegations opened a new round of direct talks in Washington running June 23-25, the US State Department said, after a call between Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. The agenda centers on enforcing the renewed ceasefire, a 'move versus move' reciprocity mechanism, and the future of the Israeli security zone in southern Lebanon. Rubio reiterated 'the need to disarm' Hezbollah and called bilateral negotiations 'the only feasible path to reconstruction, economic recovery, and ending recurrent cycles of violence.' It is the latest in a series of direct contacts that began in April — the first such meetings since 1993 — and runs parallel to the US-Iran implementation track.

title: Smotrich vows IDF will hold south Lebanon 'for years,' won't withdraw even if US demands it
description: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich told Army Radio on June 23 that Israel will not pull its forces out of the southern Lebanon security zone 'as long as Hezbollah exists in Lebanon' and 'so long as this government remains in power' — 'it simply will not happen.' Asked about potential US pressure to remove troops to satisfy Iranian demands in the Washington-Tehran negotiations, he said Israel would stay 'for years' and would not withdraw 'even in the face of an explicit US demand,' adding 'We have made it clear to the Americans.' The remarks, naming the Beaufort Ridge, openly defied the deconfliction framework the US and Iran agreed in Switzerland and underscored the gap between Israel's stance and the deal's Lebanon provisions.

title: US-Iran talks conclude with roadmap; Iran agrees to readmit IAEA inspectors 'this week'
description: The first round of US-Iran implementation talks in Switzerland concluded on June 22 after roughly 18 hours of negotiations, with Vice President JD Vance saying Iran agreed to invite International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors back into the country 'at the minimum of this week,' calling it 'a major milestone for the American people and the first step in permanently denuclearising' Iran. Vance said four objectives were accomplished — readmitting nuclear inspectors, a mechanism to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, a deconfliction mechanism for the Lebanon ceasefire, and a process for future negotiations — adding 'We haven't built the house, but we've laid a successful foundation.' Mediators Qatar and Pakistan reported 'encouraging progress,' with envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to continue technical talks through the week as Rubio prepared to tour the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain.

title: US Treasury authorizes Iranian oil production and sales under 60-day license
description: The US Treasury Department issued a 60-day license on June 22 suspending restrictions on the production, delivery and sale of Iranian oil, implementing the sanctions-relief provision of the June 17 memorandum of understanding. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent cited 'productive talks' between Tehran and Washington in Switzerland. The waiver clears the legal path for Iranian crude to return to global markets toll-free for the duration of the ceasefire window, after which Tehran is to discuss administration of the Strait of Hormuz with Oman and the Gulf states.

title: Hormuz transits fall to 12 as ships disable transponders; Iran's foreign ministry contradicts IRGC closure
description: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz stalled on June 22, with maritime intelligence firm Windward counting just 12 transits, down from 35 on June 21 and 25 on June 20, after Iran's IRGC declared the waterway closed over Israel's Lebanon strikes. Five of eight vessels entering the strait had switched off their AIS transponders and hugged the Omani shoreline to avoid detection. CENTCOM insisted safe passage was 'intact,' reporting 55 merchant ships transited June 21, while Iran's foreign ministry told Tasnim that shipping was 'operating normally' and said a 'mechanism was set up' for safe passage after the Switzerland talks — directly contradicting its own military's closure announcement. President Trump declared the strait 'totally open' and said 'we have an oil gusher'; Brent crude slipped to just below $80 a barrel.

title: US-Iran talks make 'encouraging progress'; Lebanon de-confliction cell and Hormuz comms line set up
description: Mediators Qatar and Pakistan said the first full session of US-Iran implementation talks in Bürgenstock, Switzerland made 'encouraging progress,' announcing a roadmap toward a final deal within the 60-day window. The parties agreed to stand up a High-Level Committee to oversee further technical talks, a 'communication line' for safe maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz, and a de-confliction mechanism with Lebanon to halt Israel-Hezbollah military operations. Vice President JD Vance said 'I feel great about where we are in Lebanon' and that 'great progress has been made.' A second day of direct talks was set for June 22.

title: Trump threatens to 'hit Iran very hard again' over Hezbollah; Iran briefly pauses talks
description: President Trump posted that Iran must 'immediately stop their highly paid PROXIES in Lebanon from causing trouble' or 'we'll hit Iran very hard again, just like we did last week, only harder!!!' and told Fox News the US could resume bombing Iran and 'take over' the Strait of Hormuz if no deal is reached. Iran's parliament speaker and lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned the US to 'be careful with their statements' and said the armed forces 'are ready to respond.' Iranian state media said the Tehran delegation briefly paused talks over Trump's 'insulting message' before negotiations resumed.

title: IDF strikes 80+ Hezbollah targets after 50+ projectiles; Israel limits fire to Ali al-Taher Hill
description: The Israeli military said it struck more than 80 Hezbollah targets across southern Lebanon on June 21, calling it a response to 'repeated, ongoing, and blatant violations of the ceasefire' after Hezbollah fired over 50 projectiles at IDF troops overnight, with at least 16 reported killed. Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz ordered the IDF to hold its positions in occupied Lebanese territory and to cease fire everywhere except Ali al-Taher Hill, the site of repeated clashes. The IDF chief of staff said the army's goal in Lebanon is 'clear and unchanged — defending the north.'

title: CSIS: Iran war cost the Pentagon about $40 billion
description: A preliminary analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies found the 2026 Iran war cost the Department of Defense roughly $40 billion, with munitions — long-range, sophisticated and expensive — the largest expenditure. The first 100 hours of the war cost $3.7 billion and the cumulative cost reached about $16.5 billion by day 12; the figure excludes operational costs already in the Pentagon's $1 trillion-plus FY2026 budget. Other agencies including Homeland Security and Veterans Affairs added about $1 billion. Gas prices rose from under $3 a gallon to well over $4 during much of the war, costing US households more than $253 above pre-war levels.

title: US-Iran implementation talks open in Bürgenstock, Switzerland; emergency Lebanon session added
description: US and Iranian delegations opened the first round of implementation talks on June 21 in Bürgenstock, Switzerland, two days after the initial session collapsed over Israel's Lebanon offensive. Vice President JD Vance joined special envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential adviser Jared Kushner, while Iran's team was led by parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, with Pakistani and Qatari mediators. Negotiators added an emergency session on the Israel-Hezbollah conflict to the first day's agenda. Vance said his priorities were to 'set up the structure' of the talks, 'make progress' on the nuclear issue and secure a ceasefire in Lebanon, framing the 60-day window to reach a final deal as on track.

title: Israeli strikes kill at least 32 across south Lebanon despite renewed ceasefire; 5th IDF soldier killed
description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least 32 people across southern Lebanon on June 20, less than a day after Israel and Hezbollah renewed their ceasefire, threatening the US-Iran talks set to resume the next day. Lebanon's Health Ministry reported 16 killed and 12 wounded in the Nabatieh district, four family members including two children in Barish, seven in Qanarit, four in Sohmor, and a Lebanese soldier in Kfar Reman, amid more than 100 Israeli strikes since midnight. The IDF said Hezbollah had 'launched more than 50 projectiles toward IDF soldiers operating in southern Lebanon' overnight and that it struck Hezbollah targets in response; a fifth Israeli soldier was killed since the US-Iran deal. The Health Ministry put the cumulative Lebanon toll since March 2 at 4,057 killed and 12,121 wounded.

title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz closed again over Lebanon strikes; CENTCOM says traffic flowing
description: Iran's joint military command announced on June 20 that it had again closed the Strait of Hormuz, citing a 'clear breach' of the US-Iran memorandum triggered by Israel's continued strikes in southern Lebanon, with the IRGC Navy warning ships not to approach the waterway. US Central Command rejected the claim, insisting commercial traffic was still moving through the strait, which had seen at least 20 tankers transit on June 19 — the highest since June 2. The dueling narratives, days after the deal nominally reopened the chokepoint that carries nearly 20 percent of global oil, set the stage for the implementation talks resuming in Switzerland.

title: Trump: no Hormuz tolls for 60 days, but US may impose them as Gulf 'Guardian Angel'
description: President Trump wrote on Truth Social on June 20 that 'There will be NO TOLLS in the Hormuz Strait for 60 days during the Cease Fire Period, and there will be NO TOLLS after the 60 day period has expired, unless they are imposed by and for the United States of America, should the deal not be completed.' He framed any future US tolls as reimbursement for 'services rendered as the Guardian Angel to the countries of the Middle East.' The post rebuffed Iran's insistence that it would administer the strait and added a new financial flashpoint to the talks, hours after Tehran declared the waterway closed and CENTCOM disputed the claim.

title: Tens of thousands rally in Paris for 'Democratic Republic,' condemn Iran's execution wave
description: The Iranian diaspora held one of its largest-ever gatherings in Paris on June 20, organized by the People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK/NCRI) under the slogan 'A Democratic Republic for Iran,' drawing participants from Europe, North America and the Middle East. Speakers rejected both monarchical and theocratic rule and condemned a surge in political executions following the January 2026 uprising. Organizers said dozens of political prisoners had been executed in recent weeks; Amnesty International reported at least 78 protesters and political prisoners sentenced to death remained at risk, including 41 detained over the January protests.

title: Israel kills 47 in south Lebanon, second-deadliest day; 4 soldiers killed; Ben-Gvir: 'all of Lebanon must burn'
description: Israeli strikes killed at least 47 people and wounded 97 across southern Lebanon on June 19, the Lebanese Health Ministry said — the second-deadliest day since the Israel-Hezbollah front reignited in early March. The IDF said it hit more than 150 Hezbollah targets and that four soldiers, including a battalion commander, were killed in two separate Hezbollah drone, rocket and artillery attacks as troops pushed roughly 10 km into Lebanese territory around Nabatieh. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir declared 'all of Lebanon must burn,' while Netanyahu warned Israel would 'exact a very heavy price from Hezbollah.' Al Jazeera put total war deaths since March 2 at at least 3,912.

title: US-Iran implementation talks in Switzerland collapse; Vance cancels trip as Iran balks over Lebanon
description: The first round of US-Iran implementation talks, scheduled for June 19 in Bürgenstock, Switzerland, with Pakistani and Qatari mediators, was abruptly postponed hours before it was to begin. Vice President JD Vance scrapped his trip — the White House cited 'logistical challenges' — while Iran refused to deploy its negotiating team over Israel's continuing offensive in southern Lebanon, which Tehran insists the deal requires Israel to halt. Switzerland's foreign ministry confirmed the postponement, saying it 'remains ready to facilitate these talks.' Vance maintained the 60-day window to reach a final deal was underway and 'each side is honoring its commitments so far,' but the cancellation marked the first stumble of the day-old accord.

title: Israel and Hezbollah renew ceasefire, brokered by Qatar, US and Iran, after deadliest flare-up
description: Israel and Hezbollah agreed late on June 19 to renew their ceasefire after a day of fighting that killed at least 47 people in Lebanon and four Israeli soldiers and threatened to derail the US-Iran deal, according to two regional officials and a US official. Qatar, the United States and Iran brokered the renewal. Hezbollah did not immediately confirm and Israel did not comment, but Israel's ambassador to Washington, Yechiel Leiter, said Israel was 'firmly committed to an immediate ceasefire' provided 'Hezbollah honors the agreement and ceases its hostilities.' The truce eased pressure on the faltering US-Iran framework hours after the Switzerland implementation talks collapsed.

title: Trump calls Netanyahu a 'warrior PM,' touts 'great relationship' to calm Iran-deal rift
description: President Trump moved to repair ties with Netanyahu on June 19, calling him a 'warrior prime minister' and saying 'we've had a great relationship with Israel' during the unveiling of a new Air Force One jet gifted by Qatar. The praise reversed days of public criticism in which Trump had pressed Netanyahu to rein in the IDF's Lebanon offensive, which Washington feared would wreck the US-Iran agreement. The conciliatory tone came as Republican senators continued to attack the deal's financial terms and as the day's Lebanon fighting briefly derailed the accord's first implementation talks.

title: Khamenei okays MOU in writing; says he opposed it, talks 'not acceptance of enemy's position'
description: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei gave his first response to the US-Iran memorandum of understanding in a written statement on his Telegram channel on June 18, authorizing the deal while making clear he had opposed signing it. Khamenei said he approved the MOU only on the recommendation of President Masoud Pezeshkian and the Supreme National Security Council, and insisted that 'future negotiations do not mean acceptance of the enemy's position.' He said the officials who backed the deal had committed that 'if the American side seeks excessive concessions, they will not submit to them' — effectively pre-authorizing Iran's withdrawal from the 60-day talks — and claimed President Trump had signed 'out of desperation.' The statement cleared the way for Friday's Geneva ceremony while signaling Tehran's hardline ceiling on concessions.

title: Trump's Iran deal draws rare Republican rebuke; Trump denies '$300 billion payment'
description: President Trump's US-Iran agreement drew unusual public criticism from senior Republicans on June 18 as the $300 billion Reconstruction and Development Fund became a domestic flashpoint. Sen. Bill Cassidy called it 'the worst foreign policy blunder in decades'; Sen. Ted Cruz said 'giving billions of dollars to theocratic lunatics who want to murder us is not a good idea'; Sen. Thom Tillis, noting the US lost two F-18s, 13 dead and roughly $100 billion in the war, said 'I need more than 14 points'; and Sen. Roger Wicker warned the sum would make 'Iran's payoff under President Obama's 2015 deal look like a pittance.' Trump pushed back on Truth Social — 'There is no 300 Billion Dollar payment to Iran by the U.S. That's Fake News!' — while VP JD Vance insisted 'Not a cent of American money goes to Iran,' saying Gulf states and private investors would fund it. No country had confirmed a financial commitment, and Sen. Lindsey Graham said any nuclear deal would go to Congress for a vote.

title: Israeli drones kill 3 in south Lebanon; IDF soldier killed; Israel maps zone, refuses pullout
description: Israeli operations in southern Lebanon continued on June 18 despite the MOU's call to halt fighting on all fronts. Lebanese state media said an Israeli drone struck a car in the Kfar Tebnit area, killing two people, and a second drone killed one more in the neighboring village of Zebdine, bringing the day's toll to three. The IDF announced Master Sgt. Alexander Filin, 29, had been killed in combat in south Lebanon and that seven soldiers were wounded. Israel published an updated map of its 'security zone' and said it would not withdraw 'at this stage,' while a senior official close to Netanyahu told Reuters Israel was 'conducting stubborn negotiations' with Washington over keeping troops deployed in Lebanon.

title: Three Saudi supertankers cross Hormuz with 6M barrels; US backs $20B maritime reinsurance
description: Commercial oil traffic began returning to the Strait of Hormuz on June 18, hours after the US-Iran MOU took effect. Three Saudi-flagged supertankers sailed through the strait carrying a combined six million barrels of crude. War-risk premiums fell to roughly 1% of hull value per voyage — about $1.1 million for a modern VLCC, down from peaks of up to 10% during the blockade — and the US International Development Finance Corporation deployed $20 billion in maritime reinsurance with Chubb as lead partner to coax insurers back.
