Industry executives cautioned it would take weeks to clear the vessel backlog, with the strait expected to fully reopen within about 30 days of the June 19 formal ratification.

title: Trump says it would be 'unfair' to deny Iran ballistic missiles, abandoning a war aim
description: Speaking to reporters in Paris on June 17 after the US-Iran MOU was reached, President Trump signaled the deal would leave Iran's ballistic missile program intact, reversing one of his original justifications for the war. 'I'm saying that if other countries have them, it's a little bit unfair for them not to have some,' Trump said, adding: 'If Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and they all have some, I would say in relative proportion, I think it's okay.' Having earlier vowed to obliterate Iran's missiles, Trump now framed them as a matter of regional parity — a shift that fueled the emerging Republican backlash and alarmed Israel, which views Iran's missile arsenal as an existential threat.

title: Trump signs hard-copy US-Iran war-ending MOU at Versailles; Iran says deal 'in effect'
description: President Trump personally signed a hard copy of the 14-point, roughly 800-word US-Iran memorandum of understanding during a G7 dinner at the Palace of Versailles in France on June 17, alongside Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. The document — first signed digitally on June 14-15 by VP JD Vance and Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, with Trump witnessing — commits to an immediate and permanent cessation of operations between the US-Israel alliance and Iran, reopening the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping, and lifting US sanctions on Iranian ports and oil sales. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the MOU was finalized, signed electronically by both sides and had 'gone into effect,' adding: 'Now it is time to test the implementation of the agreement.' A formal ceremony in Switzerland remained scheduled for later in the week.

title: US releases 14-point Iran deal text at G7: oil export waivers, $300B fund, no nuclear weapons
description: At a G7 press conference in Evian, France, on June 17, the Trump administration released the terms of the US-Iran agreement. The US will issue waivers allowing the export of Iranian oil, petroleum and derivatives — covering banking, insurance and transportation — and guarantees toll-free commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz during the 60-day negotiating period. Tehran commits to 'not procure or develop nuclear weapons,' while the US and regional partners pledge to build a $300 billion Reconstruction and Development Fund for Iran, a private investment vehicle without US government grants that Reuters reported was already more than half committed and conditioned on Iran proving it had abandoned any nuclear-weapons pursuit. Trump publicly disputed the $300 billion figure even as his administration's released terms described the fund, exposing continued confusion over the deal's financial commitments.

title: Israel keeps striking south Lebanon; Hezbollah drone wounds 4 IDF troops; Iran cites 84 violations
description: Israeli air strikes and drone attacks continued across southern Lebanon on June 17 despite the US-Iran deal's call to end fighting on all fronts. Lebanon's National News Agency reported three Israeli drone strikes in Tyre that caused injuries, a drone strike in the Bint Jbeil district, an air strike on the outskirts of Kfar Tebnit, raids on Nabatieh al-Fawqa, and shelling of the Ali al-Taher heights. Hezbollah fired at least 10 rockets at Israeli forces near Kfar Tebnit and detonated a drone that wounded four Israeli soldiers, with a fifth hurt minutes later. Iran charged that Israel had violated the Lebanon ceasefire 84 times in two days and warned Israel to expect 'a harsh response' if the attacks did not stop.

title: Katz: IDF will not withdraw from Lebanon, Syria or Gaza, calls Hezbollah truce 'temporary'
description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared on June 17 that the IDF would not pull back from the 'security zones' it holds in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza 'without any time limit,' directly rejecting the US-Iran framework's demand for an end to operations in Lebanon. 'We will not compromise on Israel's security interests and the protection of our citizens, and we will not withdraw from the security zones,' Katz said, calling the ceasefire with Hezbollah temporary and warning that 'if Iran attacks Israel because of events in Lebanon, we will strike it with full force.' Echoing Netanyahu, the statement underscored that Israel — not a party to the deal — intended to keep its forces and freedom of action even as Washington and Tehran finalized the agreement.

title: First Iranian crude leaves Hormuz, but only 7 ships transit; 550+ stranded as insurers hold off
description: The first tankers carrying Iranian crude departed through the Strait of Hormuz on June 17 since the US naval blockade began two months earlier, but overall traffic remained negligible. Shipping monitor MarineTraffic counted only seven vessels through the strait since the deal was announced, against a pre-war norm of 120-140 ships a day, with more than 550 vessels still stranded on either side. Major insurers and lines stayed cautious: the Norwegian Shipowners' Mutual War Risks Insurance Association said a return to pre-war levels would 'take months,' war-risk premiums still ran 2.5-5% of vessel value, and analysts estimated mine-clearance verification alone would take about two months. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed Iran had 'mined large segments of Hormuz.' Experts projected roughly four months before shipping normalizes.

title: Iran threatens 'harsh response' over Lebanon as US says Hezbollah not covered by deal
description: Iran's military command warned on June 16 of a 'harsh response' if Israel continued its offensive in southern Lebanon, insisting the US-Iran framework requires Israel to halt operations on 'all fronts, including Lebanon.' US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee directly contradicted Tehran, reiterating that Hezbollah is not a party to and is not covered by the memorandum of understanding. The clash exposed the central ambiguity in the deal set for signing June 19 in Geneva: Iran and mediators say Lebanon is included, while Washington and Israel treat the Hezbollah front as outside its scope. Trump separately urged Netanyahu to be 'more responsible with respect to Lebanon.'

title: Israel keeps striking south Lebanon; Kfar Tebnit car strike kills driver
description: Despite the US-Iran deal, Israeli operations in southern Lebanon continued on June 16. Lebanon's National News Agency reported an Israeli strike on a car in Kfar Tebnit that killed the driver, while Israeli forces struck the village of Deir Qanoun al-Nahr. The IDF said Hezbollah fired several rockets at Israeli troops during the day and that soldiers fired warning shots and then a strike on a suspicious vehicle in an area where they were operating. The fighting eased from earlier in the week but did not stop, underscoring that the Hezbollah front remained active even as Washington and Tehran prepared to sign.

title: Vance, US officials deny Iran will get billions in frozen assets, contradicting Tehran
description: A public dispute broke out over the financial terms of the US-Iran deal. Iranian media (Mehr) and the Revolutionary Guard claimed the 14-point memorandum releases up to $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets during the 60-day negotiation, with $12 billion available before talks begin. Vice President JD Vance flatly denied it: 'When people say that billions of dollars of assets will be released, that's not true,' adding the $24 billion figure 'just doesn't appear anywhere in any of the texts.' A senior US official told Axios the Iranian account was 'spin,' calling it 'a pay-for-performance deal' under which 'no frozen funds will be released without the Iranians implementing their commitments.' The contradiction signaled the two sides still disagreed on core terms days before the scheduled June 19 signing.

title: Israeli opposition revolts over Iran deal, calls it 'worst agreement ever'
description: Israeli politicians across the spectrum turned on Netanyahu over the US-Iran deal, which much of Israel sees as a strategic defeat. Former PM Ehud Barak said 'Israel is paying the price of Netanyahu's hubris and blindness,' arguing Iran emerged stronger and Israel weaker. Opposition leader Yair Lapid called it 'one of the most shocking failures in Israel's foreign and security policy.' Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir urged Netanyahu not to compromise on dismantling Hezbollah, while Yair Golan blasted the agreement for funneling billions to Iran while leaving its nuclear infrastructure and ballistic threat intact. Netanyahu, who staked his standing on his bond with Trump, said only that 'as long as I am the prime minister of Israel,' Iran will not get a nuclear weapon.

title: Iran hangs 2 men tied to January unrest; 56 prisons launch hunger strike
description: Iran executed two men, Javad Zamani and Abolfazl Saedi, described by authorities as 'armed leaders' of the January 2026 nationwide unrest, fueling fears of a widening crackdown. The same day, prisoners in 56 facilities launched a hunger strike for the 125th week of the 'Tuesdays No to Executions' campaign, with organizers reporting more than 177 executions since the Iranian year began on March 21. Rights groups warned of imminent risk for additional death-row inmates transferred to Ghezel Hesar prison. The surge in judicial killings tracked with the regime's effort to suppress popular anger amid the war and economic collapse.

title: Netanyahu vows Israeli troops will hold south Lebanon buffer zone, defying deal
description: At a June 15 press conference, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israeli forces would remain in the roughly 570 square kilometers (220 square miles) of southern Lebanon they occupy 'for as long as necessary,' and would keep striking Hezbollah and 'Iran's terror arms.' The position directly contradicts the US-Iran framework's call for an 'immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon.' Netanyahu, whose government is not party to the deal, cast the war as an Israeli victory: 'Iran will never have nuclear weapons, not today and not tomorrow... We beheaded the leaders of the terror regime.' Israeli troops now hold ground beyond the Litani River, past the declared end point of Israel's self-proclaimed security zone.

title: US says Trump, Vance and Iran's Ghalibaf 'digitally' signed war-ending deal
description: The White House and Vice President JD Vance disclosed on June 15 that President Trump, Vance and Iran's parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf had 'digitally' signed the war-ending agreement the previous day, Sunday June 14, committing to lift the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, reopen the Strait of Hormuz and begin 60 days of nuclear negotiations. Vance said the deal was 'signed digitally yesterday' and guaranteed 'Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.' A formal signing ceremony remained scheduled for Friday, June 19, in Geneva, Switzerland, mediated by Pakistan and Qatar, with Trump indicating he would not attend and that Vance would represent the US. Trump separately claimed the Strait of Hormuz was already 'partially opened.'

title: Hormuz 'reopened' on paper but ships stay put; oil sinks to $83, US stocks hit records
description: Although Trump declared the Strait of Hormuz reopened, most vessels stayed put on June 15 as major war-risk insurers — including Skuld — kept Gulf coverage suspended and shipping body BIMCO said lines needed proof that mine-free routes existed before returning. Analysts estimated transits could take weeks to reach even 50% of pre-war levels. Markets nonetheless rallied on the deal: Brent crude fell 4.8% to $83.17 and WTI dropped 4% to $81.46 — their lowest since early March — while the Dow rose 469 points to a record 51,671, the S&P 500 gained 1.7% to 7,554 and the Nasdaq surged 3.1%. One analyst cautioned that even an immediate reopening 'will not prevent inflation from rising a bit further in the near term.'

title: Trump calls Netanyahu 'very difficult guy,' threatens to resume Iran strikes if no nuclear deal
description: In a June 15 New York Times interview, President Trump said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is 'a very difficult guy' who 'should be very thankful to us for doing this,' and warned that if Iran fails to reach a final nuclear accord he will either restart US military attacks on Tehran or make the United States 'the guardian of the Middle East' in exchange for 20% of the region's revenues. The remarks followed Trump's rebuke of Netanyahu over Israel's June 14 strike on Beirut's Dahiyeh, which Trump said nearly derailed the US-Iran memorandum of understanding aimed at ending the war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and launching 60 days of nuclear talks. Netanyahu reiterated that Israel is not a party to the deal but praised Trump's 'commitment' to denying Iran nuclear weapons.

title: Trump declares US-Iran deal 'complete'; blockade lifted, Hormuz to reopen, signing June 19
description: President Trump announced on June 14 — his 80th birthday — that 'the Deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete. Ships of the World, start your engines. Let the oil flow!' and authorized the US Navy to lift its blockade and reopen the Strait of Hormuz toll-free. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, a lead mediator alongside Qatar, said both sides had 'declared the immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon.' Under the memorandum of understanding — to be formally signed Friday, June 19, in Switzerland — Iran reaffirms a commitment to abstain from producing nuclear weapons and the parties begin 60 days of nuclear negotiations. Iran said implementation would not begin until the signing. VP JD Vance said the deal ensures 'Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.'

title: Israel strikes Beirut's Dahiyeh and Nabatieh as deal nears; 6 killed, 29 towns ordered evacuated
description: Hours before Trump declared the US-Iran deal complete, Israel struck a five-story building in Beirut's Dahiyeh suburb, killing at least 3 and wounding 7, and hit towns in the Nabatieh district including Deir al-Zahrani and Kafr Reman, where at least 3 more were killed. The IDF ordered the immediate evacuation of 29 locations — 25 in Nabatieh district and four in Sidon district — directing residents north of the Zahrani River, and said it was responding to three Hezbollah projectiles fired at northern Israel. An Iranian military official warned the strikes 'will not go unanswered,' and UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned them. Trump publicly told Netanyahu 'Let's not blow it!' and, per Fox News, privately demanded 'What the f— are you doing?', calling the Hezbollah attack 'very small and meaningless.'

title: Brent oil falls below $87 as world leaders welcome US-Iran deal; Europe signals sanctions relief
description: Brent crude fell more than 4% to below $86.50 a barrel on June 14 — its lowest since early March and roughly 20% off the 2026 peak — as markets priced in the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. World leaders welcomed the US-Iran agreement, with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer calling it a 'hugely important step forward in ending the war, ensuring regional stability and re-opening the Strait of Hormuz,' and several European nations and Japan signaling readiness to lift sanctions on Tehran in exchange for nuclear curbs. Analysts cautioned that even with a deal, clearing Hormuz mines, evacuating trapped tankers and restarting damaged production would take 'weeks to months,' with full normalization stretching into 2027.

title: Trump says US-Iran deal signs Sunday; IRGC disputes timing
description: President Trump posted on June 13 that the US-Iran peace deal was 'scheduled to get signed tomorrow, and immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL.' Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said Islamabad was preparing an electronic signing on Sunday, June 14, with a ceremony discussed for Geneva and VP JD Vance, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner expected for the US side. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps denied any Sunday signing and criticized Trump's 'unusual insistence' on the date, while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Strait of Hormuz 'service fees' remained under negotiation. Hardline protesters in Tehran questioned whether Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei — who succeeded his father Ali Khamenei, killed on the war's first day — had endorsed the talks, noting his public silence.

title: Israeli officials say US-Iran MOU 'endangers Israel's security'
description: Senior Israeli officials, quoted in Hebrew media as Netanyahu prepared to convene his security cabinet on the evening of June 13, warned that the emerging US-Iran memorandum of understanding 'endanger[s] Israel's security interests' and showed Washington had agreed to Tehran's 'main conditions' while surrendering US military leverage. They said the deal left nuclear, missile and other key issues unresolved and would deliver 'the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, the resuscitation of the regime, and a slap in the face for the Iranian public.' Israel played no direct role in the negotiations; Trump separately assured Netanyahu that any final agreement would address Iran's nuclear program, ballistic missiles and support for Hezbollah.

title: Israel strikes 70+ Hezbollah targets in 24 hours; commanders killed
description: Israel struck more than 70 Hezbollah targets across southern Lebanon in 24 hours around June 13, with air raids reported in Nabatieh city, Kfar Jouz, Blat in the Marjayoun district and the western Bekaa Valley. The military said it had killed over 10 Hezbollah field commanders in recent days as its 36th Division pressed an offensive around Nabatieh. The intensified campaign continued even as the US-brokered framework envisioned an immediate ceasefire 'across all fronts including Lebanon' — a truce Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem has rejected.

title: 78 Nobel laureates demand UN action as Iran executions accelerate
description: Seventy-eight Nobel laureates issued a joint appeal to UN Secretary-General António Guterres in mid-June demanding immediate intervention to halt Iran's accelerating wave of political executions. Amnesty International reported that at least 78 protesters and dissidents were under sentence of death and at risk of execution, including 41 people detained over the January 2026 uprising. The Iran Human Rights Society has documented at least 784 executions in 2026, which it called the highest level of political executions in 37 years, carried out under wartime internet blackouts that obscure the crackdown's scale. The US State Department condemned the surge.

title: Pakistan PM says US and Iran agree 'final text' of war-ending deal; Trump cancels strikes
description: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced on June 12 that the US and Iran had reached 'a final, agreed upon text' of a deal to end the war, saying Islamabad was 'working closely with both sides to finalize the next steps.' President Trump confirmed he had called off planned strikes on Iran, citing the breakthrough. Reported terms include a 15-20 year freeze on Iranian uranium enrichment with stockpiles destroyed on-site and removed from the country, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping, the release of $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets, and a 60-day ceasefire across all fronts including Lebanon. Iran cautioned that no 'final conclusion' had yet been reached.

title: IDF prepares Nabatieh offensive; troops reach Arnoun as Hezbollah drone wounds soldier
description: The IDF signaled it was poised to launch a ground offensive against Hezbollah in Nabatieh, a major southern Lebanese stronghold, with its 36th Division pushing deeper in recent days to operate on the outskirts of Arnoun, a village a few kilometers away. A soldier was moderately wounded by a Hezbollah drone. Separately, a Hezbollah drone struck a military zone in northern Israel, causing no injuries. The advance came even as the emerging US-brokered deal envisioned a 60-day ceasefire 'across all fronts including Lebanon,' a truce Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem has rejected.

title: IAEA Board finds Iran non-compliant; verification halted since Feb 28
description: At its June Board of Governors meeting in Vienna, the IAEA reported that Iran has refused all verification activities since February 28, 2026, when the war began, and for nearly a year has denied inspectors information about or access to its four uranium enrichment facilities and associated stockpiles. A joint 'Quad' statement by the US, UK, France and Germany noted Iran remains the only non-nuclear-weapon state to have produced and accumulated uranium enriched to 60%. The findings deepened a non-compliance determination first reached by the Board the previous year and undercut Trump's claim that the war was nearly settled.

title: Trump touts 'great settlement' MOU to end war; Iran says no final deal
description: President Trump announced on June 11 that the US and Iran had reached a 'very strong memorandum of understanding,' declaring 'We just made a great settlement of the war with Iran' and saying a signing could happen 'maybe in Europe' as early as the weekend, attended by VP JD Vance. Trump said the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz would be lifted as part of the deal and canceled further planned strikes. Tehran disputed his characterization, stating it 'has not reached a final decision regarding any agreement' and that 'US actions are affecting the diplomatic process.' Netanyahu, whose government is not party to the accord, sought assurances on removing Iran's enriched uranium and limiting its missiles.

title: Iran declares Hormuz closed, claims warship hit; US downs 2 drones
description: Iran's military command declared the Strait of Hormuz closed following the US strikes and threatened to attack any vessel attempting to pass, also claiming it had struck a US warship — a claim US Central Command denied. US forces shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones targeting commercial ships in the strait. Physical transit through the waterway had already collapsed, with PortWatch recording just 2 transits on June 7 against a pre-crisis baseline of 94 per day, leaving hundreds of commercial ships and roughly 20,000 seafarers stranded in the Persian Gulf.

title: US strike on tanker MT Settebello kills 3 Indian sailors in Hormuz
description: A US missile strike on the Palau-flagged oil tanker MT Settebello near the Strait of Hormuz on June 11 killed three Indian seafarers, part of what Washington called 'blockade enforcement operations' against vessels accused of violating its ban on Iranian oil exports. Of 24 Indian crew aboard, 21 were rescued; the dead were named as deck cadet Aditya Sharma, engine fitter Shivanand Chaurasia and chief engineer Patnala Suresh. India lodged formal protests and summoned US diplomats. UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned the deterioration could trigger 'a full resumption of the conflict, with unpredictable consequences for the region,' and the IMO said the strike was the 14th seafarer death among 46 verified attacks on shipping in the strait since the war began on February 28.

title: US strikes Iranian air defenses; Trump threatens to seize oil sector, Kharg Island
description: US Central Command launched a second day of strikes on June 10 targeting Iran's 'military surveillance capabilities, communication systems and air defense sites,' with explosions reported in Tehran, the port city of Bandar Abbas and other southern areas along the Strait of Hormuz. Trump posted that the US would be 'HITTING IRAN VERY HARD TONIGHT' and threatened to 'assume total control' of Iran's oil and gas industries, including Kharg Island, in the 'not too distant future.' The same day, US inflation data showed the fastest price rises in three years, above 4%.

title: US Apache downed in Hormuz by Iranian drone; crew rescued by sea drone
description: A US Army AH-64 Apache helicopter patrolling over the Strait of Hormuz off Oman's coast was brought down after a collision with an Iranian Shahed one-way attack drone. Its two crew members were rescued by a surface sea drone — the first such rescue ever carried out by the US military — within about two hours. Trump said Iran shot down the aircraft and that the US 'must, of necessity, respond to this attack,' and Central Command announced it had begun retaliatory strikes against Iran.

title: Israel strikes Mahshahr petrochemical complex; Hezbollah mounts 16 attacks
description: Israel struck the Mahshahr petrochemical complex in southwestern Iran on June 9, with Iranian media reporting no casualties as damage assessment continued. In southern Lebanon, Hezbollah conducted 16 operations against Israeli forces the same day using drones, guided missiles, artillery and loitering munitions against troop gatherings and military vehicles near Beaufort Castle, Odaisseh and Yohmor al-Shaqif. Trump publicly warned Netanyahu to be 'careful' or risk finding himself 'on your own very soon.'

title: Iran executes uprising protester; 2026 execution toll passes 780
description: Iran's judiciary executed Fathollah Avari, 42, arrested during the January 2026 uprising in Malard southwest of Tehran, days after hanging two men labeled as protest leaders, Mehrdad Mohammadinia and Ashkan Maleki. The Iran Human Rights Society documented at least 784 executions in 2026, a figure it said reflected a rapidly accelerating trend since March and the highest level of political executions in 37 years, carried out under wartime internet blackouts that obscure the scale of the crackdown.

title: Iran and Israel halt strikes after ~30 missiles; Trump warns Netanyahu
description: Iran and Israel paused tit-for-tat attacks on June 8 after Iran launched roughly 30 ballistic missiles since the night of June 7 — the first exchanged strikes since the ceasefire that began April 8. Iran announced a conditional halt, warning it would resume 'much more severe' and 'crushing' attacks if Israel carried out further 'aggression and hostility, including in Lebanon.' Israel said it had carried out 'an extensive strike against strategic defence systems' in Iran, and Trump pressed Netanyahu to stop, warning continued strikes risked leaving Israel 'on your own very soon.'

title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Ramat David airbase as 'warning'
description: Hours after the Beirut strike, Iran launched multiple rounds of ballistic missiles at Israel's Ramat David airbase at around 10pm local time on June 7. The Israeli army said it intercepted all the missiles and reported no damage, though sirens sounded across Israel. The IRGC called the operation 'a warning,' adding that 'if the aggressions are repeated, the responses will be broader.' Trump downplayed the attack, saying 'the Iranian strikes didn't hurt anybody. Hopefully, Israel is not going to retaliate.'

title: Israel strikes Beirut's Dahiyeh, killing 2; Iran calls it 'red line'
description: Israel struck the Dahiyeh, Beirut's densely populated southern suburbs, on the afternoon of June 7, killing at least 2 people and wounding 11. Netanyahu and Defence Minister Katz said the strike hit a Hezbollah command centre. Iran said the attack on the Lebanese capital 'crossed all red lines,' having repeatedly warned it would intervene if Israel targeted Beirut, and made an end to Israeli operations in Lebanon a condition of any ceasefire with Washington.

title: Israel and Lebanon agree conditional ceasefire; Hezbollah's Qassem rejects it
description: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a US-brokered conditional ceasefire on June 3-4 aimed at extending the truce across all of Lebanon, but Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected it, calling the deal 'a roadmap to annihilate part of the Lebanese people.' Qassem demanded a full withdrawal of Israeli forces from southern Lebanon and pledged to continue attacks as long as Israeli troops occupied parts of the country. The collapse of the deal set the stage for the renewed Israel-Iran escalation days later. The war in Lebanon had by then killed more than 3,500 people and displaced over a million.

title: Qatar joins mediation as Pakistan army chief Munir arrives in Tehran
description: A Qatari delegation held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on May 22, but Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stressed that Pakistan 'remains the main mediator' between Washington and Tehran. The same day, Pakistan's powerful army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Tehran to meet Iranian officials as part of mediation efforts to extend the ceasefire and conclude a war-ending memorandum. Qatar's role was described as secondary to Islamabad's, which has been the public face of shuttle diplomacy since the conflict began.

title: US and Iran deadlock over enriched uranium handover and Hormuz tolls
description: US and Iranian negotiators signaled progress toward a deal but remained at odds over two core issues on May 22: the disposal of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile and Iran's demand to impose tolls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran warned that the US demand to hand over its enriched uranium would 'kill the deal.' The proposed framework would have Iran reach an agreement to dispose of its stockpile, reopen the Strait, and enter time-limited nuclear talks, but the mechanism for removing the uranium remained unresolved.

title: Rubio sees 'good signs' on deal but warns Hormuz control makes it 'unfeasible'
description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on May 21 there were 'good signs' that an agreement to end the war was in sight, but warned any deal would be 'unfeasible' if Iran pursued measures to permanently control shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Rubio reiterated President Trump's criteria: stopping Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, reopening the Strait without tolls, and turning over enriched uranium. He said there was 'a pretty solid thing on the table' regarding Iran reopening the Strait and entering 'a real significant time limited negotiation on nuclear matters.'

title: Amnesty warns 78 prisoners face execution; Iran hangs 2 more
description: Amnesty International reported on May 21 that at least 78 protesters and political prisoners sentenced to death are at risk of execution in Iran, including 41 people arrested in connection with the January 2026 protests. The same day, Iran's judiciary announced the execution of two men, Ramin Zaleh and Karim Maroufpour, on charges of 'membership in separatist groups.' Amnesty said political executions have surged to levels not seen since the 1980s, with at least 40 prisoners — including 19 protesters — hanged on politically-motivated charges so far in 2026 amid wartime internet blackouts that obscure the scale of the crackdown.

title: Hezbollah drone strike critically wounds IDF combat photographer, 6 soldiers
description: A Hezbollah drone attack critically injured an Israeli combat photographer from the IDF's Operational Documentation Division along with six other soldiers — three moderately and three slightly wounded — during fighting in southern Lebanon on May 21. The strike continued a sustained Hezbollah drone campaign against Israeli forces operating inside Lebanon despite the 45-day ceasefire extension agreed in Washington on May 15.

title: Hezbollah drone critically wounds IDF brigade commander near Haddatha
description: A Hezbollah drone attack near Haddatha in southern Lebanon on May 20 critically wounded the commander of the IDF's 401st Armored Brigade, a colonel, and slightly-to-moderately wounded a lieutenant colonel. Hezbollah said it engaged an Israeli force of tanks and infantry in the area. The Lebanese health ministry reported 31 people killed in Israeli attacks over the previous 24 hours, pushing the war's death toll to 3,073.

title: NATO chiefs meet on Iran war arsenal depletion; US pulls 5,000 troops from Europe
description: NATO military chiefs from all 32 member states met at NATO HQ in Brussels on May 20, led by Supreme Allied Commander Europe Gen. Alexus Grynkewich and Secretary General Mark Rutte, to address weapons stockpile depletion caused by the Iran war. The Pentagon has spent over $29 billion on the conflict, and allies warned that Patriot interceptors and other top-grade weapons systems are being consumed faster than they can be produced. A senior NATO military source said: 'We need a lot of resources and munitions and the ability to ramp up production quickly.' Grynkewich separately confirmed the US is withdrawing 5,000 troops from Europe — canceling a 4,000+ armored brigade combat team deployment to Poland and a long-range fires battalion — and said Europe should 'absolutely' expect further reductions. The withdrawals followed German Chancellor Merz's public criticism of the US handling of the Iran war.

title: Putin and Xi hold Beijing summit, plan ~40 cooperation deals
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 19-20 for Putin's 25th visit to China, days after Trump's own Beijing summit with Xi. The two leaders signed a joint declaration on 'the formation of a multipolar world and a new type of international relations' — a 47-page document — and planned approximately 40 cooperation agreements covering industry, transport, and nuclear energy. The Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline (2,600 km, 40 billion cubic meters/year capacity) remained stalled over pricing despite a September 2025 memorandum. China has purchased over $367 billion in Russian fossil fuels since the Iran war began. Russia-China bilateral trade has roughly doubled in five years to approximately $245 billion, mostly conducted in rubles and yuan. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the leaders would discuss the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

title: Iran's Araghchi warns of 'many more surprises' if war resumes
description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on May 20 that 'a return to war will feature many more surprises,' claiming Tehran gained significant military knowledge during the 40-day conflict. The statement came one day after Trump gave Iran 'two or three days' to reach a deal and VP Vance said both sides had made 'a lot of progress.' Araghchi's warning was interpreted as signaling that Iran had studied US and Israeli tactics during Operation Epic Fury and adapted its capabilities accordingly, including possible new weapons systems or strategies not yet revealed. The comment followed Iran's formal rejection of the US 5-point proposal two days earlier and came amid Trump's publicly stated deadline of 'Friday, Saturday, Sunday' for a new Iranian proposal.

title: Vance warns Iran: strikes are 'option B,' deal deadline in days
description: Vice President JD Vance, standing in for Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt (on maternity leave), told reporters at a White House briefing on May 19: 'We think that we've made a lot of progress. We're in a pretty good spot here, but there's an option B' — meaning the restart of military operations. Vance added: 'It takes two to tango. We're locked and loaded. We don't want to go down that pathway, but the president is willing and able to go down that pathway if we have to.' He said he had just spoken to Trump, who stressed Iran can never have a nuclear weapon. Separately, Trump told reporters Iran had been given 'two or three days' to produce a deal: 'Maybe Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Something maybe early next week — a limited period of time.' Asked whether Russia might take possession of Iran's enriched uranium, Vance said it was 'not currently the plan.'

title: Israeli strikes kill 19 in southern Lebanon including 3 children
description: Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon on May 19 killed at least 19 people, including 4 women and 3 children, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. Ten were killed in Deir Qanoun al-Nahr in Tyre province — including 3 children and 3 women — when a house was destroyed. Four were killed and 10 wounded in Nabatieh, and 5 were killed in nearby Kfar Sir including one woman. The IDF said it targeted more than 25 Hezbollah infrastructure sites between Monday and Tuesday. Separately, IDF Major Itamar Sapir, 27, deputy company commander in Battalion 7008 and a reservist from Eli, was killed in an exchange of fire when a Hezbollah operative opened fire from inside a church in the village of Qouza. Sapir, who left behind a wife and 18-month-old son, was the 21st IDF soldier killed in Lebanon since March 2 and the 8th since the April 17 ceasefire. The cumulative Lebanese death toll reached 3,042.

title: Trump cancels planned Iran strike at Gulf allies' request
description: President Trump announced on Truth Social on May 19 that he was canceling a military attack on Iran scheduled for Tuesday, writing 'I have been asked by the Emir of Qatar...to hold off on our planned Military attack of the Islamic Republic of Iran.' Trump said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE believe 'a Deal will be made' and that 'serious negotiations are now taking place,' insisting on 'NO NUCLEAR WEAPONS FOR IRAN' as a condition. The cancellation came one day after Iran formally rejected the US 5-point proposal and hours before a Situation Room meeting on renewed military options that Trump had convened with Vance, Rubio, Hegseth, and Ratcliffe. Iran's President Pezeshkian responded that 'dialogue does not mean surrender.' Qatar's foreign ministry said negotiations 'need more time.'

title: Israel seizes 39 boats from Gaza-bound flotilla off Cyprus
description: Israel's navy intercepted and seized approximately 39 boats from the 54-vessel Global Sumud Flotilla — the largest civilian flotilla in support of Palestinians — 250 nautical miles from Gaza in waters near Cyprus. The flotilla carried 426 people from 39 countries and had departed from the Turkish port of Marmaris. Unlike previous interceptions, Israeli forces boarded in daylight, detaining approximately 100 activists including Margaret Connolly, a doctor and sister of Irish President Catherine Connolly. Israeli media reported detainees were transferred to a 'floating prison' before transport to Ashdod for interrogation. Turkey's Foreign Ministry condemned the operation as 'an act of piracy,' and President Erdogan called on the international community to act against what he termed an attack on 'voyagers of hope.'

title: NYT: Israel built 2 covert military bases in Iraq's desert for Iran war
description: The New York Times reported on May 18 that Israel built two covert military outposts in Iraq's Najaf desert near Karbala, approximately 100 km southwest of Baghdad, to support air operations against Iran. The installations housed special forces and served as a logistical hub for the Israeli air force, including search-and-rescue teams for downed pilots. Israel began preparing one site in late 2024. Baghdad privately lodged a formal complaint with Washington in late March after a Bedouin shepherd was killed in early March upon stumbling on one installation and reporting soldiers, helicopters, and tents around a landing strip. Iraq's deputy commander Qais al-Muhammadawi stated: 'There is no agreement or consent for any force to be present in this location.' American officials claimed Washington was not involved in the operation.

title: Lebanon war death toll passes 3,000; 9,273 wounded since March 2
description: Lebanon's health ministry reported on May 18 that the cumulative death toll from the Israel-Hezbollah war surpassed 3,000, reaching 3,020 killed — including 292 women and 211 children — with 9,273 wounded since fighting began March 2. Over one million people have been displaced. On the Israeli side, 20 soldiers, 2 civilians, 1 defense contractor, and 6 UN peacekeepers have been killed. The milestone was reached despite a ceasefire in effect since April 17 and extended into June, with Israeli strikes continuing daily across southern Lebanon. Planned direct military-to-military talks between Israel and Lebanon are set for May 29 at the Pentagon.

title: Iran judiciary confirms 39 wartime executions including 10 for espionage
description: Iran's judiciary, via its official Mizan News Agency, reported on May 18 that 39 people have been executed since the war began on February 28 — 10 on charges of spying for 'Mossad and the CIA' and 29 as 'ringleaders of espionage, terrorism, and armed riots.' The judiciary also reported lengthy prison sentences for dozens more and widespread property confiscations. IranWire reported the actual number of political executions exceeds the official figures, noting that state media 'frequently record incorrect execution dates.' Human rights organizations said the pace of sentencing and executions has surged since the ceasefire, with the regime using wartime emergency to accelerate elimination of domestic opponents from the 2025-2026 protest movement.

title: Iran rejects US 5-point proposal as 'surrender,' demands reparations
description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei announced on May 18 that Tehran had formally responded to the latest US peace proposal, rejecting it as tantamount to 'surrender.' Iranian state television reported that the US five-point plan demanded Iran keep only one nuclear site operational, transfer its entire stockpile of 60%-enriched uranium to the US, and accept 12 years of zero enrichment — while refusing to release 'even 25 percent' of Iran's frozen assets or pay any war reparations. Iran insisted on full sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, the lifting of all sanctions, release of frozen assets, and reparations for what Baqaei called an 'illegal and baseless' war. The exchange was conducted through Pakistani mediators. Trump responded on Truth Social: 'For Iran, the Clock is Ticking, and they better get moving, FAST,' warning 'there won't be anything left of them.'

title: Trump convenes NSC on renewed Iran military options for May 19
description: Axios reported on May 17 that President Trump will convene a Situation Room meeting on Tuesday, May 19, to discuss renewed military options against Iran after peace negotiations deadlocked. Vice President Vance, Secretary of State Rubio, Defense Secretary Hegseth, CIA Director Ratcliffe, Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Caine, and envoy Steve Witkoff are expected to attend. Trump had already met national security officials at his Virginia golf club on Saturday and spoke by phone with Israeli PM Netanyahu on Sunday. The meeting comes after Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal as 'totally unacceptable' and described the ceasefire as 'on life support.' Brent crude rose 1.3% to $110.70/barrel on the escalation signals.

title: IRGC threatens to 'deactivate' all US Gulf bases, claims total Hormuz blockade
description: IRGC spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari declared on May 17 that 'all U.S. military bases in the southern Persian Gulf will be deactivated' in the near future and claimed the IRGC Navy had achieved a total blockade: 'In the past 24 hours, the IRGC Navy did not allow any vessel to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.' The threat came hours after a drone struck the perimeter of the UAE's Barakah nuclear plant and Saudi Arabia intercepted three drones from Iraqi airspace. US forces had by this point diverted 81 commercial vessels and disabled 4 as part of the American counter-blockade of Iranian ports. The dueling blockades — Iran's closure of Hormuz and the US interdiction of Iranian-bound traffic — continued to paralyze Gulf shipping with roughly 1,550 vessels and 22,500 mariners stranded.

title: Israeli strikes kill 7 in Lebanon including 2 children
description: Israeli airstrikes across Lebanon on May 18 killed at least 7 people, including Islamic Jihad commander Wael Abdel Halim and his 17-year-old daughter in a strike on the outskirts of Baalbek in eastern Lebanon, and 2 children in the south. Three were killed in Tayr Felsay including a child, and 2 in Tayr Debba including another child, with 15 wounded across four towns. Two strikes also hit Sohmor in the eastern Bekaa Valley. The UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher condemned 'over 100 strikes on Lebanon in 24 hours' across the weekend, reporting 87 people killed in the May 17-18 period — the deadliest weekend since the April 17 ceasefire. WHO recorded 158 attacks on healthcare facilities since March 2, with 3 hospitals and 41 primary healthcare centers forced to close. The $308 million humanitarian appeal for Lebanon remained only 40% funded.

title: Hezbollah launches drone swarm at Ya'ara barracks in northern Israel
description: Hezbollah announced on May 17 that it struck the Ya'ara barracks in northern Israel 'with a swarm of attack drones,' marking the first time the group targeted a named Israeli military installation with a coordinated multi-drone attack. Hezbollah also claimed more than a dozen additional operations against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon the same day, including attacks on troops in the town of Khiam. The IDF said it intercepted several drones before they crossed the border. Hezbollah framed the attacks as retaliation for Israeli ceasefire violations and condemned the Lebanon-Israel Washington negotiations as 'free concessions' to the enemy.

title: Israel strikes 24+ villages across southern Lebanon day after ceasefire extension
description: Israel launched airstrikes on more than two dozen villages across southern Lebanon on May 17, one day after the 45-day ceasefire extension was announced. Strikes hit targets up to 50 kilometers from the border, with evacuation warnings issued to 9 villages including areas near Tyre. One IDF soldier was killed in combat in southern Lebanon, bringing total Israeli military deaths in Lebanon to 21 since the war began March 2. Lebanese authorities reported over 400 people killed since the ceasefire took effect on April 17, with the cumulative war toll exceeding 2,900. The Lebanese negotiating delegation called the ceasefire extension 'critical breathing space,' while displaced residents reported a new exodus toward Sidon and Beirut.

title: Saudi Arabia intercepts 3 drones launched from Iraqi airspace
description: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry announced on May 18 that it intercepted and destroyed three drones that entered Saudi airspace from Iraq on the morning of May 17. Spokesperson Major General Turki Al-Maliki stated the kingdom 'reserves the right to respond at the appropriate time and place' and pledged 'all necessary operational measures' to protect sovereignty. No group claimed responsibility, though Iran-aligned militias in Iraq have previously launched drones at Gulf states. The incident followed an April 12 protest by the Saudi Foreign Ministry to Iraq's ambassador over similar drone launches. It came on the same day a drone struck the UAE's Barakah nuclear plant, underscoring a pattern of aerial threats to Gulf states from Iraqi and western border airspace.

title: Drone strikes Barakah nuclear plant perimeter in Abu Dhabi
description: A drone struck an electrical generator on the perimeter of the UAE's $20 billion Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant in Al Dhafra, Abu Dhabi, on May 17, sparking a fire that was quickly contained. The Abu Dhabi Media Office said no injuries were reported and there was 'no impact on radiological safety levels,' with the Federal Authority for Nuclear Regulation confirming all four reactor units continued operating normally. No group claimed responsibility, though suspicion fell on Iran. Barakah — built with South Korean assistance and operational since 2020 — is the only nuclear power plant on the Arabian Peninsula and supplies roughly 25% of UAE electricity. The strike marked the first time the plant has been targeted in the war, raising international alarm about the targeting of civilian nuclear infrastructure.

title: Israel Q1 GDP contracts 3.3% annualized as war hits consumer spending
description: Israel's Central Bureau of Statistics reported on May 17 that GDP contracted at an annualized rate of 3.3% in Q1 2026 — less severe than the 4% decline forecast by economists but the sharpest contraction since the Gaza war's impact in late 2023. Consumer spending fell 4.7%, exports declined 3.7%, and government spending dropped 4.8%, while per capita GDP shrank 4.5%. Investment in fixed assets rose 12.6%, indicating continued defense and infrastructure spending. The contraction followed weeks of Iranian ballistic missile fire that closed schools and disrupted businesses after the war began February 28. The Bank of Israel projects 3.8% growth for full-year 2026, contingent on the ceasefire holding.

title: USS Gerald R. Ford returns to Norfolk after record 326-day deployment
description: The USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, returned to Naval Station Norfolk on May 16 after 326 days at sea — the longest U.S. carrier deployment since the Vietnam War. Approximately 5,000 sailors disembarked after an 11-month mission that included combat operations supporting the Iran war and the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth attended the homecoming ceremony. During the deployment, the Ford's air wing flew thousands of sorties over the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea. The carrier also endured a noncombat fire that left hundreds of crew without sleeping quarters, requiring emergency repairs on the Greek island of Crete.

title: Iran announces Hormuz toll mechanism, bars US-escorted vessels
description: Ebrahim Azizi, head of Iran's parliamentary national security committee, announced on May 16 that Iran has prepared a 'professional mechanism to manage traffic' through the Strait of Hormuz, to be unveiled soon, with designated commercial routes and fees collected for 'specialized services.' Only commercial vessels and parties cooperating with Iran will be permitted; the route remains 'closed to the operators of the so-called freedom project' — the U.S. military escort operation. Iran has already collected revenue from tolls imposed on the waterway and recently permitted passage for dozens of vessels from China, Japan, and Pakistan under its protocols. Iranian state television separately reported that European countries have begun negotiations with the IRGC Navy for transit permission. As of May 16, 78 commercial ships had been redirected from the strait, with 4 disabled.

title: IDF Capt. Recanati killed in Lebanon; Israel strikes 100 Hezbollah targets
description: Captain Maoz Israel Recanati, 24, a platoon commander in the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion from Itamar, was killed in combat in southern Lebanon on May 16, posthumously promoted from lieutenant. He was the 18th IDF soldier killed in Lebanon since the ground operation began. The IDF reported striking approximately 100 Hezbollah targets over the weekend, including observation posts, weapons storage facilities, and terror infrastructure. Hezbollah fired explosive drones, mortar shells, and rockets at Israeli forces, with projectiles landing in open areas causing no IDF injuries. The Israeli Air Force intercepted several rockets and struck two Hezbollah operatives near a launch site, triggering secondary explosions that indicated weapons in the building. Lebanon's health ministry put the total death toll at 2,969 killed and 9,112 wounded since March 2.

title: Trump warns Iran of 'very bad time,' sends nuclear proposal
description: President Trump on May 16 warned Iran would face a 'very bad time' if it did not reach a deal soon, while simultaneously sending Tehran a nuclear proposal demanding swift progress to avoid 'serious consequences.' Khamenei advisor Ali Shamkhani responded that Iran was ready to sign a nuclear deal in exchange for the quick removal of all financial sanctions, but criticized Trump's rhetoric: 'He speaks of an olive branch, but we see only barbed wire.' Iranian officials separately denied receiving a new U.S. proposal and insisted they would not abandon their right to enrich uranium. The exchange came as Iran held nuclear talks with the E3 (UK, France, Germany) and the EU's Kaja Kallas in Istanbul, with Araghchi warning that reinstating UN sanctions could lead to 'irreversible' consequences.

title: Israel finishes 2nd at Eurovision in Vienna amid 5-nation boycott
description: Israeli singer Noam Bettan finished second at the Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna on May 16 with 343 points for his trilingual (French, Hebrew, English) pop song 'Michelle,' behind Bulgaria's 'Bangaranga' at 516 points. Five countries — Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia, Spain, and Iceland — boycotted the 70th-anniversary contest over Israel's participation amid the Iran war and ongoing regional hostilities. Hundreds of protesters gathered outside the Wiener Stadthalle demanding Israel's exclusion. President Herzog called Bettan to say he 'brought honor' to Israel with a 'perfect' performance. The result — a wartime contestant finishing runner-up in Europe's largest cultural event — underscored the deepening split between governments that continued engaging Israel and those that sought to isolate it.

title: Israel and Lebanon extend ceasefire by 45 days after Washington talks
description: The US State Department announced on May 15 that Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire by 45 days after two 'productive' days of direct peace talks in Washington, with spokesman Tommy Pigott saying the extension would 'enable further progress.' Additional political negotiations will reconvene June 2-3, with a US-facilitated security track commencing May 29 at the Pentagon. The previous ceasefire — brokered April 17, extended by Trump on April 23 and again on May 7 — was due to expire May 18. Despite the extension, Lebanon's health ministry reported at least 657 people killed by Israeli attacks since the original ceasefire began on April 17. Hezbollah had demanded Lebanon cancel the Washington talks, calling them treason.

title: Israeli strikes wound 37 near Tyre including 6 hospital staff
description: Israeli airstrikes on the Tyre district of southern Lebanon on May 15 wounded at least 37 people — including 6 hospital personnel, 9 women, and 4 children — Lebanon's health ministry reported. At least two strikes hit locations near Tyre city, while a third targeted a center run by a local NGO near Hiram Hospital, injuring 7 people including 2 nurses. The IDF said it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in the Tyre area following evacuation warnings. The attacks came hours after the announcement of a 45-day ceasefire extension and while Israeli and Lebanese envoys concluded a second day of peace talks in Washington, underscoring the pattern of escalation on the ground even as diplomacy advances.

title: Trump warns Iran of 'annihilation,' posts decimation 'to be continued'
description: President Trump told Fox News's Sean Hannity on May 15 that he is 'not going to be much more patient' with Iran and that its leaders 'can make a deal, or they get annihilated,' adding 'any sane person would make a deal, but they might be crazy.' Trump separately posted on Truth Social counting 'the military decimation of Iran' among his accomplishments and adding 'to be continued!' Oil prices rose on the statements. The threats came hours after Trump announced his agreement with Xi Jinping that Iran must never have nuclear weapons, signaling the administration is pursuing maximum diplomatic and military pressure simultaneously.

title: IDF Chief Zamir's secret wartime visit to UAE disclosed
description: Israeli media disclosed on May 15 that IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir secretly visited Abu Dhabi during Operation Roaring Lion, accompanied by a US delegation, to 'strengthen cooperation across various scenarios in a war with Iran, including both defensive and offensive operations.' Security sources described the coordination as 'exceptional strategic cooperation' enabled by the Abraham Accords. The disclosure followed earlier revelations that Mossad Director David Barnea, Shin Bet Director David Zini, and PM Netanyahu himself all visited the UAE during the war, confirming Israel and the UAE operated as de facto military allies throughout the conflict.

title: Report: UAE failed to persuade Saudi Arabia and Qatar to jointly attack Iran
description: The Times of Israel reported on May 15 that UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed called Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and other Gulf leaders early in the war to argue for a collective military campaign against Iran, but all counterparts refused. The Trump administration was aware of the effort and wanted Saudi Arabia and Qatar to join. Saudi Arabia struck Iran in March but quickly pivoted to supporting Pakistani-led diplomacy. Qatar considered retaliating after Iran hit its Ras Laffan LNG plant but opted against it. The failed coordination attempt helps explain the UAE's subsequent solo actions, including its Lavan Island strike and May 1 withdrawal from OPEC.

title: Iran and UAE clash at BRICS foreign ministers meeting in New Delhi
description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the UAE of 'direct involvement in the aggression against my country' during a two-day BRICS foreign ministers meeting in New Delhi on May 14, marking a rare direct confrontation between the two nations at a multilateral forum. Araghchi called on BRICS members to 'explicitly condemn violations of international law by the United States and Israel,' characterizing Iran as 'a victim of illegal expansionism and warmongering.' Iran's Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi said 'one member country' — widely understood to be the UAE — pushed for language condemning Iran, complicating consensus. India's FM Jaishankar condemned an attack on an Indian-flagged vessel off Oman as 'unacceptable.' No joint statement was issued.

title: GCC interior ministers hold emergency meeting after Kuwait IRGC infiltration
description: GCC interior ministers convened an emergency session at the GCC secretariat in Riyadh on May 14, chaired by Bahraini Interior Minister Rashid bin Abdullah Al Khalifa, following the attempted IRGC infiltration of Kuwait's Bubiyan Island on May 13. GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi declared 'the security of the GCC states is indivisible' and ministers stressed closer cooperation among security authorities. Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, and Bahrain all condemned the infiltration as a violation of Kuwaiti sovereignty. Iran denied the allegations, claiming the four arrested nationals made an 'accidental navigation error.' Two additional alleged operatives escaped during gunfire; one Kuwaiti serviceman was wounded.

title: Trump and Xi agree Iran must never have nuclear weapons; Xi pledges no arms
description: President Trump announced on May 15 that he and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during their Beijing summit that Iran 'can never have a nuclear weapon.' Trump said Xi pledged China would not provide military equipment or weapons to Iran — though US intelligence has assessed China may have already sent shoulder-mounted missiles to Tehran. Secretary of State Rubio told reporters the US and China agreed the Strait of Hormuz should not be 'militarized,' and Trump said Xi offered to help negotiate an end to the Iran war and reopen the strait. No formal written agreement was produced. Xi also agreed to purchase 200 Boeing jets and to work on stopping fentanyl precursor flows to the US.

title: IDF kills 40+ Hezbollah fighters in south Lebanon; Israeli soldier killed by mortar
description: The IDF's 36th Division killed more than 40 Hezbollah operatives and struck approximately 75 targets in southern Lebanon on May 15, including three fighters operating a rocket launcher. The Israeli Air Force intercepted a suspicious aerial target over southern Lebanon in the early hours. Separately, Staff Sgt. Negev Dagan, 20, was killed by a Hezbollah mortar shell in southern Lebanon — the 17th IDF soldier killed in Lebanon since the ground operation began. Hezbollah claimed attacks on Israeli positions at Ras al-Naqoura, a Merkava tank in Taybeh, and a Humvee in Tayr Harfa. The operations came as the third round of Israel-Lebanon peace talks concluded a second day at the State Department, with a US official calling them 'productive and positive.'

title: CENTCOM commander tells Senate Epic Fury 'rolled back 40 years' of Iran's military
description: Admiral Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander, testified before the Senate Armed Services Committee on May 14 that Operation Epic Fury conducted 10,200+ sorties and 13,500+ strikes over 38 days, destroying 161 Iranian vessels across 16 warship classes, 90% of Iran's 8,000+ naval mines, and 85% of its ballistic missile, drone, and naval industrial base. US forces intercepted 6,000+ attack drones and 1,500+ ballistic missiles. Cooper said Iran's daily air sorties dropped from 30-100 to zero and 82% of its air defense systems were destroyed. He stated 14 US servicemen were killed in the operation. Cooper disputed the New York Times report that Iran retained 70% of its missile capacity, calling open-source numbers 'not accurate,' but acknowledged Iran retains 'nuisance capability' including fast-boat harassment and isolated strikes. He confirmed the military's investigation into the strike on an Iranian girls' school that killed approximately 150 people remains ongoing.

title: Israel's Katz warns military operations against Iran may resume soon
description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared on May 14 that 'the military operation against Iran has not been completed and may be resumed in the near future,' stressing the need to ensure Iran no longer poses an existential threat to Israel or the United States. MK Nissim Vaturi said Israel is 'closer than ever' to returning to fighting in Iran. The warnings came as US-Iran negotiations remained deadlocked over Tehran's demands for Hormuz sovereignty recognition and sanctions relief. Separately, Al Hadath reported that Trump may order the resumption of military strikes on Iran immediately upon returning from China, and that Israeli leadership had been notified of this possibility.

title: US April CPI surges to 3.8% as war drives energy prices up 17.9% annually
description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on May 12 that the Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% month-on-month in April and 3.8% year-over-year — the highest annual rate since May 2023. Core CPI excluding food and energy rose 0.4% monthly and 2.8% annually, with the monthly rate the highest since January 2025. Energy prices jumped 3.8% for the month and 17.9% year-over-year, accounting for more than 40% of the headline increase. Food prices climbed 0.5% monthly and 3.2% annually. The report followed the April PPI data showing wholesale prices surging 6.0% annually, confirming the Iran war's energy shock is driving a broad-based inflation acceleration that is complicating the Federal Reserve's rate-cutting plans.

title: Vessel seized off Fujairah, directed toward Iranian waters
description: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on May 14 that a vessel at anchor was seized by 'unauthorized personnel' approximately 38 nautical miles northeast of Fujairah at 0545 GMT and directed toward Iranian waters. The ship's identity was not disclosed and no group claimed responsibility. Maritime intelligence firm Windward AI tracked 342 active Iranian fast-attack boats across five monitored zones of the Strait of Hormuz on May 14, down from 454 on May 13, using 'swarm-style formations' and 'escort-like behavior.' All large-hull commercial vessels in the strait remained stationary, with a total halt in traffic. Iran has laid claim to expanded 'sovereignty' rights in and around the strait under a newly redrawn map of Iranian waters that appears to cover the area where the vessel was seized.

title: Hezbollah drone strikes Rosh Hanikra, injuring 3 Israeli civilians
description: An explosive drone launched by Hezbollah struck a parking area near Rosh Hanikra on the Israel-Lebanon border at 09:02 GMT on May 14, injuring 3 Israeli civilians — 2 seriously and 1 lightly. No warning sirens sounded, indicating the drone evaded Israeli air defense detection systems. The IDF called the attack 'a blatant violation of the ceasefire understandings by the terrorist organization Hezbollah.' Israel launched retaliatory strikes on Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon. The attack came on the same day as the opening of a third round of US-brokered Israel-Lebanon peace talks in Washington.

title: Iran's World Cup squad given public sendoff in Tehran amid war
description: Thousands gathered in Tehran's Enqelab Square on May 13-14 for a public sendoff of Iran's national football team ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States — the host nation currently at war with Iran. Football Federation president Mehdi Taj called it 'the best sendoff in the last four World Cup campaigns.' Iran is drawn in Group G against New Zealand, Belgium, and Egypt, opening June 15 in Los Angeles. The team will train in Turkey before traveling to the US, but visa complications remain unresolved: an IRGC-affiliated delegation was previously turned back at Toronto's airport, and FIFA has been asked to guarantee entry for all team staff. Iran demanded guarantees for its flag, anthem, and security at stadiums.

title: Trump and Xi hold formal summit at Great Hall of the People in Beijing
description: President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a formal summit on May 14 at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, with a military honor guard, brass band playing The Star-Spangled Banner, and schoolchildren waving flags. Xi told Trump: 'A stable bilateral relationship is good for the world. We should be partners, not rivals.' Trump called Xi a 'great leader' and predicted 'a fantastic future together.' The US delegation included Secretary of State Rubio, Treasury Secretary Bessent, Defense Secretary Hegseth, and CEOs Elon Musk (Tesla), Jensen Huang (Nvidia), and Tim Cook (Apple). Discussions covered trade, rare earth elements, semiconductors, Taiwan, and the Iran war — with Trump pressing Xi to use China's leverage as Iran's largest oil buyer to push Tehran toward a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. No concrete agreements were announced.

title: 51 GOP senators and 177 House Republicans demand zero Iran enrichment
description: Fifty-one Republican senators — every GOP senator except Rand Paul — and 177 House Republicans (80% of the caucus) sent a letter to President Trump on May 14 demanding that any deal with Iran require the 'total dismantlement' of its uranium enrichment capability. 'The scope and breadth of Iran's nuclear buildout have made it impossible to verify any new deal that allows Iran to continue enriching uranium,' the letter stated. Led by Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jim Risch and Sen. Pete Ricketts, the letter responded to mixed signals from the administration after Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff briefly suggested 3.67% enrichment might be acceptable before reversing course. Iran holds approximately 400 kg of uranium enriched to 60%, and the IAEA assesses it could reach weapons-grade 90% within one to two weeks.

title: Israel-Lebanon third round of peace talks opens in Washington
description: Israel and Lebanon opened a third round of US-facilitated peace talks at the State Department on May 14, with sessions scheduled through May 15. Lebanon's delegation is led by former Ambassador Simon Karam, accompanied by Ambassador Nada Mouawad and Military Attaché Oliver Hakmeh. Israel's delegation is led by Strategic Affairs Minister Ron Dermer, with Ambassador Yehiel Leiter. The talks aim to advance a comprehensive agreement covering full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon, border delineation, prisoner exchanges, the return of displaced residents, and reconstruction. The round builds on the April 23 session chaired by President Trump, who announced a three-week ceasefire extension. Hezbollah demanded Lebanon cancel the talks, calling them treason.

title: Netanyahu reveals secret March 26 wartime visit to UAE; Abu Dhabi denies
description: Israeli PM Netanyahu's office disclosed on May 13 that he secretly visited the UAE on March 26, meeting President Mohammed bin Zayed in Al-Ain for several hours while US-Israeli strikes on Iran were underway. MBZ 'personally drove the PM in his personal car from the plane to the palace,' according to former PMO spokesperson Ziv Agmon. Netanyahu's office called it a 'historic breakthrough in relations.' Mossad Chief David Barnea and Shin Bet Chief David Zini also made separate visits to the UAE during the war to coordinate on Iranian threats. The UAE Foreign Ministry denied the claims, stating: 'Any claims regarding unannounced visits or undisclosed arrangements are entirely unfounded.' The disclosure came one day after Huckabee confirmed Israel deployed Iron Dome batteries to the UAE. The UAE conducted strikes on Iran's Lavan Island refinery in early April.

title: Pentagon considers 'Operation Sledgehammer' if Iran ceasefire collapses
description: NBC News reported on May 13 that the Pentagon is considering renaming the Iran war 'Operation Sledgehammer' if the ceasefire collapses, replacing the current 'Operation Epic Fury' designation that was formally ended on May 5. US officials said the name change could allow the Trump administration to argue it restarts the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock requiring congressional authorization — a legal maneuver to avoid seeking a formal vote. Trump told reporters the ceasefire has a '1% chance of living.' Operation Sledgehammer is not the only name under consideration. The discussions underscore how seriously the administration is weighing a resumption of major combat operations against Iran.

title: Israeli drone strikes kill 8 including 2 children on highway south of Beirut
description: Israeli drone strikes hit vehicles on the main coastal highway linking Beirut to southern Lebanon in the Jiyeh area, approximately 20 km south of Beirut, on May 13, killing at least 15 people including 2 children in three separate strikes. Vehicles were described as 'severely damaged, their exteriors charred and torn apart.' The IDF simultaneously issued forced displacement orders for six southern Lebanese villages, warning residents to evacuate at least 1,000 meters. The strikes came one day before a third round of US-brokered Lebanon-Israel direct talks in Washington. Lebanon's health ministry said at least 380 people have been killed since the April 17 ceasefire, with the total death toll surpassing 2,800 since March 2.

title: Trump departs for Beijing; tells reporters Iran war 'will not be long'
description: President Trump departed Washington for Beijing on May 13 for a state visit and summit with President Xi Jinping, his first trip to China since 2017. Trump told reporters he would have a 'long talk' on Iran with Xi but downplayed the need for Beijing's help, saying 'we have Iran very much under control.' He predicted the war's end would trigger sharp drops in oil prices and inflation, noting hundreds of oil tankers were waiting to leave the region. Trump also said 'I don't think about Americans' financial situation' when asked about the war's economic toll. The summit agenda includes trade, Taiwan, AI, and the Iran war, with formal meetings scheduled for May 15-16.

title: Hegseth tells Congress Iran war has cost at least $29 billion in 74 days
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told lawmakers on May 13 that the Iran war has cost the US at least $29 billion in munitions and equipment over 74 days, excluding damage to US bases from Iranian attacks. The figure exceeded the $25 billion estimate the Pentagon provided to Congress two weeks earlier. A Harvard Kennedy School expert estimated in April the total cost could reach $1 trillion. Hegseth stated that military escalation remains an option if diplomacy fails.

title: US intel: Iran retains 70% of mobile launchers, restored 30 of 33 Hormuz missile sites
description: The New York Times reported on May 13 that classified US intelligence assessments show Iran retains approximately 70% of its mobile missile launchers and pre-war missile stockpiles despite 39 days of US-Israeli airstrikes. Iran has also restored access to 30 of 33 missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz, undermining US claims of having degraded Iran's military capability by 90%. The assessment raises questions about whether a resumption of strikes could meaningfully change Iran's military posture.

title: Kuwait arrests 4 IRGC members attempting to infiltrate Bubiyan Island
description: Kuwaiti security forces arrested four alleged IRGC members attempting to infiltrate Bubiyan Island, Kuwait's largest island near the Iraqi border, by sea on May 13. A Kuwaiti soldier was injured during the operation. The incident marked the first reported Iranian ground infiltration attempt against a Gulf state during the conflict, escalating beyond the missile and drone attacks that have characterized Iran's campaign against Gulf states since February.

title: IEA: Global oil stocks down 250 million barrels; 14 mb/d shut in from Gulf
description: The International Energy Agency published its May Oil Market Report on May 13, warning that global oil stockpiles fell by 250 million barrels over March and April combined — a drawdown rate of 4 million barrels per day. More than 14 mb/d of Gulf oil production is now shut in, with cumulative supply losses of 12.8 mb/d since February. The IEA projected world oil demand would contract by 420,000 b/d year-on-year in 2026 to 104 mb/d, with the steepest drops in petrochemicals and aviation. North Sea Dated crude averaged $120.36/bbl in April with a nearly $50/bbl intra-month range. The market remains in deficit through Q4 2026 unless the Strait of Hormuz reopens.

title: UAE designates 21 Hezbollah-linked individuals and entities as terrorists
description: The UAE Cabinet approved Resolution No. 63 of 2026 on May 13, designating 16 Lebanese nationals and 5 Lebanon-based organizations on its Local Terrorist List over links to Hezbollah. All UAE regulatory authorities were ordered to freeze assets of those listed within 24 hours. In March, Abu Dhabi had arrested five members of a 'terrorist network' linked to Hezbollah and Iran allegedly targeting UAE financial stability. The designation followed months of Iranian missile and drone attacks on the UAE — totaling 551 ballistic missiles, 29 cruise missiles, and 2,263 UAVs intercepted since the war began.

title: Senate rejects 7th war powers resolution in closest vote yet, 49-50
description: The Senate rejected a seventh Democratic attempt to limit Trump's Iran war powers on May 13, with a motion to discharge the resolution from committee failing 49-50 — the closest vote yet. Three Republicans broke ranks: Rand Paul, Susan Collins, and Lisa Murkowski, who voted for the first time to advance the measure, saying 'We're in a different place than we were last time we voted on this.' Sen. John Fetterman was the sole Democrat to oppose. The resolution, led by Sen. Jeff Merkley, would have required Trump to 'remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran' unless Congress declared war. Sen. Jim Risch countered: 'The hostilities ended with the April 7 ceasefire. They're over — full stop.' Sen. Tim Kaine predicted: 'There will be a day, and it might be soon, where this Senate will say to the president, stop this war.'

title: Iran executes alleged Mossad spy Ehsan Afreshteh, 6th since war began
description: Iran executed Ehsan Afreshteh, 32, on May 13 on charges of 'espionage and intelligence cooperation in favor of Israel,' making him the sixth person executed on espionage charges since the war began. According to Iranian court documents, Afreshteh was recruited by Mossad in Turkey, trained in Nepal, and systematically funneled intelligence from Iranian military and cyber institutions to Israel. Iran Human Rights reported he was subjected to forced confessions, prolonged solitary confinement, and denial of access to a lawyer of his choosing. Iran also executed Mohammad Abbasi on May 13 for killing a police officer during January 2026 protests.

title: US wholesale prices surge 6% YoY in April, highest since Dec 2022
description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on May 13 that the US Producer Price Index rose 1.4% month-on-month in April — nearly triple the 0.5% Dow Jones consensus forecast — and 6.0% year-on-year, the highest annual increase since December 2022. Goods prices jumped 2.0%, led by a 15.6% surge in gasoline, with more than three-quarters of the broad-based increase traced to a 7.8% jump in final demand energy prices driven by the Iran war's disruption of Gulf oil flows. Services rose 1.2%, the largest monthly gain since March 2022, with two-thirds attributed to a 2.7% rise in trade services as tariff costs widened.

title: Iranian MP threatens 90% weapons-grade uranium enrichment if US resumes strikes
description: Ebrahim Rezaei, Iranian MP for Dashtestan and spokesperson for parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, posted on X on May 12 that Iran could enrich uranium to weapons-grade 90% if the US resumes military strikes, saying the option would be discussed in parliament. Iran holds approximately 400 kg of uranium enriched to 60% — enough for roughly 10 nuclear weapons if further enriched. The IAEA has assessed Iran could reach weapons-grade material within one to two weeks. The threat represented the most explicit nuclear escalation signal from an Iranian official since the ceasefire began on April 8.

title: Trump calls Iran proposal 'garbage,' aides say he mulls resuming combat
description: President Trump escalated his rejection of Iran's counter-proposal on May 12, calling it 'a piece of garbage' he 'didn't even finish reading' and declaring the ceasefire 'on massive life support.' CNN reported that Trump aides said he is 'more seriously considering a resumption of major combat operations' than at any point since the ceasefire began. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf responded that the US has 'no alternative but to accept' Tehran's 14-point proposal. The diplomatic impasse came one day before Trump's departure for Beijing, where he plans to press Xi Jinping on Iran. A regional source told CNN the talks are unlikely to advance until after the Trump-Xi meeting.

title: Huckabee reveals Israel deployed Iron Dome batteries and personnel to UAE
description: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee publicly confirmed at a Tel Aviv University event on May 12 that Israel sent Iron Dome anti-missile batteries and personnel to the UAE to defend against Iranian attacks — the first time Israel has deployed its air defense system to another nation. 'Israel just sent them Iron Dome batteries and personnel to help operate them,' Huckabee said, attributing the cooperation to the 2020 Abraham Accords. The disclosure came after Iran fired over 550 ballistic missiles and 2,200 drones at the UAE during the war. The UAE maintained up to 17 daily flights to Israel when Western carriers withdrew. US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz had also referenced the deployment the previous evening.

title: IDF intercepts Houthi drone near Eilat; first attack on city since ceasefire
