description: The IDF intercepted a drone launched by Yemen's Houthis near Eilat on May 12, marking the first attack on the southern Israeli city since the Iran ceasefire took effect on April 8. The drone was shot down off the coast of Eilat. The IDF said no sirens sounded 'according to protocol' because the drone did not pose a threat to populated areas. The Houthis joined the war on March 28 by launching a ballistic missile at Israel and have continued sporadic attacks despite the ceasefire.

title: Israeli strikes kill 6, wound 7 in Kfar Dounine despite Lebanon ceasefire
description: Israeli strikes hit a house in Kfar Dounine, a town 95 km south of Beirut, on the night of May 12, killing 6 people and wounding 7, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The wounded were transported to hospitals in Tyre. Separately, the IDF issued evacuation orders for Sohmor in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley. The strike brought Lebanon's cumulative death toll to over 2,800 since March 2, with the April 17 ceasefire failing to halt Israeli operations. Israeli military losses in Lebanon stand at 18 soldiers and one civilian contractor.

title: Hezbollah fires surface-to-air missile at Israeli drone over Lebanon; IDF retaliates
description: Hezbollah fired a surface-to-air missile at an Israeli drone operating over southern Lebanon on May 12, in what the IDF said was a 'failed' launch that caused no damage or injuries. The Israeli Air Force subsequently struck a suspect fleeing the missile launch site on a motorcycle. Separately, Hezbollah claimed it conducted 20 military operations on May 11 against Israeli forces across eight areas in southern Lebanon — including Taybeh, Naqoura, and Adaisseh — using strike drones, artillery, and missiles. Hezbollah's media chief stated the group believes FPV drone casualties can force an Israeli withdrawal more effectively than negotiations.

title: UN warns Hormuz fertilizer blockade could push 45 million into hunger
description: Jorge Moreira da Silva, head of the UN task force on Hormuz humanitarian access, warned on May 12 that the strait's closure could force 45 million additional people into hunger and starvation. 'We have a few weeks ahead of us to prevent what will likely be a massive humanitarian crisis,' he told AFP in Paris. One-third of global fertilizer trade transits the Strait of Hormuz, and the blockade has halted virtually all shipments since March. The UN proposed a humanitarian corridor requiring just five vessels daily, which could be operational within seven days, but Moreira da Silva said the US, Iran, and Gulf states have shown insufficient 'political will.' Full normalization would take three to four months even if the strait reopened immediately.

title: US sanctions 12 entities for IRGC oil sales to China; offers $15M reward
description: The US Treasury sanctioned 12 individuals and entities — 3 IRGC officials from the Shahid Purja'fari Oil Headquarters, 4 Hong Kong-based companies, 4 UAE-based firms, and 1 Omani entity — for facilitating Iranian oil sales to China under 'Operation Economic Fury.' Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: 'Economic Fury will continue to deprive the regime of funding.' The State Department simultaneously offered up to $15 million for information disrupting IRGC financial networks. The sanctions targeted shell companies that arrange payment for Iran's oil allotments to China, which accounts for 80-90% of Tehran's oil exports. The announcement came one day before Trump's departure for a state visit to Beijing (May 13-15), where he plans to press Xi Jinping on Iran and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Trump proposes suspending 18.4-cent federal gas tax as prices hit $4.52
description: Trump told CBS News he wants to suspend the 18.4-cent-per-gallon federal gas tax 'for a period of time' as the national average hit $4.52 per gallon — up over 50% from $3.00 before the war. 'We're going to take off the gas tax for a period of time, and when gas goes down, we'll let it phase back in,' Trump said. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO) announced he would introduce legislation Monday to suspend the tax, and Rep. Anna Paulina Luna said she would file a companion House bill. The suspension would cost the federal government approximately $500 million per week and drain the Highway Trust Fund that finances road construction and transit. The diesel tax is 24.4 cents per gallon. Six states already have gas prices near or above $5, with California exceeding $6.

title: Lebanese president urges US envoy to pressure Israel on strikes and demolitions
description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met US Ambassador Michel Issa at Baabda Palace on May 11 and demanded Washington pressure Israel to 'halt fire and military operations and the destruction and bulldozing of homes' in southern Lebanon. Lebanon's health ministry reported 74 people killed by Israeli strikes in the preceding three days despite the April ceasefire, bringing the total to 2,869 killed since March 2. The IDF issued forced displacement warnings for 9 additional towns across Nabatieh (Rihan, Jarjou, Kfar Rumman, Nmairiyeh, Arabsalim, Harouf) and eastern Lebanon (Jmayjmeh, Mashghara, Qlayaa). Separately, a third round of Israeli-Lebanese ambassador-level talks was confirmed for May 14-15 in Washington, with Lebanon's delegation headed by former ambassador Simon Karam. Hezbollah demanded the government cancel the talks.

title: Oil surges 5% as markets react to collapse of US-Iran diplomacy
description: Oil prices surged nearly 5% on May 11 after Trump rejected Iran's counter-proposal as 'totally unacceptable.' Brent crude rose 4.3% to $105.70 per barrel and WTI jumped 4.96% to $100.20 — the first time WTI crossed $100 since the ceasefire rally. The spike reflected market fears that the diplomatic impasse would prolong the Strait of Hormuz disruption, which has removed approximately 21 million barrels per day from global markets. Oil prices are up roughly 45% since the war began on February 28. The Indian rupee also fell sharply, prompting the Reserve Bank of India to intervene in currency markets.

title: Modi urges 1.4 billion Indians to conserve fuel, work from home amid oil shock
description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, speaking at a BJP rally in Hyderabad on May 11, urged citizens to conserve fuel, postpone foreign travel for one year, delay gold purchases for one year, use public transport, carpool, and switch to electric vehicles. 'We got used to work-from-home, virtual meetings and video conferencing during Covid-19. The need of the hour is to bring back those methods,' Modi said. India imports 85% of its fuel and relies on the Strait of Hormuz for approximately 50% of its crude, 60% of LNG, and nearly all LPG supplies. UBS Securities cut India's FY2027 growth forecast from 6.7% to 6.2%. The appeal made India — the world's most populous nation and third-largest oil importer — the first major economy to publicly ask citizens to change daily behavior because of the war.

title: Iran FM spokesman calls US demands 'unreasonable,' defends counter-proposal
description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei responded to Trump's rejection on May 11 by calling Iran's counter-proposal 'generous and responsible' and accusing Washington of 'unreasonable and one-sided demands.' Baghaei said: 'Our demand is legitimate: demanding an end to the war, lifting the blockade and piracy, and releasing Iranian assets that have been unjustly frozen.' He cited the US withdrawal from the JCPOA in 2018 as evidence that 'the United States has repeatedly proven unreliable.' He added: 'Whenever we are forced to fight, we will fight and whenever there is room for diplomacy, we will seize that opportunity.' The statement hardened Iran's negotiating posture ahead of Trump's planned May 13-16 Middle East tour to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE.

title: Iran sends counter-proposal via Pakistan; Trump rejects it as 'totally unacceptable'
description: Iran transmitted its counter-proposal to the US peace plan through Pakistani mediators on May 10. Tehran demanded recognition of Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, war compensation, release of frozen assets, lifting of OFAC sanctions on oil sales within 30 days, end of the naval blockade, and cessation of hostilities on all fronts including Lebanon. The response notably omitted any mention of Iran's nuclear program — the US proposal's central demand. An Iranian official called the response 'realistic and positive.' Trump posted on Truth Social: 'I don't like it — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' and accused Iran of 'playing games with the United States, and the rest of the World, for 47 years.' Iranian state media framed the US proposal as demanding Iran's 'surrender to Trump's greed.'

title: Drone hits cargo ship in Qatari waters near Mesaieed Port
description: A drone struck a commercial cargo vessel traveling from Abu Dhabi in Qatari territorial waters northeast of Mesaieed Port on May 10, causing a limited fire with no casualties. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a bulk carrier hit approximately 23 nautical miles northeast of Doha. Qatar's Defense Ministry confirmed the strike and the foreign ministry 'strongly condemned' the attack. No group claimed responsibility. The strike came on the same day Kuwait intercepted drones targeting oil facilities and the UAE shot down 2 Iranian drones, extending the pattern of Gulf maritime attacks despite the month-old ceasefire.

title: Sen. Kelly reveals US expended 45% of precision missiles; Hegseth threatens probe
description: Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) said on CBS Face the Nation that Pentagon briefings revealed the US military had expended at least 45% of its Precision Strike Missiles and over 50% of THAAD interceptors as of April 21, calling the depletion 'shocking.' Kelly cited Tomahawks, ATACMS, SM-3, THAAD rounds, and Patriot interceptors, warning replenishment would take 'years' and leave the US 'less safe' for a potential conflict with China over Taiwan. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accused Kelly of 'blabbing on TV (falsely & dumbly) about a *CLASSIFIED* Pentagon briefing' and announced the Pentagon legal team would review whether Kelly 'violated his oath.' Kelly responded by posting video of a public hearing where Hegseth himself said replenishing stockpiles would take 'years.' CBS reported the war had cost at least $50 billion.

title: Israel strikes medic stations in Bint Jbeil; 552 killed since ceasefire
description: Israel struck two Health Authority medical stations in Qalawiya and Tibnin in the Bint Jbeil district on May 10, killing 2 paramedics. A separate strike on an ambulance post in Majdal Selem killed another medic and injured 2 more. The Lebanese Health Ministry said Israel 'directly targeted' the medical points and condemned the strikes as violations of 'international laws and humanitarian norms.' The UN reported at least 103 Lebanese medical workers killed and 230 injured in over 130 Israeli strikes since March 2. Lebanon's cumulative toll reached 2,846 killed and 1.2 million displaced, with 552 killed since the April 16 ceasefire alone. Civil defense chief Ali Safiuddin in Tyre said: 'We're under threat every second, every day... we know we've already given up our lives by working here.'

title: IRGC says missiles 'locked onto' US targets; threatens 'heavy assault'
description: Iran's IRGC issued its most explicit military threat of the ceasefire period on May 10. The IRGC Aerospace Force declared: 'IRGC Aerospace Force missiles and drones have locked onto American targets in the region and the enemy aggressor's ships. We are awaiting the order to fire.' The IRGC Navy Command warned: 'Any aggression against Iran's oil tankers and commercial vessels will result in a heavy assault against one of the American centres in the region and the enemy's ships.' Separately, Army spokesman Brigadier General Amir Akraminia warned that countries enforcing US sanctions 'will certainly face problems passing through the Strait of Hormuz.' The threats came after the US disabled two Iranian tankers on May 8 and as Washington awaited Tehran's formal response to the 14-point peace proposal.

title: Kuwait and UAE intercept Iranian drones targeting infrastructure
description: Kuwait's armed forces detected and intercepted hostile Iranian drones at dawn on May 10, with some targeting oil facilities, power stations, and water desalination plants, causing infrastructure damage. The UAE Defense Ministry separately reported intercepting 2 drones 'coming from Iran.' The attacks continued Iranian strikes on Gulf states despite the month-old ceasefire, following the May 8 attack that injured 3 in the UAE. Iran's cumulative fire against the UAE since the war began has included 551 ballistic missiles, 29 cruise missiles, and 2,263 UAVs intercepted.

title: Qatari LNG tanker transits Hormuz — first passage since war began
description: The Qatari LNG tanker Al Kharaitiyat sailed from Ras Laffan toward the Strait of Hormuz en route to Pakistan's Port Qasim, marking the first transit by a Qatari LNG vessel through the strait since the war began on February 28. Iran approved the shipment — a government-to-government gas sale from Qatar to Pakistan — as a confidence-building measure toward both Qatar and Pakistan, which is mediating the US-Iran peace talks. LSEG shipping data confirmed the vessel's course. QatarEnergy declined to comment. The transit came as relative calm prevailed around the strait after days of sporadic US-Iran clashes, and as Washington continued to await Tehran's formal response to the 14-point peace proposal.

title: Satellite images reveal 52 km² oil slick off Iran's Kharg Island
description: Satellite imagery from Copernicus Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Sentinel-3 satellites revealed an oil slick covering more than 52 square kilometers (20 square miles) off the west coast of Iran's Kharg Island, the country's primary oil export terminal handling 90% of exports. Orbital EOS told the New York Times that more than 3,000 barrels of oil may have been released. The cause remained unclear — Kharg has been struck multiple times by US and Israeli forces since March. Iran denied the spill. The Conflict and Environment Observatory said the slick was 'drifting south' and 'unlikely to be addressed appropriately' given wartime conditions.

title: Iran parliament security chief warns Hormuz could close 'forever'
description: Ebrahim Azizi, head of Iran's parliamentary national security commission, warned that the Strait of Hormuz could be permanently closed to countries supporting US-backed resolutions. 'We warn governments, including microstates like Bahrain, that siding with the U.S.-backed resolution will bring severe consequences. The Strait of Hormuz is a vital lifeline; do not risk closing it on yourselves FOREVER,' Azizi said. The threat escalated Iran's Hormuz rhetoric from temporary wartime closure to permanent exclusion, specifically targeting smaller Gulf states that have supported US diplomatic initiatives.

title: Hezbollah explosive drones wound 3 Israeli soldiers near Misgav Am
description: Hezbollah launched several explosive drones at Israeli soldiers operating near the Lebanese border on May 9, severely wounding one IDF reservist and moderately injuring a reservist officer and another soldier near Misgav Am. A separate drone struck the Shlomi helicopter landing pad, damaging an unmanned engineering vehicle without causing casualties. Hezbollah claimed it 'targeted a gathering of Israeli enemy army soldiers near Misgav Am' in response to 'the Israeli enemy's violation of the ceasefire.' The IDF Air Force intercepted several additional projectiles aimed at Israeli troops. In retaliation, the IDF struck over 85 Hezbollah infrastructure sites in 24 hours, including weapons storage facilities, launcher positions, and an underground weapons production facility in the Beqaa Valley.

title: Israeli drone strikes on highway south of Beirut kill 4
description: Three Israeli drone strikes on vehicles south of Beirut killed 4 people on May 9 — the first strikes this close to the Lebanese capital since the April 17 ceasefire. Two strikes hit the highway linking Beirut to Sidon, killing one person in the town of Saadiyat where an AP journalist confirmed a body on the road, while the third struck a road leading to Lebanon's Chouf region, killing three. The strikes expanded Israel's targeting beyond southern Lebanon into the greater Beirut commuter corridor. Separately, strikes across southern Lebanon killed at least 13 more, including 7 in Saksakiyeh (with a child), 3 in Bourj Rahhal, and a Syrian man with his 12-year-old daughter in Nabatiyeh. Lebanon's health ministry denounced the 'deliberate violence against civilians and children' as violations of international humanitarian law.

title: Rubio and Witkoff meet Qatari PM in Miami; Qatar joins Iran mediation
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and special envoy Steve Witkoff met Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani in Miami on May 9 to discuss Iran peace talks, according to Axios. The meeting came a day after Al Thani told al-Araby al-Jadeed there was a 'high probability' the US and Iran would reach a deal, and after he met Vice President JD Vance at the White House on May 8 to discuss LNG markets, regional stability, and the Iranian conflict. Qatar has been operating as a go-between alongside Pakistan's lead mediation role, though Doha has been reluctant to take a more prominent position for fear of blame if talks collapse. The diplomatic flurry came as Washington awaited Tehran's response to the 14-point MOU that would formally end the war before addressing Iran's nuclear program.

title: Trump threatens 'Project Freedom Plus' if Iran rejects deal
description: President Trump warned on the White House South Lawn that Washington may revive and expand the suspended Strait of Hormuz escort operation if Iran does not accept the US peace proposal. 'We may go back to Project Freedom if things don't happen... it would be Project Freedom Plus, meaning Project Freedom plus other things,' Trump said, without elaborating. He added: 'We'll go a different route if everything doesn't get signed up, buttoned up.' Pakistan, which is mediating the talks, asked the US not to resume the military operation. The threat came as Washington awaited Tehran's formal response to the 14-point MOU that would end the war before addressing Iran's nuclear program.

title: Rubio in Rome says US expects Iran peace deal response 'today'
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking to reporters in Rome during a visit to Pope Leo XIV, said the US expected Iran's response to the peace proposal on Friday. 'We're expecting a response from them,' Rubio said. 'We'll see what the response entails. The hope is it's something that can put us into a serious process in negotiation.' Iran's foreign ministry said it was still reviewing the proposal and would relay its response through Pakistani mediators. The statement came as sporadic clashes between Iranian and US forces continued in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran's Fars news agency reporting ongoing confrontations despite the ceasefire.

title: Israeli strikes kill 31 across southern Lebanon; paramedics hit
description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least 31 people across southern Lebanon on May 9 — one of the deadliest days since the March 2 invasion — including a civil defense rescue worker. In Toura (Tyre district), two airstrikes killed 5 and wounded 3, with rescue operations ongoing for a missing girl under rubble. Near Sheikh Ragheb Harb Hospital in Toul, a building was destroyed and 4 paramedics were injured. Strikes hit targets across Marjayoun, Hasbaya, Bint Jbeil, Nabatiyeh, Sidon, and Jezzine districts, targeting vehicles, motorcycles, and residential areas. Artillery shelling struck Mansouri and Buyout al-Sayyad. The IDF issued mass evacuation warnings for towns near Tyre including Tayr Debba, Al Abbasiyeh, Burj Rahhal, and Ain Baal. The IDF separately reported striking 85+ Hezbollah targets in 24 hours, including an underground weapons facility in the Beqaa Valley.

title: CIA assesses Iran can withstand US naval blockade for four months
description: A CIA analysis concluded Iran could endure the US naval blockade of its ports for approximately four months before facing severe economic pressure, according to a US official briefed on the assessment. The finding suggested US leverage over Tehran remained limited as both nations sought to resolve the conflict. A senior intelligence official disputed the conclusion, stating the blockade 'is inflicting real, compounding damage — severing trade, crushing revenue, and accelerating systemic economic collapse.' The assessment surfaced as sporadic clashes continued between Iranian and US forces in the Strait of Hormuz on May 9, and as the US awaited Iran's response to the peace proposal.

title: US schedules third round of Israel-Lebanon talks for May 14-15
description: The State Department announced the US will host a third round of Israel-Lebanon peace talks on May 14-15 in Washington, building on the April 23 round led by President Trump. Lebanon's delegation will be led by Simon Karam and Israel's by Ron Dermer. Discussions will focus on 'a framework for lasting peace and security arrangements, the full restoration of Lebanese sovereignty throughout its territory, the delineation of borders, and creating concrete pathways for humanitarian relief and reconstruction in Lebanon.' The announcement came as fighting in southern Lebanon continued unabated, with the IDF breaking through Hezbollah defenses in three sectors on May 8 — occupying Buyut al-Siyad, crossing the Litani River near Deir Sirian, and advancing toward Rishafah.

title: IRGC seizes Barbados-flagged tanker Ocean Koi in Gulf of Oman
description: Iran's IRGC Navy seized the Barbados-flagged oil tanker M/T Ocean Koi in the Gulf of Oman in what it called a 'special operation,' claiming the vessel had 'attempted to disrupt oil exports and the interests of the Iranian nation.' Press TV released video of Iranian forces boarding and detaining the ship. The seizure came hours after US-Iran clashes in the Strait of Hormuz and the same day the US disabled two more Iranian-flagged tankers (M/T Sea Star III and M/T Sevda) by firing precision munitions into their smokestacks — bringing to four the total vessels disabled enforcing the blockade. Bloomberg reported the Ocean Koi appeared to be carrying Iranian oil, suggesting Iran seized a vessel transporting its own crude.

title: US disables two more Iranian tankers; blockade traps 70+ vessels
description: US Navy forces disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers — M/T Sea Star III and M/T Sevda — by firing precision munitions into their smokestacks as they attempted to dock at Iranian ports in the Gulf of Oman on May 8, bringing the total vessels disabled to four since the blockade began. Admiral Bradley Cooper stated: 'US forces in the Middle East remain committed to full enforcement of the blockade of vessels entering or leaving Iran.' The blockade was now preventing 70+ tankers carrying 166+ million barrels worth an estimated $13 billion from entering or leaving Iranian ports. Over 20 warships, 200+ aircraft, and 15,000 troops were enforcing the interdiction. A total of 57 commercial vessels had been redirected since the blockade's April 12 start.

title: Iran fires 2 ballistic missiles and 3 drones at UAE; 3 injured
description: Iran launched 2 ballistic missiles and 3 drones at the United Arab Emirates on May 8, injuring 3 people. The attack brought Iran's cumulative fire against the UAE since the war began to 551 ballistic missiles, 29 cruise missiles, and 2,263 UAVs intercepted, with 230 total injuries. The strikes came hours after US forces struck Iranian military facilities at Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, and Bandar Kargan in response to Iranian attacks on US destroyers. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman accused the US of a 'reckless military adventure,' while IRGC officials claimed Iran's missile inventory stood at '120% of prewar levels' — contradicting US intelligence assessments that Iran had expended approximately 75% of its stockpile.

title: US sanctions 14 entities for supplying Iran's Shahed drone network
description: The US Treasury and State Department imposed sanctions on 14 entities across China, Hong Kong, Dubai, and Belarus for aiding Iran's military procurement and Shahed drone production. Treasury Secretary Bessent stated: 'The targeting of U.S. service members will not go unanswered.' The State Department separately sanctioned three Chinese firms — Meentropy Technology/MizarVision, The Earth Eye, and Chang Guang Satellite Technology — plus Iran's MINDEX defense export arm for providing satellite imagery and intelligence support to Iranian forces. One sanctioned firm, Pishgam Electronic Safeh Company, had procured thousands of servomotors found in downed Shahed-136 drones. The sanctions came days before Trump's planned visit to China to meet President Xi Jinping, and Treasury warned of potential secondary sanctions against Chinese 'teapot' oil refineries processing Iranian crude.

title: Iran rejects enrichment freeze; calls US deal proposal 'wish-list'
description: Iran signaled it would reject key terms of the US one-page peace proposal, with officials declaring nuclear enrichment 'non-negotiable' and refusing to transfer its 440kg stockpile of 60%-enriched uranium abroad. Lawmaker Ebrahim Rezaee called the proposal 'more of an American wish-list than a reality.' Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf mocked the negotiations on social media. Iran's foreign ministry said it was still reviewing the proposal and would convey its response to Pakistani mediators, but insisted on sequencing — war cessation and sanctions relief first, nuclear program second — rejecting the US demand to bundle both into a single MOU. The hardened stance contrasted sharply with Axios reports two days earlier that Iran was close to agreeing on enrichment terms.

title: Israeli strikes kill 12 across southern Lebanon; paramedic and child among dead
description: Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon killed at least 12 people and wounded dozens on May 8, with a paramedic and a child among the dead. The IDF also killed two Hezbollah operatives and three Palestinian Islamic Jihad members in separate targeted strikes. Since March 2, Israeli operations in Lebanon have killed more than 2,700 people, displaced over 1.2 million, and established a six-mile-plus buffer zone in the south that Israel says it will hold 'indefinitely.' Hezbollah's attack rate has more than doubled its 2024 peak frequency, with a veteran special forces officer telling the Christian Science Monitor the militia 'has more [weapons] now than before' due to weapons transfers from Syria.

title: Israeli strikes kill 11 in Nabatiyeh; UN calls Beirut attack 'alarming'
description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least 11 people across three towns in Lebanon's Nabatiyeh district — Doueir, Harouf, and Habboush — on May 7. In Habboush, the Lebanese health ministry confirmed 8 killed including one child and two women, with 21 wounded. The strikes came hours after the IDF killed Radwan Force commander Balout in Beirut's Dahieh. UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric called the Beirut strike 'a very alarming development,' adding the UN was 'deeply worried about reports of civilians being killed, including children.' Over 126,000 displaced Lebanese remain sheltered in 600+ collective facilities. Five UNIFIL peacekeepers have been killed since fighting resumed March 2.

title: Iran attacks 3 US destroyers in Hormuz; US strikes 3 Iranian ports
description: Iranian forces launched missiles, drones, and fast-attack boats at three US Navy destroyers — USS Truxtun, USS Mason, and USS Rafael Peralta — as they transited the Strait of Hormuz on May 7, in the second Iranian barrage against US warships in three days. US forces responded with five-inch naval guns, CIWS, .50-caliber fire, and Apache helicopters firing Hellfire missiles. CENTCOM then struck Iranian military facilities at three ports — Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, and Bandar Kargan — targeting missile and drone launch sites, command and control locations, and ISR nodes. CENTCOM stated 'no US assets were struck' and called the Iranian attacks 'unprovoked.' Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya headquarters claimed the US had violated the ceasefire by targeting an Iranian tanker in Iranian waters, and said its response caused 'significant damage' to US ships. Trump called the exchange a 'love tap' and insisted the ceasefire remained in effect, adding: 'Just like we knocked them out again today, we'll knock them out a lot harder, and a lot more violently, in the future, if they don't get their Deal signed, FAST!'

title: Rubio meets Pope Leo XIV at Vatican amid Trump-papacy rift over Iran war
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican for over 45 minutes on May 7 — the first meeting between a Trump administration official and the pontiff in nearly a year. The two discussed the Iran war, Lebanon, and conflicts in Africa. The State Department said the meeting 'underscored the strong relationship between the United States and the Holy See and their shared commitment to promoting peace and human dignity.' The meeting followed weeks of extraordinary public tension between Trump and the first North American pope, who had condemned the 'delusion of omnipotence' fueling the war. Rubio dismissed the notion he was attempting to reset relations, but Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni described the discussion as covering 'areas of disagreement.'

title: WaPo: Satellite images show Iran damaged 228 structures at 15 US bases
description: A Washington Post investigation published May 6-7, using satellite imagery verified via EU Copernicus and Planet Labs data, revealed Iranian strikes had damaged or destroyed at least 228 structures and pieces of equipment across 15 US military sites in the Gulf — far exceeding Pentagon disclosures. The heaviest damage was at Naval Support Activity Bahrain (5th Fleet HQ), Ali al-Salem Air Base, Camp Arifjan, and Camp Buehring in Kuwait. Imagery showed a destroyed E-3 Sentry AWACS aircraft, damage to Patriot and THAAD air-defense positions, collapsed hangars, destroyed fuel depots, and strikes on radar and communications systems at al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar. The investigation confirmed 7 US service members killed (6 in Kuwait, 1 in Saudi Arabia) and over 400 troops injured, with at least 12 suffering serious injuries.

title: Rep. Barrett introduces AUMF capping Iran operations at July 30
description: Republican Rep. Tom Barrett of Michigan introduced the 2026 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iran on May 7, granting President Trump congressional authority to 'demolish, degrade or defeat' Iran's nuclear weapons program, enforce the blockade, and ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz — but with a hard expiration of July 30, 2026 with a 30-day wind-down period. The bill prohibits occupying or seizing Iranian territory. Barrett noted the War Powers Resolution's 60-day clock expired on May 1, after which the Trump administration told Congress the 'use of military force had concluded' — despite ongoing military operations including the May 7 Hormuz strikes. The bill represented the first Republican attempt to reassert congressional war powers since the conflict began February 28.

title: Israel kills Radwan Force commander in first Beirut strike since ceasefire
description: Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs (Dahieh) on the evening of May 6 — the first strike on the Lebanese capital since the April 17 ceasefire — killing Hezbollah Radwan Force commander Ahmed Ali Balout. The IDF said Balout 'commanded dozens of terror attacks against IDF soldiers operating in Southern Lebanon, including anti-tank missile attacks and the detonation of explosive devices,' and led efforts to rebuild the Radwan Force and its 'Conquer the Galilee' plan to infiltrate northern Israel. The strike was ordered by PM Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz. Lebanon's health ministry reported at least 11 others killed in strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon on the same day. Approximately 25,000 residents in Galilee communities sought bomb shelters after a UAV was launched toward Israeli territory.

title: US Super Hornet disables Iranian tanker M/T Hasna enforcing naval blockade
description: A US Navy F/A-18E Super Hornet from USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) fired 20mm cannon rounds at the Iranian-flagged tanker M/T Hasna, disabling its rudder after the vessel refused to comply with repeated warnings while transiting toward an Iranian port in the Gulf of Oman. CENTCOM stated the blockade — established April 12 — 'remains in full effect' and that 52 commercial vessels had been instructed to reverse course or return to port. The M/T Hasna was unladen at the time. The incident marked the first time US forces fired on a commercial vessel to enforce the blockade. Approximately 15,000 US service members are deployed enforcing the interdiction across Navy warships, Army helicopters, and Air Force fighters.

title: France sends Charles de Gaulle carrier through Suez toward Hormuz
description: France's nuclear-powered aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle and its escort vessels transited the Suez Canal on May 6, repositioning from a two-month eastern Mediterranean deployment to the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. The carrier's air wing includes 20 Rafale jets, two E-2C Hawkeye early warning aircraft, and three helicopters. France's defense ministry said the move was to 'prepare for a future mission to restore free navigation in the Strait of Hormuz,' part of a UK-French multinational initiative with over 40 nations pledging support — separate from the US-led Project Freedom. France emphasized the deployment was defensive and distinct from US military operations in the region.

title: Netanyahu convenes security cabinet; demands all enriched uranium leave Iran
description: PM Netanyahu convened Israel's Diplomatic-Security Cabinet on May 6 and issued a rare public statement pushing back on reports that Israel was caught off guard by the US-Iran negotiations. 'I speak with President Trump almost daily. My people and his people speak daily,' Netanyahu said. He set Israel's red line for any deal: 'The most important goal is to remove the enriched material from Iran, all the enriched material, and to dismantle Iran's enrichment capabilities.' Netanyahu added that Trump 'believes he can achieve this one way or another' and instructed the IDF and security agencies to 'be prepared for any scenario' — including a return to fighting if the deal fails to meet Israeli demands.

title: Trump threatens 'much higher level' bombing if Iran rejects deal
description: President Trump posted on Truth Social: 'Assuming Iran agrees to give what has been agreed to, which is perhaps a big assumption, the already legendary Epic Fury will be at an end.' He added: 'If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before.' The ultimatum came hours after Axios reported the US and Iran were nearing a 14-point MOU to end the war. Trump also said the US had 'very good talks' with Iran over the past 24 hours and that a deal was 'very possible.' Iran's FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei confirmed Tehran was reviewing the US proposal and would relay its response to mediator Pakistan.

title: IRGC Navy announces safe Hormuz passage under 'new protocols'
description: Iran's IRGC Navy posted on X: 'We thank captains & shipowners in the Persian Gulf & Gulf of Oman for complying with Iran's Strait of Hormuz regulations & contributing to regional maritime security. With the aggressor's threats neutralized & new protocols in place, safe, stable passage through SOH will be ensured.' The statement did not specify what the new protocols entailed but referenced 'designated corridors' for ship passage. It came hours after Trump paused Project Freedom, and signaled Iran intended to reassert control over Hormuz transit on its own terms rather than accept US-led escort operations. Iran introduced a new mechanism allowing ships to pass through designated corridors in the Strait.

title: Two IDF soldiers wounded by Hezbollah drones in south Lebanon
description: Two IDF soldiers were wounded when Hezbollah detonated explosive drones near their position in southern Lebanon on May 6 — one severely, one lightly. Both were evacuated for medical treatment. The IDF responded by striking approximately 25 Hezbollah targets over 24 hours, including weapons storage facilities and military structures, and killed multiple operatives. IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir visited the El-Khiam area to conduct operational assessments. Separately, the IDF intercepted a hostile aircraft before it crossed into Israeli territory. Hezbollah claimed 'fierce clashes' were taking place in Bint Jbeil, with rocket and drone strikes targeting Merkava tanks.

title: Israel strikes kill 6 in Lebanon; IDF orders evacuation of 12 villages
description: Israeli air strikes on southern and eastern Lebanon killed at least 6 and wounded 3 on May 6. In Zellaya, western Bekaa, an airstrike killed municipal council head Ali Qassem Ahmad and three family members in their home. Two more were killed by artillery shelling in the southern village of Mayfadoun. The IDF simultaneously issued urgent evacuation warnings to residents of 12 towns and villages in southern Lebanon — including some north of the Litani River — claiming Hezbollah had violated the ceasefire. Fighter jets, drones, and artillery were used. Al Jazeera reported the strikes violated the US-brokered ceasefire effective since April 17.

title: Axios: US and Iran nearing 14-point MOU to end war
description: Axios reported May 6 that the White House believes it is close to a one-page, 14-point memorandum of understanding with Iran to end the war and begin 30 days of detailed nuclear negotiations. The MOU, negotiated by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner with Iranian officials, would include mutual lifting of blockades, US sanctions removal, and an Iranian moratorium on uranium enrichment of at least 12 years (Iran proposed 5, the US demanded 20). Two sources said Iran would agree to remove its highly enriched uranium from the country — a key US priority Tehran had previously rejected. The US expects Iranian responses on several points within 48 hours. Sources cautioned nothing has been agreed yet but called this the closest the parties have been to a deal since February 28.

title: Oil plunges 12% on deal reports; Brent falls below $100 for first time since April
description: Oil prices crashed on May 6 after Axios reported the US and Iran were nearing a deal. WTI crude fell over 12% to $89.76/barrel — the largest single-day drop since the April 8 ceasefire — while Brent dropped below $100 for the first time since mid-April. The plunge reversed the previous day's surge to $114.44 (the 2026 high). Markets rallied on renewed hopes for Hormuz reopening. The move came one day after Trump paused Project Freedom, citing 'great progress' toward a deal. Goldman Sachs analyst Yulia Zhestkova Grigsby warned Europe still faces 'large risks of jet fuel shortages this summer,' with UK supplies most at risk as the continent has lost 75% of its jet fuel imports.

title: CMA CGM container ship hit by possible cruise missile in Hormuz; crew injured
description: The Maltese-flagged CMA CGM San Antonio (2,824 TEU), owned by French shipping giant CMA CGM, was struck by an unknown projectile — possibly a cruise missile per CBS reporting — while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on May 5. Several crew members were injured and evacuated for medical care. The vessel sustained damage and went dark, ceasing AIS transmission. The attack occurred during the first day of Project Freedom, the US-led corridor to escort stranded commercial ships. UKMTO confirmed the incident, bringing total maritime incidents since February 28 to 46, with 10 confirmed seafarer fatalities across all incidents. Trump paused Project Freedom hours later.

title: Rubio and Lavrov hold first phone call in 6 months; discuss Iran and Ukraine
description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke by phone with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov on May 5 — their first call in more than six months. The call was held at Lavrov's request and covered the US-Russia relationship, the Iran war ceasefire, potential regional escalation, and the Ukraine conflict. Russia's foreign ministry described the conversation as 'constructive and businesslike.' The call came less than a week after Putin spoke with Trump and ahead of Trump's scheduled May 14-15 Beijing summit with Xi Jinping, as great-power diplomacy intensified around a potential Iran deal.

title: Rubio: Israel-Lebanon peace deal 'imminently achievable'; Hezbollah the obstacle
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that an Israel-Lebanon peace deal was 'imminently achievable,' adding: 'The problem with Israel and Lebanon is not Israel or Lebanon, it's Hezbollah.' The comments came as the US sought to separate the Lebanon track from the broader Iran negotiations. Rubio also reported that 10 civilian sailors had been killed in escalating Hormuz violence. The diplomatic signal aligned with the broader shift: with Epic Fury declared over and Project Freedom paused, the administration was pivoting from military operations to parallel diplomatic tracks on Iran nuclear issues and Lebanon peace.

title: Iran FM Araghchi meets Wang Yi in Beijing; first China visit since war began
description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing on May 6 — his first visit to China since the war began on February 28. The meeting came days before President Trump's scheduled visit to Beijing, allowing Tehran to demonstrate it retains major-power diplomatic options. Araghchi had previously dismissed Project Freedom as 'Project Deadlock,' writing on X that 'events in the Strait of Hormuz have made it crystal clear that there is no military solution to the political crisis.' Iran's foreign ministry said talks covered bilateral relations and regional developments. For Tehran, the visit signaled it is not diplomatically isolated despite two months of war.

title: Rubio declares Operation Epic Fury 'over'; Trump notifies Congress
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that Operation Epic Fury — the roughly two-month US-Israeli offensive air campaign against Iran launched February 28 — had effectively ended. Rubio said the US had 'achieved the objectives' of the war and shifted to a 'defensive' posture: 'This is not an offensive operation; this is a defensive operation.' Trump formally notified Congress of the operation's completion. Rubio warned Iran faces 'catastrophic destruction to their economy' but acknowledged Project Freedom alone would not solve 'the whole Straits problem.' The declaration marked the official end of the offensive phase that began with 900+ sorties on Day 1.

title: Trump pauses Project Freedom after 1 day, cites 'great progress' on Iran deal
description: President Trump announced Tuesday evening that Project Freedom — the US military operation to guide stranded ships through the Strait of Hormuz launched just Monday morning — was being paused 'for a short period of time to see whether or not the Agreement can be finalized and signed.' Trump said the decision was made 'at the request of Pakistan,' which has mediated indirect US-Iran talks, and cited 'Great Progress' toward 'a Complete and Final Agreement.' The US blockade of Iranian ports would remain in place. The abrupt about-face came hours after the administration had framed the operation as a life-or-death matter for 23,000 stranded sailors from 87 countries. Only two US-flagged vessels had successfully transited before the pause.

title: Hegseth: 'ceasefire is not over' despite 10+ Iranian attacks since April 8
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told reporters that 'the ceasefire is not over,' characterizing the Hormuz exchanges of fire as a 'separate and distinct project' from the broader truce. 'We expected there would be some churn at the beginning, which happened,' Hegseth said. Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Gen. Dan Caine revealed Iran had attacked US forces 'more than 10 times' since the April 8 ceasefire but said it 'fell below the threshold of restarting major combat operations.' Hegseth stressed the ceasefire's future 'ultimately rests with President Donald Trump,' adding: 'Right now the cease-fire certainly holds, but we're going to be watching very, very closely.'

title: UAE reports second day of Iranian missile and drone attacks; IRGC denies all
description: The UAE Ministry of Defence reported its air defense systems engaged Iranian missiles and drones for the second consecutive day, following the May 4 barrage of 12 ballistic missiles, 3 cruise missiles, and 4 drones. Details of the May 5 interceptions were limited, with the ministry not specifying exact numbers. Iran's IRGC categorically denied the attacks, stating it had 'not carried out any missile or drone operations against the UAE in recent days' and calling the claims 'absolutely denied and devoid of any truth.' The denial covered both the May 4 and May 5 strikes, despite the UAE having presented physical evidence of the previous day's Fujairah fire.

title: Iran judiciary vows to execute 'enemy's mercenaries without leniency'
description: Iran's judiciary and security authorities declared on state television they would 'act decisively against the enemies' mercenaries without leniency until the very last one.' The statement came as execution pace continued: the UN confirmed at least 21 executions on national security charges since the start of 2026, with over 4,000 arrested. Authorities seized assets of 22 individuals in Semnan Province, confiscating property from those deemed 'linked with the Zionist regime and hostile countries.' Political prisoners across 56 Iranian prisons launched a coordinated hunger strike marking the 119th consecutive week of the 'No to Executions Tuesdays' campaign.

title: Trump says war could last '2-3 more weeks'; refuses to confirm ceasefire
description: In a phone interview with Hugh Hewitt, President Trump refused to say whether the ceasefire with Iran was over, stating: 'Well, I can't tell you that.' He projected the war could continue for 'probably another two weeks' or 'maybe three weeks,' adding: 'Time is not of the essence for us.' Trump dismissed Iran's enriched uranium stockpile: 'From a standpoint of value, it's not very valuable. Probably can't be used.' He claimed Iran's navy had been destroyed — 'they had 159 ships, Hugh, now they have none. They're all at the bottom of the sea' — and said the outcome is binary: 'We either make the right deal or we win very easily.'

title: Iran parliament speaker Ghalibaf: 'We have not even begun yet'
description: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X that 'the new equation of the Strait of Hormuz is in the process of being solidified,' accusing the US and allies of jeopardizing maritime security 'through the violation of the ceasefire and the imposition of a blockade.' He warned: 'We know full well that the continuation of the status quo is intolerable for America; while we have not even begun yet.' The statement signaled Iran views the Hormuz standoff as strategically favorable to Tehran and intends to escalate if Project Freedom continues.

title: Brent crude surges 5.8% to $114.44 — highest close of 2026
description: Brent crude futures rose 5.8% to close at $114.44 per barrel on Monday — the highest settlement price of 2026 — as Project Freedom's launch triggered Iranian attacks on commercial shipping and the UAE. Prices have risen more than 50% since the war began in late February. Analyst June Goh of Sparta Singapore said markets are pricing in 'more oil infrastructure damage and the likelihood that the Strait of Hormuz will be shut beyond the timeline that the Trump administration has laid out.' US gasoline hit a record $4.46/gallon national average. An estimated 14.5 million barrels per day remain offline due to the Hormuz closure.

title: 2 IDF soldiers wounded in Hezbollah clash near Deir Seryan; 17 Lebanese killed
description: Hezbollah fighters opened fire on Israeli troops attempting to advance near the town of Deir Seryan in south Lebanon, inside the IDF's declared 10-km 'yellow line' buffer zone. The IDF confirmed two soldiers were moderately wounded in the clash. Israeli forces returned fire and the Air Force struck Hezbollah positions including buildings and anti-tank missile launch posts. Separately, Israeli strikes killed 17 Lebanese and wounded 35 over the preceding 24 hours, including 4 killed in Meiss Ej Jabal. The violence continued despite the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire declared April 16.

title: US intelligence: Iran nuclear breakout timeline unchanged despite 2 months of strikes
description: US intelligence assessments concluded that the time Iran would need to build a nuclear weapon has not changed since last summer, despite two months of a war Trump launched partly to stop Iran from developing a bomb. The unchanged timeline suggests that destroying Iran's remaining stockpile of 440.9 kg of highly enriched uranium — believed stored in Isfahan tunnels — remains necessary to significantly impede Tehran's nuclear capability. The assessment undercut the administration's narrative that military operations had degraded Iran's nuclear program, and came as Trump publicly dismissed the uranium as 'not very valuable' and 'probably can't be used.'

title: OPEC+ approves 188,000 bpd output increase for June; first meeting without UAE
description: OPEC+ agreed to raise production quotas by 188,000 barrels per day for June at a virtual Sunday meeting — the group's first since the UAE's exit from OPEC effective May 1. Seven producers participated: Algeria, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Oman, Russia, and Saudi Arabia. The increase represented less than 2% of the 14.5 million bpd disrupted by the Hormuz closure. Saudi Arabia's actual March production stood at 7.76 million bpd against a quota of 10.29 million bpd, illustrating how export constraints — not quotas — are the binding limitation. Oil remained above $125/barrel at the time of the decision. The UAE withdrew from OPEC on April 28 after 59 years, citing frustration with production quotas.

title: UAE orders nationwide remote learning May 5-8 after Iran missile strikes
description: The UAE Ministry of Education ordered all nurseries, schools, and universities to switch to distance learning from May 5-8, covering all students, teachers, and administrative staff nationwide. The Ministry of Higher Education confirmed universities would also shift to remote instruction, exempting only clinical training, laboratory, and examination programmes. Dubai's KHDA issued a parallel directive for all private schools. The decision followed Iran's May 4 missile and drone attacks on the UAE. The Ministry stated the situation 'will be reassessed' before any return to physical classes.

title: Iran fires 12 ballistic missiles, 3 cruise missiles, 4 drones at UAE; Fujairah oil fire wounds 3
description: Iran launched its first attack on the UAE since the April 8 ceasefire. The UAE Defence Ministry reported engaging 12 ballistic missiles, 3 cruise missiles, and 4 drones fired from Iran. Three missiles were intercepted over UAE waters and a fourth crashed into the sea. One drone struck the Fujairah Petroleum Industries Zone, sparking a large fire and wounding three Indian nationals. Iran initially denied planning any attack, with a military source telling state media Iran had 'no pre-planned programme to attack the mentioned oil facilities.' However, an IRGC-linked social media account later posted visuals claiming credit. The UAE Foreign Ministry condemned 'the renewed terrorist, unprovoked Iranian attacks, targeting civilian sites' and reserved 'the full and legitimate right to respond.' Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Jordan, France, Germany, and the UK condemned the strikes.

title: US helicopters sink 6 Iranian fast boats during Project Freedom launch in Hormuz
description: U.S. Apache and MH-60 Seahawk helicopters destroyed six Iranian fast boats that attempted to interfere with commercial shipping during the first day of Operation Project Freedom. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper reported that Iran 'launched multiple cruise missiles, drones, and small boats' and that U.S. forces 'defeated each and every one.' Trump later claimed seven boats were destroyed: 'We've shot down seven small Boats or, as they like to call them, fast Boats.' Iran's military denied the claim, with a senior official stating: 'The US claim that it sank a number of Iranian war boats is false.' Two U.S.-flagged vessels successfully transited the strait; USS Truxtun and USS Mason navigated the strait without sustaining hits.

title: Maersk Alliance Fairfax becomes first commercial ship to exit Hormuz under US escort
description: The Alliance Fairfax, a U.S.-flagged vehicle carrier operated by Maersk's Farrell Lines subsidiary, exited the Persian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz accompanied by U.S. military assets — the first commercial vessel to transit the strait under Operation Project Freedom. Maersk confirmed the transit was 'completed without incident.' The ship had been stranded in the Gulf since late February when shipping through the strait collapsed amid missile, drone, and mine threats. Approximately 2,000 ships with 20,000 crew remain stranded in the Gulf awaiting safe passage.

title: Trump warns Iran will be 'blown off face of the earth'; declines to confirm ceasefire
description: President Trump warned in a Fox News interview that Iran would be 'blown off the face of the earth' if it attacks U.S. Navy vessels carrying out Project Freedom. When asked whether the ceasefire between the US and Iran remains in effect, Trump declined to confirm it, marking the first time either side refused to acknowledge the truce's validity. Treasury Secretary Bessent stated the US has 'absolute control' of the Strait and called Iran's navy 'a band of pirates.' The comments came after Iranian forces fired missiles and deployed boats against commercial shipping during Project Freedom's first day of operations.

title: South Korean cargo ship HMM Namu hit by explosion near Strait of Hormuz
description: The South Korean-operated cargo ship HMM Namu reported a fire and explosion while anchored near the Strait of Hormuz off the UAE coast. Trump posted that Iran had 'taken some shots at unrelated Nations with respect to the Ship Movement, PROJECT FREEDOM, including a South Korean Cargo Ship,' adding: 'Other than the South Korean Ship, there has been, at this moment, no damage going through the Strait.' South Korea's presidential office said it was unclear if the explosion was caused by an Iranian attack, and no meeting of the National Security Council had been called. The incident occurred amid coordinated Iranian attacks on shipping and the UAE during Project Freedom's first day.

title: NATO chief: Europeans have 'gotten the message' on defense spending from Trump
description: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte acknowledged American frustration with European allies regarding the Iran war, stating that European leaders 'have gotten the message' and 'heard it loud and clear' about increasing defense spending. 'Europeans are stepping up, a bigger role for Europe and a stronger NATO,' Rutte said. His comments came after President Trump announced withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany and threatened deeper cuts, following criticism from German Chancellor Merz that Washington was being 'humiliated' by Iran in negotiations.

title: Iran executes 7, including 3 protesters; human rights groups cite torture concerns
description: Iran's judiciary executed seven people: three at Vakilabad prison in Mashhad linked to January protests—Mehdi Rasouli (25), Mohammad Reza Miri (21), and Ebrahim Dolatabadi—and four at Dastgerd prison in Isfahan under qisas (retaliatory justice) for murder convictions. Human rights groups said Rasouli accepted charges only after 'being beaten and tortured,' while the Hengaw Organization said Dolatabadi was executed despite 'no evidentiary proof being presented against him.' Since February 28, Iran's judiciary has executed at least 30 individuals linked to January protests or espionage charges.

title: Iran claims two missiles hit US frigate in Hormuz Strait; Pentagon denies
description: Iran's military claimed that two missiles struck a U.S. Navy frigate in the Strait of Hormuz after it ignored warnings from Iran's navy to halt operations. The Iranian army statement alleged the strike occurred without providing evidence. U.S. Central Command immediately denied the claim, stating no such attack had taken place. The allegation came hours after President Trump announced Project Freedom would begin guiding stranded merchant ships through the strait. Iran's Foreign Ministry warned that any American interference in the 'new maritime regime of the Strait of Hormuz' would be considered a ceasefire violation.

title: Trump announces 'Project Freedom' to escort ships through Hormuz; Iran warns ceasefire violation
description: President Trump announced 'Project Freedom,' a naval operation to guide stranded merchant vessels through the Strait of Hormuz beginning Monday. CENTCOM committed guided-missile destroyers, 100+ land- and sea-based aircraft, multi-domain unmanned platforms, and 15,000 service members. Admiral Brad Cooper stated: 'Our support for this defensive mission is essential to regional security and the global economy.' Trump called it 'a Humanitarian gesture' but warned: 'If, in any way, this Humanitarian process is interfered with, that interference will, unfortunately, have to be dealt with forcefully.' US officials clarified it is not a direct escort — Navy ships will be 'in the vicinity' and provide mine-avoidance routing. Iran's parliamentary National Security Commission head Ebrahim Azizi responded: 'Any American interference in the new maritime regime of the Strait of Hormuz will be considered a violation of the ceasefire,' adding: 'The Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf would not be managed by Trump's delusional posts!'

title: Iran confirms receipt of US written counter-proposal via Pakistan
description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei confirmed Tehran received a formal US written response to its 14-point peace plan, transmitted through Pakistani intermediaries. Baghaei said the response is being 'reviewed.' The development revealed active back-channel diplomacy continuing despite Trump's public rejection of Iran's proposal the previous day and Rubio's dismissal of its terms. Iran's 14-point plan proposed a 30-day timeline to end the war, phased Hormuz reopening, sanctions relief, and deferral of nuclear talks to a later stage. The formal US counter-response suggested Washington may be signaling flexibility on sequencing that its public rhetoric denied.

title: Israel kills 41 in Lebanon in 24 hours; total dead since March 2 reaches 2,659
description: Israeli forces launched 50 airstrikes across southern Lebanon in a 24-hour period, killing 41 people and injuring 11 others, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. Targets included Shoukine in Nabatieh district (3 killed), Kfar Dajjal village (2 killed), Lwaizeh village (3 killed), and locations in Tyre district. The cumulative death toll from Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2 reached 2,659 with 8,183 injured. Over one million Lebanese remain displaced. Hezbollah responded by targeting 'multiple gatherings of Israeli soldiers and vehicles in front-line towns' using fiber-optic cable drones against Israeli tanks. The strikes continued despite the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire declared April 16 and extended until mid-May.

title: Somali pirates hijack oil tanker M/T Eureka off Yemen; 4th incident in weeks
description: Armed assailants boarded and seized the oil tanker M/T Eureka off Yemen's southeastern Shabwa province, diverting it through the Gulf of Aden toward the Somali coast. The crew's fate remains unknown. Yemen's Coast Guard said it is 'working with international partners and relevant authorities in the Gulf of Aden to recover the tanker and ensure the safety of the crew.' The hijacking is at least the fourth near Somalia in recent weeks, as piracy surges with naval forces distracted by the Strait of Hormuz blockade and diverted shipping routes. The UK Maritime Trade Operations raised the piracy threat level along the Somali coast to 'substantial,' while EU naval forces cited the Iran war giving piracy groups a 'window of opportunity.'

title: IRGC: Trump must choose 'impossible military operation or bad deal'
description: The IRGC intelligence department declared that 'Trump must choose between an impossible military operation or a bad deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran,' adding that 'the room for US decision-making has narrowed.' The statement cited Iran's one-month deadline for the US to end its naval blockade, and claimed a shift in Russia, China, and European countries' tone toward Washington. The statement came as Trump said on social media he would 'soon be reviewing the plan Iran has just sent' but that Iran has 'not yet paid a big enough price for what they have done to Humanity, and the World, over the last 47 years.' Iran's deputy FM Gharibabadi said 'the ball is in America's court to choose the path of diplomacy or to continue the confrontational approach.'

title: Spirit Airlines ceases all operations; 17,000 jobs lost to fuel crisis
description: Spirit Airlines began an immediate wind-down of operations on May 2, canceling 4,119 scheduled flights carrying 809,638 passengers and putting 17,000 employees out of work. The airline's restructuring plan had assumed jet fuel at $2.24/gallon, but prices climbed to $4.51/gallon due to the Iran war's disruption of oil supplies. A $500 million White House bailout collapsed after a final board meeting on May 1 failed to reach agreement. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said: 'If no one else wants to buy them, why would we buy them?' No US carrier of Spirit's size — 5% of domestic flights at peak — has liquidated in two decades. The shutdown was expected to raise fares across the entire US airline industry.

title: Italy warns Iran nuclear program is 'red line'; Araghchi calls stance irresponsible
description: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi in a phone call that 'for Italy, the development of an Iranian nuclear programme for military purposes represents a red line, with the concrete risk of triggering a dangerous nuclear arms race in the region.' Tajani urged Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and to use its influence over Hezbollah to cease strikes against Israel. Araghchi rejected the position, expressing 'regret at the unconstructive and irresponsible approach of certain European countries in repeating unfounded accusations regarding the Iranian nuclear issue,' insisting Iran's program is 'exclusively peaceful.' The exchange highlighted Europe's emerging mediating role between Washington and Tehran.

title: Rubio dismisses Iran 14-point proposal; demands nuclear concessions first
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected Iran's 14-point peace proposal, insisting that any deal must address Tehran's nuclear program. 'The nuclear question is the reason why we're in this in the first place,' Rubio said. He dismissed Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under its own conditions as unacceptable, characterizing it as: 'Yes, the straits are open, as long as you coordinate with Iran, get our permission, or we'll blow you up, and you pay us.' Rubio acknowledged Iran is 'serious about getting themselves out of the mess that they're in' but said competing 'hardliner factions' in Tehran are complicating negotiations. The rejection deepened the diplomatic impasse with no new talks scheduled.

title: Nick Stewart, FDD-linked lobbyist, joins Iran negotiating team at Kushner's request
description: The White House confirmed that Nick Stewart, a former State Department official and lobbyist for the Foundation for Defense of Democracies — a hawkish think tank supportive of military action against Iran — joined the Iran negotiating team as policy adviser to Special Envoy Steve Witkoff. Stewart was brought on at Jared Kushner's request. He previously worked for Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY), who called him 'one of America's sharpest experts on Iran policy.' His appointment drew Congressional scrutiny over his qualifications for sensitive diplomacy. Stewart joined the team that traveled to Islamabad in early April alongside VP Vance, Kushner, and Witkoff.

title: Pentagon orders 5,000 troops withdrawn from Germany; Trump vows deeper cuts
description: The Pentagon announced withdrawal of approximately 5,000 troops from Germany over the next 6-12 months, including one brigade combat team and a long-range fires battalion. Germany hosts over 35,000 U.S. service members. The next day, Trump escalated: 'We're going to cut way down. And we're cutting a lot further than 5,000.' The withdrawal followed Chancellor Merz saying the U.S. was being 'humiliated' by Iran and criticizing Washington's lack of strategy. Republican armed services committee chairs said they were 'very concerned,' warning the decision risked 'undermining deterrence and sending the wrong signal to Vladimir Putin.' German Defense Minister Pistorius said American presence benefits both sides.

title: Trump calls US Navy 'like pirates'; Iran condemns as 'admission of piracy'
description: President Trump boasted at a Florida rally that the naval blockade is 'a very profitable business,' describing how the Navy seizes Iranian ships and cargo. 'We took over the ship. We took over the cargo, took over the oil. It's a very profitable business,' he said, adding: 'We're sort of like pirates.' Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei condemned the remarks as a 'damning admission of the criminal nature of their actions,' stating: 'This is the outright legalization of piracy and armed robbery on the high seas. Welcome to the return of the pirates — only now, they operate with government-issued warrants, sail under official flags, and call their plunder law enforcement.'

title: CENTCOM: 48 ships redirected in 20 days; blockade costs Iran $4.8B
description: U.S. Central Command announced that 48 vessels have been redirected from Iranian ports since the blockade began on April 13 — up from 42 reported three days earlier — with three ships turned back in the preceding 20 hours. Pentagon press secretary Joel Valdez stated: 'The United States' blockade in the Strait of Hormuz is operating with full force and delivering the decisive impact we intended.' Pentagon officials told Axios the blockade has cost Iran approximately $4.8 billion in lost oil revenue. Separately, shipping traffic through the Strait has dropped over 90% from pre-conflict levels, with approximately 20,000 seafarers stranded on 2,000 vessels in the Persian Gulf.

title: IDF bulldozes Catholic convent in Yaroun; military claims Hezbollah used site
description: Israeli military bulldozers destroyed parts of a Catholic convent belonging to the Basilian Salvatorian Sisters in the southern Lebanese village of Yaroun. Superior General Gladys Sabbagh confirmed: 'What we heard is that it was destroyed with bulldozers.' The compound included a school closed since 2006 and a clinic recently relocated to Rmeich; two nuns had evacuated due to fighting. The IDF admitted damaging a 'religious building' but claimed it had 'no religious signs' visible and that soldiers 'prevented any further damage' once informed. The military alleged Hezbollah used the compound to fire rockets at Israel 'on several occasions.' The incident drew condemnation from Lebanese Christian leaders.

title: Trump calls criticism of Iran war 'treasonous'; claims hostilities 'terminated'
description: President Trump said he considers it 'treasonous' for critics to say the U.S. is not 'winning' the war with Iran. 'We get the radical left to say, we're not winning, we're not winning. They don't have any military left,' Trump told supporters in Florida. The same day, Trump formally notified Congress that hostilities have 'terminated,' writing: 'On April 7, 2026, I ordered a 2-week ceasefire. The ceasefire has since been extended. There has been no exchange of fire between United States Forces and Iran since April 7, 2026. The hostilities that began on February 28, 2026, have terminated.' The notification contradicted his simultaneous threats to resume strikes.

title: Trump rejects Iran's peace proposal; warns he'll 'blast them away'
description: President Trump declared he is 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest peace proposal, submitted through Pakistani mediators on May 1. 'They're asking for things I can't agree to,' Trump said, without specifying which terms he rejected. He warned he would 'blast them away' if negotiations fail, adding the US may be 'better off' without a deal. Iran's military responded by declaring conflict is 'likely' to restart and that forces are 'fully prepared for any new adventures or foolishness from the Americans.' The rejection left talks stalled since the April 12 Islamabad collapse, with no new round scheduled.

title: State Dept bypasses Congress for $8.6B in arms sales to 4 Middle East allies
description: Secretary of State Rubio invoked an emergency declaration to bypass congressional review for $8.6 billion in military sales: $4.01 billion in Patriot air defense replenishment to Qatar, $2.5 billion for an integrated battle command system to Kuwait, $992.4 million in Advanced Precision Kill Weapon Systems (APKWS) each to Qatar and Israel, and $147.6 million in APKWS to the UAE. Principal contractors include BAE Systems, RTX, Lockheed Martin, and Northrop Grumman. The emergency bypass was the second of the war, following the March 7 $650 million sale.

title: 14 IRGC soldiers killed defusing unexploded ordnance in Zanjan province
description: Fourteen IRGC specialized demolition personnel were killed and two wounded when an unexploded munition detonated during a clearance operation in northwestern Zanjan province. The IRGC said the dead were 'experienced, trained, and specialized personnel' who had previously neutralized over 15,000 items including three GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrators and 9,500 bomblets. Over 1,200 hectares of agricultural land in the province remain contaminated by cluster bombs and aerial mines from US-Israeli airstrikes. The incident was the single deadliest loss of Iranian military personnel since the April 7 ceasefire.

title: IRGC Navy announces 'new rules' over 2,000 km of Gulf coastline
description: The IRGC Navy announced enforcement of 'new rules' governing nearly 2,000 km of Iran's southern coastline, spanning the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. The statement said the measures would turn the waters into 'a source of pride and power for the dear people of Iran, and a source of security and prosperity for the region.' The new maritime regime will be aligned with Supreme Leader Khamenei's directives, effectively formalizing IRGC control over Iran's coastal waters during the blockade standoff. The announcement came as Washington warned shipping companies against paying Iran's Hormuz transit tolls, threatening sanctions for non-compliance.

title: US sanctions Chinese oil terminal Qingdao Haiye over Iran crude imports
description: The State Department sanctioned Qingdao Haiye Oil Terminal Co., Ltd., a China-based crude oil terminal that received tens of millions of barrels of Iranian crude in 2025, along with its president Xingchun Li, UK-based Thriving Times International, and Hong Kong-based Onboard Ship Management Limited. Beijing rejected the sanctions as 'unlawful unilateral measures.' The action targeted what Treasury described as key intermediaries in Iran's petroleum export network — the regime's 'most critical economic lifeline' — and furthered Trump's NSPM-2 maximum-pressure directive.

title: Israeli strikes kill 12 across southern Lebanon; Berri accuses Israel of ceasefire cover
description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least 12 people across southern Lebanon on Friday, hitting Kfar Dajal (2 killed), Lwaizeh (3 killed), Shoukin (2 killed), and other villages. Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri accused Israel of using the ceasefire as 'cover to intensify attacks.' Lebanon's cumulative death toll since March 2 surpassed 2,600, with over 1 million displaced. Separately, Hezbollah fired rockets and explosive drones at IDF troops in southern Lebanon; projectiles exploded near forces but caused no injuries.

title: USS Gerald R. Ford departs Middle East after record 10-month deployment
description: The USS Gerald R. Ford, the Navy's most advanced aircraft carrier, departed the Middle East for its homeport in Norfolk, Virginia, ending a deployment exceeding 10 months — the longest for a US carrier since the Vietnam War. The Ford participated in Operation Epic Fury from its opening day. Its departure reduced the US carrier presence from three strike groups to two, with the USS Abraham Lincoln and USS George H.W. Bush remaining in the Arabian Sea enforcing the naval blockade. The Pentagon said the withdrawal did not represent a change in military capability, calling two carrier groups the 'typical' regional posture.

title: Iran executes 21-year-old karate champion arrested during protests
description: Iran executed Sassan Azadvar Joonqani, 21, a karate champion from Isfahan province, at dawn at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan. Arrested on January 8 during nationwide protests, he was charged with moharebeh ('enmity against God') and 'effective cooperation with the enemy' for allegedly attacking security force vehicles. Human rights group Hengaw said he was subjected to severe physical and psychological torture to force a confession. Iran's judiciary chief stated courts should process detainee cases 'outside normal procedures' at faster pace. The UN reported at least 21 executions and over 4,000 arrests since the war began; Amnesty International documented at least 19 executions in recent weeks.

title: Trump threatens to pull US troops from Italy and Spain over Iran war stance
description: President Trump extended his troop-reduction threats from Germany to Italy and Spain, telling reporters: 'Italy has not been of any help to us and Spain has been horrible, absolutely horrible.' When asked if he was considering pulling troops, Trump responded: 'Yeah, probably.' As of December 2025, the US stations 12,662 active-duty troops in Italy and 3,814 in Spain. Spain previously closed its airspace to US military aircraft involved in Iran strikes. The threat — covering three NATO allies in 48 hours — marked the most aggressive US posture toward European basing since NATO's founding.

title: Murkowski to introduce AUMF if White House lacks war plan within one week
description: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) announced she will introduce an Authorization for Use of Military Force when the Senate returns May 11 if the White House does not present a 'credible plan' for the war. 'I do not accept that we should engage in open-ended military action without clear direction or accountability,' she said in a floor speech. Murkowski became the third Republican to break with the White House on war powers, following Collins's War Powers vote and Paul's consistent opposition, but took a different approach: rather than trying to halt the war, her AUMF would force the administration to define objectives and a strategy. She distinguished her stance from the six failed Democratic War Powers resolutions, saying they 'attempted to stop this conflict without establishing a path forward.'

title: Tehran air defenses fire for 20 minutes against unidentified drones
description: Air defense systems activated across western, central, and southeastern Tehran on Thursday night, firing for approximately 20 minutes against what Iranian state media described as 'small aircraft and reconnaissance drones.' Tasnim and Fars news agencies reported the situation returned to 'normal' afterward. No attribution was given for the drones. The incident occurred during the ceasefire, raising questions about whether surveillance overflights are continuing. Iran's air defenses had not been publicly activated since the April 7 ceasefire took effect.

title: Hezbollah drone kills IDF Sgt. Liem Ben Hamo, 19, in southern Lebanon
description: Sgt. Liem Ben Hamo, 19, of the Golani Brigade's 13th Battalion from Herzliya, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive drone in the village of Qantara in southern Lebanon at approximately 10:20 AM. Another soldier was moderately wounded. Hezbollah launched two drones at the position; troops intercepted one, but the second struck nearby. Ben Hamo was the 16th IDF soldier killed in Lebanon since Operation Roaring Lion began on February 28. The attack was separate from a second Hezbollah drone strike hours later that wounded 12 soldiers at an artillery position near Shomera in northern Israel.

title: UAE bans citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq
description: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal travel ban prohibiting Emirati citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, citing 'current regional disturbances.' The ministry urged all UAE nationals currently in those countries to 'leave immediately and return home.' The ban reflected the UAE's assessment that all three countries remain active conflict zones despite the ceasefire — Iran under naval blockade, Lebanon under continued Israeli strikes, and Iraq home to US troops and Iranian-backed militias. The UAE joined OPEC's exit the previous day, signaling a broader strategic realignment away from the region's instability.

title: Israeli strikes kill 30+ in southern Lebanon; deadliest day since ceasefire
description: Israeli airstrikes killed more than 30 people across southern Lebanon on May 1 — the deadliest single day since the April 17 US-mediated ceasefire — according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes further undermined the ceasefire framework as Israel continued operations beyond its declared buffer zone. Lebanon's cumulative toll since March 2 reached at least 2,586 killed and more than 8,020 wounded, with over 1 million displaced — 20% of the country's population.

title: War Powers 60-day deadline expires; Trump claims ceasefire pauses clock
description: The 60-day War Powers Resolution deadline expired on May 1, the statutory limit for unauthorized military operations. The Trump administration argued the ceasefire pauses the clock. 'We are in a ceasefire right now, which our understanding means the 60-day clock pauses or stops,' Defense Secretary Hegseth told Congress. Sen. Tim Kaine (D-VA) countered that the statute contains no such provision. House Speaker Mike Johnson claimed the US is 'not at war' with Iran. Multiple Democrats said they would sue Trump in federal court if the war continues without authorization. Trump indicated he 'might need' to restart military operations against Iran.
