title: Pezeshkian calls US blockade 'intolerable' extension of military operations
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian denounced the US naval blockade, calling it 'an extension of military operations against a nation paying the price for its resistance and independence' and declaring the situation 'intolerable.' He warned that 'any attempt to impose a blockade and maritime restrictions on the waterway is contrary to international law and a threat to regional nations' interests and global peace.' The statement, issued on Persian Gulf National Day alongside Supreme Leader Khamenei's address, framed the blockade as a ceasefire violation ahead of Iran's expected delivery of a revised three-phase peace proposal to Pakistan.

title: Senate rejects War Powers Resolution 49-50; Collins breaks with GOP
description: The Senate rejected a Democratic-led War Powers Resolution to end military operations against Iran by a vote of 49-50, the closest margin yet and the sixth failed attempt since the war began. Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) became the first Republican to vote for the measure, joining Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY) and declaring: 'Further military action against Iran must have a clear mission, achievable goals and a defined strategy.' Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA) was the sole Democrat to vote against. The one-vote margin — matching the House's 214-213 defeat on April 16 — showed war opposition intensifying across both chambers but still short of constraining the executive.

title: Israel seizes Gaza-bound flotilla near Crete; 175 activists detained
description: Israeli naval forces seized 22 of 58 vessels in the Global Sumud Flotilla approximately 1,000 km from Gaza near Crete — the farthest-ever interception of an aid flotilla, dwarfing the previous record of 72 nautical miles. Israeli military speedboats used drones, communications jamming, and armed raiding parties, ordering activists to kneel at gunpoint. The 175 detained crew members were transferred to Greek authorities on May 1. Turkey's foreign ministry condemned the seizure as 'an act of piracy.' The flotilla, which departed Italy, was described as the largest humanitarian aid convoy to attempt reaching Gaza during the war.

title: Khamenei breaks silence: nuclear and missile capabilities are 'national assets'
description: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued his first public statement since the war began, marking National Persian Gulf Day. In remarks read on state television — Khamenei has communicated only through written statements since being wounded in the February 28 strike that killed his father — he declared Iran's nuclear and missile capabilities 'national assets' that 90 million Iranians 'will protect just as they protect the country's waters, land and airspace.' He vowed to 'secure the Persian Gulf region and eliminate the hostile enemy's misuse of this waterway,' adding: 'Foreigners who come from thousands of kilometers away to act with greed and malice there have no place in it — except at the bottom of its waters.' The statement effectively ruled out trading away nuclear or missile programs in any deal.

title: CENTCOM briefs Trump on 'short and powerful' strike plan to break deadlock
description: Axios reported that CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper briefed President Trump on Thursday on new military options against Iran, including a plan for 'short and powerful' strikes on infrastructure targets designed to force Tehran back to the negotiating table with more flexibility on the nuclear issue. Additional options included a ground operation to seize part of the Strait of Hormuz to reopen it to commercial shipping, and a special forces mission to secure Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Trump told Axios he viewed the blockade as 'somewhat more effective than the bombing' and sees it as his primary leverage, but would consider military action if Iran refuses to negotiate. Iran's IRGC Aerospace Force Commander Majid Mousavi warned Iran would respond with 'long and painful strikes.'

title: Hezbollah drone wounds 12 IDF soldiers inside northern Israel
description: A Hezbollah explosive drone struck an armored cargo carrier near the northern Israeli community of Shomera in the Western Galilee, wounding 12 soldiers — the largest single-incident casualty toll from a Hezbollah drone since the war began. Two soldiers were moderately wounded; the rest sustained light injuries. The cargo carrier caught fire and several nearby artillery shells exploded from the blast. The IDF is investigating whether the drone was guided by a fiber-optic cable, which is immune to electronic jamming. The drone also detonated near a school in Shomera, marking the first time an explosive drone reached the Western Galilee. The attack underscored Hezbollah's shift to near-daily precision drone strikes against Israeli forces.

title: Brent crude hits $126 wartime high; US gas reaches $4.30/gallon
description: Brent crude surged to $126 per barrel on Thursday — the highest intraday price since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine and a new wartime high — before pulling back to $114.70 by session close. West Texas Intermediate topped $110. Deutsche Bank analysts attributed the spike to 'a report from Axios, suggesting that an escalation in the conflict was still being considered as an option.' US inventory data showed sharp declines in crude and fuel stockpiles while exports surged to record highs above 6 million barrels per day. The national average gasoline price hit $4.30 per gallon, the highest since July 2022, up 44% since the war began. Global oil prices have risen for eight consecutive trading sessions.

title: Israeli strikes kill 28 across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least 28 people across southern Lebanon on April 30 — the deadliest day in weeks — striking Jebchit (4 killed including a child), Toul (5 killed), Zebdine (6 killed near a cemetery by drone), Harouf (2 killed), Qana (2 killed), Kfar Rumman (a Lebanese soldier and family members killed), and Qlawiyah (1 killed). Over 70 people were wounded including children. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun demanded Israel 'cease targeting civilians, paramedics, civil defence, and humanitarian organisations.' Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri called for an international fact-finding committee. Lebanon's cumulative toll since March 2 reached 2,586 killed and 8,020 wounded.

title: IDF orders evacuation of 8 south Lebanon villages beyond buffer zone
description: The IDF issued evacuation notices for eight southern Lebanese villages located outside its declared buffer zone: Al-Samia, Al-Hania, Al-Qalila, Wadi Jilo, Al-Kanisa, Kafra, Majdal Zoun, and Siddiqin. The orders signaled a potential expansion of Israeli military operations beyond the territory it already occupies, contradicting the April 17 ceasefire framework. The evacuation notices followed Israel's request to Trump for a 2-3 week deadline on Lebanon talks, after which Jerusalem wants US blessing for an expanded campaign against Hezbollah.

title: Ghalibaf mocks US blockade: 'No wells exploded — try 30 days'
description: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf taunted the Trump administration over the naval blockade's effectiveness, posting on X that no Iranian oil wells had 'exploded' after three days of blocked exports as US officials had predicted, adding: 'Try 30 and we'll Livestream it.' He called Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's strategic advice 'junk' and claimed the blockade had only spiked global oil prices to $120 per barrel, with '$140 as the next stop.' Ghalibaf argued the policy was harming American consumers, not Iran. In response, Trump posted on Truth Social: 'Iran can't get their act together. They don't know how to sign a nonnuclear deal. They better get smart soon!' and told Axios Iran must 'cry uncle' before the blockade ends.

title: Israel asks Trump for 2-3 week deadline on Lebanon talks
description: Israel asked President Trump to limit diplomatic efforts with Lebanon to a 2-3 week window, after which Jerusalem wants US blessing for an expanded military campaign against Hezbollah, Israeli media reported. Israeli officials argued that ongoing Hezbollah drone and rocket attacks on IDF troops — six Israeli fatalities since the April 17 ceasefire — are eroding deterrence while diplomacy stalls. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir declared there 'is no ceasefire' in southern Lebanon. If no breakthrough is reached by mid-May, Israel intends to launch a major escalation in Lebanon, effectively setting a parallel deadline to the broader Iran peace process.

title: UN: Iran has executed 21 and arrested 4,000+ since war began
description: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk reported that Iran has executed 21 people since the war began on February 28 — 9 linked to the January 2026 protests, 10 for alleged opposition group membership, and 2 on espionage charges. More than 4,000 people have been detained on national security charges since March 9, with the UN documenting enforced disappearances, torture, and mock executions, disproportionately targeting ethnic and religious minorities. 'I am shocked and alarmed. The Iranian authorities continue to severely restrict people's rights,' Türk said. Trump claimed he had persuaded Iran to halt approximately 800 executions; Tehran denied both claims.

title: Trump and Putin hold 90-minute call on Iran and Ukraine
description: President Trump and Russian President Putin spoke for over 90 minutes in a call initiated by Moscow, described by Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov as 'frank and businesslike.' Putin renewed Russia's offer to serve as a third country to handle Iran's 970 pounds of highly enriched uranium that Washington demands Tehran surrender. Trump dismissed the offer, telling Putin: 'I'd much rather have you be involved with ending the war with Ukraine.' Putin proposed a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine during Victory Day celebrations on May 9; Trump 'actively supported this initiative.' Putin warned of 'inevitable and extremely damaging consequences' if the US and Israel resume strikes on Iran. The call marked the most substantive Trump-Putin engagement on the Iran conflict to date.

title: USS Gerald Ford to depart Middle East after record 295-day deployment
description: The USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier will depart the Middle East in coming days and return to Norfolk, Virginia, the Washington Post reported, ending the longest post-Vietnam War carrier deployment at 295 days — surpassing the USS Abraham Lincoln's 294-day COVID-era record. Defense Secretary Hegseth said 'operational requirements demanded additional assets in real time' that led to repeated extensions. The Ford's roughly 4,500 sailors have been deployed since June 2025. Two carriers remain in the region: the USS George H.W. Bush (arrived the previous week) and the USS Abraham Lincoln (deployed since January), enforcing the blockade from the Arabian Sea.

title: CENTCOM: Blockade has redirected 42 vessels, trapping $6B in Iranian oil
description: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper announced that US forces have redirected 42 commercial vessels attempting to enter or exit Iranian ports since the blockade began on April 13. Cooper reported 41 tankers carrying 69 million barrels of oil are now unable to reach market, representing over $6 billion in revenue Iran cannot access. 'The blockade is highly effective and U.S. forces remain fully committed to total enforcement,' Cooper said. The update came as vessel congestion at Iran's Chabahar port quadrupled from 5 ships pre-blockade to over 20, and Hormuz transit held at approximately 13 crossings per day — roughly 5% of pre-war levels.

title: Iran rial hits record low of 1.81M per dollar amid blockade
description: Iran's national currency plunged to a record low of 1.81 million rials per US dollar on the black market, a 12% decline in a single week, as the US naval blockade choked Tehran's remaining oil export revenue. The rial has lost roughly a third of its value since the war began on February 28. Economists warned the collapse will further fuel inflation in a country where imported goods — food, medicine, electronics, and raw materials — are priced against the dollar. The currency's slide reflected market expectations that the blockade will persist for months, with peace talks stalled and Iran's revised proposal not expected until Friday at the earliest.

title: Trump threatens US troop reduction in Germany after Merz criticism
description: President Trump threatened to reduce the approximately 34,500 US troops stationed in Germany, posting on social media: 'The United States is studying and reviewing the possible reduction of Troops in Germany, with a determination to be made over the next short period of time.' The threat came after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the US was being 'humiliated' by Iran and expressed doubts about the war from 'the very beginning.' Trump fired back: 'The Chancellor of Germany, Friedrich Merz, thinks it's OK for Iran to have a Nuclear Weapon. He doesn't know what he's talking about!' Germany hosts US European Command, US Africa Command, Ramstein Air Base, and Landstuhl Regional Medical Center — critical nodes for US global military operations.

title: Hegseth defends $1.5T defense budget in first war testimony to Congress
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth appeared before the House Armed Services Committee for his first congressional testimony since the Iran war began, defending a proposed $1.5 trillion FY2027 defense budget — the largest in US history. Democrats pressed Hegseth on the war's ballooning costs, the drawdown of critical munitions stockpiles, and the bombing of a school that killed children. Republicans also challenged Hegseth's firing of Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George mid-war. Sen. Thom Tillis demanded: 'Tell us why. You know these are important positions. We are in a war posture with Iran.' The hearing marked Congress's first formal oversight of the conflict 60 days after it began.

title: IAEA chief says Iran's enriched uranium likely intact at Isfahan
description: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told the Associated Press that the majority of Iran's highly enriched uranium — 440.9 kg enriched to 60% purity, a short technical step from weapons-grade 90% — is likely still stored in tunnels at the Isfahan Nuclear Technology Center. Grossi said roughly 200 kg is believed to be at the site, which has not been inspected since June 2025. Airbus satellite imagery showed a truck carrying 18 blue containers entering a tunnel at Isfahan on June 9, 2025, just before the 12-Day War, and the IAEA believes the material has remained there since. 'We haven't been able to inspect or to reject that the material is there and that the seals — the IAEA seals — remain there,' Grossi said. The disclosure underscored that despite months of US-Israeli strikes on Iran's nuclear infrastructure, Tehran's most sensitive fissile material may be beyond reach in hardened tunnels.

title: Iran threatens Bab el-Mandeb closure via Houthi allies
description: Alaaeddin Boroujerdi, Deputy Head of Iran's National Security Committee in parliament, warned that Iran could retaliate against the US naval blockade by directing its Houthi allies in Yemen to shut the Bab el-Mandeb strait — the second of the Middle East's two critical maritime chokepoints. Boroujerdi declared Iran 'will never relinquish its control over the Strait of Hormuz' and said the importance of Bab el-Mandeb 'may be no less than that of the Strait of Hormuz,' adding that Iran's 'Yemeni allies are waiting to block it.' Closure of both straits simultaneously would cut off roughly one-quarter of the world's energy supply. The threat marked the most explicit linkage yet between Iran's Hormuz strategy and Houthi capabilities at Bab el-Mandeb.

title: Israeli strikes kill 8 in Lebanon including 3 paramedics; army troops hit
description: Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon killed 8 people and wounded at least 30, including the first direct targeting of Lebanese army troops since the April 17 ceasefire. In Majdal Zoun, a 'double-tap' strike killed 5 people including 3 Lebanese Civil Defense paramedics trapped under rubble while conducting a rescue mission, and wounded 2 Lebanese army soldiers accompanying the patrol with civilian bulldozers. In Jebchit, 2 were killed and 13 wounded; in Jwaya, 1 killed and 15 wounded including 5 children and 5 women. Lebanese PM Nawaf Salam called the paramedic killings a 'war crime.' Lebanon's cumulative toll since March 2 reached 2,534 killed and 7,863 wounded.

title: WSJ: Trump orders aides to prepare extended Iran blockade
description: President Trump directed aides to prepare for a prolonged naval blockade of Iran, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials. In a Situation Room meeting on Monday, Trump concluded that continuing economic pressure through port restrictions carried less risk than resuming bombing or walking away from the conflict. CENTCOM reported vessel congestion at Iran's Chabahar port had quadrupled from 5 ships pre-blockade to over 20. The decision effectively shelved Iran's latest Hormuz proposal and signaled Washington's strategy has shifted from seeking a rapid diplomatic resolution to a long-term economic squeeze.

title: UAE quits OPEC effective May 1 amid Iran war energy crisis
description: The United Arab Emirates announced its withdrawal from OPEC effective May 1, the most significant departure from the cartel since Qatar left in 2019. Energy Minister Suhail Mohamed al-Mazrouei said the decision reflects 'the UAE's long-term strategic and economic vision and evolving energy profile.' The UAE has 4.8 million barrels per day of production capacity but has been capped at roughly 3.2 million bpd under OPEC quotas. Rystad Energy warned the withdrawal removes a significant shock absorber from oil markets, forcing Saudi Arabia to bear more responsibility for price stability. The move came as Brent crude topped $111/barrel and the Iran war has shattered OPEC's ability to coordinate production amid the Hormuz crisis.

title: GCC summit in Jeddah rejects Iran's Hormuz actions, calls for missile shield
description: Gulf Cooperation Council leaders held an extraordinary consultative summit in Jeddah, chaired by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, in their first collective gathering since the war began. The leaders issued a categorical rejection of Iran's Strait of Hormuz closure and any transit fees or restrictions, demanding restoration of pre-crisis shipping conditions. They called for development of a joint ballistic missile early warning system and broader military integration across the six-member bloc. Qatar warned against using the waterway as leverage and cautioned of a potential 'frozen conflict.' The summit marked the GCC's strongest unified response to Iran's maritime actions since the war began.

title: US sanctions 35 entities in Iran's shadow banking network
description: The Treasury Department sanctioned 35 entities and individuals operating Iran's covert financial network, targeting what it called 'tens of billions of dollars' in sanctions evasion and terrorism financing. OFAC designated 22 entities in Hong Kong, the UAE, and Turkey for facilitating Iranian oil sales benefiting the IRGC and Quds Force. The sanctions targeted 'rahbars' — private companies that execute payments through shell company accounts at foreign banks on behalf of the IRGC and National Iranian Oil Company. Treasury Secretary Bessent warned financial institutions of 'severe consequences' for engaging with Iran's shadow banking infrastructure and specifically threatened sanctions against any firm paying Hormuz transit tolls to the IRGC.

title: IDF destroys largest Hezbollah tunnel network near Qantara
description: The IDF announced it had located and destroyed the largest Hezbollah underground complex found in southern Lebanon — two parallel tunnels near Qantara, 11 km from the Israeli border, spanning 2 km in length and reaching depths of 25 meters. The tunnels were built over a decade with 'direct guidance' from Iran and designed to house thousands of Radwan Force elite fighters, containing weapons caches, sleeping quarters, water tanks, and communications infrastructure. Destruction required hundreds of tons of explosives; the Geological Survey of Israel detected the blasts on its seismic monitoring system. Units from Division 36, the 7th Armored Brigade, Golani Brigade, and Yahalom special engineering unit participated in the week-long mapping and demolition operation.

title: World Bank forecasts 24% energy price surge, largest since 2022
description: The World Bank's Commodity Markets Outlook projected a 24% increase in energy prices for 2026 — the largest surge since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine — driven by the Hormuz closure removing over 10 million barrels per day from global supply. Brent crude is forecast to average $86/barrel for the year, up from $69 in 2025, with a severe scenario pushing the average to $115 if further infrastructure damage occurs. The report projected a 16% rise in overall commodity costs. Brent traded above $111 on the day of the report's release, well above the baseline forecast, suggesting current prices already reflect the severe scenario.

title: Hezbollah drone kills Israeli defense contractor and his son is wounded
description: A Hezbollah explosive drone struck a bulldozer in southern Lebanon, killing 44-year-old Amer Hujairat, a civilian contractor working for the Defense Ministry's engineering company, and lightly wounding his 19-year-old son who was working alongside him. The son was evacuated to Ziv Hospital in Safed. Hujairat, from Shfaram, was demolishing structures in a southern Lebanese village when the drone detonated. Hezbollah claimed responsibility, saying it targeted an Israeli bulldozer. Hujairat's death — the sixth Israeli fatality since the Lebanon ceasefire began April 17 — marked the first killing of a civilian contractor in the conflict.

title: Hezbollah drone severely wounds IDF soldier in southern Lebanon
description: A Hezbollah explosive drone struck IDF troops in southern Lebanon, seriously wounding one soldier and lightly wounding another — the fourth and fifth Israeli military casualties since the Lebanon ceasefire began April 17. The IDF said troops attempted to intercept a 'suspicious aerial target' in a separate incident the same morning. Secretary of State Rubio stated Israel had 'a right to defend itself from an attack from Hezbollah elements.' The attack came two days after Sgt. Idan Fooks was killed by a similar drone strike, underscoring Hezbollah's sustained use of first-person-view drones to target Israeli forces despite the truce.

title: Kpler: Iran has 12-22 days of oil storage left as blockade chokes exports
description: Research firm Kpler reported that Iran's unused onshore oil storage capacity will be exhausted within 12 to 22 days, raising the prospect of forced production cuts of up to 1.5 million barrels per day by mid-May, Bloomberg reported. Iranian crude exports have collapsed from 1.85 million bpd in March to roughly 567,000 bpd — a 70% drop — since the US naval blockade took effect in early April. Kpler said no tankers have successfully evaded the blockade around the Strait of Hormuz. Goldman Sachs estimated Iran has already curtailed 2.5 million bpd of daily crude production. Total usable onshore storage stands at approximately 39 million barrels, with Kharg Island holding 20-30 million barrels, but operational constraints reduce effective working volumes. The storage crisis represents the blockade's most concrete economic pressure on Tehran to date.

title: Guterres demands Hormuz reopening at UN Security Council maritime debate
description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres addressed a high-level Security Council debate on maritime security, delivering his strongest statement yet on the Hormuz crisis: 'I appeal to the parties: Open the Strait. Let ships pass. No tolls. No discrimination. Let trade resume. Let the global economy breathe.' Guterres warned that over 20,000 seafarers remain stranded at sea and more than 2,000 commercial vessels are trapped in dangerous conditions, calling the disruption the most severe to supply chains since the COVID-19 pandemic and Ukraine war. He cited the strait's role carrying one-fifth of global oil and nearly one-third of internationally traded fertilizers, warning the crisis is 'cascading into empty fuel tanks, empty shelves and empty plates.' The IMO Secretary-General declared there is 'no safe transit anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz.' The debate was the Security Council's first formal session focused on the maritime dimension of the conflict.

title: Rubio rejects Iran's Hormuz proposal as 'unacceptable'
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying the US cannot accept any deal where Tehran retains control over the waterway. Rubio told Fox News: 'If what they mean by opening the strait is yes, it's open — but you must coordinate with us, get our permission, or we'll blow you up and charge you anyway, then that is not opening.' He acknowledged the proposal was 'better than what we thought they were going to submit' but insisted any final deal must block Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed Trump had discussed the proposal with his national security team but declined to comment on next steps. The rejection hardened the US negotiating position as Araghchi continued shuttle diplomacy across the region.

title: German Chancellor Merz says Iran is 'humiliating' the United States
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz delivered an unusually blunt rebuke of both Iran's negotiating tactics and US strategy, telling students in Marsberg: 'An entire nation is being humiliated by the Iranian leadership, particularly by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.' Merz warned Washington lacks a clear exit strategy, comparing the conflict to Afghanistan and Iraq: 'The problem with conflicts like this is always you don't just have to get in — you have to get out again.' He described Iran as 'clearly stronger than one thought' and said the war was directly impacting Germany's economy. Merz confirmed Germany remains ready to deploy minesweepers to Hormuz shipping routes contingent on a ceasefire. The remarks underscored deepening divisions between Washington and European NATO allies over the war.

title: Hezbollah's Qassem rejects Israel talks; Aoun calls war 'treason'
description: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem categorically rejected Lebanon's direct negotiations with Israel, calling them a 'grave sin' and demanding the government 'stop direct negotiations with the Israeli enemy.' He declared: 'We will not give up our weapons, and the Israeli enemy will not remain on a single inch of our occupied land.' Qassem also demanded Lebanon annul its March 2 decision criminalizing Hezbollah. President Joseph Aoun fired back: 'What we are doing is not treason. Rather, treason is committed by those who take their country to war to achieve foreign interests.' Aoun said he seeks an armistice agreement modeled on the 1949 accord, asking Hezbollah: 'When you went to war, did you first obtain national consensus?' The exchange marked the sharpest public rift between the Lebanese government and Hezbollah since the war began.

title: Iran proposes Hormuz reopening deal; nuclear talks deferred
description: Iran conveyed a new proposal to the US through Pakistani, Egyptian, Turkish, and Qatari mediators offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend the ceasefire toward a permanent end to fighting, with nuclear negotiations deferred until after the US lifts its naval blockade, Axios reported. FM Araghchi told mediators over the weekend that there is no consensus within Iran's leadership on how to address US demands. White House spokesperson Olivia Wales responded: 'The United States holds the cards and will only make a deal that puts the American people first, never allowing Iran to have a nuclear weapon.' Trump separately told reporters Iran has 'about three days' before the blockade's full effects take hold. The proposal marked a significant tactical shift from Tehran's earlier insistence on simultaneous nuclear and Hormuz negotiations.

title: IDF strikes Beqaa Valley for first time in 3 weeks; 14 killed in Lebanon
description: The IDF launched airstrikes against Hezbollah infrastructure in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley — the first strikes in the eastern region in three weeks — along with targets in southern Lebanon, killing 14 people and wounding 37, according to Haaretz. The IDF destroyed a Bint Jbeil sector headquarters, triggering secondary explosions indicating stored weapons, and killed three Hezbollah operatives near the forward defense line. IDF helicopter teams from Unit 669 evacuated wounded soldiers under active Hezbollah drone fire, intercepting one drone while another detonated near troops. The strikes expanded Israel's target set beyond the southern security zone into Hezbollah's eastern logistics heartland, a day after Sgt. Idan Fooks was killed by a Hezbollah drone. Lebanon's cumulative war toll rose to 2,509 killed and over 7,750 wounded.

title: Iran bans steel exports through May 30 after strikes destroy 25% of capacity
description: Iran banned all steel slab and sheet exports through May 30, the first wartime trade restriction on a non-energy industrial sector. The ban followed Israeli and US strikes that destroyed approximately 10 million tons of annual steel production capacity — roughly 25-30% of Iran's total, according to Etemad newspaper. The steel industry, Iran's second-largest export sector after oil, had already been under EU sanctions banning trade in Iranian steel and metals. The export halt signaled that wartime damage to industrial infrastructure was beginning to constrain Iran's ability to maintain civilian economic activity, not just military operations.

title: Araghchi arrives in Russia to brief Putin on stalled war diplomacy
description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met President Vladimir Putin at the Boris Yeltsin Presidential Library in St. Petersburg — the most senior Iranian diplomatic engagement with Moscow since the war began. Putin told Araghchi: 'We see how courageously and heroically the Iranian people are fighting for their independence and sovereignty,' pledging 'we will do everything that serves your interests...so that peace can be achieved as soon as possible.' Araghchi flew from Oman after stops in Pakistan and meetings with Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said, continuing an intensive regional tour as US-Iran negotiations remain frozen. Russia's Vienna envoy Mikhail Ulyanov publicly criticized Washington's approach, saying officials should abandon 'blackmail' and ultimatums. The meeting signals Iran is securing Russian backing to strengthen its negotiating position before any resumption of talks.

title: Hezbollah drone kills IDF Sgt. Idan Fooks; first direct truce combat death
description: Hezbollah struck IDF soldiers in southern Lebanon with an explosive-laden drone, killing 19-year-old Cpl. Idan Fooks of the 7th Armored Brigade's 77th Battalion (posthumously promoted to sergeant) and wounding six others — including an officer and three soldiers with severe injuries. Fooks, from Petah Tikva, was the third Israeli soldier killed since the Lebanon ceasefire began April 17, but the first killed by a direct Hezbollah attack during the truce. Senior Israeli officials warned American counterparts that 'if Hezbollah continues attacking IDF soldiers, Israel will be unable to maintain its current measured response.' The IDF launched retaliatory airstrikes and artillery across southern Lebanon targeting Hezbollah operatives and infrastructure. Separately, the Confrontation Line Forum declared an 'orange' alert, announcing border school closures starting Tuesday, and the Home Front Command restricted gatherings to 1,500 in northern border communities.

title: Bennett and Lapid merge parties to challenge Netanyahu in wartime elections
description: Former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced a party merger under the banner 'Together, Led by Bennett,' uniting their factions to challenge Netanyahu in elections that must be held before October. Bennett declared: 'I am taking the most Zionist and most patriotic step we have ever taken, for our country. The era of division is over.' An N12 poll from April 23 showed the combined ticket could win 28 Knesset seats against Likud's 25, making it the first credible electoral threat to Netanyahu's war leadership. Lapid's Yesh Atid had fallen to 7 seats alone, down from 24. The merger was the most significant Israeli political realignment since the war began, framing the upcoming election as a referendum on Netanyahu's conduct of the conflict.

title: Pezeshkian tells Pakistan: Iran won't negotiate under US blockade
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif in a 50-minute phone call that Tehran rejects 'imposed negotiations' under threats or siege, demanding the US 'first remove operational obstacles, including the blockade' before any talks can proceed. Pezeshkian said ongoing US actions were 'undermining trust and complicating any path to dialogue.' The statement hardened Iran's diplomatic position beyond FM Araghchi's earlier framework proposal, effectively conditioning any future negotiations on the lifting of the naval blockade — the same blockade the US considers its primary leverage. Araghchi, meanwhile, arrived in Muscat to meet Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq before a planned return to Islamabad and onward trip to Russia, while part of his delegation flew back to Tehran to 'consult and obtain the necessary instructions on issues related to ending the war.'

title: Israeli strikes kill 6 in Yohmor al-Shaqeef and Safad al-Battikh during ceasefire
description: Israeli forces struck a truck and a motorbike in the town of Yohmor al-Shaqeef in the Nabatieh district, killing four people. A separate airstrike on Safad al-Battikh in the Bint Jbeil district killed two and wounded 17. The IDF said it 'eliminated' three Hezbollah operatives in a vehicle 'loaded with weapons,' another on a motorcycle, and two armed operatives elsewhere. The strikes came one day after Netanyahu ordered the military to 'forcefully attack Hezbollah targets' and marked the third consecutive day of lethal Israeli operations in Lebanon since the ceasefire was extended for three weeks on April 23. Lebanon's cumulative war death toll stood at 2,491 killed and 7,719 wounded.

title: Pezeshkian urges Iranians to conserve electricity amid war damage
description: President Pezeshkian called on Iranians to reduce electricity consumption, saying: 'We have asked our dear people a simple request — reduce their own electricity and energy consumption. Instead of 10 lights, two lights should be turned on in the house.' He warned that while there were no shortages 'at present,' the US and Israel aimed to sow 'dissatisfaction' among the Iranian people by targeting infrastructure. Iran generates nearly 80% of its electricity from natural gas, but aging infrastructure, sanctions-blocked investment, and wartime damage to power facilities have strained the grid. Trump has repeatedly threatened to destroy Iran's power plants but has not followed through during the ceasefire. The appeal was the first public acknowledgment by Iran's president that the war is affecting civilian energy supply.

title: Trump cancels Witkoff/Kushner Pakistan trip; Araghchi leaves with no deal
description: President Trump cancelled envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's planned trip to Islamabad for a third round of US-Iran talks. Trump told Fox News: 'I said, nope, you're not making an 18-hour flight to go there. We have all the cards.' The cancellation came after Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi departed Pakistan without a breakthrough, having presented what he called 'a workable framework to permanently end the war' to Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif, Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, and FM Ishaq Dar. Araghchi posted on X: 'Have yet to see if the U.S. is truly serious about diplomacy.' He flew to Muscat, Oman, with plans to visit Russia before returning to Islamabad. Trump said he received a new proposal from Tehran offering 'a lot but not enough,' and blamed 'tremendous infighting and confusion' within Iran's leadership. The collapse marked the third failed attempt at direct talks since the April 8 ceasefire.

title: Hezbollah fires projectiles at northern Israel; Netanyahu orders strikes 'with force'
description: Hezbollah launched two projectiles at northern Israel, triggering air raid sirens in Manara, Margaliot, and Misgav Am — the second ceasefire violation since the truce began April 16. The IDF intercepted one projectile; the other landed in an open area with no casualties. Hezbollah also launched explosive drones toward Israeli troops south of the Forward Defense Line, detonating near soldiers without causing injuries. PM Netanyahu ordered the IDF to strike Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon 'with force,' and the military struck multiple Hezbollah structures, killed three terrorists on a motorcycle, and hit two armed operatives near the Litani River. Reserve paratroopers also uncovered anti-tank missiles in a weapons storage facility and dismantled infrastructure in the Bint Jbeil area. Israel separately requested US pressure on Lebanon to act against Hezbollah outside the IDF's Forward Defense Line, warning the ceasefire could collapse without American intervention.

title: USS Pinckney intercepts shadow fleet tanker MV Sevan; 37th vessel redirected
description: The guided-missile destroyer USS Pinckney (DDG-91) intercepted the Iranian-linked tanker M/V Sevan in the Arabian Sea after a helicopter from the Pinckney tracked and identified the vessel. The Sevan, one of 19 vessels sanctioned by Treasury for transporting billions of dollars in Iranian oil, gas, propane, and butane to foreign markets, was forced to turn back toward an Iranian port under escort. CENTCOM stated: 'The merchant vessel is currently complying with U.S. military direction to turn back to Iran under escort.' The interception brought the total number of vessels redirected since the April 13 blockade began to 37. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said the blockade now extends 'from the Gulf of Oman to other waters,' signaling an expanding enforcement perimeter.

title: Iran executes Erfan Kiani over alleged Mossad links and protest charges
description: Iran hanged Erfan Kiani in the early hours of Saturday after the Supreme Court upheld his death sentence. The judiciary-affiliated Mizan news agency said Kiani was convicted of acting as a 'hired thug of Mossad,' destruction and arson of public and private property, wielding a machete, and 'spreading fear and terror across Isfahan' during nationwide protests in January. Tasnim News Agency described him as one of the 'main operatives' in a Mossad-assigned mission during the Isfahan unrest. No evidence of the alleged Mossad link was publicly presented. Human rights group Hengaw reported Kiani was the eighth protest detainee executed in Iranian prisons since the war began on February 28, part of a pattern in which Tehran has accelerated political executions under wartime emergency — averaging one execution every 48 hours, more than half the total political executions recorded in all of 2025.

title: Iran reopens Tehran airport; first international flights in 56 days
description: Iran's Imam Khomeini International Airport resumed international flights on April 25, ending a 56-day shutdown caused by the war. State-owned Iran Air and Mahan Air operated the first departures to Istanbul, Muscat, and Medina; Flightradar24 confirmed at least 3 flights to Istanbul departed Saturday morning. The Civil Aviation Organisation of Iran (CAO) confirmed that technical checks were complete and that 'no-fly zones' over western and central Iran had been lifted for commercial traffic. The reopening is part of a phased plan to gradually restore full passenger services while monitoring the security situation. The closure had stranded thousands of Iranian citizens abroad and severely disrupted the flow of essential medical supplies.

title: IDF kills 8 in Lebanon despite extended ceasefire; death toll reaches 2,491
description: Israeli forces killed 6 Hezbollah fighters in a firefight in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, after an IDF Oketz Unit canine revealed the location of a Hezbollah cell — all 6 were killed within 90 minutes of identification. The IDF canine was killed in the operation. Separately, an Israeli airstrike killed 2 people in the town of Touline, and artillery fire wounded several in Yater. Hezbollah lawmaker Ali Fayyad stated: 'The ceasefire is meaningless in light of Israel's insistence on hostile acts, including assassinations, shelling, and gunfire.' The Lebanese Health Ministry updated the war's toll to 2,491 killed and 7,719 wounded since March 2. PM Netanyahu accused Hezbollah of 'trying to sabotage' the ceasefire. UN Secretary-General Guterres called for full compliance with cessation of hostilities.

title: Treasury freezes $344M in cryptocurrency linked to Iran's Central Bank
description: As part of the 'Economic Fury' sanctions package, OFAC sanctioned multiple cryptocurrency wallets attributed to the Central Bank of Iran, with links to the IRGC-Qods Force and Hezbollah. Tether coordinated with OFAC to freeze $344.2 million in USDT across two wallet addresses. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the action, which targeted Iran's digital-asset sanctions evasion infrastructure. Chainalysis estimates Iran's crypto ecosystem reached approximately $7.8 billion in 2025, with IRGC-linked activity representing roughly half by Q4. The crypto freeze complemented the same day's Hengli refinery and shadow fleet sanctions, extending 'Economic Fury' from physical oil infrastructure into digital finance.

title: 11-year-old Nesya Karadi dies from Passover eve cluster munition wounds
description: Nesya Karadi, 11, died at Sheba Medical Center near Tel Aviv from wounds sustained in an Iranian cluster munition strike on Bnei Brak on Passover eve (April 1). The girl was asleep when the siren sounded and was critically injured by a submunition before she could reach shelter. Her parents, Rabbi Elazar and Hila Karadi, had named her Nesya ('miracle of God') after her birth, which they described as miraculous. She is the 21st person killed by Iranian missile strikes in Israel since February 28, bringing the war's total Israeli death toll to 28. The death came as US envoys prepared for a third round of talks with Iran in Islamabad.

title: Witkoff and Kushner fly to Islamabad as Araghchi arrives for Iran talks
description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt announced that US special envoy Steve Witkoff and senior adviser Jared Kushner would travel to Islamabad on Saturday morning for Pakistan-mediated talks with Iran — the third round of US-Iran negotiations since the ceasefire. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad Friday, but Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei stated: 'No meeting is planned to take place between Iran and the U.S.' VP Vance, who led the first Islamabad delegation, will not attend; the White House said he is 'on standby.' Araghchi will present Iran's 'considerations regarding ending the imposed war,' according to Iranian state media. Trump told Reuters that Iran is 'making an offer' and talks are 'set to resume.' The contradictory signals — Washington announcing direct talks, Tehran denying them — reprised the pattern from every prior negotiating round.

title: Netanyahu reveals he hid prostate cancer diagnosis during Iran war
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu disclosed that he was diagnosed with early-stage prostate cancer and underwent radiation therapy approximately two months earlier — concealing his condition throughout the most intense phase of the Iran war. 'I requested to delay its publication by two months so that it would not be released at the height of the war,' Netanyahu said, citing concern it would generate 'false propaganda against Israel.' Dr. Aharon Popovtser, director of Hadassah Hospital's oncology unit, confirmed the cancer was detected during routine monitoring after December 2024 prostate surgery and stated: 'We can say based on the findings of these tests that the disease has disappeared.' Netanyahu, 76, had faced AI-generated death hoaxes in March, recording a Jerusalem café video to refute them. The revelation raised questions about wartime decision-making by a leader undergoing cancer treatment while directing operations against Iran.

title: Treasury sanctions China's Hengli refinery and ~40 shippers over Iranian oil
description: The US Treasury Department sanctioned Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery Co., Ltd. — China's second-largest independent refinery with 400,000 barrels/day capacity — for processing Iranian crude since at least 2023. OFAC simultaneously designated approximately 40 shipping companies and 19 'shadow fleet' vessels responsible for transporting billions of dollars' worth of Iranian crude oil, LPG, and petrochemicals. The sanctions package, branded 'Economic Fury,' targeted the global network enabling Iran's oil exports despite the blockade. The action came weeks before a planned Trump-Xi meeting, deliberately escalating US-China economic friction over Iran. Hengli had generated 'hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue for the Iranian military,' according to Treasury. The sanctions represented the largest single-day Iran-related enforcement action of the war.

title: Trump extends Jones Act waiver 90 days to ease wartime fuel costs
description: The Trump administration extended its Jones Act waiver by 90 days through mid-August, allowing foreign-flagged tankers to transport oil between US ports — a measure normally prohibited to protect domestic shipping. The original 60-day waiver, issued March 18 as the Hormuz closure removed one-fifth of global oil supply, enabled foreign tankers to move approximately 9 million barrels of oil, boosting effective domestic shipping capacity by about 70%. White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said: 'This waiver extension provides both certainty and stability for the US and global economies.' The extension reflected political urgency: a Reuters/Ipsos poll released the same day found 77% of registered voters blame Trump for rising gas prices, including 55% of Republicans. US gas averaged $4.06/gallon, up from $2.98 before the war. Analysts questioned whether the waiver meaningfully reduces consumer prices, with the Center for American Progress estimating only a 3-cent reduction on the East Coast.

title: Baker Hughes: Strait of Hormuz may not fully reopen until H2 2026
description: Baker Hughes CFO Ahmed Moghal told investors that the oilfield services giant is planning on the assumption that the US-Iran conflict continues through end of June and the Strait of Hormuz may not be fully operational until the second half of 2026. The assessment aligned with a Dallas Fed Energy Survey in which nearly 80% of oil and gas executives said the strait will not reopen until August or later. The closure has removed 10% of global oil volumes and 20% of global LNG supplies. Baker Hughes and rival SLB both reported rising oil exploration spending as producers outside the Gulf rush to fill the supply gap, with Baker Hughes noting 'persistent risk premiums for oil and LNG prices.' Brent crude traded above $105/barrel. The industry consensus contradicted optimistic White House messaging about an imminent diplomatic resolution.

title: Pentagon email floats suspending Spain from NATO over Iran war
description: Reuters reported that an internal Pentagon email outlined options to punish NATO allies who refused to support US operations in the Iran war, including suspending Spain from the alliance and reassessing US diplomatic backing for Britain's Falkland Islands claim. The email described access, basing, and overflight rights as 'just the absolute baseline for NATO' and aimed at 'decreasing the sense of entitlement on the part of the Europeans.' Spain banned the use of its Rota and Moron bases and closed its airspace to all US military aircraft involved in the war. Pentagon Press Secretary Kingsley Wilson confirmed the document's thrust: 'The War Department will ensure that the president has credible options to ensure that our allies are no longer a paper tiger and do their part.' NATO's founding charter contains no mechanism to expel or suspend a member state. The email escalated tensions beyond the previously reported White House 'naughty and nice' ranking of allies, moving from classification to proposed punitive action.

title: Hezbollah fires 4 rockets at Shtula; IDF destroys launchers within minutes
description: Hezbollah fired four rockets at the northern Israeli border community of Shtula at approximately 11:30 PM Thursday, the first rocket attack since the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire took effect April 16. The IDF said all rockets that crossed the border were intercepted. Hezbollah stated the salvo was 'in defence of Lebanon and its people, and in response to the Israeli enemy's violation of the ceasefire and its targeting of the town of Yater in southern Lebanon.' The IDF said it destroyed the launcher used in the attack 'within several minutes,' along with a second launcher 'that was loaded and ready to be launched' at Israeli troops. The exchange underscored the fragility of the truce hours after Trump announced a three-week extension and as Brent crude surged above $106/barrel — the first time above $100 in two weeks.

title: USS George H.W. Bush enters CENTCOM; US fields 3 carriers in region
description: The aircraft carrier USS George H.W. Bush and its strike group — including destroyers USS Mason, USS Donald Cook, and USS Ross with Destroyer Squadron 22 — entered the US Central Command area of responsibility after sailing around the Horn of Africa. The arrival gave the US three carrier strike groups in the Middle East simultaneously, joining the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln. The Bush carries a high-energy laser weapon tested in partnership with AeroVironment and the US Army in October 2025, the first such system deployed to a combat theater. USNI News confirmed the carrier's entry into CENTCOM. The three-carrier posture represents the largest US naval concentration in the region since the war began, with 50,000+ US service members now deployed despite the indefinite ceasefire.

title: UK-France host 30+ nation Hormuz military planning conference at Northwood
description: Military planners from over 30 nations concluded a two-day conference at the UK's Permanent Joint Headquarters at Northwood, north London, advancing detailed planning for a multinational mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. UK Defence Secretary John Healey said: 'The task, today and tomorrow, is to translate the diplomatic consensus into a joint plan to safeguard freedom of navigation.' The conference discussed command and control structures, military capabilities, and force deployment, aiming to establish 'an independent and strictly defensive multinational mission to protect merchant vessels, reassure commercial shipping operators and conduct mine clearance operations.' Plans will activate 'as soon as conditions permit, following a sustainable ceasefire agreement.' The conference built on the 51-nation Paris summit where Macron and Starmer called for 'unconditional, unrestricted, and immediate re-opening' of the strait.

title: US Navy seizes supertanker M/T Majestic X carrying Iranian oil in Indian Ocean
description: US military forces boarded and seized the Guyana-flagged supertanker M/T Majestic X (formerly Phonix) in the Indian Ocean between Sri Lanka and Indonesia. The vessel, a Very Large Crude Carrier capable of transporting 2 million barrels of oil, was bound for Zhoushan, China. The US Treasury Department had sanctioned the ship in 2024 for smuggling Iranian crude. The Pentagon stated: 'We will continue global maritime enforcement to disrupt illicit networks and interdict vessels providing material support to Iran, wherever they operate.' The seizure — occurring in the INDOPACOM area of responsibility, far from the Middle East theater — demonstrated the global reach of US enforcement operations and came one day after the IRGC seized two container ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: China, Russia, Iran hold joint IAEA meeting on nuclear program
description: Chinese, Russian, and Iranian officials met jointly with IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi on April 24 to discuss Iran's nuclear program, Chinese state media reported. The trilateral meeting — the first of its kind during the war — came two days before a planned third round of US-Iran negotiations scheduled for April 26 in Muscat, Oman. The coordinated diplomatic front underscored Beijing and Moscow's effort to position themselves as counterweights to Washington's demands for permanent Iranian nuclear disarmament. Russia and China have consistently opposed the reimposition of UN 'snapback' sanctions on Iran, challenging their legality at the Security Council. The meeting followed Lavrov's earlier visit to Beijing where he and Xi reaffirmed strategic cooperation, and preceded Pakistan's continued shuttle diplomacy to revive stalled US-Iran talks.

title: Trump orders Navy to 'shoot and kill' boats laying mines in Hormuz
description: President Trump posted on Truth Social: 'I have ordered the United States Navy to shoot and kill any boat, small boats though they may be...that is putting mines in the waters of the Strait of Hormuz. There is to be no hesitation.' He simultaneously ordered mine-sweeping operations to continue 'at a tripled-up level.' The directive came as only 3 tankers crossed the strait on Wednesday versus a pre-war daily average of 129, and as the Pentagon assessed Iran had deployed 20+ mines in the waterway. Trump added: 'No ship can enter or leave without the approval of the United States Navy. It is Sealed up Tight, until such time as Iran is able to make a DEAL.' The order risked jeopardizing the fragile ceasefire, with the US Navy having already turned back 33 vessels since the blockade began April 13.

title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extended 3 weeks after White House talks
description: President Trump announced a three-week extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire following a second round of talks at the White House — the first direct Israel-Lebanon negotiations since 1993. Trump, VP Vance, Secretary of State Rubio, Ambassador to Israel Huckabee, and Ambassador to Lebanon Issa met with Israeli and Lebanese representatives in the Oval Office. Trump posted: 'The Ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon will be extended by THREE WEEKS.' He said he looks forward to hosting PM Netanyahu and President Aoun at the White House during the extended period. Lebanese officials cautioned that a trilateral summit is unlikely while Israel occupies 6% of Lebanon's territory and continues strikes despite the truce. The original 10-day ceasefire had begun April 16. Rubio credited Trump's involvement for making the extension possible.

title: Katz: Israel awaiting US 'green light' to return Iran to 'Stone Age'
description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared that Israel is 'prepared to renew the war against Iran' and awaiting US authorization. 'The IDF is ready both defensively and offensively, and the targets have been marked,' Katz said. He specified two objectives: 'first and foremost to complete the elimination of the Khamenei dynasty' and to 'return Iran to the Dark Age and the Stone Age by destroying key energy and electricity facilities and dismantling its national economic infrastructure.' The remarks came one day after Trump extended the Iran ceasefire indefinitely, and as planned US-Iran talks in Pakistan remained in limbo after Tehran called its decision not to participate 'definitive.' Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father as supreme leader after the Feb 28 strike, has not appeared publicly.

title: Iran collects first toll revenue from ships transiting Strait of Hormuz
description: Iran announced it had collected its first revenue from tolls imposed on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Parliament Deputy Speaker Hamidreza Haji Babaei told Tasnim News Agency: 'First revenues from transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz have been deposited into the Central Bank account.' Charges vary by vessel type, cargo volume, and assessed risk level; analysts project up to $20 million in daily revenue from oil tankers alone. Iran's central bank denied earlier reports that payments were being accepted in cryptocurrency and Chinese yuan, insisting only cash currency was used. The toll system formalizes Iran's wartime control of the strait, transforming it from a military chokepoint into a revenue-generating mechanism managed by the IRGC — a development first signaled when Iran's parliament began drafting a Hormuz toll law in late March.

title: IEA chief: 'biggest energy security threat in history' with 13M barrels/day lost
description: IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol warned on Wednesday that the world faces 'the biggest energy security threat in history,' with 13 million barrels per day of oil removed from global markets — far exceeding the 5 million bpd lost in each of the 1970s oil crises. Birol noted that 100 billion cubic meters of natural gas have also been lost, surpassing the 75 billion cubic meters disrupted by the Ukraine war. Only 3 tankers crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday versus a pre-war daily average of 129. Brent crude traded above $103/barrel Thursday morning after briefly dipping below $100 the previous week. The IEA had already released 400 million barrels of emergency reserves in early March. Birol said reopening the strait is 'the cure,' as mine-clearing alone could take six months even after hostilities end.

title: Pezeshkian says Iran open to dialogue but US blockade prevents talks
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian posted on X that Tehran 'wants to continue peace talks' but that the 'US' breach of commitments, blockade and threats are the main obstacles to genuine negotiations.' He accused Washington of 'endless hypocritical rhetoric and contradiction between claims and actions,' responding directly to Trump's indefinite ceasefire extension while maintaining the naval blockade. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf separately reiterated that Iran will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz while the US blockade persists, calling it a 'blatant violation' of ceasefire terms. Foreign ministry spokesman Baqaei stressed diplomacy must serve Iranian 'national interests and security.' The statements marked Iran's first coordinated presidential-level response to Trump's open-ended ceasefire extension.

title: Pentagon tells Congress Hormuz mine-clearing could take 6 months
description: A senior Defense Department official told the House Armed Services Committee in a classified briefing that clearing Iranian mines from the Strait of Hormuz could take at least six months, and that no mine-clearing operation is likely to begin until the war ends. The Pentagon assessed that Iran deployed 20 or more mines in and around the strait. The timeline contradicts Trump's recent Truth Social claim that Iran 'with the help of the United States' had removed or was removing all sea mines. The assessment alarmed both Democrats and Republicans, signaling that oil and gasoline prices may remain elevated long after a peace agreement is reached. The Washington Post first reported the briefing.

title: Politico: White House compiles NATO 'naughty and nice' list over Iran war
description: Politico reported that the Trump administration compiled a classified ranking of NATO member states based on their support for the US war against Iran, prepared ahead of NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte's April 8-12 Washington visit. Three European diplomats and a Pentagon official confirmed the document's existence. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth stated: 'Model allies that step up will receive our special favor. Allies that still fail to do their part for collective defense will face consequences.' Romania and Poland, which opened bases for Operation Epic Fury, are on the 'good' list. Spain, France, and the UK — which refused or delayed assistance — are on the blacklist. The ranking deepens the transatlantic rift, coming weeks after NATO formally rejected Trump's call for military support.

title: Pentagon removes 15 wounded troops from Iran war casualty count
description: The Pentagon's official casualty tally dropped from 428 to 413 wounded-in-action on Tuesday without public explanation, The Intercept reported. The count had risen steadily from 385 on the day the ceasefire took effect (April 8) to 428 on Monday. A US government official called the unexplained removal 'the definition of a cover-up.' Two Pentagon spokespersons said they were unable to field questions, claiming only the 'duty officer' could respond but that person was unavailable. The Intercept had previously documented broader patterns of casualty undercounting, including the omission of 200+ sailors injured in the USS Gerald R. Ford fire and the death of Maj. Sorffly Davius at Camp Buehring, Kuwait. Official US war dead remain listed at 13.

title: USS George H.W. Bush carrier group 3-5 days from Middle East; US to field 3 carriers
description: The USS George H.W. Bush carrier strike group, which departed Norfolk on March 31 with Carrier Air Wing 7 and 5,000+ sailors, is expected to arrive in the Middle East within 3-5 days after transiting around the Horn of Africa, Ynet reported. Its arrival will give the US three carrier strike groups in the region — the most since the war began. Simultaneously, CBS News reported additional deployments including three missile destroyers, an amphibious assault ship carrying 2,500 Marines, and a dock landing ship, pushing total US forces in the region above 50,000 service members, compared to 30,000-40,000 pre-war. The buildup continued despite the indefinite ceasefire extension, with 17 warships and 100+ aircraft enforcing the naval blockade.

title: Trump says 'no time frame' for ending Iran war, denies midterms influence
description: President Trump told Fox News on Wednesday there is 'no time frame' and 'no time pressure' on the extended ceasefire or pending peace talks with Iran, a significant shift from his initial prediction that the war would last four to six weeks. Asked whether the November 2026 midterm elections were driving his desire to end the conflict, Trump responded: 'People say I want to get it over because of the midterms, not true.' The statement came one day after he extended the ceasefire indefinitely, and as Iran continued to refuse to send a delegation for a second round of talks. Brent crude held near $98/barrel.

title: Israeli strike kills journalist Amal Khalil in al-Tiri; rescue workers fired on
description: An Israeli airstrike struck a building in the southern Lebanese village of al-Tiri where Al-Akhbar newspaper reporter Amal Khalil and freelance photojournalist Zeinab Faraj had taken shelter while covering the war. The strike hit shortly after a separate strike on a civilian vehicle on the town's main road. Rescue workers reached Faraj, who was seriously wounded, but Israeli forces fired on the rescue team, forcing them to halt attempts to reach Khalil. Her body was recovered nearly six hours later, shortly before midnight. The Committee to Protect Journalists confirmed her death. Khalil had covered the Israel-Hezbollah conflict since October 2023 and is the fourth media worker killed by Israel in Lebanon since the war began in March. At least five people were killed in Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon on the same day.

title: Pentagon fires Navy Secretary Phelan; Hung Cao takes acting role during blockade
description: Navy Secretary John Phelan departed the Trump administration 'effective immediately' on Wednesday, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell announced on behalf of Secretary of War Hegseth. No reason was given for the abrupt exit, which came one day after Phelan delivered a keynote at the Sea-Air-Space symposium touting Trump's next-generation battleship initiative. Undersecretary Hung Cao — a Naval Academy graduate, former special operations officer, and 2024 Virginia GOP Senate nominee — assumed the acting role. The departure marks the second top Pentagon civilian ousted during the war, following Hegseth's firing of Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George on April 3. Phelan's exit came as the Navy enforces the blockade of Iranian ports with 16+ warships and has interdicted or turned back 31 vessels.

title: Senate rejects 5th Iran war powers resolution 46-51; weekly votes pledged
description: The Senate for a fifth time rejected a resolution to constrain President Trump's authority to wage war on Iran, voting 46-51 on a discharge motion forced by Sen. Tammy Baldwin (D-WI). The resolution would have required withdrawal of US forces unless Congress authorized further action. Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA) again voted with Republicans against the measure; Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY) again crossed the aisle to support it. Three senators did not vote: Chuck Grassley (R-IA), Dave McCormick (R-PA), and Mark Warner (D-VA). Senate Minority Leader Schumer said: 'Every day we hear new promises from the Trump administration — that victory has been achieved, that peace is at hand — and every day we see the opposite.' Democrats vowed to force weekly votes as long as the war persists. The margin has narrowed from the initial 40-55 on March 4.

title: Second French UNIFIL peacekeeper dies from Hezbollah ambush wounds in Lebanon
description: Corporal Anicet Girardin of France's 132nd Cynotechnical Infantry Regiment died Wednesday from wounds sustained in a weekend ambush in southern Lebanon's Ghanduriyeh. President Macron announced: 'Corporal Anicet Girardin, brought home yesterday from Lebanon where he was badly wounded by Hezbollah fighters, died this morning of the consequences of his wounds.' Girardin was part of an explosive ordnance disposal team clearing a booby-trapped road to re-establish access to isolated UNIFIL positions when the team came under attack. Staff Sergeant Florian Montorio of the 17th Parachute Engineer Regiment was killed in the same ambush. Hezbollah denied responsibility. Girardin is the third French soldier killed in the war overall, after Montorio and Arnaud Frion, who died from an Iranian drone strike in Iraq's Kurdistan region. Both Macron and UN Secretary General Guterres blamed Hezbollah for the attack.

title: Lufthansa cancels 20,000 flights through October as jet fuel doubles from war
description: Lufthansa Group announced it will remove 20,000 short-haul European flights from its summer schedule through October, saving approximately 40,000 metric tonnes of jet fuel. European jet fuel has reached $188 per barrel, a 106.5% year-over-year increase driven by the Hormuz closure and Gulf refinery damage. The first wave of 120 daily cancellations took effect immediately, targeting unprofitable routes at Frankfurt and Munich hubs. Three routes were eliminated entirely: Bydgoszcz and Rzeszów in Poland, and Stavanger in Norway. Other European carriers followed suit: SAS cut 1,000 flights, KLM cancelled 160, Norse Atlantic axed transatlantic routes, and Aer Lingus reduced 500 flights — all citing the Iran war fuel crisis. The IEA had warned days earlier that Europe has roughly six weeks of jet fuel remaining.

title: IRGC fires on 3 container ships in Hormuz and seizes 2 — hours after ceasefire extension
description: Hours after Trump extended the ceasefire, the IRGC Navy attacked three container ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz in rapid succession. At approximately 3:55 UTC, an IRGC gunboat fired machine guns and RPGs at the Liberia-flagged, Greek-owned Epaminondas without radio warning 15 nautical miles northeast of Oman, causing heavy damage to the bridge despite the vessel having transit permission. At 6:38 UTC, the Panama-flagged Euphoria (UAE-owned) was fired upon 8 nautical miles west of Iran with no damage. The Panama-flagged MSC Francesca was then hit 6 nautical miles off Iran's coast, sustaining hull and accommodation damage. The IRGC subsequently seized the Epaminondas and MSC Francesca, claiming they were 'operating without required authorisation and manipulating navigation systems,' and transferred both to Iranian territorial waters. UKMTO and BBC Verify confirmed all three attacks. No casualties were reported. Brent crude rose to $98.48 before settling at $97.91.

title: EU launches €222B AccelerateEU energy crisis package at Cyprus summit
description: The European Commission formally proposed the AccelerateEU package at a two-day EU summit in Cyprus dominated by the energy crisis and Iran war fallout. The plan redirects €184 billion in unspent National Recovery and Resilience Plan funds and €38 billion in Cohesion funds toward energy relief measures including mandatory one-day-per-week telework for companies, energy vouchers for vulnerable households, temporary excise duty reductions, optimized jet fuel distribution between member states, discounted public transit, and subsidized heat pump leasing. Commissioner Dan Jorgensen warned the 'oil price crisis could last months or years even if peace is struck.' Transport Commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas said emergency stocks exist but 'will only be released if necessary.' The IEA had warned days earlier that Europe has roughly six weeks of jet fuel remaining. EU hydrocarbon spending has risen over €22 billion since hostilities began.

title: Trump claims Iran 'collapsing financially,' losing $500M daily from Hormuz closure
description: President Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran is 'collapsing financially' and losing '$500 Million a day' from the Strait of Hormuz closure, claiming Tehran's 'Military and Police are complaining that they are not getting paid.' He added that intermediaries had approached him 'four days ago, saying, Sir, Iran wants to open up the Strait immediately.' Iran's Agriculture Minister Gholamreza Nouri countered that the US blockade has had 'minimal impact,' citing that '85 percent of agricultural products and basic goods are produced domestically.' China's foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun warned the region stands at a 'critical juncture transitioning between war and peace.' The statements came as 20,000 seafarers and approximately 2,000 ships remained stranded in the Gulf, and Iran reported over 2 million jobs lost due to the war and blockade.

title: Hezbollah fires rockets and drones at northern Israel — first attack since Lebanon ceasefire
description: Hezbollah fired rockets and attack drones at a military position in northern Israel on Tuesday, the first attack since the April 16 Israel-Lebanon ceasefire took effect. Hezbollah said it targeted a position that had been striking southern Lebanon, accusing Israel of 'attacking civilians and destroying homes in breach of the truce.' The IDF said it intercepted a drone, struck the rocket launcher, and called the attack a 'blatant violation' of the ceasefire. No casualties were reported on either side. The attack came one day before the second round of US-mediated Israel-Lebanon ambassador-level talks was scheduled in Washington for Thursday April 24. Lebanon's disaster management unit separately raised the cumulative war death toll to 2,454 killed and 7,658 wounded since March 2 — up from 2,387 on April 20, with the increase driven by body recovery in areas previously subjected to heavy Israeli strikes.

title: Trump extends Iran ceasefire indefinitely, cancels Vance Islamabad trip
description: President Trump reversed course and extended the Iran ceasefire with no new deadline, posting on Truth Social: 'Based on the fact that the Government of Iran is seriously fractured...we have been asked to hold our Attack on the Country of Iran until such time as their leaders and representatives can come up with a unified proposal.' He added the US military would 'continue the Blockade and, in all other respects, remain ready and able.' The White House then cancelled VP Vance's planned trip to Islamabad, saying the US awaits 'a unified proposal from the Iranians.' Pakistan PM Sharif thanked Trump for accepting his request to extend the truce. Ghalibaf adviser Mahdi Mohammadi dismissed the extension as 'means nothing,' calling the blockade 'no different from bombardment' and warning the extension was 'a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike.' Iran's semi-official Tasnim agency said Tehran's position would be 'officially announced later.' Brent crude spiked 3.14% to $98.48 before retreating; only 3 ships transited Hormuz in 24 hours.

title: US Treasury sanctions 14 entities supporting Iran's missile and drone programs
description: The Treasury Department sanctioned 14 individuals, entities, and aircraft in Iran, Turkey, and the UAE for procuring or transporting weapons components for Iran's UAV and ballistic missile programs and Mahan Air. Targets included Dubai-based Chabok FZCO, accused of procuring US-origin aircraft sensors and components for Mahan Air, and Iranian money exchanger Kamal Sabah Balkhkanlu. Treasury also identified two aircraft as blocked property of Mahan Air, which has transported IRGC operatives, weapons, and funds. Treasury stated the action aims to prevent Iran from 'reconstituting its production capacity' as the US 'continues to deplete Iran's ballistic missile inventories.' The sanctions were announced on the eve of the ceasefire deadline, even as the US publicly sought to restart negotiations — underscoring the administration's 'maximum pressure while negotiating' posture.

title: Vance departs for Islamabad; Iran state TV says no delegation has left for talks
description: Vice President JD Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner departed for Islamabad on Tuesday for a second round of Iran talks, with the ceasefire set to expire Wednesday evening Washington time. However, Iranian state television announced that 'no delegation from Iran has departed for Islamabad, whether it is the main or subsidiary delegation, primary or secondary,' contradicting earlier reports from Iranian sources that a delegation was expected Tuesday. Trump posted on Truth Social that 'Iran has Violated the Cease Fire numerous times!' while Iran's FM spokesman Baqaei reiterated Tehran has 'no plans for the next round of negotiation.' Brent crude traded at $94.89/barrel. The talks — if they occur — would be the most senior US-Iran engagement since the Round 1 collapse on April 12.

title: Ghalibaf warns Iran has prepared 'new cards on the battlefield' during ceasefire
description: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on social media Tuesday that Iran has used the two-week ceasefire to prepare militarily, stating: 'In the past two weeks, we have prepared to reveal new cards on the battlefield.' He criticized Trump for 'imposing a siege and violating the ceasefire' and reiterated Iran will not negotiate 'under the shadow of threats.' The IRGC separately warned it would target any vessel attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without authorization. Ghalibaf did not elaborate on what the 'new cards' entailed, but the statement implied Iran had rearmed, repositioned, or developed new capabilities during the truce — a signal that resumption of hostilities could involve escalated Iranian firepower.

title: Iran executes Amirali Mirjafari for alleged Mossad-linked mosque arson during January protests
description: Iran hanged Amirali Mirjafari at dawn on Tuesday for allegedly attempting to set fire to Tehran's Gholhak Grand Mosque and leading what authorities called a 'Mossad network's anti-security operation' during the January 2026 protests. The judiciary's Mizan News Agency reported the execution, stating Mirjafari confessed to setting 'fire to trash cans and motorcycles in Dowlat Street and near the Metro station' on January 9 — though notably the confession made no mention of the mosque. Amnesty International said Iranian courts 'rely on confessions obtained under duress' and that 11 men face imminent execution over protest participation after 'grossly unfair trials based on forced confessions.' UN Special Rapporteur Mai Sato noted 'at least 100 people were executed in January 2026 alone.' The execution brought wartime political killings to at least 13.

title: Netanyahu at Memorial Day says Iran war prevented 'another Holocaust'
description: Prime Minister Netanyahu told the state Memorial Day ceremony at Mount Herzl that 'the ayatollah regime in Iran planned another Holocaust. It sought to destroy us with nuclear weapons and thousands of ballistic missiles. Had we not acted decisively, the names Natanz, Fordo, and Isfahan might have joined Auschwitz, Majdanek, and Treblinka.' He credited Israel and the US for having 'dismantled that machinery of destruction in advance' and 'removed an immediate existential threat.' Separately, Mossad Director David Barnea revealed for the first time that an agent known only as 'Mem,' who died in a 2023 boat sinking on Lake Maggiore in Italy while working with Italian intelligence to prevent Iran from acquiring advanced weapons, had led operations that 'significantly influenced the success of the campaign against Iran.'

title: Israeli settlers kill two Palestinians including 13-year-old at Al-Mughayyir school
description: Israeli settlers opened fire near a school in the village of Al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, killing a 13-year-old student and a 38-year-old man and wounding four others, the Palestinian Red Crescent reported. Witnesses said five settlers — some in civilian clothing, some in military uniform — were herding livestock near the school when students came out to see who they were. The settlers opened fire at the school windows; the boy was killed after stepping outside to use the bathroom. The Israeli military said it was 'looking into the incident.' The attack occurred during Israel's Memorial Day commemorations and amid the broader regional war, during which settler violence in the West Bank has intensified under the cover of military operations in Lebanon and Iran.

title: Israel strikes Qaaqaaiyet el-Jisr and Khiam during Lebanon ceasefire; 6 wounded
description: Israeli forces struck the southern Lebanese towns of Qaaqaaiyet el-Jisr and Khiam during the 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, wounding six people in Qaaqaaiyet el-Jisr and demolishing homes in Khiam, according to Al Jazeera's live reporting. The strikes continued Israel's pattern of ceasefire violations in southern Lebanon, where the IDF maintains five divisions operating south of its self-declared 'forward defense line.' The attacks came as the State Department confirmed a second round of Israel-Lebanon direct talks would take place Thursday in Washington, with Lebanese diplomat Simon Karam leading Beirut's delegation. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated: 'These negotiations are not a weakness...They are a decision stemming from strength in our belief in our rights.'
