Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem rejected the talks as 'losing concessions.'

title: Trump tells Bloomberg ceasefire expires Wednesday evening; extension 'highly unlikely'
description: President Trump told Bloomberg News in a phone interview that the Iran ceasefire will end 'Wednesday evening Washington time' and that extending it is 'highly unlikely' if no deal is reached. He added the US naval blockade of Iranian ports 'stays in place until a deal is signed,' saying: 'I'm not opening it until a deal is signed.' The statement set a hard deadline of approximately 8 PM ET on Wednesday April 22 — clarifying what had been an ambiguous expiry date. Energy Secretary Chris Wright separately told CNN that the Strait of Hormuz will likely remain closed until a permanent deal is reached and that US gas prices, which hit a national average of $4.05/gallon, may not return below $3 'until next year.' The remarks came as the White House confirmed special envoy Steve Witkoff would depart Sunday night for Islamabad, though Iran had not confirmed participation in a second round of talks.

title: Iran executes two MEK members at Karaj prison; judiciary vows 'no leniency'
description: Iran executed Hamed Validi, 45, a civil engineer and father of one daughter, and Mohammad Masoum 'Nima' Shahi, 38, a technical worker, at Karaj Central Prison at dawn on April 20. Both were convicted of espionage linked to Mossad and membership in the People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK). They had been arrested on May 13, 2025 — one month before the war began — and sentenced by Branch 3 of the Revolutionary Court of Karaj, with the Supreme Court confirming the sentence by September 27, 2025. Their families and lawyers received no prior notice of the execution; the state-run Mizan News Agency announced it at 6:35 AM. The executions brought the wartime total to at least 12 political prisoners executed since hostilities began, part of what HRANA called 'a noticeable acceleration in executions.' Separately, Iran has seized assets of over 400 journalists and artists abroad for allegedly supporting 'hostile foreign actors.'

title: UAE dismantles Iran-linked Velayat-e Faqih terror cell; arrests 27 suspects
description: The UAE State Security Service announced it had dismantled a covert cell linked to Iran's Velayat-e Faqih doctrine and arrested 27 members. The suspects were charged with establishing and operating a secret organization from within the UAE, pledging allegiance to foreign entities, conducting clandestine recruitment and indoctrination of Emirati youth, collecting funds through unofficial channels and transferring them to 'suspicious foreign entities' abroad, and holding meetings with 'terrorist elements.' The State Security Service said the cell aimed to 'spread misleading ideas among Emirati youth and recruit them to serve foreign loyalties, incite against the country's foreign policy.' The names and mugshots of all 27 suspects were posted publicly. The arrests came amid the broader Iran war, during which the UAE has intercepted 537 ballistic missiles, 2,256 drones, and 26 cruise missiles, with 13 killed and 224 wounded.

title: Lebanon health ministry: 2,387 killed and 7,602 wounded since Israeli escalation began March 2
description: Lebanon's health ministry reported the cumulative death toll from Israeli attacks since the March 2 escalation had reached 2,387, with 7,602 wounded. The toll rose by 332 deaths since the April 12 count of 2,055 — meaning roughly 42 Lebanese were killed per day during the eight-day period that included the April 16 Israel-Lebanon ceasefire. Separately, the Israeli military released casualty data showing 15 IDF soldiers killed and 690 wounded (42 serious, 96 moderate, 552 minor) in the Lebanon ground operation, including 37 soldiers wounded in a single 24-hour period between April 18-19. The figures underscored that the Lebanon ceasefire had not halted the killing on either side, with Israel continuing strikes on southern towns and Hezbollah maintaining resistance against the IDF's five-division ground presence south of the Litani River.

title: Iran launches drone strikes on US warships in Gulf of Oman in retaliation for Touska seizure
description: Iran's armed forces launched drone strikes against US military vessels in the Gulf of Oman hours after the USS Spruance seized the Iranian cargo ship Touska. Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency reported the strikes came 'in response to the US attack on the Iranian vessel earlier in the day.' A Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters spokesman confirmed Iran 'intended to continue responding to piracy policy and attacks on behalf of the US side.' No damage to US vessels was reported, and neither CENTCOM nor Tehran disclosed the number of drones used or specific ships targeted. The strikes marked the first Iranian military action against US forces since the April 8 ceasefire took effect, raising the prospect of full hostilities resuming 48 hours before the truce expires.

title: Trump says Vance won't go to Islamabad over security; White House contradicts within hours
description: President Trump told ABC News that Vice President JD Vance would not travel to Islamabad for the second round of Iran talks, citing Secret Service concerns about a 24-hour turnaround to provide adequate security. Hours later, a White House official contradicted Trump, stating Vance would lead the US delegation as planned. Earlier in the day, UN Ambassador Mike Waltz and Energy Secretary Chris Wright had both publicly indicated Vance would lead the negotiations. The confusion unfolded as four US government aircraft with communications equipment landed at a Pakistan Air Force base on Sunday, and Pakistani authorities sealed Islamabad's Red Zone and deployed over 10,000 security personnel for the expected talks — preparations for a meeting Iran had already said it would not attend.

title: Israel exposes IRGC terror cell that planned drone attacks in Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Georgia
description: The Mossad, IDF, and Shin Bet announced in a joint statement they had exposed an IRGC-backed terror network that targeted Israeli officials, Western military installations, and energy infrastructure across multiple countries. The cell operated from Azerbaijan under the direction of two IRGC commanders killed during the war: Rahman Moqadam, head of the IRGC Intelligence Special Operations Division (Unit 4000), who recruited and trained operatives, and Mahdi Yekeh-Dehghan ('the Doctor'), who led the network in Azerbaijan. The cell planned explosive drone attacks on the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline in Turkey and Georgia, and targeted the Israeli embassy and a synagogue in Baku. Turkish authorities had arrested six suspects, including an Iranian national, in coordinated raids across five provinces in January after discovering intelligence-gathering activities.

title: IDF kills armed Hezbollah operative who crossed forward defense line in south Lebanon
description: Troops of the 769th 'Hiram' Regional Brigade killed an armed operative who crossed the IDF's newly declared forward defense line in southern Lebanon and approached soldiers 'in a manner that posed an immediate threat,' the IDF said. The killing came as the IDF published a map of its 'Forward Defense Line' on Telegram, revealing five divisions plus Israeli Navy forces operating simultaneously south of the line to 'dismantle Hezbollah terror infrastructure.' The IDF said it regards the Litani River as the new security boundary with Hezbollah and will remain in southern Lebanon indefinitely unless Hezbollah agrees to disarm. A Lebanese lawmaker, Ali Hassan Khalil (Hezbollah-aligned), accused Israel of 'varying degrees of destruction' in 39 occupied southern villages, calling the damage 'a clear war crime.'

title: Iran rejects second round of Islamabad talks via IRNA, cites US 'excessive demands'
description: Iran's official state news agency IRNA announced Tehran will not attend a second round of US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad, citing 'US excessive demands and unreasonable, unrealistic requests, repeated changes in positions, continued contradictory statements.' IRNA stated the 'continuation of the so-called naval blockade, which is considered a violation of the ceasefire understanding, along with threatening rhetoric' made talks impossible, concluding: 'Under these conditions, no clear prospect for productive talks is envisaged.' IRNA also accused Washington of a 'blame game,' claiming the US lied about Iran's participation to pressure Tehran. The rejection came hours after Trump announced he was dispatching VP Vance, envoy Witkoff, and Jared Kushner to Islamabad Monday — and two days before the ceasefire expires Wednesday.

title: USS Spruance fires on and seizes Iranian cargo ship Touska in Gulf of Oman
description: The USS Spruance, an Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, intercepted the Iranian-flagged cargo vessel Touska in the Gulf of Oman as it sailed toward Bandar Abbas. After six hours of ignored warnings, the Spruance directed the crew to evacuate the engine room and fired several rounds from its 5-inch MK 45 gun into the engine room, disabling propulsion. Marines from the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit boarded and took custody of the vessel, which was under US Treasury sanctions for 'prior history of illegal activity.' Trump announced the seizure on Truth Social, saying the Navy 'stopped them right in their tracks by blowing a hole in the engineroom.' Iran's joint military command called the boarding 'armed piracy' and a ceasefire violation, vowing the armed forces 'will soon respond and retaliate.' It was the first US attack on and seizure of a merchant vessel since the blockade began.

title: Trump threatens to 'blow up' Iran if no deal signed; sends Vance team to Islamabad
description: President Trump escalated rhetoric beyond his earlier 'got cute' remarks, telling Fox News: 'If they don't sign this thing, the whole country is going to get blown up.' On Truth Social he wrote: 'We're offering a very fair and reasonable DEAL, and I hope they take it because, if they don't, the United States is going to knock out every single Power Plant, and every single Bridge, in Iran.' He said the US was 'preparing to hit [Iran] harder than any country has ever been hit before.' Trump also claimed the blockade costs Iran '$500 Million Dollars a day' while the US 'loses nothing.' Despite the threats, Trump announced he was dispatching VP JD Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner to Islamabad on Monday for a new round of negotiations — signaling simultaneous coercion and diplomacy with 48 hours until the ceasefire expires.

title: IDF soldier photographed smashing Jesus statue in south Lebanon; IDF confirms
description: A photograph showing an Israeli soldier using a sledgehammer to destroy a statue of Jesus Christ on a cross in the Maronite Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon went viral, garnering over 5 million views on X. The IDF confirmed the image's authenticity on April 19 and stated the soldier's conduct was 'wholly inconsistent with the values expected of its troops.' The Northern Command opened an investigation and pledged to assist the Christian community in restoring the statue. Palestinian-Israeli Knesset member Ayman Odeh wrote: 'We'll wait to hear the police spokesperson claim that the soldier felt threatened by Jesus.' The incident, which occurred during the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, sparked international outrage over Israel's treatment of religious sites in occupied territories.

title: Ghalibaf says Iran 'far from final deal' despite progress; no date set for talks
description: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a nationally televised address that negotiations with Washington have produced 'progress' but 'there are many gaps and some fundamental points remain. We are still far from the final discussion.' He asserted Iran was 'victorious in the field' and accepted the ceasefire only because 'they accepted our demands.' He emphasized Iran controls the Strait of Hormuz: 'It is impossible for others to pass through the Strait of Hormuz while we cannot.' Separately, Deputy FM Khatibzadeh said at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum that no date has been set for a new round of face-to-face talks, demanding a 'framework agreement' first and blaming Washington's 'maximalist' approach. Egypt's FM Badr Abdelatty struck a more optimistic tone, saying Cairo and Islamabad hope to secure a final agreement 'in the coming days.' The ceasefire expires Wednesday April 22.

title: Iran's Foundation of Martyrs reports 3,468 killed in war with US and Israel
description: Iran's state-run Foundation of Martyrs and Veterans Affairs announced the war's official Iranian death toll has reached 3,468. Foundation head Ahmad Mousavi told ISNA that 3,468 'martyrs fell during the recent conflict,' up from 3,375 reported by the Legal Medicine Organisation on April 12. The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) had independently documented at least 3,636 deaths as of April 7 — including 1,701 civilians (among them 254 children), 1,221 military personnel, and 714 unclassified — suggesting the official figure understates the true toll. AFP noted it could not independently verify figures due to reporting restrictions inside Iran.

title: Trump says Iran 'got a little cute'; war cabinet convenes at White House
description: President Trump expressed frustration with Iran's Hormuz re-closure, saying: 'They got a little cute, as they have been doing for 47 years. They wanted to close up the strait again. They can't blackmail us.' Senior administration officials — including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, CIA Director, and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff — were seen arriving at the White House for what appeared to be a war cabinet session three days before the ceasefire expires on April 22. Trump maintained that negotiations are progressing but warned Iran could not use Hormuz as leverage. The Saturday meeting signaled intensifying contingency planning as the administration weighs whether to extend the ceasefire or resume strikes.

title: IDF confirms first strikes on Hezbollah since Lebanon ceasefire began
description: The Israeli military confirmed carrying out 'several strikes' in southern Lebanon against Hezbollah operatives who 'violated the ceasefire understandings,' marking the first acknowledged offensive action since the truce took effect at midnight April 17. The IDF said operatives approached the 'yellow line' separating IDF-controlled areas and conducted 'air and ground attacks' with 'support artillery fire.' The IDF stated it 'will not allow harm to Israeli civilians and IDF soldiers and will take all necessary measures.' Hezbollah called the strikes a ceasefire violation; parliament member Hassan Fadlallah said: 'We contacted the leadership in Iran and informed them of Israeli violations.' A US official clarified that while offensive operations are prohibited, the truce allows 'defensive strikes against planned, imminent, or ongoing attacks.' The strikes came one day after Trump declared Israel 'PROHIBITED' from bombing Lebanon.

title: Oil surges back toward $98 as Hormuz re-closure reverses Friday's 11% crash
description: Brent crude surged to $98.01 per barrel and WTI climbed to $93.19, nearly erasing Friday's 11-12% crash that had been triggered by Iran's brief Hormuz reopening. The whipsaw — the largest two-day oil price reversal of the war — reflected the IRGC's re-closure of the strait less than 24 hours after FM Araghchi declared it 'completely open.' The S&P 500's record close on Friday was overtaken by renewed supply fears. The rebound confirmed that the market's brief euphoria over Hormuz reopening was premature, with physical oil flows through the strait remaining near zero. Three days before the ceasefire expires, Brent had returned to within striking distance of the $100 psychological barrier that analysts warned could trigger a second wave of global fuel rationing.

title: Iran's internet blackout hits 50 consecutive days, longest nationwide shutdown on record
description: Iran's wartime internet blackout — imposed on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes began — reached 50 consecutive days (1,176 hours), making it the longest nationwide internet shutdown ever recorded in any country, according to monitoring group NetBlocks. A highly restricted domestic intranet remains operational, allowing access only to local websites and state-run news. Iranians caught using VPNs to access banned platforms receive threatening text messages warning of arrest. Iran's Communications Minister estimated the shutdown costs $35.7 million per day; independent analysts put the true impact at $70-80 million daily when including indirect costs. NetBlocks called the measure 'unprecedented for a connected society.'

title: Iran SNSC declares Hormuz under control until war ends; reviews new US proposals
description: Iran's Supreme National Security Council issued a formal statement declaring it will maintain 'oversight and control over traffic' through the Strait of Hormuz 'until the definitive end of the war and the establishment of lasting peace.' The SNSC imposed conditions including mandatory transit certificates, Iran-designated routes, full vessel information disclosure, and payment of 'security, safety, and environmental protection' fees. The statement warned that as long as the US blockade continues, Iran 'will consider it a violation of the ceasefire and will prevent even the limited and conditional opening of the Strait.' Separately, the SNSC confirmed it is reviewing new US proposals delivered through Pakistani mediator Field Marshal Asim Munir but has not yet responded, and stated a second round of negotiations is 'contingent on the United States aligning its demands with battlefield realities.'

title: India summons Iranian ambassador after IRGC fires on Indian-flagged VLCC in Hormuz
description: India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri summoned Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Fathali to express 'deep concern' after IRGC gunboats fired on the Indian-flagged VLCC Sanmar Herald — carrying approximately 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil — in the Strait of Hormuz. Leaked VHF radio audio captured the ship's captain telling Iranian forces: 'You gave me clearance to go...you are firing now!' The UK Maritime Trade Operations center confirmed the gunboats approached with 'no VHF challenge' before opening fire at 09:20 UTC, approximately 20 nautical miles northeast of Oman. A second Indian-flagged vessel was also struck by projectiles. India emphasized the strait is 'an international trade route that should remain open to all commercial shipping.' The diplomatic protest marked the first time a major non-belligerent state formally confronted Iran over Hormuz enforcement actions.

title: French UNIFIL soldier killed in Hezbollah ambush in southern Lebanon
description: Staff Sgt. Florian Montorio of France's 17th Parachute Engineer Regiment was killed and three UNIFIL peacekeepers wounded in an ambush near Deir Kifa in southern Lebanon. The patrol was opening a route to an isolated UNIFIL post when an armed group attacked at close range. Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin said Montorio was 'hit by a direct shot' from a light weapon. President Macron stated: 'Everything suggests that responsibility for this attack lies with Hezbollah,' and demanded Lebanese authorities 'immediately arrest those responsible.' Hezbollah denied involvement, expressing 'surprise at positions that rushed to make baseless accusations.' The attack occurred one day after the 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire took effect.

title: IDF soldier dies from booby-trap blast in southern Lebanon during ceasefire
description: Command Sgt.-Maj. (Res.) Barak Kalfon, 48, of the 226th Brigade from Adi, was killed by an explosive device in southern Lebanon, the IDF announced Saturday. Two soldiers were moderately injured and one lightly injured in the same blast. The IDF said the device had been planted before the ceasefire began and the incident was 'not being defined as a ceasefire violation.' Kalfon, married with two daughters, was the 14th Israeli soldier killed in the Lebanon war. The death came less than 24 hours after the 10-day ceasefire took effect at midnight April 17.

title: Trump extends Russian oil sanctions waiver to May 16, reversing Treasury refusal
description: The Trump administration renewed a temporary waiver permitting countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil transported by sea, effective immediately through May 16. The waiver covers an additional 100 million barrels of Russian exports, bringing the combined total with the earlier Iranian waiver to approximately 200 million barrels. The reversal was striking: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had explicitly told reporters two days earlier that Washington would not renew the waiver. A Treasury spokesperson called it 'a balancing act between geopolitical strategy and global energy needs.' Russia's special envoy Kirill Dmitriev celebrated the decision on Telegram. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen opposed easing restrictions, and lawmakers from both parties criticized the move as weakening pressure on Moscow while the Ukraine war continues.

title: IRGC gunboats fire on tanker and two merchant vessels in Strait of Hormuz
description: Two Iranian Revolutionary Guard gunboats opened fire on an Indian-flagged supertanker approximately 20 miles northeast of Oman in the Strait of Hormuz, forcing it to turn around. Two additional merchant vessels reported being hit by gunfire as they attempted to cross the strait. The UK Maritime Trade Operations center confirmed the incidents; no injuries were reported and vessels were reported safe. The attacks came hours after the IRGC declared the strait had 'returned to its previous state' under military control, representing the first use of force to enforce the re-closure. CENTCOM reported 23 vessels had complied with US blockade directions to turn around since the blockade began.

title: IRGC reverses Hormuz reopening <24h after Araghchi declared it 'completely open'
description: Iran's joint military command announced the Strait of Hormuz has 'returned to its previous state' and is under 'strict management and control of the armed forces,' reversing Foreign Minister Araghchi's declaration less than 24 hours earlier that the strait was 'completely open.' The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters — Iran's unified military command — accused the US of 'piracy and maritime robbery under the so-called blockade' and said Iran had allowed 'managed passage of a limited number of oil tankers and commercial vessels in good faith' but that Washington failed to uphold commitments. The IRGC stated restrictions will remain 'until the US completely lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.' Ship tracking data showed approximately two dozen vessels had moved toward the strait Friday morning before most turned back. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned on Telegram that Iran's navy was ready to inflict 'new bitter defeats' on adversaries.

title: Trump declares Israel 'PROHIBITED' from bombing Lebanon; IDF drone kills 1 minutes later
description: President Trump posted on Truth Social: 'Israel will not be bombing Lebanon any longer. They are PROHIBITED from doing so by the U.S.A. Enough is enough!!!' He told Axios: 'Israel has to stop. They can't continue to blow buildings up. I am not gonna allow it.' Israeli PM Netanyahu and his advisers were 'personally shocked and alarmed,' according to Axios — the post contradicted the State Department's ceasefire text, which preserved Israel's right to strike 'in self-defense, at any time, against planned, imminent, or ongoing attacks.' Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter scrambled to get White House clarification. Minutes after Trump's post, an IDF drone struck a motorcycle between the southern Lebanese towns of Kounine and Beit Yahoun, killing one person — the first confirmed fatality during the ceasefire. The IDF did not comment on the strike. Lebanon's cumulative death toll reached 2,196 killed and 7,185 wounded.

title: Trump warns US will 'start dropping bombs again' if no Iran deal by April 22
description: Aboard Air Force One, President Trump warned that if no deal is reached by the ceasefire's April 22 expiry: 'I don't know. Maybe I won't extend it — but the blockade is going to remain... Unfortunately, we'll have to start dropping bombs again.' He said the naval blockade would 'remain in full force and effect as it pertains to Iran until such time as our transaction with Iran is 100 per cent complete and fully signed.' At a Turning Point USA event in Phoenix, he called it 'a great and brilliant day for the world,' claiming to have received 'some pretty good news 20 minutes ago' about Iran. He said Iran 'can be trusted' because 'they have had enough' and that the US plans to retrieve enriched nuclear material through excavation coordinated with Iranian officials — a claim no Iranian official confirmed.

title: Iranian sources: Round 2 of US-Iran talks set for Monday in Islamabad
description: Iranian officials told CNN and ANI that the next round of US-Iran peace negotiations will take place Monday April 21 in Islamabad, Pakistan — one day before the April 8 ceasefire expires on April 22. Negotiators from both sides are expected to arrive Sunday. Pakistani officials told MS NOW the deal is 'more than 80 percent' complete but both sides need to show flexibility. Trump told Axios he expected a deal 'in the next day or two,' saying Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff would participate. The first round on April 11-12 lasted 21 hours without agreement; sticking points remain on Iran's nuclear program, Hormuz governance, and wartime damages.

title: Macron and Starmer convene 51-nation Paris summit; launch Hormuz naval mission without US
description: French President Macron and British PM Starmer co-chaired a summit at the Elysee Palace with 51 countries — including German Chancellor Merz and Italian PM Meloni in person — launching the 'Strait of Hormuz Maritime Freedom of Navigation Initiative.' The strictly defensive multinational mission will protect merchant vessels, reassure shipping operators, and conduct mine clearance once a sustainable ceasefire holds. The US was deliberately excluded as a belligerent. France committed a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, helicopter carrier, and frigates; the UK offered mine-hunting drones from RFA Lyme Bay. Over a dozen countries pledged assets. Starmer accused Iran of 'holding the world's economy to ransom.' Macron said the mission was limited to 'non-belligerent countries.' Military planners will meet in London the following week.

title: Ghalibaf warns Hormuz will close again if US blockade persists; calls Trump '7 lies in 1 hour'
description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf — who led Iran's 70-member delegation at the first Islamabad talks — warned that the Strait of Hormuz reopening was conditional: 'If the blockade continues, the Strait of Hormuz will not remain open.' He added: 'The President of the United States made seven claims in one hour, all seven of which were false,' and declared 'If you fight, we will fight.' He insisted all transit requires 'Iranian authorization' on designated routes. His intervention undercut the market euphoria triggered by FM Araghchi's reopening announcement hours earlier and exposed the internal tension between Iran's diplomatic and hardline factions.

title: Oil plunges 11%, Wall Street hits records on Hormuz reopening
description: Brent crude fell 11.5% to $87.94/barrel and WTI plunged 12% to $83.33/barrel after Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz 'completely open' for commercial vessels. The S&P 500 leaped 1.2% to a new all-time high, extending its third straight week of gains — the longest streak since Halloween. The Dow Jones surged as much as 1,100 points before closing up 868 (1.8%). The Nasdaq rose 1.63%. Oil had traded above $100/barrel earlier in the crisis. Shipping giant Hapag-Lloyd said it would continue avoiding the strait while monitoring conditions, signaling the market rally may overstate the physical reality of resumed oil flows.

title: Iran declares Hormuz 'completely open'; IRGC mandates authorization for all vessels
description: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced: 'The passage for all commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz is declared completely open for the remaining period of ceasefire, on the coordinated route as already announced by the Ports and Maritime Organisation.' The reopening — linked to the Lebanon ceasefire that began at midnight — ended 46 days of closure that the IEA called the largest oil supply disruption in history. However, the IRGC Navy immediately imposed conditions: all vessels must transit on Iran-designated routes with 'explicit authorization of the IRGC's naval forces,' military vessels remain barred, and ships linked to 'hostile states' are prohibited. Trump celebrated the opening but said the US naval blockade 'remains in full force' until a deal is signed, claiming Iran had 'agreed to never close the Strait of Hormuz again' — a claim Tehran did not confirm.

title: Trump claims Iran agreed to surrender enriched uranium; says deal 'very close'
description: President Trump told reporters at the White House that Iran has 'agreed to almost everything' and 'agreed to give us back the nuclear dust that's way underground because of the attack that we made with the B-2 bombers,' claiming Tehran would surrender its enriched uranium stockpile. He said a deal could extend beyond 20 years and talks may resume in Islamabad 'as early as this weekend,' adding he might travel to Pakistan to sign it. Iran's state broadcaster IRIB immediately mocked the claims, quoting a Persian proverb: 'The camel dreams of cottonseed; sometimes gulping it down, sometimes eating it grain by grain!' Iran maintained its right to enrich uranium is 'indisputable' but said the level of enrichment is 'negotiable.' No Iranian official confirmed any agreement on surrendering enriched material.

title: Iran's Deputy FM rejects any temporary ceasefire; Rezaei threatens to sink US ships
description: Iran Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh told the Antalya Diplomacy Forum: 'We are not accepting any temporary ceasefire.' He insisted any truce must encompass every active battleground 'from Lebanon to the Red Sea,' calling comprehensive scope a 'red line' for Tehran. Separately, Mohsen Rezaei — former IRGC commander-in-chief and top aide to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei — told Fars News Agency that Iran would sink US ships if Washington continues to 'police' the Strait of Hormuz, and that he would welcome a US ground invasion as an opportunity to take American soldiers hostage. Rezaei stated he personally opposes the ceasefire. The twin statements exposed a hardline faction actively working against the diplomatic track that Pakistani mediators are pushing toward an April 22 deadline.

title: Celebrations erupt across Beirut as Lebanon ceasefire begins; displaced families head south
description: Fireworks, tracer rounds, and celebratory gunfire lit up Beirut's skyline just after midnight as the 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire took effect. Displaced families packed cars and headed south along Lebanon's coastal highway before dawn, crossing damaged bridges bombed during the war — the first significant return movement since fighting began March 2. Both the Lebanese army and the IDF warned civilians not to return south of the Litani River. Lebanon's cumulative death toll reached 2,196 — including 260 women and 172 children — with 7,185 wounded and over 1 million displaced, approximately 20% of the population. Lebanese PM Nawaf Salam called the ceasefire 'a central Lebanese demand we have pursued since the first day of the war.'

title: House War Powers Resolution fails 214-213; one vote preserves Trump war authority
description: The House of Representatives voted down a War Powers Resolution 214-213, with one member voting present, failing by a single vote to force a debate on limiting President Trump's authority to wage war on Iran. Only one Republican — Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) — broke ranks to vote with Democrats. One Democrat, Rep. Jared Golden (D-ME), voted against. Sponsored by Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY), the resolution was the closest Congress came to challenging the war's legal basis. The Senate had blocked a companion measure the previous day. The razor-thin margin contrasted with the Senate's 40-59 rejection of Sanders' arms-block resolutions, suggesting war opposition is stronger in the House.

title: IDF destroys Qasimiyeh Bridge and strikes 380+ Hezbollah targets before Lebanon ceasefire
description: Israeli warplanes destroyed the Qasimiyeh Bridge connecting Tyre and Sidon with two consecutive airstrikes followed by drone strikes, severing the last remaining road between the two major southern Lebanese cities and cutting off tens of thousands of residents. The IDF struck more than 380 Hezbollah targets in the 24 hours before the ceasefire took effect at midnight — including launchers, headquarters, and militant positions — in a final escalation surge. Separately, Israeli airstrikes killed 11 civilians in southern Lebanon hours before the truce: three in the Sidon district and eight in the Zahrani area, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The Lebanese army said the bridge destruction left no land route for humanitarian access to Tyre.

title: Hegseth reveals Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei alive but wounded and disfigured
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth disclosed at a Pentagon press briefing that Iran's new Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei — who succeeded his father Ali Khamenei after the February 28 assassination strike — is alive but 'wounded and disfigured,' having been injured in the same airstrike that killed his predecessor. Hegseth said Iran's 'command and control capabilities were highly degraded.' The revelation was the first US confirmation of the new supreme leader's physical condition and may explain his limited public appearances since assuming power on March 8. Mojtaba Khamenei had broken weeks of silence on April 9, vowing revenge while ordering ceasefire compliance.

title: Israeli artillery shells Khiam and Dibbine within 30 minutes of Lebanon ceasefire
description: Israeli artillery struck the southern Lebanese towns of Khiam and Dibbine approximately 30 minutes after the 10-day ceasefire took effect at midnight local time, with machine gun fire also reported during sweeping operations. Reconnaissance aircraft were observed over the Rashaya region and western slopes of Jabal al-Sheikh in the western Bekaa Valley. IDF Arabic-language spokesperson Avichay Adraee warned residents not to return south of the Litani River 'until further notice,' citing 'Hezbollah's ongoing terrorist activities.' The Lebanese army separately warned civilians to avoid 'approaching areas where Israeli occupation forces have advanced.' The violations echoed the 2024 Lebanon ceasefire, which saw more than 10,000 violations — mostly by Israeli forces — according to UN peacekeepers.

title: Trump announces 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire; Netanyahu keeps troops in 'expanded security zone'
description: President Trump announced via Truth Social that Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu agreed to a 10-day ceasefire effective 5 PM EST (midnight Israel time), growing out of the first direct Israel-Lebanon talks since 1993 held Tuesday in Washington. Trump invited both leaders to White House peace talks and directed VP Vance and Secretary Rubio to work toward 'a Lasting PEACE.' Netanyahu confirmed but stated: 'We are remaining in Lebanon in an expanded security zone' and Israel 'had not agreed to withdraw.' Lebanon committed to 'take meaningful steps to prevent Hezbollah and all other rogue non-state armed groups' from attacking Israel; Israel preserved the right to 'take all necessary measures in self-defense.' A senior Hezbollah official told NBC News the group would consider compliance 'if Israel is fully committed to a complete cessation of hostilities.' Lebanese PM Nawaf Salam welcomed the deal. The ceasefire may be extended 'by mutual agreement if progress is demonstrated.' Lebanese casualties since March 2: over 2,100 killed including 172 children and 91 healthcare workers, over 1 million displaced — 20% of the population.

title: Pentagon: 10,000+ troops enforce blockade with 16 warships; Hegseth threatens infrastructure bombing
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told a Pentagon briefing the Iran blockade will continue 'as long as it takes,' warning: 'If Iran chooses poorly, then they will have a blockade and bombs dropping on infrastructure, power and energy.' He said US forces were 'locked and loaded' on Iran's 'critical dual-use infrastructure, remaining power generation and energy industry.' Gen. Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, said 14 ships had turned around in three days and the blockade applies to 'all ships, regardless of nationality, heading into or from Iranian ports.' Over 10,000 American troops are enforcing the blockade with 16 warships — 11 destroyers, 3 amphibious assault ships, 1 aircraft carrier, and 1 littoral combat ship — representing 'less than 10% of America's naval power,' per Hegseth. No ships have been boarded; the Navy is warning Iran-linked vessels it could fire warning shots or escalate. CENTCOM Admiral Brad Cooper: 'We're rearming, we're retooling, and we're adjusting our tactics, techniques and procedures.'

title: NBC: Half of Iran's missile launchers intact; Iran digging out weapons despite 'destroyed' claim
description: NBC News reported that roughly half of Iran's ballistic missile launchers remain intact and thousands of one-way attack drones survive, with multiple underground missile stockpiles undamaged — contradicting Defense Secretary Hegseth's claim last week that Iran's missile program was 'functionally destroyed.' At the same Pentagon briefing, Hegseth acknowledged Iran is 'digging out' remaining missiles and launchers but insisted: 'You have no defense industry, no ability to replenish your offensive or defensive capabilities.' U.S. intelligence also reported China was planning to provide new air defense weaponry to Iran in coming weeks, though Trump said Beijing gave assurances it would not send arms. Separately, NBC revealed Iran obtained a Chinese satellite in late 2024 used to monitor US military sites, capturing images of Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia in mid-March — days before IRGC strikes hit the base.

title: USS Spruance forces Iranian cargo ship back to Iran; CENTCOM says 10 vessels turned back
description: The guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance (DDG 111) intercepted an Iranian-flagged cargo vessel that had departed Bandar Abbas and attempted to evade the US naval blockade by transiting along the Iranian coastline after exiting the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM said the Aegis destroyer 'successfully redirected the vessel, which is heading back to Iran,' marking the first named US Navy interdiction since the blockade was declared fully implemented. CENTCOM reported: 'Ten vessels have now been turned around and ZERO ships have broken through since the start of the U.S. blockade on Monday.' The enforcement action on day 3 of the blockade contradicted shipping-data reports of at least two sanctioned supertankers still entering the Gulf.

title: Hezbollah rocket attack wounds 5 IDF soldiers at Bint Jbeil; drone strikes Nahariya
description: A Hezbollah rocket attack in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, wounded five Israeli soldiers — one seriously, four lightly — all evacuated for medical treatment, the IDF announced. Separately, Hezbollah claimed two drone attacks targeting Israeli forces near Nahariya in northern Israel, stating via Telegram it struck 'a logistics base belonging to the Israeli army's 146th Division using a squadron of attack drones' and conducted a second strike on a settlement near the Liman barracks. The attacks expanded Hezbollah's resistance pattern one day after Israel and Lebanon launched their first direct talks since 1993 in Washington, validating Hezbollah chief Qassem's vow that 'the battlefield will speak for itself.' The incidents brought the weekly IDF casualty count in Bint Jbeil to at least 15 wounded and one killed.

title: IEA warns 'six weeks of jet fuel left'; ACI Europe flags full-blown aviation crisis
description: IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol warned Europe has 'maybe six weeks or so of jet fuel left' even if the Strait of Hormuz reopened immediately, because tanker voyages from Kuwait to Rotterdam take six weeks. Airports Council International Europe's April 9 letter to the European Commission warned that without 'significant and stable' Hormuz shipping resumption within three weeks, 'a full-blown crisis for EU aviation will become reality.' Jet fuel prices in the US have nearly doubled from $2.50/gallon on Feb 27 to $4.88/gallon on April 2. On Monday nearly 7% of all global flights — 7,049 of 104,618 scheduled — were cancelled, with 14.6% of North American departures grounded. United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby announced cuts to approximately 5% of planned Q2-Q3 2026 routes, while average US airfares hit $465 — the highest since at least 2019.

title: S&P 500 closes above 7,000 for first time; Nasdaq hits record as war losses erased
description: The S&P 500 rose 0.8% (56 points) to close at 7,023 — its first-ever close above 7,000 — while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.6% (377 points) to 24,016, eclipsing its October 2025 record of 23,958. The dual record capped a two-week rally in which US equities erased every loss tied to the Iran war, driven by Trump's declaration that the conflict is 'very close to over' and reports that Washington and Tehran had reached an 'in principle' agreement to extend the ceasefire. Trump told Fox Business the market 'is going to boom,' adding: 'We've beaten them militarily, totally.' The rally decoupled equities from oil pain: WTI crude had plunged 7.9% the same day below $92/barrel.

title: US, Iran reach 'in principle' agreement to extend ceasefire two weeks; Washington hedges
description: Regional officials told the Associated Press the United States and Iran reached an 'in principle agreement' to extend the April 8 two-week ceasefire — set to expire April 21 — by another two weeks to allow more diplomacy. Bloomberg and Fortune confirmed both sides are 'weighing' the extension. A senior US official responding to the report told Reuters that Washington 'has not formally agreed' to any extension. Mediators are pushing for compromise on three sticking points that derailed the Islamabad talks: Iran's nuclear program, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and compensation for wartime damages. US negotiators reportedly favor a 5-year enrichment moratorium; Iran had rejected a 20-year demand.

title: IAEA chief Grossi in Seoul: inspector access 'indispensable' for any Iran deal
description: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told a press conference in Seoul that verification of any Iran peace agreement must be 'very detailed,' warning: 'Iran has a very ambitious, wide nuclear programme. So all of that will require the presence of IAEA inspectors; otherwise you will not have an agreement, you will have an illusion of an agreement.' Grossi said the agency must 'provide the indispensable safeguard verification component' of any settlement. His intervention raised the technical bar for a deal as Pakistani mediators shuttled toward a second round of talks. Tehran has denied IAEA inspectors access to nuclear facilities damaged by US-Israeli strikes since February 28, making independent verification of enrichment suspension currently impossible.

title: Netanyahu: Iran ceasefire 'could turn on a dime'; Israel ready for resumed fighting
description: PM Benjamin Netanyahu told a cabinet meeting the Iran ceasefire 'could turn on a dime,' signaling the truce's fragility as Israel continues operations against Hezbollah. 'It is too early to say how this will end, or even how it will progress. And in light of the possibility that the fighting may resume, we are prepared for any scenario,' Netanyahu said. He reiterated Israel's demands: 'We want to see Iran's enriched material removed, and we want to see the elimination of its enrichment capability inside Iran.' Netanyahu's public declaration he 'backs Trump's blockade' aligned Israel's PM with Washington's maximum pressure posture — even as Pakistani mediators pushed toward a second round of talks — and put daylight between Netanyahu and US negotiators reportedly willing to accept a 5-year enrichment moratorium.

title: US Treasury refuses to renew Iran oil sanctions easing; tightens shadow fleet pressure
description: The US Treasury Department announced it will not renew a temporary authorization that had permitted the sale of Iranian crude and petroleum products loaded onto ships before March 20. The waiver, originally set to expire April 19, had been issued to ease wartime energy price shocks. Treasury simultaneously sanctioned more than two dozen individuals, companies, and vessels tied to Iran's illicit oil transportation network, tightening pressure on Tehran's 'shadow fleet' as the naval blockade enters its fourth day. The move signaled Washington will not let the blockade be softened by exemptions, despite ongoing efforts to revive talks.

title: Senate rejects Sanders arms-block resolutions 40-59 and 36-63; record Democratic support
description: The Senate rejected two resolutions introduced by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) to block arms sales to Israel — a $295 million armored bulldozer sale failed 40-59, and a separate measure to block 1,000-pound bomb transfers failed 36-63. All Republicans opposed both measures. More than 80% of the Democratic caucus voted to block the bulldozer sale — the highest support Sanders has secured in three years of forcing such votes and more than double his 2024 tally. Democrats voting against both resolutions included Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, Richard Blumenthal, Chris Coons, John Fetterman, Kirsten Gillibrand, and Jacky Rosen. Sanders said: 'The overwhelming majority of American people do not want to continue to give weapons to Netanyahu.' The votes marked a watershed in Democratic-Israel relations but fell short of reversing Secretary Rubio's emergency authorization.

title: Pakistan Army Chief Munir arrives Tehran with US message for second round of talks
description: Field Marshal Asim Munir, chief of Pakistan's army, arrived in Tehran on Wednesday evening with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and a delegation of officials, carrying what Pakistani state media called 'a new message from Washington' for a potential second round of US-Iran negotiations. Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi greeted Munir — dressed in military gear — at the airport. Munir's rare diplomatic mission — conducted in parallel with PM Sharif's Gulf-Turkey tour — is the most senior Pakistani engagement of the war. Pakistani sources said mediators are 'optimistic about a potential major breakthrough on the nuclear front' but named 'elements in Tehran, in Washington, DC, and biggest of them all...Israel' as the primary detractors. Trump told reporters to brace for 'amazing two days' as the war is 'close to over.'

title: IDF Chief Zamir: Air Force 'armed and ready' for immediate strike on Iran
description: IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir toured southern Lebanon with senior Northern Command officers and announced that the General Staff has approved updated plans for continued combat 'both on the Lebanese front and against Iran.' Zamir stated: 'We are at a very high level of readiness. Israeli Air Force planes are armed and ready, and the targets are loaded into the systems. We know how to launch them for a powerful strike immediately.' He added that in coordination with US forces, Israel had struck the Iranian regime 'hard' and weakened its defensive capabilities. The public threat — issued as Pakistani mediators shuttled toward a second round of talks — underscored Israel's posture that the Iran ceasefire is conditional, not final.

title: Israeli 'triple-tap' strikes kill 4 Lebanese paramedics in Mayfadoun
description: Three consecutive Israeli airstrikes on the southern Lebanese village of Mayfadoun, near Nabatiyeh, killed four Lebanese rescue workers and wounded six others in a 'triple-tap' pattern targeting successive responder teams. The first strike killed two paramedics from Lebanon's Hezbollah-affiliated Islamic Health Committee responding to a civilian distress call. A second Islamic Health Committee team dispatched to evacuate colleagues was struck, wounding three. A third team from Nabatiyeh Emergency Services and the Amal-linked Islamic Risala Scout Association was hit, killing two more medics. Islamic Health Committee official Abou Haidar Hayya said: 'Ambulances are protected under all international laws and conventions...when those prohibitions collapse, we have nothing left.' At least 91 Lebanese medical workers have been killed since March 2. The strikes occurred one day after Israel-Lebanon held their first direct talks since 1993 in Washington.

title: Iran suspends all petrochemical exports citing domestic shortages from April 6 strikes
description: Iran's National Petrochemical Company suspended all petrochemical product exports 'until further notice' to prioritize domestic market supply, state media Mehr News reported. The decision cited damage from April 6 airstrikes on two petrochemical plants in the South Pars region. Petrochemicals constitute Iran's largest non-oil export earner — roughly 29 million tons and approximately $13 billion annually — supplying Turkey, China, India, and Southeast Asia with plastics, polymers, and agricultural chemicals. The self-imposed export halt compounds the US naval blockade's impact and is expected to drive global polymer and plastics prices sharply higher, disrupting supply chains already strained by pre-war South Pars strikes.

title: Xi meets Lavrov in Beijing; Russia offers to fill China's energy gap
description: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the Great Hall of the People, with both sides condemning US military action against Iran and reaffirming their 'strategic cooperation.' Lavrov told Chinese counterparts Russia could 'fill the resource gap' created by the Hormuz blockade, offering to expand crude and LNG supplies to Beijing. China imports approximately one-third of its oil through the Strait of Hormuz, and 90% of Russia's Q1 2026 crude exports went to China and India. The meeting crystallized the Russia-China response to the blockade: Moscow profits from elevated prices, Beijing secures alternative supply, and both cement Iran's pivot east. Lavrov reiterated Russia's position that the conflict has 'no military solution.'

title: IEA declares 'Code Red'; calls Iran crisis worse than 1973+1979+2022 combined
description: IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol issued the agency's most severe warning in its 52-year history at an emergency Paris briefing, declaring the Iran conflict a 'total systemic failure' of the global energy artery and characterizing the crisis as surpassing the combined impact of the 1973 Arab oil embargo, 1979 Iranian revolution, and 2022 Russia invasion shocks. The Hormuz closure and blockade removed an estimated 21 million barrels/day of oil and 20% of the world's LNG from the market — versus the 1973 embargo's 5 million b/d loss. Birol warned an immediate supply chain collapse could trigger a depression 'worse than the Great Recession.' Brent crude briefly touched $185/barrel (up 28%) on the warning; the S&P 500 dropped 4.2% in a single session. Unlike prior shocks, the crisis paralyzes oil and gas markets simultaneously, threatening electricity grids across Europe and Asia.

title: Iran threatens to block all Gulf and Red Sea shipping if US blockade persists
description: Iranian armed forces commander Gen. Ali Abdollahi declared the US naval blockade 'a violation of the ceasefire' and threatened to prevent 'any exports and imports' across the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and Red Sea if the US continues 'creating insecurity for Iranian commercial ships and oil tankers.' The threat expanded Iran's retaliatory posture to explicitly include the Red Sea for the first time, raising the specter of coordinated disruption alongside Houthi forces at the Bab el-Mandeb strait. The statement came hours after CENTCOM announced the blockade was 'fully implemented' and had 'completely halted economic trade going into and out of Iran by sea.'

title: Saudi Arabia pledges $3B to Pakistan; extends $5B deposit
description: Saudi Arabia committed $3 billion in additional deposits to Pakistan and extended an existing $5 billion deposit by removing previous rollover conditions, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb announced, with disbursement expected within a week. The financial backing came as PM Sharif departed on a shuttle diplomacy tour to revive US-Iran talks — effectively underwriting Pakistan's role as ceasefire mediator. Pakistan faces a $3.5 billion debt repayment to the UAE by month's end and needs to maintain $18 billion in reserves under its IMF program.

title: Pakistan PM Sharif begins Saudi-Qatar-Turkey tour to revive US-Iran talks
description: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif departed for a four-day diplomatic tour (April 15-18) to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey, accompanied by Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, aiming to facilitate a second round of US-Iran peace talks before the April 21 ceasefire expires. Bilateral meetings are scheduled in Riyadh and Doha, with multilateral talks planned at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum. A diplomat confirmed Tehran and Washington agreed in principle to further talks, though location, timing, and delegation composition remain undecided, with Islamabad and Geneva under consideration. Trump said talks could happen 'over the next two days,' calling it 'more likely' they would be in Pakistan.

title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth to 3.1%; warns war could trigger recession
description: The IMF released its World Economic Outlook, cutting 2026 global growth to 3.1% from 3.3% projected in January, with global inflation expected at 4.4% (up 0.6 points). Chief Economist Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas warned the impact would be 'highly uneven,' hitting conflict-zone and commodity-importing countries hardest. Regional cuts: Middle East & North Africa slashed 2.8 points to 1.1%, Iran to -6.1% contraction (down 7.2 points), Eurozone to 1.1%, Saudi Arabia to 3.1% (from 4.5%), US trimmed 0.1 point to 2.3%. In a 'severe scenario' where energy shocks persist and central banks raise rates, global growth could fall to 2% in 2026-2027.

title: Iran sentences 4 January protesters to death; first woman faces execution
description: Branch 26 of Tehran's Revolutionary Court, under Judge Iman Afshari, sentenced four detainees from the January 2026 protests to death on charges of 'operational actions for the hostile government of the United States and hostile groups': Mohammad Reza Majidi-Asl, Bita Hemmati, Behrouz Zamani-Nejad, and Kourosh Zamani-Nejad. Each also received five years for 'assembly and collusion' with full property confiscation. Hemmati is the first woman sentenced to death in connection with the protests. A fifth defendant, Amir Hemmati, received five years and eight months. HRANA reported inmates in 56 prisons held hunger strikes for the 116th consecutive week of the 'No to Executions' campaign.

title: Pope Leo XIV condemns 'delusion of omnipotence'; Trump calls him 'weak'
description: Pope Leo XIV — the first American pontiff — condemned the 'delusion of omnipotence' fueling the Iran war during a vigil at St. Peter's Basilica, calling for an end to the 'madness of war.' Trump responded on social media: 'I don't want a pope who criticizes the president of the United States.' He called Leo 'weak' and 'terrible,' adding: 'If I wasn't in the White House, Leo wouldn't be in the Vatican.' Departing for an 11-day Africa tour starting in Algeria, Leo told NBC News: 'I have no fear neither of the Trump administration, nor speaking out loudly about the message of the Gospel.' The Vatican-White House rift marked the most prominent institutional opposition to the war from within the US establishment.

title: Israel, Lebanon hold first direct talks since 1993; agree to launch negotiations
description: Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter and Lebanese Ambassador Nada Mouawad held a two-hour meeting in Washington — the first direct diplomatic engagement between the two countries since 1993 — with Secretary of State Marco Rubio participating. A joint US-Israel-Lebanon statement said participants held 'productive discussions' and agreed to 'launch direct negotiations at a mutually agreed time and venue.' The statement said negotiations could curb Iran's influence and 'unlock significant reconstruction assistance and economic recovery for Lebanon.' Leiter stated: 'We are both united in liberating Lebanon from an occupation power dominated by Iran called Hezbollah.' Rubio framed the session as foundational: 'This is a process, not an event.' Lebanon's President Aoun expressed hope the talks would 'mark the beginning of the end of the suffering of the Lebanese people.' Hezbollah rejected the framework entirely.

title: Oil plunges 7-8% as US-Iran talks-resume hopes build; WTI falls below $92
description: WTI crude futures plunged 7.9% to fall below $92/barrel on Tuesday — their lowest level in three weeks — while Brent dropped 4.6%, driven by Trump's statement that 'something could be happening over the next two days' in Islamabad and Vice President Vance's remark: 'I feel very good about where we are.' UN Secretary-General Guterres called talks resuming 'highly probable.' The sell-off erased the blockade premium from Monday's surge. Trump told reporters he views the conflict 'as very close to over.' Treasury Secretary Bessent characterized current economic pain as justified, noting oil prices remain 'transient.' The average US gasoline price stood at $4.12/gallon. The IEA warned the ongoing conflict could wipe out global oil demand growth this year, producing the first annual decline since the pandemic.

title: Pentagon declares Hormuz blockade 'fully implemented'; interdicts 2 tankers
description: CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper announced the naval blockade 'has been fully implemented' with over 10,000 sailors, Marines, and airmen, more than a dozen warships, and dozens of aircraft executing the operation. In the first 36 hours, US forces 'completely halted economic trade going into and out of Iran by sea,' turning back six merchant vessels and interdicting two oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. More than 20 non-Iranian ships safely transited. CENTCOM issued a Notice to Mariners warning: 'Any vessel entering or departing the blockaded area without authorization is subject to interception, diversion, and capture.' Humanitarian shipments — food, medical supplies, and essential goods — receive authorization subject to inspection. The Pentagon reported 399 US service members wounded since the war began, with 354 returned to duty.

title: 10 IDF paratroopers wounded in Bint Jbeil firefight; battalion commander seriously hurt
description: Ten paratroopers from the 101st Battalion were wounded in a firefight with three Hezbollah gunmen inside Bint Jbeil — three seriously, one moderately, six lightly. The soldiers exchanged fire with the cell; two Hezbollah fighters were killed by combined infantry, tank, and airstrike fire, and the third was killed attempting to flee. Separately, the commander of the 401st Brigade's 52nd Armored Battalion was seriously wounded in the Bint Jbeil area and evacuated by helicopter to hospital. The IDF Home Front Command warned that 'Hezbollah might temporarily increase its attacks on Israel's North' to influence the Israel-Lebanon negotiations opening in Washington. The IDF also captured three Hezbollah Radwan special forces fighters who 'initially put up a strong fight, but eventually they were overwhelmed' and transferred them for interrogation.

title: Sanders forces Senate vote to block $500M Israel arms sale; 100 arrested at NYC protest
description: Senator Bernie Sanders announced he will force a Senate vote on Wednesday April 16 on legislation to block a nearly $500 million arms transfer to Israel — including bombs and bulldozers — that Secretary Rubio authorized via emergency determination just six days into the Iran war, bypassing the statutory congressional notification period. The bill is unlikely to pass in the Republican-controlled Senate but forces lawmakers to take a public position. Separately, nearly 100 protesters were arrested outside the offices of Senators Schumer and Gillibrand in New York at a Jewish Voice for Peace-led demonstration demanding the senators block the weapons sale. JVP's Sonya Meyerson-Knox said: 'Our senators need to listen to their constituents... Stop arming Israel.' Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries announced House Democrats will compel a vote on an Iran war powers resolution.

title: Sanctioned Chinese tankers defy US blockade, transit Hormuz on Day 1
description: Three US-sanctioned tankers transited the Strait of Hormuz on the first full day of the American blockade, testing Washington's enforcement resolve. The Chinese-owned Rich Starry — blacklisted in 2023 for helping Iran evade sanctions — carried approximately 250,000 barrels of methanol from the UAE's Hamriyah port; it had reversed course on an initial Monday attempt before succeeding Tuesday. The Murlikishan, which has transported Russian and Iranian oil, headed into the strait en route to load fuel oil in Iraq. The Panama-flagged Peace Gulf, which typically moves Iranian naphtha, sailed toward the UAE's Hamriyah. None were intercepted by the US Navy, raising immediate questions about the blockade's credibility and scope.

title: Xi proposes 4-point Middle East framework in first public war remarks
description: Chinese President Xi Jinping made his first public statement on the Iran war, pledging China would play a 'constructive role' in promoting peace. Meeting Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, Xi proposed a four-point framework: respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity of Gulf states, adherence to international rule of law ('cannot mean use when it suits, lose when it doesn't'), a UN-based world order, and coordination of security and development. Separately, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the US blockade 'dangerous and irresponsible,' warning it 'will only intensify contradictions, exacerbate tensions, undermine the already fragile ceasefire.' China imports approximately one-third of its oil through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Lavrov arrives Beijing for Wang Yi talks on Middle East de-escalation
description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov received a red-carpet welcome in Beijing for a two-day visit (April 14-15), with talks scheduled with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on 'international and regional issues of common concern.' The visit — one day after Lavrov told Iran's Araghchi the conflict has 'no military solution' — signals deepening Russia-China coordination on the Middle East crisis. Wang and Lavrov had agreed on April 5 to work together on de-escalation. The simultaneous presence in Beijing of Lavrov, Spanish PM Sanchez, Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince, and Vietnam's To Lam turned the Chinese capital into an alternative diplomatic hub to Washington as the ceasefire's second week began.

title: IDF Sgt. Maj. Bianco killed in Lebanon; first soldier lost since ceasefire
description: Sergeant Major (Res.) Ayal Uriel Bianco, 30, of the 188th Brigade from Katzrin, was killed in southern Lebanon when his military Humvee overturned during operations — the first Israeli soldier killed since the April 7 US-Iran ceasefire began. One reservist was moderately wounded and two others lightly injured in the same incident. The IDF emphasized that Israel's ceasefire with Iran 'does not include Lebanon,' where ground operations continue. The Israeli military death toll in the war reached 937. Separately, Pezeshkian told Macron in a phone call that Iran is 'prepared to continue talks solely within the framework of international laws,' blaming US 'excessive demands' for the Islamabad collapse.

title: Hezbollah's Qassem demands Lebanon cancel Washington talks with Israel
description: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem delivered a televised address demanding Lebanon take 'a historic and heroic stance' by canceling the April 15 Washington meeting with Israel. Qassem said: 'Israel clearly states that the goal of these negotiations is to disarm Hezbollah. So how can you go to negotiations whose objective is already clear?' He called the talks a 'free concession' to Israel requiring Lebanese consensus that does not exist, and accused Beirut of 'backstabbing' Hezbollah by declaring its military activities illegal. Qassem vowed: 'We will not rest, stop or surrender. Instead, we will let the battlefield speak for itself.' The Lebanese government did not indicate it would withdraw from the talks.

title: Trump claims Iran 'reached out' to resume talks; oil cuts early gains
description: President Trump told reporters Iran had contacted the US to resume negotiations: 'We've been called by the other side. They'd like to make a deal very badly.' The claim — unconfirmed by Tehran — shifted market sentiment: WTI crude, which had surged 9% to $107/barrel in early Monday trading on blockade fears, retreated to under $98/barrel by afternoon, cutting gains to less than 2%. Brent settled near $103/barrel. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said oil prices would remain elevated until 'meaningful ship traffic' resumed through Hormuz but predicted prices would 'peak' within weeks. The nationwide US gasoline average reached $4.125/gallon, up from $2.98 pre-war.

title: Israel and Lebanon announce direct Washington talks for April 15
description: Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter confirmed Israel agreed to 'formal peace negotiations' with Lebanon on Tuesday April 15, hosted by US Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa in Washington. Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad will represent Beirut. The two sides disagree fundamentally on scope: Lebanon's presidency said talks aim to establish a ceasefire, while Israel insists on negotiating Hezbollah's disarmament and a broader peace agreement — refusing to discuss any ceasefire. Hezbollah-affiliated lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah rejected the talks entirely. The announcement came as Lebanon's death toll from Israeli strikes reached 2,089 since March 2, with over 1.2 million displaced.

title: Lavrov tells Araghchi conflict has 'no military solution'
description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov called Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi and told him the conflict has 'no military solution,' urging Iran to prevent any resumption of hostilities. Lavrov confirmed 'Russia's unwavering readiness' to assist in resolving the crisis. Araghchi briefed Lavrov on the failed Islamabad talks. The call represented Moscow's most direct pressure on Tehran since the war began — Russia has benefited from elevated oil prices (estimated $45-151 billion in additional 2026 budget revenues) but fears the conflict spiraling further, particularly given Russian engineers still working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant.

title: China-Pakistan present 5-point initiative; Wang Yi warns ceasefire 'very fragile'
description: Chinese FM Wang Yi told Pakistani FM Ishaq Dar in a phone call that the ceasefire is 'very fragile' and the region is 'at a critical turning point,' urging the international community to 'take a clear stand against any action that could undermine the ceasefire or escalate confrontation.' The two unveiled a joint 5-point initiative for preserving the truce, which Wang said 'reflects the consensus of the international community.' Separately, Pakistani, Egyptian, and Turkish mediators launched shuttle diplomacy: FM Dar spoke with Egyptian and Turkish counterparts, then with US envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian FM Araghchi, aiming to arrange fresh dialogue before the April 21 ceasefire expiry.

title: Iran demands war reparations from 5 Gulf states at UN
description: Iran's UN Ambassador formally demanded compensation from Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, and Jordan, claiming they 'breached their international obligations toward the Islamic Republic of Iran under international law' by allowing their territory to be used for US-Israeli strikes. Iran argued the five states owe reparations for enabling the air campaign. None of the named countries responded publicly. The demand came as the UAE had itself demanded compensation from Iran for missile and drone strikes that killed 13 people and injured 224 across Emirati territory, and after the UAE intercepted 537 ballistic missiles, 2,256 drones, and 26 cruise missiles since the war began.

title: IDF encircles Bint Jbeil; claims 100+ Hezbollah fighters killed
description: The IDF's 98th Division — Paratroopers, Commando, and Givati brigades — completed the encirclement of the Hezbollah stronghold of Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon and began an assault on the town. IDF spokesman Colonel Avichay Adraee announced the operation, claiming Israeli forces killed over 100 Hezbollah fighters including Radwan Force members through 'face-to-face' clashes and airstrikes over the preceding week. The IDF estimated approximately 150 Hezbollah operatives had been in the area at the start of the operation and said 'only a small number of terrorists remains.' Full operational control is expected within days. Bint Jbeil, 5 km from the Israeli border, holds symbolic significance from the 2006 war. Separately, Israeli strikes killed at least 4 people in Mabrouh.

title: Iran condemns US blockade as 'act of piracy'; threatens severe response
description: Iran's armed forces declared the US naval blockade of Iranian ports — which took effect at 10:00 AM ET (14:00 GMT) — 'an illegal act' that 'amounts to piracy,' rejecting CENTCOM's authority to restrict vessel movement in international waters. The IRGC Navy warned that any military vessels approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be 'considered a violation of the ceasefire and will be dealt with severely.' CENTCOM clarified the blockade applies to 'all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports' on the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman but 'will not impede freedom of navigation for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to and from non-Iranian ports' — a narrower scope than Trump's original threat to block 'any and all ships.' The distinction between Trump's rhetoric and CENTCOM's operational rules created what Al Jazeera called 'conflicting information' from US officials.

title: France and UK announce conference to launch Hormuz defensive mission
description: French President Macron announced that France and the UK will organize a conference 'in the coming days' for countries willing to contribute to a 'peaceful, multinational mission' to restore free transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Over 15 countries are participating in planning under French leadership. Macron emphasized the mission would be 'strictly defensive' and 'separate from the warring parties,' designed to escort commercial vessels once conditions allow. The initiative represents a European-led alternative to the US military approach — operating outside NATO to avoid alliance splits — and implicitly positions the EU as a neutral guarantor of navigation rights that Tehran might accept, unlike a US-enforced blockade.

title: Germany slashes fuel tax by €0.17/liter as war energy shock deepens
description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced Germany will cut fuel taxes by €0.17 per liter on petrol and diesel for two months, financed by a tobacco tax increase. Employers can also provide tax-free bonuses up to €1,000. Merz said the measure 'will very quickly improve the situation for drivers and businesses.' German fuel prices had topped €2/liter as the Hormuz crisis and blockade announcement pushed oil back above $100/barrel. Leading economic institutes slashed Germany's 2026 growth forecast to 0.6%, down from 1.3% pre-war. The move followed similar emergency fuel-tax cuts across Europe — Poland set daily maximum prices, Austria cut fuel duties — making Germany the largest economy to resort to direct price intervention since the crisis began.

title: Trump orders US Navy blockade of all Iranian ports through Hormuz
description: Hours after the Islamabad talks collapsed, Trump posted on Truth Social that the US Navy would 'begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships' entering or leaving the Strait of Hormuz, warning Iranian forces would be 'BLOWN TO HELL' if they fired on US vessels or civilian shipping. CENTCOM clarified the blockade targets only maritime traffic to and from Iranian ports, starting April 13 at 10:00 AM ET, and 'will not impede freedom of navigation for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to and from non-Iranian ports.' Iran's IRGC warned that any military vessels approaching the strait 'will be considered a violation of the ceasefire and will be met with severe force,' while insisting the strait remains open for civilian traffic under Iranian regulations. Trump stated: 'We're not going to let Iran make money on selling oil to people that they like. It's going to be all or none.'

title: Oil surges 7-8% on Hormuz blockade; stock futures plunge
description: Brent crude jumped 7.4% to $102/barrel and US crude surged 8% above $104/barrel in overnight trading after Trump's blockade announcement, erasing much of the post-ceasefire decline. Wholesale gasoline prices spiked 6% and heating oil jumped 10%. S&P 500 futures fell 0.8%, Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 1.3%, and Dow futures declined over 500 points. The blockade announcement reversed the market's cautious optimism from the 16-ship Hormuz transit on Sunday — the busiest day since the ceasefire — and signaled that the diplomatic failure would translate directly into tighter energy supply.

title: Araghchi says Iran was 'inches away' from deal; blames US maximalism
description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran had been 'inches away' from signing an 'Islamabad MoU' but encountered 'maximalism, shifting goalposts, and blockade' from the US side. President Masoud Pezeshkian stated agreement remained possible if the US 'abandons its totalitarianism and respects the rights of the Iranian nation.' The Iranian framing contrasted sharply with Vance's 'best and final offer' language, suggesting Tehran wanted to keep the diplomatic channel alive while Washington was already pivoting to coercion. A US official disclosed the five non-negotiable demands: end all uranium enrichment, dismantle major enrichment facilities, accept a broader peace framework, end funding for Hamas/Hezbollah/Houthis, and fully open Hormuz without tolls.

title: US intel: China preparing MANPAD air-defense shipments to Iran
description: CNN reported, citing US intelligence, that China is preparing to deliver shoulder-fired MANPAD anti-aircraft systems to Iran within weeks, routing shipments through third countries to mask their origin. The transfer would represent the first confirmed Chinese weapons delivery to Iran during the war and a direct challenge to Washington days before Trump's planned visit to Beijing. Trump warned China would face 'big problems' if it proceeded. A Chinese embassy spokesperson denied the report: 'China has never provided weapons to any party to the conflict; the information in question is untrue.' The revelation undercut China's role as a ceasefire broker — Beijing had helped mediate the April 7 truce alongside Pakistan.

title: IDF Merkava tank rams UNIFIL Italian vehicles twice in south Lebanon
description: UNIFIL reported that IDF soldiers rammed Italian peacekeeping vehicles with a Merkava tank on two occasions in south Lebanon's Bayada area, causing 'significant damage' in one instance. Israeli soldiers also blocked a road used to access UNIFIL positions. Over the preceding week, the IDF had fired 'warning shots' that struck UNIFIL vehicles — one landing a meter from a dismounted peacekeeper — destroyed surveillance cameras at UNIFIL headquarters in Naqura and five other positions, and spray-painted headquarters windows to obstruct perimeter visibility. Italy's contingent later downplayed the incidents as resulting from 'vehicle maneuvers,' but the pattern of obstruction drew condemnation from UN officials.

title: Israeli strike on Qana kills 5; infant killed at funeral in Srifa
description: Israel struck approximately 30 locations across southern Lebanon and the West Bekaa on Sunday. In Qana — site of the notorious 1996 massacre — an airstrike killed 5 people including 3 women and wounded 25, targeting 'homes and infrastructure.' In Srifa, a strike killed 1.5-year-old Taleen Saeed and several relatives who had gathered for her father's funeral; the father had been killed in an April 8 strike. Grandfather Nasser Saeed: 'They said it was a ceasefire. We went up to the village...suddenly we felt like a storm was landing right on us.' Separately, a drone strike killed Lebanese Red Cross paramedic Hassan Badawi during a mission cleared by UNIFIL. Lebanon's total death toll reached 2,055 including 165 children and 87 health workers.

title: Two supertankers U-turn in Hormuz minutes after Islamabad talks collapse
description: Empty VLCCs Agios Fanourios I (Greek-owned, managed by Eastern Mediterranean Maritime, Iraq-bound) and Shalamar (Pakistan National Shipping Corporation, headed for Das Island, UAE) reversed course near Iran's Larak Island within minutes of the Islamabad talks breakdown being confirmed. The vessels had approached from the Gulf of Oman late Saturday following Iran's approved northern corridor through Iranian territorial waters near Qeshm and Larak islands. A third vessel, Mombasa B, continued through the strait between the two islands. Bloomberg reported the U-turns as the most immediate market signal of the diplomatic failure, with oil futures expected to gap higher on Monday's open.

title: Iran's internet blackout enters day 44 — longest nationwide shutdown ever recorded
description: Iran's internet blackout reached its 44th consecutive day, with NetBlocks confirming it as the longest nationwide internet shutdown on record in any country. Access to the global internet remained at roughly 1% of pre-war levels, with most Iranians limited to a slow state-controlled intranet providing access only to government-approved services and news. Iran's Communications Minister acknowledged the shutdown costs the economy $35.7 million per day. The blackout was first imposed during the January 2026 protests and renewed after the February 28 US-Israeli strikes began, creating an information vacuum that has hampered humanitarian coordination, financial transactions, and civilian communication for over six weeks.

title: Islamabad talks collapse after 21 hours; Vance presents 'best and final offer'
