description: VP Vance concluded 21 hours of direct US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad — the highest-level meeting since 1979 — without a deal, then departed immediately after a 4-minute press conference. Vance said the US sought 'a fundamental commitment' from Iran not to develop nuclear weapons but 'we haven't seen that yet.' He called the US proposal a 'best and final offer,' adding: 'I think that we were quite flexible, we were quite accommodating.' Sources close to the Iranian delegation told Al Jazeera the US was 'looking for an excuse to leave' and that 'the ball is in America's court.' Iranian media said the talks failed due to 'excessive demands' from Washington. No timeline for resumed discussions was set.

title: Israeli strikes kill 11 in southern Lebanon; hospital area hit
description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least 11 people in southern Lebanon on Sunday. In Tuffahta, 8 were killed and 9 wounded (5 critically). In the Toul district near Nabatieh, 3 were killed in multiple consecutive strikes that sent thick smoke plumes near Nabih Berri Governmental University Hospital, with structures reduced to rubble. The cumulative Lebanon toll surpassed 2,020 killed and 6,436 wounded since March 2. The strikes continued as Vance's Islamabad talks were collapsing, underscoring Iran's argument that Israel's Lebanon campaign renders the ceasefire 'meaningless.'

title: Hormuz sees 16 ships transit — busiest day since ceasefire began
description: At least 16 commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday morning, including three crude oil tankers flying Chinese, Hong Kong, and Liberian flags — the busiest single day since the April 8 ceasefire. The uptick followed Saturday's US mine-clearing operation and suggested some shipowners were testing the corridor despite Iran's continued restrictions. However, traffic remained roughly 90% below the pre-war average of 130-160 daily transits, and more than 600 vessels including 325 tankers remained stranded in the Gulf.

title: US destroyers transit Hormuz for mine-clearing; Iran denies and threatens response
description: CENTCOM announced that guided-missile destroyers USS Frank E. Peterson and USS Michael Murphy transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday to begin mine-clearing operations. Admiral Brad Cooper stated: 'Today, we began the process of establishing a new passage, and we will share this safe pathway with the maritime industry soon.' Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters 'strongly denied' the transit occurred, while the IRGC Navy warned: 'Any attempt by military vessels to pass through the Strait of Hormuz will be dealt with severely.' US intelligence had assessed at least a dozen mines in the waterway, including Iran-manufactured Maham 3 moored mines and Maham 7 seabed-sticking mines. CENTCOM said underwater drones would join the effort in coming days.

title: Trump says deal outcome 'makes no difference'; warns China on Iran weapons
description: Speaking at the White House before departing for Miami, Trump declared: 'Whether we make a deal or not makes no difference to me. Regardless of what happens, we win. We totally defeated that country.' He warned China that supplying weapons to Iran would mean 'China's going to have a big problem.' On Hormuz mine-clearing, Trump claimed the US had 'the most sophisticated mine equipment in the world' and the strait would open 'in the not-too-distant future.' The remarks — dismissing the talks his own VP was leading — set the stage for the collapse of negotiations hours later and signaled the US was preparing domestic framing for a return to military operations.

title: Vance arrives in Islamabad; highest-level US-Iran engagement since 1979
description: VP JD Vance landed in Islamabad at 12:06 PM local time to lead the US delegation — alongside Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper — in the highest-level US-Iran engagement since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Vance met Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif, who called the weekend a 'make-or-break moment.' Vance told reporters: 'If the Iranians are willing to negotiate in good faith, we are certainly willing to extend an open hand,' but warned: 'Don't try to play us.' Three hours after arrival, formal negotiations had not commenced as Iran insisted on preconditions. Pakistan sealed Islamabad's Red Zone with shipping containers and deployed hundreds of police and paramilitary forces.

title: Ghalibaf demands Lebanon ceasefire and frozen assets before talks begin
description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X that two preconditions must be met before negotiations with the US can start: a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of Iran's blocked assets abroad. Ghalibaf wrote: 'These two matters must be fulfilled before negotiations begin.' The demand threatened to derail talks before they started. A US official responded: 'False. The meetings have not even started yet,' denying Washington had agreed to unfreeze assets. Iran's frozen reserves are scattered across multiple jurisdictions — roughly $7 billion in Qatar, $6-10 billion in Iraq, and approximately $20 billion in China. Oil prices jumped on the news as traders reassessed the likelihood of a deal.

title: Israel rejects Hezbollah ceasefire; agrees only to Lebanon 'peace talks'
description: Israel announced it would not discuss a ceasefire with Hezbollah when it meets Lebanese officials at the US State Department on Tuesday (April 15). Ambassador Yechiel Leiter stated Israel 'agreed to begin formal peace negotiations' with Lebanon but refused any discussions involving Hezbollah as a party. Hezbollah-affiliated lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah rejected the direct Israel-Lebanon talks entirely, calling them violations of Lebanon's national pact. The disconnect — Israel seeking permanent peace while refusing a truce, Lebanon wanting a ceasefire before substantive talks — left the Tuesday meeting's prospects uncertain.

title: Israeli strikes kill 10 in southern Lebanon; 3 emergency workers among dead
description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least 10 people in southern Lebanon on Saturday, including three civil defense emergency workers — the latest targeting of first responders that Lebanon's Health Ministry condemned as 'systematic.' A residential building in Mayfadoun, Nabatieh district, was destroyed. In Beirut's Caracas neighborhood, civil defense crews continued searching rubble three days after earlier strikes, with 6 confirmed dead and a teenager still missing under a collapsed roof. The cumulative Lebanon toll reached approximately 1,960 killed and 6,300+ wounded since March 2.

title: Brent crude posts steepest weekly decline since August 2022
description: Brent futures settled at $95.20/barrel on Friday, down 12.7% for the week — the steepest weekly decline since August 2022 — as the ceasefire's initial promise of Hormuz reopening drove a massive selloff. US crude fell 13.4% weekly to $96.57. The drop followed a near-13% single-day plunge after the ceasefire announcement on April 8, the biggest one-day fall since the 1991 Gulf War outside COVID. However, prices remained roughly 50% above pre-war levels, and Brent briefly traded above $99 mid-week as traders priced in the ceasefire's fragility and continued supply disruptions from damaged Saudi and Gulf infrastructure.

title: Saudi Finance Minister al-Jadaan arrives in Islamabad for talks
description: Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan arrived in Islamabad on Saturday, signaling Riyadh's direct engagement in the US-Iran peace process despite Saudi Arabia's extensive infrastructure damage from Iranian strikes during the war. Saudi Arabia lost 1.3 million bpd of export capacity from pipeline and processing plant damage. Al-Jadaan's presence added economic weight to Pakistan's mediation, with Saudi Arabia positioning itself as a stakeholder in any deal that would reopen Hormuz and stabilize Gulf energy markets.

title: Hormuz traffic falls to 2 ships; 600+ vessels stranded in Gulf
description: Only 2 commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence — down from 9 in the prior 48 hours and a pre-war average of 130-160 daily. More than 600 vessels, including 325 loaded tankers, remained stranded in the Persian Gulf. Trump claimed the strait would 'open up fairly soon' but offered no specifics. Iran continued requiring advance permission, new navigation lanes closer to its mainland, and avoidance of mine-hazard zones, while an Iranian parliamentarian reiterated that Israeli-linked tankers were 'absolutely prohibited.'

title: US inflation surges to 3.3% as war drives record 21.2% gasoline spike
description: The March CPI report showed US consumer prices rose 3.3% year-over-year — up from 2.4% in February — the fastest pace in nearly two years. Monthly prices jumped 0.9%, triple February's 0.3%. Gasoline prices surged 21.2% in a single month, the steepest monthly increase since the Bureau of Labor Statistics began tracking in 1967. Fuel oil climbed 30.7%. Energy overall drove nearly three-quarters of the monthly increase. Consumers paid an estimated $8.4 billion in additional fuel costs in the first month of the war. Core CPI (excluding food and energy) rose a modest 0.2%, suggesting underlying inflation remained contained while the war-driven energy shock dominated.

title: Starmer and Trump discuss military options to reopen Strait of Hormuz
description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer revealed he and Trump discussed 'military capabilities and the logistics of actually moving vessels through the strait' during a Thursday phone call. Starmer said the UK was leading a coalition of more than 30 countries focused on the Hormuz reopening — a significant escalation from the UK's previous diplomatic-only approach. The call signaled Britain positioning itself as the primary European partner in any military Hormuz operation, despite NATO's broader refusal to join the Iran campaign.

title: Netanyahu expels Spain from US-led Gaza coordination center
description: Netanyahu ordered Spain's removal from the Civil-Military Coordination Centre (CMCC) in Kiryat Gat — the US-led multinational facility overseeing Gaza ceasefire implementation and aid delivery involving nearly 20 countries. Netanyahu stated: 'Spain has defamed our heroes, the soldiers of the IDF... I have instructed today to remove Spain's representatives.' Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar cited Spain's 'obsessive anti-Israel bias.' The expulsion followed Spain's reopening of its Tehran embassy the previous day and its earlier closure of airspace to US warplanes. Spain's FM Albares called the move 'further evidence of Netanyahu's contempt for the international community.'

title: Lebanon-Israel ambassadors hold first-ever call; agree to Tuesday talks
description: Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad and Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter held a three-way phone call mediated by US Ambassador to Lebanon Michael Issa — the first direct contact between Lebanon and Israel at the ambassadorial level in decades. The parties agreed to meet at the US State Department on Tuesday to discuss a ceasefire declaration and begin US-sponsored negotiations. However, fundamental gaps remained: Lebanon insisted on a ceasefire before substantive talks, while Israel refused to discuss a truce with Hezbollah. The diplomatic channel opened as Israeli strikes continued killing dozens daily in southern Lebanon.

title: Israeli strike on Nabatieh government building kills 13 Lebanese security forces
description: An Israeli airstrike hit a State Security directorate building in the southern city of Nabatieh, killing 13 Lebanese state security personnel — the single deadliest strike against Lebanese government forces in the war. President Joseph Aoun condemned the attack, stating that 'targeting state institutions will not deter Lebanon from defending its sovereignty.' The strike was the largest on Nabatieh since fighting began. At least 28 people were killed across Lebanon on April 10, pushing the cumulative toll to 1,953 killed and 6,303 wounded since March 2.

title: Former FM Kamal Kharrazi dies from injuries sustained in April 1 strike
description: Kamal Kharrazi, 76, head of Iran's Strategic Council on Foreign Relations and former foreign minister (1997-2005), died Thursday from injuries sustained when a US-Israeli strike hit his Tehran residence on April 1. His wife was killed in the same attack. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei offered condolences, calling him a 'tireless soldier of diplomacy.' Kharrazi was a member of the Expediency Discernment Council and one of Iran's most prominent diplomatic figures, having served as a key advisor on foreign policy to both the elder and younger Khamenei. His death removed another senior figure from Iran's dwindling pool of experienced diplomats.

title: Zelenskyy reveals 228 Ukrainian experts shooting down Iranian drones in Middle East
description: President Zelenskyy disclosed that 228 Ukrainian military experts had been deployed across several Middle Eastern nations to shoot down Iranian Shahed drones, using Ukraine's domestically produced 'Sting' interceptor drones proven against Russian drone attacks. Zelenskyy told reporters Wednesday (embargoed until Friday): 'This was not about a training mission or exercises, but about support in building a modern air defense system that can actually work.' In exchange, Ukraine received weapons to protect its energy infrastructure, oil and diesel supplies, Patriot system missiles, and financial arrangements. The operations occurred before the April 8 ceasefire.

title: Kuwait accuses Iran of drone attacks on vital facilities during ceasefire
description: Kuwait accused Iran and its proxies of launching drone attacks on April 9 that targeted vital oil installations, power stations, and a National Guard site, causing 'significant material damage' but no injuries. Kuwait's Foreign Ministry stated: 'Continuation of these blatant attacks undermines regional efforts that resulted in the ceasefire announcement.' The IRGC denied responsibility via Tasnim News Agency, claiming it had 'not launched any attacks on Gulf countries since the ceasefire' and that any Iranian strike would be publicly acknowledged. Kuwait called the attacks a 'blatant violation' of international law and the UN Charter.

title: Saudi Arabia confirms Iranian strikes cut East-West pipeline by 700,000 bpd
description: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry issued its first official confirmation that Iranian strikes had damaged key energy infrastructure, including a pumping station on the East-West pipeline (the kingdom's only Hormuz-bypass export route), the Manifa and Khurais oil processing plants, and refining facilities in Jubail, Ras Tanura, Yanbu, and Riyadh. The pipeline lost approximately 700,000 bpd — about 10% of Saudi export capacity — with Manifa and Khurais losing an additional 600,000 bpd combined. The 1.3 million bpd total loss struck at Saudi Arabia's ability to export oil via the Red Sea, the only route available while Hormuz remained effectively closed.

title: Spain reopens Tehran embassy; first Western country to restore presence
description: Spain's Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares announced Spain would immediately reopen its embassy in Tehran and ordered Ambassador Antonio Sanchez-Benedito to return, making Spain the first Western country to restore diplomatic presence in Iran since embassies were evacuated on March 7. Albares said: 'We want to contribute from all fronts, including from Tehran, to efforts for peace.' Spain's FM also accused Israel of 'flouting the ceasefire' with its continued Lebanon strikes. Israeli FM Gideon Saar condemned the move as 'shameless alignment with Tehran.'

title: Vance in Budapest dismisses Iran's 10-point plan as 'written by ChatGPT'
description: VP Vance, in Budapest to campaign for Hungarian PM Viktor Orbán ahead of April 12 elections, dismissed Iran's 10-point peace proposal to reporters. Vance claimed he had 'seen at least three different drafts of the proposals' and said 'The first 10-point proposal was something that was submitted, and we think, frankly, was probably written by ChatGPT.' He called the publicized version the work of a 'random yahoo in Iran submitting it to public access television.' The remarks came days before Vance was set to lead US negotiations in Islamabad, raising questions about the seriousness of American engagement with Iran's framework.

title: Trump: US forces stay in place near Iran, ready for 'next conquest'
description: Trump posted on Truth Social late Wednesday that 'All US ships, aircraft, and military personnel will remain in place in, and around, Iran, until such time as the REAL AGREEMENT reached is fully complied with.' He warned that if terms were not met, 'the Shootin' Starts, bigger, and better, and stronger than anyone has ever seen before.' Trump boasted that US forces were 'Loading Up and Resting, looking forward, actually, to its next Conquest.' The bellicose language — posted one day into the ceasefire — contrasted sharply with the diplomatic process underway in Islamabad and drew immediate criticism from Iran's delegation.

title: Hezbollah missile triggers sirens in central Israel and Tel Aviv
description: Hezbollah launched a missile at Israel on Friday that triggered air raid sirens across central Israel including Tel Aviv — a significant range escalation from its usual northern Israel targets. The IDF confirmed the missile was intercepted; Magen David Adom reported no casualties. Hezbollah claimed it targeted 'Israeli military infrastructure in the northern city of Haifa' in the late hours of Thursday. The strike came two days after Israel's Operation Eternal Darkness killed 303 in Lebanon, and represented Hezbollah's most ambitious targeting since the ceasefire, reaching deeper into Israel than any previous attack in the current conflict.

title: WHO demands Israel reverse Beirut Jnah evacuation order
description: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged Israel to rescind its evacuation order for Beirut's Jnah district, which contains Rafik Hariri University Hospital and Al Zahraa Hospital — two major referral facilities with approximately 450 patients, including 40 in ICU. Tedros said evacuation was 'operationally unfeasible' as no alternative facilities exist. The affected area also includes a health ministry complex and five shelters housing over 5,000 displaced people. Both hospitals were operating at full capacity treating casualties from the April 8 strikes.

title: Hengaw: 7,650 killed in 40-day war; 6,620 military, 1,030 civilians
description: Kurdish human rights group Hengaw published its 10th war report covering February 28 to April 8, documenting at least 7,650 killed — dramatically higher than HRANA's 3,636 figure. The toll includes 6,620 military personnel (predominantly IRGC and army), 1,030 civilians (13.5% of total), at least 189 children, and 215 women. In the four Kurdish border provinces alone, 1,630 military and 112 civilians were killed. The report also documented 14 political prisoner executions during the war and over 2,700 arrests by security institutions. The wide gap between Hengaw and HRANA figures reflects the difficulty of counting military deaths in an active conflict.

title: Hormuz remains at standstill: 9 ships in 48 hours, zero oil tankers
description: Forty-eight hours into the ceasefire, only 9 vessels had transited the Strait of Hormuz — all bulk carriers, with zero oil or gas tankers among them — versus the pre-war average of 100+ daily. UAE oil company CEO Sultan Al Jaber stated bluntly: 'The Strait of Hormuz is not open. Access is being restricted, conditioned and controlled.' Iran required ships to obtain permission, follow new lanes closer to Iran's mainland, and avoid areas marked hazardous on its mine map. An estimated 136 million barrels of crude and refined products remained stranded in the Gulf, with over 230 loaded tankers waiting inside. An Iranian parliamentarian declared Israeli-linked tankers 'absolutely prohibited.'

title: Trump attacks Carlson, Kelly, Owens, Jones as 'nut jobs' over Iran war
description: Trump posted a 485-word Truth Social tirade against Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly, Candace Owens, and Alex Jones — four of the most prominent right-wing media figures — for opposing the Iran war. Trump called them 'stupid people' with 'Low IQs' running 'third rate podcasts,' said Carlson 'should see a good psychiatrist,' called Owens 'crazy,' and described Jones as saying 'some of the dumbest things.' The attack exposed a widening fracture within Trump's base, as the four had intensified criticism after his 'whole civilization will die' threat, arguing the war contradicted his 'no new wars' campaign pledge.

title: US-Iran peace talks open in Islamabad; Vance and Ghalibaf lead delegations
description: The first direct US-Iran negotiations since the war began opened at Islamabad's Serena Hotel, with VP JD Vance, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner leading the US side and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and FM Abbas Araghchi leading Iran's delegation. Pakistan declared a 2-day public holiday (April 9-10), sealed the Red Zone with shipping containers, and deployed hundreds of additional police and paramilitary forces. Deputy PM Ishaq Dar facilitates using an indirect 'shuttle' format — delegations sit in separate rooms with Pakistani officials carrying messages between them. Egypt and Pakistan serve as ceasefire guarantors. The talks must convert the 2-week ceasefire (expiring April 22) into a permanent agreement, with Iran's 10-point plan and uranium enrichment as the central disputes.

title: House Republicans block Democratic war powers vote on Iran
description: Rep. Glenn Ivey (D-MD) attended Thursday's 11:30am pro forma House session and attempted to pass an Iran war powers resolution via unanimous consent. Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), presiding over the session, ignored Ivey's request and gaveled the House out of session, effectively killing the effort. Democrats vowed to force a vote by calling the privilege of the resolution when the House returns to full session next week. Rep. Sara Jacobs (D-CA) stated: 'War powers is a privileged resolution, we plan on calling the privilege next week when we're back.'

title: Israel strikes al-Abbassieh and 5 southern Lebanon towns after Eternal Darkness
description: Israeli strikes continued the day after Operation Eternal Darkness, hitting al-Abbassieh (at least 7 killed, several wounded) and targeting Kafra, Jmaijmeh, Safad al-Battikh, Majdal Selem, and Deir Antar near the Qasmiyeh bridge. Artillery shelling damaged the town of Haris. The IDF also struck crossings over the Litani River and approximately 10 weapons storage facilities. The continued strikes deepened the rift over whether Lebanon falls within the US-Iran ceasefire, with Araghchi warning: 'The US must choose between a ceasefire or continued war via Israel. It cannot have both.'

title: Iranians flood Tehran streets celebrating ceasefire as 'victory' over US
description: Thousands of Iranians took to the streets of Tehran overnight after the ceasefire announcement, converging on Enqelab-e Eslami (Islamic Revolution) Square waving Iranian flags and carrying portraits of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Celebrants burned US and Israeli flags. Iranian state media framed the ceasefire as proof the 'criminal US' accepted 'the general framework' of Iran's 10-point proposal. Celebration and skepticism coexisted — many Iranians expressed relief at the bombing pause while doubting the truce would hold.

title: Houthis operate ship-screening 'tollbooth' in Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb
description: Iran's Houthi allies expanded their selective-access system in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Red Sea, using AIS signals to screen vessels by political identity and allowing only ships that publicly distance themselves from the US and Israel to pass. Ships began transmitting messages emphasizing non-affiliation with Washington and Tel Aviv, with some indicating armed guards aboard. The system mirrors Iran's Hormuz 'tollbooth' model. A senior Iranian source told Reuters: 'If the situation gets out of control, Iran's allies will also close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.' Oil diverted from Hormuz increased Bab el-Mandeb traffic by 21% in March.

title: Netanyahu orders direct Lebanon talks at Trump's request
description: PM Netanyahu instructed officials to begin 'direct negotiations with Lebanon as soon as possible' on disarming Hezbollah and establishing formal peace relations. The move came after Trump urged Netanyahu in a Wednesday call to scale back strikes on Lebanon. Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter will represent Israel; Lebanon's Ambassador Nada Hamadeh-Moawad will lead Beirut's delegation. The first meeting is expected next week at the US State Department, led by US Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa. VP Vance said Israel 'has actually offered to check themselves a little bit in Lebanon.' However, an Israeli official told CNN: 'There is no ceasefire at the moment. Talks will be held under fire.' Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called the proposal 'the only path forward.'

title: Mojtaba Khamenei breaks silence; vows revenge, orders ceasefire compliance
description: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued his first public statement since the ceasefire, delivered via Iranian state television as a written declaration. Khamenei vowed to 'take revenge' for his slain father and all those killed in the war, and said Iran would bring management of the Strait of Hormuz 'into a new phase.' But he simultaneously ordered compliance: 'This is not the end of the war, but all military units must obey orders and uphold the ceasefire.' The statement was his first confirmed communication since the war began, ending weeks of speculation about his location and the regime's leadership continuity.

title: Oil rebounds above $100 as Hormuz stays blocked; only 4 ships transit
description: Oil prices reversed much of the ceasefire-day plunge as markets realized the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed. WTI crude rose 6% to $100.27/barrel; Brent added 4% to $98.26/barrel. Only 4 ships transited Hormuz on Wednesday — the lowest since March 31 — versus the normal ~135 daily. Over 400 oil-laden tankers and dozens of LNG carriers remained anchored outside the Gulf. Tehran required ships to obtain permission before passage. Shipping firm Hapag-Lloyd warned normalization was 'weeks, if not months' away. The US national average gas price hit $4.17/gallon.

title: Dow surges 1,325 points on ceasefire; S&P up 2.5%, Nasdaq 2.8%
description: US stock markets rallied sharply on the ceasefire announcement. The Dow Jones surged 1,325 points (2.9%) to close at 47,910; the S&P 500 jumped 166 points (2.5%) to 6,783; the Nasdaq rose 2.8%. Market analyst Nigel Green noted: 'Markets have been primed for this moment — positioning had become defensive, volatility was elevated, and energy prices were reflecting worst-case assumptions.' The rally came despite oil prices rebounding the following day as Hormuz remained effectively closed.

title: US demands allies submit Hormuz security plans within days
description: Bloomberg reported the US demanded European allies, Japan, and Canada submit concrete plans to secure the Strait of Hormuz within 'a few days,' shifting post-war maritime security burden to partners. The request was delivered during Trump's White House meeting with NATO Secretary General Rutte, and in parallel discussions at the Pentagon and State Department. The UK-led coalition of 40+ nations was pressed for specific commitments beyond general pledges. The demand effectively told allies: if you want Hormuz open, you help keep it open.

title: Iranians mark arbaeen for Khamenei; Mojtaba unseen since war began
description: Thousands of Iranians gathered in Tehran and cities across Iran to mark 40 days (arbaeen) since Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's assassination on February 28, carrying flags and portraits of the slain leader. Home mourning ceremonies were held April 8-10 with mass recitation of Surah Al-Fath. Notably, successor Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared publicly since the war began, raising questions about his location and the regime's leadership continuity. The arbaeen traditionally marks the end of the formal Shiite mourning cycle.

title: Iran ambassador deletes post on Islamabad delegation; talks uncertain
description: Iran's ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, posted then quickly deleted a social media announcement that an Iranian delegation would arrive 'tonight in Islamabad for serious talks based on 10 points proposed by Iran.' An embassy official told AFP the post was removed due to 'timing' concerns. Hours later, Pakistan deployed hundreds of additional police and paramilitary forces in Islamabad, sealing off parts of the city with shipping containers around the Red Zone. The deletion created uncertainty about whether Iran would participate constructively in Friday's scheduled talks.

title: Israel launches 'Operation Eternal Darkness'; 303 killed in Lebanon
description: Israel launched Operation Eternal Darkness, its largest strike on Lebanon since the war began, hitting over 100 Hezbollah targets in approximately 10 minutes starting at 14:00 EEST with 50 fighter jets and 160 munitions. Targets included command centers, intelligence facilities, missile infrastructure, Radwan Force sites, and aerial/naval units across Beirut, southern Lebanon, Sidon, Tyre, and the Bekaa Valley. Lebanon's health ministry initially reported 254 killed; the toll was revised on April 9 to 303 killed and 1,150 wounded, making it the war's deadliest day in Lebanon. Cumulative Lebanese death toll reached 1,888 killed and 6,092 wounded. A strike hit a funeral in Shmestar killing 10 mourners; three girls were killed in Adloun; Doctors Without Borders staff were injured at Hiram Hospital in Tyre. Defense Minister Katz claimed over 200 Hezbollah militants killed, with total Hezbollah fighter deaths exceeding 1,400.

title: FBI, NSA, CISA warn Iran hackers disrupting US water and energy sites
description: A joint advisory from the FBI, NSA, CISA, and Department of Energy warned that Iranian government-linked hackers had breached and disrupted multiple US oil and gas and water/wastewater facilities. The hackers exploited internet-facing programmable logic controllers (PLCs) manufactured by Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, causing industrial processes to shut down and forcing facilities to switch to manual operations. The advisory called it an 'escalation' of Tehran's cyber campaign since the war began, noting the attacks 'tested the safety systems at US industrial plants that protect human life.'

title: HRANA reports 3,636 killed in Iran war; 1,701 civilians
description: The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) published an updated death toll for the 40-day Iran war: 3,636 killed including 1,701 civilians, 1,221 military personnel, and 714 unclassified. At least 15% of civilian casualties were under 18. The figures cannot be independently verified as Iran has not released official casualty numbers. HRANA's count is widely cited by international media and rights organizations as the most comprehensive tracker of the war's human toll.

title: Ghalibaf calls Islamabad peace talks 'unreasonable' amid violations
description: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf escalated his rhetoric from the previous day's complaints, declaring the upcoming Islamabad talks 'unreasonable' given Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon, Israeli drone overflights of Iranian airspace, and US demands that Iran abandon uranium enrichment. Ghalibaf insisted enrichment would continue under ceasefire terms, directly contradicting Trump's claim that Iran agreed to halt enrichment. The statement raised doubts about whether Iran would participate constructively in Saturday's scheduled negotiations.

title: UK, France, Germany, Australia demand Lebanon ceasefire inclusion
description: UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper stated 'We want to see Lebanon included in the ceasefire,' calling Israel's strikes 'deeply damaging.' France, Germany, Australia, and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres echoed the demand, calling for 'quick progress towards a substantive negotiated settlement.' The joint pressure contradicted Washington and Tel Aviv's insistence that Lebanon was excluded from the US-Iran truce. Cooper's statement marked the UK's most explicit break with the US on the Lebanon question since the war began.

title: Israel kills Hezbollah SG Qassem's nephew in Beirut strike
description: The IDF struck and killed Ali Yusuf Harshi, personal secretary and nephew of Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem, in a targeted Beirut strike. The IDF also hit approximately 10 weapons storage facilities and two key crossings north and south of the Litani River used for transferring weapons. The targeted assassination of a senior figure in Qassem's inner circle signaled Israel's intent to continue decapitating Hezbollah leadership despite the US-Iran ceasefire.

title: Trump warns 'the shootin' starts' if ceasefire terms not met
description: Trump posted on Truth Social warning that 'the Shootin' Starts' if the ceasefire agreement is violated, adding that 'all US ships, aircraft, and military personnel will remain in place' until the 'real agreement is fully complied with.' The US maintains 50,000 troops in the Middle East with two carrier strike groups, nearly 20 warships, and over a dozen air squadrons. VP Vance reinforced the threat, telling reporters: 'If Iran fails to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the president is not going to abide by our terms.'

title: Lebanon declares national day of mourning after 303 killed
description: PM Nawaf Salam declared Thursday April 9 a national day of mourning following Israel's deadliest single-day attack on Lebanon, with the death toll revised upward to 303 killed and 1,150 wounded. All public institutions closed, flags flew at half-staff, and broadcast programming was adjusted. Salam vowed to mobilize 'all of Lebanon's political and diplomatic resources to stop the Israeli killing machine.' Cumulative Lebanese death toll from the war reached 1,888 killed and 6,092 wounded. Hundreds gathered in Times Square, New York, demanding a permanent end to the war and halt to Lebanon bombing.

title: IRGC downs Israeli Hermes 900 drone over Fars province
description: Iran's IRGC intercepted and destroyed an Israeli Hermes 900 surveillance drone over Lar in Fars province using its new aerospace defense system integrated into Iran's air defense network. The IRGC declared the overflight a 'flagrant violation' of the ceasefire, warning that 'the entry of any aircraft of the American and Zionist enemies into Iranian airspace — even without military operations — will be considered a violation' triggering a 'decisive response.' The drone's wreckage was reportedly seized for technical examination.

title: Hezbollah fires rockets at Manara; first strike since ceasefire
description: Hezbollah fired rockets at the kibbutz of Manara in northern Israel early Thursday, its first attack since the US-Iran ceasefire took effect. Hezbollah stated it was informed the ceasefire included Lebanon and had halted attacks Wednesday, but Israel's massive Lebanon strikes violated the truce. Hezbollah warned: 'This response will continue until the Israeli-American aggression against our country and our people ceases.' The IDF reported intercepting incoming missiles. The attack underscored the fragility of a ceasefire whose scope remains disputed.

title: Trump slams NATO in Rutte meeting: 'Tested, and they failed'
description: Trump met NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at the White House for over two hours, using the session to denounce allied inaction during the Iran war. Spokeswoman Karoline Leavitt quoted Trump: 'They were tested, and they failed.' Rutte told CNN afterward: 'He is clearly disappointed with many NATO allies, and I can see his point.' Trump then posted on Truth Social: 'NATO WASN'T THERE WHEN WE NEEDED THEM, AND THEY WON'T BE THERE IF WE NEED THEM AGAIN. REMEMBER GREENLAND.' Bloomberg reported Trump raised the possibility of US withdrawal from the alliance during the meeting.

title: House Democrats demand Iran war powers vote at Thursday session
description: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries announced Democrats would demand passage of a War Powers Resolution via unanimous consent at Thursday's 11:30am pro forma session, following it with a public address from the Capitol grounds. The push gained momentum after Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-TX) reversed his previous opposition, having voted against an earlier war powers measure that failed 219-212 on March 5. Jeffries framed Trump's 'whole civilization will die' threat as proof the president's war authority must be curtailed.

title: Pezeshkian tells Pakistan: Lebanon ceasefire is 'essential condition'
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif that a ceasefire in Lebanon is an 'essential condition' of Iran's 10-point peace plan, directly contradicting US and Israeli claims that Lebanon is excluded from the truce. The statement escalated the dispute that had already prompted Iran to re-close the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Tasnim news agency reported Tehran would withdraw from the ceasefire entirely if Israeli attacks on Lebanon continued, raising the prospect of the 2-week truce collapsing before Islamabad talks begin Friday.

title: Ghalibaf accuses US of violating 3 ceasefire conditions; Vance disputes
description: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused the US of 'openly and clearly' violating three of Iran's 10 ceasefire conditions: failing to halt strikes on Lebanon, violating Iranian airspace with drones, and denying Iran's right to uranium enrichment. VP Vance dismissed the complaints, calling them a 'legitimate misunderstanding' and stating the US never promised to include Lebanon. Vance added: 'Iran would be dumb to let the talks collapse over Lebanon.' The US also said the 10-point plan published by Iran was not the version approved as the basis for negotiations.

title: IRGC navy publishes Hormuz mine map with safe shipping corridors
description: Iran's IRGC navy posted maps showing alternative shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz to avoid naval mines — the first official Iranian acknowledgment of mine placement in the waterway. The safe entry path runs from the Sea of Oman north of Larak Island; the exit path passes south of Larak Island. Despite the ceasefire's Hormuz reopening pledge, only 2 ships — the Greek-owned NJ Earth and Liberia-flagged Daytona Beach — transited overnight, with traffic still 90% below normal. Over 800 freighters remained trapped inside the Gulf.

title: Vance to lead US delegation at Islamabad peace talks Friday
description: Trump announced Vice President JD Vance will lead the US negotiating team at the first round of direct US-Iran talks in Islamabad on Friday, April 10. Special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will also participate. Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif invited both delegations, with the talks aimed at converting the 2-week ceasefire into a permanent agreement. Iran confirmed its participation, with FM Araghchi expected to lead Tehran's delegation.

title: Hegseth declares Iran's defense-industrial base 'completely destroyed'
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon 'has done its part' and that Iran's defense-industrial base has been 'completely' destroyed after 40 days of strikes. Hegseth framed the ceasefire as a military victory, stating the US had achieved all its operational objectives. The claim could not be independently verified. Iran's armed forces have not publicly acknowledged the extent of damage to their military infrastructure.

title: Gulf states attacked hours after ceasefire; Qatar intercepts 7 missiles
description: Five Gulf states reported Iranian attacks hours after the ceasefire announcement. Qatar intercepted 7 ballistic missiles and multiple drones. Saudi Arabia downed 9 drones. Kuwait's defenses engaged 28 drones targeting oil installations and power stations, with 'severe material damage' at Kuwait Petroleum Corp facilities. A fire broke out at Abu Dhabi's Habshan gas complex from interception debris, injuring 3. Bahrain intercepted a drone over Sitra Island, injuring 2 citizens. Iran attributed the strikes to launches initiated before the ceasefire took effect.

title: Oil plunges 14-16% on ceasefire; WTI drops to $94.52, Brent to $93.73
description: Oil prices collapsed on the ceasefire announcement. West Texas Intermediate fell 14.3% to $94.52/barrel; Brent crude dropped 13.1% to $93.73/barrel — the largest single-day decline since the war began. S&P 500 futures surged 2.3%. Both benchmarks remained well above pre-war levels (~$70/barrel in late February). Analysts cautioned that prices could reverse if the ceasefire collapses or if Hormuz remains effectively closed despite Iran's reopening pledge.

title: Iran re-halts Hormuz shipping after Israel's Lebanon strikes
description: Iran halted oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz hours after the first vessels were allowed to pass under the ceasefire, citing Israel's massive Lebanon strikes as a violation of the truce. Iran's semi-official Fars news agency reported the passage suspension. Only 3 ships had left the region on Wednesday, versus the normal ~135 daily transits. Over 800 freighters remained stuck inside the Gulf. FM Araghchi stated: 'The Iran–US ceasefire terms are clear and explicit: The US must choose — ceasefire or continued war via Israel. It cannot have both.'

title: Netanyahu declares ceasefire excludes Lebanon; Iran threatens deal collapse
description: PM Netanyahu stated the US-Iran ceasefire 'does not include Lebanon,' directly contradicting Pakistani PM Sharif's claim that the deal covers 'Lebanon and elsewhere.' Netanyahu added the ceasefire is 'not the end of the war' and that 'all goals will be achieved.' Iran responded that Lebanon's inclusion is non-negotiable, with Araghchi warning the US must choose between the ceasefire and allowing Israeli strikes on Lebanon. The dispute immediately threatened the fragile truce.

title: US and Iran agree to 2-week ceasefire; Pakistan brokers deal 90 min before deadline
description: Pakistan's PM Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir requested Trump halt strikes planned for that night, and at 9:48pm ET — 90 minutes before Trump's 8pm deadline effectively expired — Trump announced a 2-week ceasefire on Truth Social. Terms: US and Israel suspend strikes on Iran; Iran commits to 'COMPLETE, IMMEDIATE, and SAFE OPENING of the Strait of Hormuz'; negotiations begin Friday in Islamabad. Iran and Oman can charge transit fees for reconstruction. Neither side committed to sanctions lifting, frozen assets, or US troop withdrawal. The ceasefire is extendable by mutual agreement.

title: Iran strikes Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait; 15 US soldiers injured
description: An Iranian UAV struck the Ali al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, injuring 15 American soldiers. The base has served as a key staging area for US air operations since the war began. Separately, Iran fired 7 ballistic missiles intercepted by Saudi Arabia, and a reported strike hit the al-Jubail refineries. In Bahrain, traffic on the King Fahd Causeway was halted following an Iranian attack. Iran stated its 'restraint in targeting oil infrastructure in the region would no longer apply' following the Kharg Island strikes.

title: Iranian civilians form human chains at power plants against Trump's threat
description: Hundreds of Iranian civilians formed human chains around power plants across Iran after Trump threatened to destroy the country's entire electrical grid by 8pm ET. Fars news agency broadcast footage of crowds encircling the Kazerun combined-cycle power plant in Fars Province. The demonstrations spread to multiple facilities, with participants declaring they would shield civilian infrastructure with their bodies. Iran has an installed power capacity of ~90 GW serving 85 million people.

title: US strikes Kharg Island military targets ahead of Trump's deadline
description: US forces struck dozens of military targets on Kharg Island hours before Trump's 8pm deadline, including IRGC positions on the island's northern side. The strikes avoided oil and gas infrastructure — Kharg handles ~90% of Iran's oil exports. In response, Iran declared that its restraint on targeting Gulf oil infrastructure 'would no longer apply,' raising the prospect of retaliatory strikes on Saudi, Emirati, and Kuwaiti energy facilities. Separately, strikes hit two shipbuilding companies in Khorramshahr and multiple sites across Isfahan, Shiraz, Yazd, Parchin, and Bandar Chabahar.

title: US-Israel destroys 8 bridges and 10+ railway segments across Iran
description: The IDF destroyed sections of 8 bridges across Iran used for transporting weapons and military equipment, hitting targets in Tehran, Karaj, Tabriz, Kashan, and Qom. Netanyahu stated: 'Yesterday we destroyed transport aircraft and dozens of helicopters, and today we attacked the railway lines and bridges.' Approximately 10 railway segments were also struck, including the Kashan railway bridge (killing 2), the Tabriz-Zanjan rail bridge, and tracks near Karaj. The infrastructure campaign fulfilled Trump's April 6 threat that Tuesday would be 'Bridge Day.'

title: Trump warns 'a whole civilization will die tonight' ahead of Iran deadline
description: At 8:07am ET, Trump posted on Truth Social: 'A whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again. I don't want that to happen, but it probably will.' The statement prompted White House denials that nuclear weapons were being considered. House Minority Leader Jeffries called Trump 'completely unhinged.' Amnesty International's Agnès Callamard said the threats 'reveal a staggering level of cruelty and disregard for human life.' Senate Minority Leader Schumer issued a rare joint statement warning the threat could constitute war crimes.

title: IDF destroys dozens of aircraft at 3 Tehran-area airports
description: The Israeli Air Force struck three airports in the Tehran area overnight — Bahram, Mehrabad, and Azmayesh — destroying dozens of Iranian military aircraft on the ground. The IDF said the strikes aimed to deliver a decisive blow to both the Iranian air force and the IRGC air force. Mehrabad also serves as Tehran's domestic civilian airport. Separate strikes hit targets in Shiraz, Isfahan, Karaj, and Qom.

title: Israel strikes South Pars petrochemical complex; half of Iran's output halted
description: Israeli warplanes struck the South Pars petrochemical complex in Asaluyeh, targeting the Jam and Damavand facilities. Defense Minister Israel Katz described the sites as 'critical assets responsible for around half of Iran's petrochemical output.' Production was suspended. A separate strike hit a petrochemical facility near Marvdasht. Combined with the April 4 Mahshahr strikes, Iran has now lost the majority of its operational petrochemical capacity.

title: IDF kills IRGC Intelligence chief Khademi and Quds Force Unit 840 commander
description: Israel killed Majid Khademi, head of the IRGC Intelligence Directorate since June 2025, and Yazdan Mir (also known as Asghar Bakeri), commander of Unit 840 — the Quds Force's special operations division responsible for overseas attacks. The IDF confirmed both eliminations. Separately, Brigadier General Masoud Zare, commander of Iran's Air Defense College, was killed April 5 in an Israeli strike in Isfahan.

title: Iranian missile kills 4 in Haifa residential building
description: An Iranian ballistic missile scored a direct hit on a residential building in Haifa, killing 4 civilians and injuring approximately 10. Cumulative Israeli civilian toll since the war began: 23 killed and over 7,035 injured. A total of 6,700 residents from 42 municipalities have been evacuated from damaged homes. Iran's attack frequency has dropped to 7.7 waves daily over the past week, down from the 12.4 daily average since the war began.

title: Iran rejects temporary ceasefire; sends 10-clause counter-proposal via Pakistan
description: Iran conveyed a formal response to US ceasefire demands through Pakistan, rejecting any temporary ceasefire as allowing 'adversaries to pause and prepare for continuation of the conflict.' Iran's 10-clause counter-proposal demands a permanent end to hostilities, a legal protocol for Strait of Hormuz transit using transit-fee revenue for war reparations, full lifting of sanctions, and reconstruction aid. Mediators from Egypt, Pakistan, and Turkey are discussing a two-phase framework: a 45-day ceasefire followed by permanent peace negotiations. A White House official called the 45-day plan 'one of many ideas' being discussed.

title: Trump sets Tuesday 8pm ET Hormuz deadline; threatens bridges and power plants
description: Trump extended his Hormuz ultimatum by 20 hours to Tuesday April 7 at 8pm ET, posting on Truth Social: 'Tuesday will be Power Plant Day, and Bridge Day, all wrapped up in one, in Iran.' He told reporters 'the entire country can be taken out in one night' and that the US would 'take Iran's oil.' Crude prices jumped from $112 to $114/barrel during his press conference. EU Council President Costa responded that targeting civilian infrastructure 'is illegal.'

title: Lebanon expels Iranian ambassador, bans Hezbollah's military wing
description: Lebanon's Council of Ministers voted to ban Hezbollah's military and security apparatus and ordered the group to hand over its weapons. Foreign Minister Youssef Ragi announced Lebanon is expelling Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Reza Raouf Sheibani, declaring him persona non grata for Iran's 'continuing interference in Lebanon's internal affairs.' The moves represent Lebanon's sharpest break with Hezbollah and Iran since the group's founding in 1982.

title: Iran's Velayati threatens Bab al-Mandeb closure alongside Hormuz
description: Ali Akbar Velayati, adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, posted on X that 'the unified command of the Resistance front views Bab al-Mandeb as it does Hormuz,' warning: 'If the White House dares to repeat its foolish mistakes, it will soon realize that the flow of global energy and trade can be disrupted with a single move.' The threat implies Iran-backed Houthis could blockade the Red Sea's southern chokepoint, through which ~12% of global trade passes, in addition to the already-closed Strait of Hormuz.

title: Iran hangs Ali Fahim, 23; 10th political prisoner executed in 8 days
description: Iran executed Ali Fahim, 23, convicted of involvement in an attack on a Tehran Basij militia base during the January protests. Human rights groups said Fahim was tortured and denied legal counsel during an expedited trial. IHR director Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam said: 'These executions are part of the Islamic republic's strategy of survival — waging war against its own people under the shadow of external conflict.' Authorities have executed 10 political prisoners in the past 8 days — 4 for protest charges, 6 for alleged MEK membership.

title: IAEA warns Bushehr strikes risk 'severe radiological accident'
description: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi warned that ongoing military strikes near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant could cause a 'severe radiological accident' with consequences extending beyond Iran's borders. A projectile struck an area approximately 250 feet from the reactor — the fourth time the site has been targeted since the war began. The most recent previous strike, on April 4, killed a security staff member. Grossi urged an immediate ceasefire around all nuclear facilities.

title: UAE intercepts 60 Iranian projectiles; Fujairah communications building hit
description: UAE air defenses engaged 9 ballistic missiles, 1 cruise missile, and 50 UAVs launched from Iran on April 5. An Iranian UAV struck a communications building in Fujairah, on the Gulf of Oman coast. Borouge petrochemical plant caught fire from falling interception debris. Operations at Khor Fakkan port were suspended for damage assessment. Bahrain intercepted 13 drones in the same period, bringing its cumulative interceptions since February 28 to 188 ballistic missiles and 466 drones.

title: Iranian drones hit Kuwait power plants and desalination facilities again
description: Iranian drone strikes damaged two additional Kuwait power and water desalination plants, knocking out two electricity-generating units. Approximately 90% of Kuwait's drinking water comes from desalination plants, deepening concerns about civilian water supply. Fires broke out at the Shuwaikh Oil Sector Complex, with Kuwait Petroleum Corp reporting 'significant material losses.' In Bahrain, drones struck Gulf Petrochemical Industries and a Bapco Energies oil storage tank, starting fires that were later contained.

title: Israeli Easter Sunday strikes kill 11 across Lebanon
description: Israeli airstrikes on Easter Sunday killed at least 11 people across Lebanon. A strike on Kfarhata village killed 7 including a 4-year-old child. In Beirut's Jnah neighborhood, 4 were killed and 39 injured. Eight additional airstrikes hit southern Beirut suburbs. The IDF also struck two Hezbollah-controlled 'Al-Amana' gas stations, bringing the total gas stations destroyed since Operation Roaring Lion to over 15. A Lebanese army soldier was killed in a separate strike in southern Lebanon.

title: Missing F-15 WSO rescued from Iran; CIA deception campaign, dozens of special forces used
description: The missing F-15E Weapons System Officer — shot down over Iran on April 3 — was rescued by US special forces early Sunday after evading capture in the mountains for over a day. The CIA ran a deception campaign, spreading false intelligence inside Iran that the WSO had already been found and was being ground-exfiltrated, buying time for the actual rescue. Trump described the operation as 'one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in U.S. History,' involving dozens of special forces personnel and dozens of warplanes. The WSO sustained injuries and was flown to Kuwait for treatment. During the operation, Iran struck two US Black Hawk helicopters — both returned to base — and claimed to have also downed an HC-130 tanker aircraft.

title: UAE intercepts 23 ballistic missiles and 56 UAVs; Oracle Dubai office hit by debris
description: The UAE Ministry of Defence reported intercepting 23 ballistic missiles and 56 UAVs launched from Iran on April 4 — the largest single-day attack on the UAE since the war began. Debris from one interception struck the facade of Oracle's office in Dubai Internet City; no injuries were reported. The IRGC claimed it deliberately targeted Oracle's data center; Dubai's Media Office called the claim 'fake news.' The IRGC has previously threatened US tech companies operating in the Gulf, naming Apple, Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Boeing as potential targets.

title: IDF destroys 2 Bekaa Valley bridges linking Sohmor and Mashghara
description: Israeli warplanes destroyed two bridges linking Sohmor and Mashghara in the western Bekaa Valley after IDF spokesman Avichay Adraee warned residents to evacuate. The strikes isolated the western Bekaa from the rest of Lebanon and cut Hezbollah's supply routes between Syria and the south. Israel has now destroyed at least 8 bridges over or near the Litani River since intensifying operations in early March. Humanitarian organizations warned the destruction blocks delivery of food, medicine, and emergency services to towns already cut off by displacement orders.

title: Iran cluster submunitions hit near IDF Kirya HQ in Tel Aviv; school and parking lot damaged
description: Two Iranian cluster submunitions struck a parking lot adjacent to the IDF's Kirya military headquarters in Tel Aviv and damaged a nearby school; no injuries were reported at the base itself. Iran fired multiple missile salvos across central Israel throughout the day, injuring 6 people across Tel Aviv, Bnei Brak, Petah Tikva, Givatayim, Ramat Gan, and Rosh HaAyin, with multiple cars destroyed by shrapnel in Ramat Gan.

title: US-Israel strikes Mahshahr petrochemical hub in Khuzestan; 5 killed, 170 injured
description: US-Israeli airstrikes hit the Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Economic Zone in Khuzestan Province, killing at least 5 people and injuring approximately 170. Facilities targeted included the Fajr 1, Fajr 2, Rajal, and Amir Kabir petrochemical plants. The IDF confirmed the strikes, stating the sites produced materials for ballistic missiles; all production was halted. Separate strikes hit an auxiliary building at the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant compound and Shahid Beheshti University in Tehran — marking more than 30 universities struck since the war began.

title: Trump issues 48-hour Hormuz ultimatum; Iran general: 'gates of hell will open for you'
description: Trump posted on Truth Social: 'Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them,' demanding Iran open the Strait of Hormuz or face massive strikes by Monday. Iran's Gen. Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi dismissed the ultimatum as a 'helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action,' adding: 'The gates of hell will open for you.' FM Araghchi said Iran remains open to diplomacy but the US 15-point plan is 'unreasonable.' The 48-hour deadline expires April 6, coinciding with Trump's extended pause on energy infrastructure strikes.

title: A-10 Warthog downed near Hormuz during F-15 rescue mission; pilot ejects into Kuwait
description: A US Air Force A-10 Thunderbolt II was struck by Iranian hostile fire while flying combat search-and-rescue support for the downed F-15E crew. The pilot managed to maneuver the damaged aircraft into Kuwaiti airspace before ejecting safely and was rescued. US officials confirmed the loss to the New York Times. It was the second American aircraft lost in under 24 hours — Iran claimed responsibility for both shootdowns — and marked the first A-10 lost in combat since the aircraft's introduction in 1977.

title: Iran shoots down US F-15E over Iran; 1 crew rescued, 1 missing
description: Iran shot down a US F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet over Iranian territory, the first American aircraft lost in the conflict. Both crew members ejected safely. US special forces located and rescued one crew member on Iranian soil; the second remains missing. Iran offered a bounty to civilians in the area to join the search. Israel suspended airstrikes in areas 'relevant' to the rescue operation to avoid endangering the missing airman. Weapons experts confirmed debris photos were consistent with an F-15E Strike Eagle.

title: Iranian drones hit Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery and desalination plant
description: Iranian drones struck Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery for the third time since the war began, sparking fires at operational units. A separate strike hit a Kuwaiti power-and-desalination plant, causing 'material' damage — the second confirmed hit on Kuwait's water infrastructure in four days. No employees were reported injured. Kuwait blamed Iran; the IRGC denied responsibility. Kuwait's 1.6 million residents depend heavily on desalinated water, raising concerns about civilian water supply.

title: Drone strike destroys Red Crescent aid warehouse in Bushehr province
description: A drone strike at approximately 5:30 a.m. hit an Iranian Red Crescent Society warehouse in Choghadak, Bushehr province. Bushehr Red Crescent Director General Ehsan Izadpanah confirmed two aid containers, two buses, and multiple emergency vehicles were destroyed. No casualties were reported. The IFRC did not attribute blame. Three IFRC personnel have been killed since the war began on February 28.

title: Hegseth fires Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George and two other generals
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth forced Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George into immediate retirement, along with Gen. David Hodne (Transformation and Training Command) and Maj. Gen. William Green Jr. (Chief of Chaplains). The NYT reported George clashed with Hegseth over the blocking of four officer promotions — two Black officers and two women — from a list of 29. George had requested a meeting to discuss the issue two weeks prior; Hegseth refused. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell thanked George for his 'decades of service.' Gen. Chris LaNeve is expected to serve as acting chief of staff.

title: French and Japanese ships make first Western/Asian Hormuz crossings since war began
description: The Maltese-flagged CMA CGM Kribi, owned by France's CMA CGM (world's third-largest container line), transited the Strait of Hormuz eastbound — the first Western European-linked vessel to cross since the war began. The ship navigated the approved corridor between Qeshm and Larak islands after coordinating with Iranian maritime authorities. Separately, the Japanese LNG tanker SOHAR LNG entered the strait, attempting the first Japanese crossing since the conflict started. Strait traffic remains down approximately 90% since March 1, with only ~150 vessels transiting per Lloyd's List Intelligence.

title: Three UNIFIL peacekeepers wounded by explosion in southern Lebanon
description: An explosion inside a UNIFIL position near Adaisseh in southern Lebanon wounded three peacekeepers, two of them seriously. The source of the explosion remains unknown. This was the third UNIFIL incident in a week: an Indonesian peacekeeper was killed on March 29, and two more were killed the following day near the Israeli border. Cumulative since March 2: 10 IDF soldiers and 2 civilians killed on the Lebanon front; 1,045 Hezbollah attack waves recorded.

title: Oil surges 11% as war escalation fears mount; WTI hits $111.54
description: WTI crude surged 11.4% to $111.54/barrel while Brent jumped 7.8% to $109.03, erasing days of de-escalation optimism. WTI continued trading above Brent, an unusual inversion indicating severe near-term US supply anxiety. The spike was driven by the F-15 shootdown, continued Gulf strikes on energy infrastructure, and Trump's threat that the US 'hasn't even started destroying what's left in Iran. Bridges next, then Electric Power Plants!' US gas prices reached $4.09/gallon, 37% above pre-war levels.

title: UAE intercepts 19 missiles and 26 drones; Habshan gas facility hit
description: UAE air defenses engaged 19 ballistic missiles and 26 drones launched from Iran on Thursday. An Iranian strike hit the Habshan gas processing complex in Abu Dhabi — a major facility — forcing operations to suspend during emergency response. Falling debris injured 12 people: 7 Nepalese nationals and 5 Indian nationals. Cumulative UAE toll since February 28: 2 service members killed and 191 injured. Bahrain also sounded warning sirens with highway traffic diverted due to falling debris.

title: Iranian missile kills 1 in Tel Aviv; train station damaged by shrapnel
description: An Iranian missile struck a residential building in Tel Aviv, killing one civilian and wounding two others. Shrapnel damaged a nearby train station. Iran maintained its 'consistent attack pattern' throughout the day with multiple salvos targeting the Tel Aviv metropolitan area, with secondary attacks on southern, northern, and Jerusalem regions. Cumulative Israeli civilian toll: 19 killed, over 6,594 injured since the war began. The IDF identified 434 total Iranian attack waves since the conflict started.

title: IDF advances to Litani River, reoccupies pre-2024 ceasefire positions; Lebanese army withdraws
description: Israeli forces advanced deeper into southern Lebanon, reaching the Litani River and reoccupying positions held before the November 2024 Hezbollah ceasefire. The Lebanese Armed Forces withdrew from border villages as Israeli troops moved in. Israeli strikes killed 27 people and wounded 105 in Lebanon on Thursday alone — the single deadliest day in Lebanon since the war began. Cumulative Lebanese dead since March 2: 1,345, including 125 children.

title: Iran executes 18-year-old protester Amirhossein Hatami, 84 days after arrest
description: Iran hanged 18-year-old musician Amirhossein Hatami at Ghezel Hesar Prison, 84 days after his arrest during the January 2026 protests. He was charged with attacking a Basij militia facility. His trial lasted one day in Branch 15 of Tehran's Revolutionary Court — presided over by Judge Abolqasem Salavati, known as the 'Judge of Death' — with court-appointed counsel he did not choose. Televised confessions obtained under duress were broadcast 10 days after his arrest. Amnesty International called it 'the arbitrary execution of a teenage protester' following a 'grossly unfair' trial.

title: US-Israeli strikes devastate Tehran's Pasteur Institute; Iran calls it 'barbaric assault'
description: US-Israeli strikes heavily damaged the Pasteur Institute of Iran, a century-old medical research center in Tehran that has produced vaccines and conducted infectious disease research since 1920. Iranian FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei called it 'heartbreaking, cruel, despicable, and utterly outrageous — a barbaric assault on basic human core values.' The Health Ministry warned of a 'direct assault on international health security.' Neither the US nor Israel claimed responsibility. The same day, strikes hit the Karaj B1 commuter bridge near Tehran twice, and forced Iran's two largest steel plants offline with 6-12 month restart estimates. Iran's cumulative war dead reached 3,519 including 1,598 civilians and at least 244 children, with over 113,000 civilian sites damaged per Iran's Red Crescent.

title: Iran and Oman draft protocol requiring permits and tolls for Hormuz transit
description: Iran's Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi announced that Iran and Oman are drafting a bilateral protocol to 'supervise and coordinate' all vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Ships would need advance permits from Iranian and Omani authorities; Gharibabadi insisted the requirements 'do not constitute restrictions' but aim to 'facilitate and ensure safe passage.' Fortune reported vessels are being charged up to $2 million per transit, with Iran doubling its pre-war oil export revenues from the tolls. US equities reversed earlier losses and turned green on the news, as markets read the protocol as a step toward partial reopening. The protocol is described as a 'peacetime framework' in its final internal drafting stages before formal negotiations with Oman.

title: 40 nations join UK-led coalition demanding Iran reopen Strait of Hormuz
description: UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper convened a virtual meeting of 40 nations — including France, Germany, Italy, Canada, Japan, UAE, Bahrain, Panama, Nigeria, and Scandinavian and Baltic states — to address the Hormuz blockade. Cooper declared: 'We have seen Iran hijack an international shipping route to hold the global economy hostage.' The coalition signed a joint statement demanding Iran cease blocking attempts and pledging to 'contribute to appropriate efforts to ensure safe passage.' France's Macron called military force 'unrealistic' and urged direct diplomatic engagement with Tehran. The GCC separately urged UN Security Council action. Iran responded that 'non-hostile' vessels may transit freely; the strait remains closed only to 'enemy nations and their allies.'

title: Oil surges 9% as Trump speech signals prolonged war; WTI hits $108.95
description: US crude (WTI) surged nearly 9% to $108.95/barrel on Thursday while Brent climbed over 5% to $106.55, reversing the previous day's dip below $100. Traders interpreted Trump's primetime speech — threatening to bomb Iran's power grid to 'the Stone Ages' and pledging 2-3 more weeks of 'extremely hard' strikes — as a signal the war would not end quickly. WTI traded above Brent for the first time in the conflict, an unusual spread indicating severe near-term supply anxiety. The Iran-Oman Hormuz protocol partially offset the spike, with equities recovering intraday, but the net move erased days of de-escalation optimism.

title: EU considers fuel rationing; diesel up 30% in Germany, France; Commissioner: 'long crisis'
description: The European Union began assessing fuel rationing and emergency oil reserve releases as EU-average petrol prices reached €1.87/liter (+14% since Feb 28) and diesel hit €2.07/liter (+30.2%). Germany and France saw diesel surge 32%+ each. EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen stated: 'This will be a long crisis... energy prices will be higher for a very long time.' Asian nations have moved further: Vietnam and Thailand introduced fuel subsidies, Myanmar imposed alternating driving days, and in Bangladesh fuel thefts have turned violent with pump workers killed.

title: Iran fires largest missile salvo of war at Israel on Passover eve; 11-year-old girl critical
description: Iran launched its largest ballistic missile barrage since the war began, firing at least 10 missiles at central Israel just before Passover seder. The IDF reported six separate salvos throughout the day targeting central and northern Israel. Most missiles were intercepted, though cluster-bomb warheads caused damage in Bnei Brak, Rosh HaAyin, and Petah Tikva — one bomblet struck a playground. An 11-year-old girl in Bnei Brak was hospitalized in critical condition; a 13-year-old boy and 36-year-old woman suffered serious shrapnel wounds. At least 25 people were wounded across 20 sites.

title: Trump claims Iran asked for ceasefire; Tehran calls it 'false and baseless'
description: Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran's 'new regime president' has 'just asked the United States of America for a CEASEFIRE,' adding 'Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion.' He set reopening the Strait of Hormuz as a precondition. Iran's Foreign Ministry called the claim 'false and baseless.' FM Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera that messages have been exchanged with US envoy Steve Witkoff but there are 'no negotiations' and Iran has 'zero' trust in Washington. Axios reported the two sides are discussing a ceasefire-for-Hormuz deal via intermediaries including Pakistan.

title: Trump threatens to pull US out of NATO over allies' refusal to join Iran war
description: In a Telegraph interview, Trump said he is 'beyond reconsideration' of NATO membership after allies declined to support US operations in Iran. He told Reuters withdrawal is 'absolutely, without question' on the table and mocked the UK Royal Navy: 'You don't even have a navy.' Secretary of State Rubio said 'If we can't use those bases when we need them, then NATO becomes a one-way street.' UK PM Starmer dismissed it as 'noise,' calling NATO 'the single most effective military alliance the world has ever seen.' The 2024 NDAA requires two-thirds Senate approval to withdraw.

title: Trump tells nation war 'nearing completion'; threatens to bomb Iran to 'Stone Ages'
description: Trump delivered his first primetime address since the war began, speaking for under 20 minutes from the White House Cross Hall. He claimed 'overwhelming victories,' said Iran's navy is 'absolutely destroyed' and missile capability 'dramatically curtailed,' and declared the US had 'totally obliterated those nuclear sites.' He acknowledged 13 US servicemembers killed. Trump threatened to hit Iran's electric grid into 'the Stone Ages' if no deal, and vowed to strike 'extremely hard over the next two to three weeks.' He denied seeking regime change but said 'regime change has occurred because of all of their original leaders' death.' Oil prices jumped 4% as traders read the speech as a sign the war would not end quickly. His economic approval rating hit a career low of 31% with gas at $4.06/gallon.

title: Israeli strike in Beirut kills Hezbollah Iraq commander Yousef Hashem and 6 others
description: An Israeli naval strike in Beirut's Jnah district killed Haj Youssef Ismail Hashem, Hezbollah's military commander for Iraq operations, plus 6 others including commander Mohammad Baqir al-Naboulsi. A source said 'the strike came from warships, and that had not been accounted for.' Hezbollah confirmed Hashem's death, calling him a 'beacon of the Islamic Resistance.' He is the highest-ranking Hezbollah official killed since the war began, inheriting his position from Ali Karaki who was killed alongside Hassan Nasrallah in September 2024. 26 others were wounded.

title: Iranian drones hit Kuwait airport fuel tanks; major fire, no casualties
description: Iranian drones struck fuel storage tanks belonging to Kuwait Aviation Fuelling Company (KAFCO) at Kuwait International Airport, triggering a large fire. Civil Aviation Authority spokesman Abdullah Al Rajhi called it a 'blatant assault.' Firefighters extinguished the blaze; no casualties were reported. The airport remains closed to commercial operations after cumulative damage from attacks since late February disabled radar systems and Terminal 1 infrastructure.

title: Iranian missile strikes QatarEnergy tanker Aqua 1 off Doha; 21 crew evacuated
description: Iran fired three cruise missiles toward Qatar; air defenses intercepted two while the third struck the Panama-flagged tanker Aqua 1 operating under QatarEnergy contract, 17 nautical miles north of Doha. Two projectiles hit the vessel — one caused a fire (extinguished), one lodged unexploded in the engine room. All 21 crew were evacuated safely with no casualties or environmental damage. Iranian attacks have knocked out 17% of Qatar's LNG export capacity, sidelining 12.8 million tons/year of output for 3-5 years.

title: Houthis fire ballistic missiles at southern Israel in third attack since joining war
description: The Houthis announced they fired ballistic missiles at 'sensitive targets' in southern Israel, marking their third attack on Israel since entering the war on March 28. Military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree stated: 'Israel's aggression, crimes and attacks on Lebanon, Iran, Iraq and Palestine will only push us towards further military escalation.' The attack coincided with Iran's largest missile salvo, forcing millions of Israelis into shelters.

title: IDF hits 15 weapons sites in Tehran overnight; 400+ strikes in 48 hours using 650 munitions
description: The IDF announced overnight airstrikes hit 15 Iranian weapon production sites in Tehran, including a 'central complex' of the defense ministry producing advanced anti-aircraft missiles, plus air defense systems, launch sites, and ballistic missile storage. In the previous 48 hours the IDF conducted over 400 strikes using more than 650 munitions. Additional targets hit on Day 33 included pharmaceutical manufacturer Tofigh Daru in Tehran, Isfahan steel plants, and the Shahid Haqqani civilian pier in Bandar Abbas.

title: UAE intercepts 5 ballistic missiles and 35 drones; 1 killed in Fujairah from debris
description: UAE air defenses engaged 5 ballistic missiles and 35 UAVs launched from Iran on Wednesday. Cumulative UAE interceptions since February 28: 438 ballistic missiles, 19 cruise missiles, 2,012 drones. Debris from an intercepted drone killed a Bangladeshi national at Al-Rifa'a farm in Fujairah, while an Indian national was injured in Umm Al Quwain's industrial area. Total UAE casualties since war began: 12 killed and over 190 injured.

title: Brent crude drops below $100 intraday as de-escalation hopes surge
description: Brent crude fell as low as $98.52/barrel on Wednesday, dipping below $100 for the first time since early March, before settling around $101-102. The drop followed Trump's statements about ending the war in 2-3 weeks and reports of backchannel ceasefire discussions. The 'war premium' shed nearly $20 across several trading sessions. Asian shares jumped on de-escalation optimism. US gas prices hit $4.06/gallon, and Trump's economic approval rating fell to a career low of 31%.

title: Bahrain reports fire at business facility from Iranian attack
description: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said civil defense crews extinguished a fire at a business facility caused by an Iranian attack on Wednesday. The strike was part of a broader wave of Iranian attacks across the Gulf on April 1 that also hit Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. Cumulative Bahrain casualties since the war began: at least 2 dead and over 50 injured.

title: UK to host 35-nation Hormuz conference; IRGC claims strait 'fully' under its control
description: Britain announced it will host a virtual meeting Thursday with 35 nations to assess diplomatic options for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Ship transits have dropped 95% — from 130/day in February to 6 in March — stranding an estimated 20,000 seafarers in the war zone. The IRGC countered that the strait is 'fully' under its control. Oil executives warn that unless the strait reopens by mid-April, the world faces an 'oil cliff' as strategic petroleum reserves run dry.

title: WSJ: Trump willing to end war without reopening Strait of Hormuz
description: The Wall Street Journal reported Trump told aides he is willing to end the war even if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, assessing that prying it open would push the conflict beyond his 4-6 week timeline. The plan: achieve core objectives (destroying Iran's navy, missile stocks, defense industry, nuclear capability), wind down hostilities, then pressure Tehran diplomatically to restore shipping. If that fails, Washington would press European and Gulf allies to lead a Hormuz reopening operation. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed Hormuz reopening is not among 'core objectives.' Defense Secretary Hegseth echoed Trump, saying allies 'ought to be prepared to step up on this critical waterway.'

title: UAE intercepts 12 missiles and 36 drones; cumulative toll: 11 dead, 188 injured since Feb 28
description: UAE air defenses intercepted 8 ballistic missiles, 4 cruise missiles, and 36 drones launched from Iran on Tuesday. Cumulative UAE interceptions since February 28: 433 ballistic missiles, 19 cruise missiles, and 1,977 drones. Total UAE casualties since the war began: 11 killed (2 armed forces members, 1 Moroccan contractor, 8 civilians of Pakistani, Nepali, Bangladeshi, Palestinian, and Indian nationalities) and 188 injured. The figures underscore the relentless pace of Iranian attacks on Gulf states even as the air campaign enters its fifth week.

title: Iran International: 4,700 Iranian security forces killed since war began
description: Iran International reported that at least 4,700 Iranian security forces have been killed since the war began on February 28 — far exceeding the Iranian Red Crescent's civilian toll of 1,900 dead as of March 27. The combined figures suggest total Iranian deaths may exceed 6,600. Separately, the Alma Research Center documented 9 Iranian ballistic missile attack waves in the preceding 24 hours, with Iran's cumulative total reaching 413 attack waves against Israel since February 28, killing 19 Israeli civilians and injuring over 6,130.

title: IRGC threatens 18 US companies including Apple, Google, Boeing; sets April 1 deadline
description: The IRGC issued a statement naming 18 US companies as 'legitimate targets,' including Microsoft, Google, Apple, Intel, IBM, Tesla, Boeing, Dell, HP, Cisco, Oracle, Meta, JPMorgan Chase, General Electric, and Nvidia.
